docs.title: Account deletion
docs.description: Explains how a player deletes their own account from inside the game, the recent sign-in rule, what is erased and what stays, and the app-store privacy expectation.
headings: What is erased and what stays?
docs.body:
# Account deletion

A player can delete their own account from inside the game. The Apple App Store and Google Play expect apps that allow account creation to also offer in-app account deletion; this endpoint meets that expectation. Deletion is **irreversible**: neither the player nor an operator can bring a deleted account back.

## Request

First get a CSRF token ([Sessions and CSRF](sessions-and-csrf.md#csrf-çift-gönderim)); then:

```http
POST /v1/auth/account/delete
content-type: application/json
x-crx-env: <environment-id>
x-csrf-token: <csrf-token>

{ "confirm": "delete_my_account" }
```

The player id does not come from the body; it comes from the session. `confirm` is an explicit confirmation; a missing or different value is rejected with `422`. A successful request returns `204` and clears the session and refresh cookies.

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint works only with a **player session**. You cannot delete a player through it with a server key (`Bearer crx_…`); you get `401`. To delete a player as an operator, use the player page in the panel.

## Recent sign-in rule

- A **guest account** is deleted directly.
- For an **account with a linked identity** (email/password, Google or another provider) the session's **sign-in moment** must be at most **10 minutes** ago. Otherwise the server deletes nothing and answers `403` with this body:

```json
{ "code": "recent_sign_in_required" }
```

The app then has the player sign in again and repeats the request. The time is counted from **the sign-in itself**, not from a session refresh; even a player who has been in an open session all day must sign in again. If the sign-in moment cannot be proven, the server stays on the safe side and gives the same `403`.

## What is erased and what stays?

Deletion runs in a single database transaction; either everything happens or nothing does:

| Data | Result |
|---|---|
| Sessions | All are revoked; open realtime connections close. |
| Linked identities (email/password, Google…) | Detached; the password and provider tokens are erased. The same email or the same Google account can later start as a **new player**. |
| Player data (`player data` blobs) | Erased. |
| Player row | Not removed; it is anonymized (`Deleted player`, email and image cleared) and marked deleted. |
| Audit events | Unchanged. The deletion is added as a new `player_self_deleted` event; the event carries no email or provider id. |
| Wallet ledger and plugin records | Unchanged (append-only); because the player row is anonymous, the person cannot be resolved from these records. |

> [!WARNING]
> Free-form personal data that plugins keep in their own tables is not erased by this endpoint. If your plugin stores personal data, you must wire up your own deletion flow separately.

## Errors and limits

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `204` | The account was deleted. |
| `401` | No/invalid session, the player is not active (banned or already deleted), or a server key was presented. A banned player cannot escape the ban through deletion. |
| `403` without a body | CSRF rejection. |
| `403` `recent_sign_in_required` | A fresh sign-in is required; nothing was deleted. |
| `422` | `confirm` is missing or is not `delete_my_account`. |
| `429` | The limit of 5 attempts per hour per player was exceeded. |

## SDK

In the TypeScript SDK:

```ts
try {
  await client.session.deleteAccount({ confirm: "delete_my_account" });
  // the state is now signedOut; take the player to the sign-in screen.
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof CrxError && error.reason === "recent_sign_in_required") {
    // have the player sign in again, then repeat the call
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}
```

On success the SDK ends the session as a password change does and returns `{ status: "signedOut" }`. On `recent_sign_in_required` the session and the account are unchanged. If the response is lost after the request was sent, the outcome is uncertain (`UnknownOutcome`): the SDK does not retry blindly, and the app's `restore()` call decides the real state. The Unity SDK does not have this method yet.

## App-store privacy note

Put an in-app "Delete my account" button where players can reach it, ask for an explicit confirmation before the click is acted on, and wire the button to the `deleteAccount` call. State in your privacy text which data remains after the account is deleted (the wallet ledger stays, anonymized). The deleted account's email and provider id are freed; if the same person registers again they start from scratch.

## Related pages

- [Sessions and CSRF](sessions-and-csrf.md)
- [Guest sign-in](guest.md)
- [Rate limits](../reference/rate-limits.md)

docs.title: Account linking
docs.description: Describes guest upgrade, linking and unlinking a provider identity, listing linked identities, and the conflict rules.
docs.body:
# Account linking

A player's identity is recognized by `player.id`; sign-in methods are the paths **linked** to this identity. This page describes a guest's move to a permanent account, linking and unlinking a Google identity, listing linked identities, and what happens in conflict cases.

> [!NOTE]
> Open Play does **not merge** accounts. If an identity is linked to another player, the request is rejected; the progress of two players is never combined into one account by any means. The only exception is [Google's automatic linking by email](oauth.md#automatic-linking-by-email) rule; even that prevents a new player from being created and adds the identity to the **existing** account.

## From guest to permanent account (upgrade)

A guest player moves to a permanent account in two ways; in both, `player.id` does not change, the guest secret is retired, and a new session is opened:

| Path | Call | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Email and password | `POST /v1/auth/guest/upgrade/email` · TS `upgradeGuest` · Unity `UpgradeGuestAsync` | [Email and password](email-password.md#guest-upgrade) |
| Google | `POST /v1/auth/link/google` + callback · TS `linkOAuth` + `completeOAuth` | [Sign in with Google](oauth.md#linking-guest-progress-to-google) |

Upgrade is **for guest players only**: for a player who is not a guest, email upgrade gives `422`. Email/password cannot be added later to an account that was created with Google or is already registered.

## Listing linked identities

```http
GET /v1/auth/identities
x-crx-env: <environment-id>
```

```json
{
  "player_id": "0192…",
  "identities": [ { "provider": "google", "linked_at": "2026-11-03T10:00:00+00:00" } ]
}
```

- A session is required (otherwise `401`). The response carries `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
- Only **provider** identities are listed (`google`, …); email/password sign-in is not listed. The provider's account ID (`sub`), email, and tokens are **not** in the response.
- TypeScript: `session.listIdentities()` returns `{ playerId, identities: [{ provider, linkedAt }] }` (`camelCase`); the response is strictly validated, an unexpected shape becomes `CrxError(Contract)` and does not drop the session.

This endpoint is enough to show "Link Google" or "Google linked" on your "My account" screen.

## Linking an identity

`POST /v1/auth/link/{provider}` starts an OAuth flow for the player in the session and returns `{url, state}`; the player is redirected to `url`, and on return the [callback](oauth.md#2-complete) completes it. Rules:

- **One identity per provider:** if this provider is already linked on the player, **starting** gives `422` (`unprocessable: provider_already_linked`).
- **Session binding:** the callback must come with the session of the player who started the link; a callback with no session or with another player's session gets `403`.
- **Identity on another player:** if the Google identity is linked to another player, the callback gives `409` (`already exists: account_already_linked`); the guest progress is left untouched.
- A verified email is **not required**; email-less accounts can also link.
- Start and callback rates: 30 / 60 s and 60 / 60 s per IP.

## Unlinking an identity

```http
POST /v1/auth/unlink/google
x-crx-env: <environment-id>
x-csrf-token: <csrf-token>
```

`204`. A session is required. Errors:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `400` | The last remaining provider identity cannot be unlinked (so the account is not locked out) |
| `404` | There is no identity linked to this provider |

> [!NOTE]
> Because a player today usually has a single provider identity, the unlink call in practice mostly gets `400`. The endpoint is in place to be used when a second provider is added. **There is no SDK helper for unlink**; use raw REST.

## Conflict table

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| A guest tries to upgrade with an email whose address is registered to another account | `409`; the guest session is not damaged |
| A guest links to Google and the Google identity is on another player | `409 account_already_linked` |
| A guest links to Google and the email Google verified matches another player's email | `409 account_already_linked` (no merge) |
| A registered player tries to link the same provider a second time | `422 provider_already_linked` |
| A new Google identity matches the email of an existing email/password account (Google vouches) | The identity is **automatically linked** to that account, and the player enters that account |
| Linking to a banned account | Rejected (`403`) |

docs.title: Authentication overview
docs.description: Summarizes the player sign-in methods, the shared request rules, the response format, the rate limits, and which method maps to which SDK call.
headings: Rules that apply to every call
docs.body:
# Authentication overview

This page summarizes how a player signs in to Open Play: which methods exist, which rules they all share, and which page to go to for details. If you are wiring up player sign-in, start here.

## Sign-in methods

| Method | When? | SDK | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Guest** | Quick start without an account; progress is kept on the same device | TS: `signInGuest` · Unity: `SignInGuestAsync` | [Guest sign-in](guest.md) |
| **Email and password** | A permanent account; includes password reset and change | TS and Unity: sign-up, sign-in, upgrade, password operations | [Email and password](email-password.md) |
| **Google** (OAuth) | One-click web sign-in; if there is a verified email, it links automatically to the existing account | TS: `startGoogleOAuth`, `completeGoogleOAuth` · Unity: none | [Sign in with Google](oauth.md) |
| **Native platform proof** (Apple, Game Center, Play Games) | Native mobile sign-ins | **No SDK helper yet**; HTTP endpoint only | [Sign in with Google › Native proofs](oauth.md#native-platform-proofs) |
| **Magic link** | A single-use link sent by email | **No SDK helper yet**; the server endpoint exists | [Email and password › Magic link](email-password.md#magic-link) |

Which methods to offer players is the game's choice; for Google to work, it must be configured in the environment (**Game settings › Sign-in methods**).

Topics after sign-in: [Sessions and CSRF](sessions-and-csrf.md), [Account linking](account-linking.md), [Server-side verification](server-verification.md).

## Which method should I choose?

- **If an account is not required**, start with guest; as the player progresses, link them to email or Google with **guest upgrade**. The player ID (`playerId`) does not change.
- **If you want multiple devices**, you need email/password or Google; a guest identity depends on the secret the device stores.
- For **native mobile sign-in** (Apple, Game Center, Play Games), HTTP endpoints exist, but the SDKs have no helper.

## Rules that apply to every call

The rules below apply to all endpoints under `/v1/auth/*`.

**1. Environment header.** Every request carries `x-crx-env: <environment-id>`. If it is missing or not a UUID, the response is `401`.

**2. Content type.** Requests with a body are sent with `Content-Type: application/json`.

**3. CSRF.** Every request other than `GET` requires double-submit CSRF protection: the `__Secure-crx.csrf` cookie and a matching `x-csrf-token` header. On every successful use the token is returned and changes. You first get a token with `GET /v1/auth/csrf`. Details: [Sessions and CSRF](sessions-and-csrf.md#csrf-double-submit).

**4. Origin check.** For state-changing requests coming from a browser, the `Origin` domain must be bound to the environment. See [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md#domains-and-trusted-origins).

**5. Field names are `snake_case`.** Request and response bodies use `snake_case` (`display_name`, `bootstrap_token`, `old_password`). Two exceptions: `displayName` in the `GET /v1/auth/session` response, and the body/response of `POST /v1/auth/session/display-name` (`displayName`). The SDKs hide this difference from you and present `camelCase`.

**6. Error bodies.** Errors are mostly **plain text** (`permission denied`, `rate limited`…). The only meaningful error with a JSON body is the `403` `{"code":"account_banned","message":"account banned"}` response for a banned account. Status codes: `400` invalid input, `401` environment or session missing/invalid, `403` denied (wrong password, CSRF, expired token — **the distinction is deliberately not leaked**), `409` conflict, `422` unprocessable, `429` rate limit. Details: [Errors](../reference/errors.md).

## Successful sign-in response

The sign-in, sign-up, refresh, and OAuth callback endpoints return the same envelope and write two cookies (`__Secure-crx.session`, `__Secure-crx.refresh`; `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`, `Max-Age=15552000` = 180-day upper bound):

```json
{
  "player": {
    "id": "0192…",
    "display_name": "Guest",
    "email": null,
    "email_verified": false,
    "is_guest": true,
    "image": null,
    "created_at": "2026-11-03T10:00:00+00:00"
  },
  "tokens": {
    "session_token": "<64 hex>",
    "refresh_token": "<64 hex>",
    "access_token": "<jwt>",
    "expires_in_secs": 900
  },
  "is_new_player": true
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `player.id` | The permanent player ID (UUID). Does not change on guest upgrade |
| `player.is_guest` | Whether the account is still a guest |
| `tokens.session_token` | An opaque session token. Can also be used with `Authorization: Bearer` instead of the cookie |
| `tokens.refresh_token` | Only for `/v1/auth/refresh` and `/v1/auth/logout` |
| `tokens.access_token` | A short-lived (15 min) EdDSA JWT; it is for offline verification by your game server. See [Server-side verification](server-verification.md) |
| `tokens.expires_in_secs` | The lifetime of the access JWT (seconds) |
| `is_new_player` | `true` if the call created a new player |

> [!WARNING]
> In browser games, do not store the session and refresh tokens in JavaScript; the cookies are `HttpOnly`, and that is what they are for. The SDKs do not put token bodies in state, logs, or errors.

## Rate limits

The auth endpoints are subject to **fixed-window** rate limits. When exceeded, `429` and the plain text `rate limited` are returned; **there is no `Retry-After` header**: you must wait out the window yourself. Do not resend a failed attempt immediately.

| Limit | Key | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Opening a guest (including re-sign-in) | IP | 30 / 60 s |
| Email sign-in | IP | 5 / 60 s |
| Failed email sign-in lock | address + IP | 10 / 15 min (while locked, even the correct password gets `429`; a successful sign-in refunds the allowance) |
| Sign-up | IP · address | 10 / 60 s · 5 / 15 min |
| Guest upgrade | IP · guest player · address | 10 / 60 s · 30 / 60 s · 5 / 15 min |
| Password change | IP · account | 10 / 60 s · 6 / 60 s |
| Password reset request (forgot) and magic link | IP · address | 5 / 60 s · 5 / 15 min |
| Password reset (reset) | IP | 5 / 60 s (shared bucket with forgot and magic link) |
| OAuth start | IP | 30 / 60 s |
| OAuth callback | IP | 60 / 60 s |
| Display name change | player | 10 / hour |

If there is an extra proxy in front of the server and the trusted proxy addresses have not been declared, all players fall into a single IP bucket. See [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md#calling-from-the-browser-direct-cors-or-reverse-proxy).

## Endpoint summary

| Method and path | Session | Description | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/auth/csrf` | not required | Generates a CSRF token | [Sessions and CSRF](sessions-and-csrf.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/sign-in/guest` | not required | Guest sign-in | [Guest](guest.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/sign-up/email` | not required | Sign-up | [Email](email-password.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/sign-in/email` | not required | Sign-in | [Email](email-password.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/guest/upgrade/email` | guest session | Upgrades a guest to email | [Email](email-password.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/change-password` | required | Changes the password; all sessions close | [Email](email-password.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/forgot-password` | not required | Requests a reset email | [Email](email-password.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/reset-password` | not required | New password with a token | [Email](email-password.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/sign-in/magic-link` · `GET /v1/auth/magic-link/verify` | not required | Magic link | [Email](email-password.md#magic-link) |
| `GET /v1/auth/oauth/providers` | not required | Providers enabled in the environment | [OAuth](oauth.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/sign-in/oauth/{provider}` | not required | Starts OAuth (`{url, state}`) | [OAuth](oauth.md) |
| `GET /v1/auth/callback/{provider}` · `POST` (form) | not required, or required for link | Completes OAuth | [OAuth](oauth.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/native/{provider}` | not required | Native platform proof | [OAuth › Native](oauth.md#native-platform-proofs) |
| `POST /v1/auth/link/{provider}` | required | Starts linking an identity | [Account linking](account-linking.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/unlink/{provider}` | required | Unlinks an identity | [Account linking](account-linking.md) |
| `GET /v1/auth/identities` | required | Linked identities | [Account linking](account-linking.md) |
| `GET /v1/auth/session` | required | Session and profile | [Sessions](sessions-and-csrf.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/session/display-name` | required | Changes the display name | [Sessions](sessions-and-csrf.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/account/delete` | required | Deletes the player's own account (irreversible) | [Account deletion](account-deletion.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/refresh` | refresh token | Refreshes the session (rotation) | [Sessions](sessions-and-csrf.md) |
| `POST /v1/auth/logout` | refresh token | Closes the session | [Sessions](sessions-and-csrf.md) |
| `GET /v1/auth/jwks` | not required | JWT verification keys | [Server-side verification](server-verification.md) |

The `/v1/auth/organization/*` endpoints (player organizations) are being **deprecated**: they work, but every response carries a `Deprecation` header and they are not described in this document. The `/v1/auth/admin/*` endpoints are for player administration with a server key (list, ban, rename, session revocation) and are listed in the [endpoint reference](../reference/endpoints.md).

## Banned accounts

When an operator bans a player, all of the player's sessions are revoked and their open realtime connection closes. How the player appears at sign-in:

- A banned email account with the **correct password**: `403` and `{"code":"account_banned","message":"account banned"}`. A wrong password or an unknown address is an indistinguishable plain-text `403`; the ban status does not leak.
- **A banned guest:** if a guest sign-in is made with the same bootstrap secret, or by presenting the banned player's old session, `403 account_banned` is returned again and **no new player is created**.
- `GET /v1/auth/session` returns `401` for a banned account (the ban code does not leak); refresh, the OAuth callback, and guest upgrade are rejected indistinguishably for a banned owner.
- The response contains no ban reason or end time.
- **SDK behavior:** in TypeScript the session state becomes `banned`; in Unity `SessionStatus.Banned`. Neither opens a new guest, and neither deletes the stored guest secret (so a banned player cannot escape by opening a new guest). Show the player that the account is suspended; do not build a retry loop.

docs.title: Sessions and CSRF
docs.description: Describes carrying the session with a cookie or Bearer, lifetimes, refresh and sign-out, the single active session option, and double-submit CSRF protection.
docs.body:
# Sessions and CSRF

A player who signs in is given a **session**. This page describes how the session is carried, how long it lives, how it is refreshed and closed, and the **CSRF** (cross-site request forgery) protection that is required on state-changing requests. If you use an SDK, it manages most of this for you; if you are writing raw REST, this page is the contract.

## How the session is carried

The server reads the session from one of two places; the cookie first, otherwise the `Authorization` header:

| Channel | Who uses it? | Format |
|---|---|---|
| **Cookie** | Browser games | `__Secure-crx.session=<64 hex>` (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`) |
| **Bearer** | Clients without cookies (command line, some native clients) | `Authorization: Bearer <session_token>` (the opaque token in the sign-in response) |

Every player request also carries `x-crx-env: <environment-id>`. What is carried on the Bearer path is the **opaque session token**; it is not the access JWT (that is for offline verification by your game server: [Server-side verification](server-verification.md)).

### Reading the session

```http
GET /v1/auth/session
x-crx-env: <environment-id>
```

```json
{
  "environment_id": "0192…",
  "player_id": "0192…",
  "session_id": "0192…",
  "is_guest": false,
  "active_organization_id": null,
  "displayName": "Alex",
  "email": "alex@example.com"
}
```

`email` is `null` for guest and email-less (Google-only) accounts. The response carries personal data and comes with `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. If there is no session, it has been revoked, it has expired, or the account is banned, **`401`** is returned (the distinction does not leak).

## Lifetimes

| Item | Duration |
|---|---|
| Session and refresh window | **30 days, sliding** |
| Absolute upper bound | **180 days** (from the start of the session family; cannot be exceeded by any means) |
| Access JWT | 15 minutes |
| Cookie `Max-Age` | 15,552,000 s (180 days); it is only an upper bound, the decision is on the server |
| CSRF cookie | 15 minutes |

- **Sliding:** when the player makes a request with the session at least once a day, the session end is pushed 30 days ahead (without exceeding the upper bound). Every refresh also pulls the duration back to 30 days.
- A session that makes no request for 30 days dies. On day 180 even an active session ends; the player signs in again (a guest returns to the same account with the same secret).
- Keeping a realtime connection open does **not** extend the session.

## Refresh

```http
POST /v1/auth/refresh
content-type: application/json
x-crx-env: <environment-id>
x-csrf-token: <csrf-token>

{}
```

The refresh token is carried in the body (`{"refresh_token":"…"}`) or in the `__Secure-crx.refresh` cookie (the body takes precedence; if the cookie is present, the body can be empty). The response is `200` and a **new** session and refresh pair (the cookies are also renewed; the shared sign-in envelope). The old refresh token counts as used.

- **Reuse detection:** presenting a used refresh token again **revokes the entire session family** (a defense against a stolen token).
- Error: `403` (the token is invalid, expired, reused, or a CSRF rejection).
- The SDKs refresh on their own when needed; you do not call it.

## Sign-out

```http
POST /v1/auth/logout
content-type: application/json
x-crx-env: <environment-id>
x-csrf-token: <csrf-token>

{}
```

`204`; the session is revoked and the cookies are deleted (`Max-Age=0`). The call is **idempotent**: an unknown token succeeds silently. If there is no refresh token at all (the cookie and the body are empty), `400` is returned.

Password change, password reset, and an operator ban also revoke sessions; see the relevant pages.

## Single active session (optional)

The **Game settings › Sign-in methods › Sign-in settings › Single active session** switch in the panel (super admin only) is turned on per environment. When it is on, every sign-in path that gives the player a new session **revokes the player's other sessions** after the new session is written ("the latest sign-in wins").

- The switch does not close open sessions at the moment it is turned on; it applies only from the next sign-in.
- Refresh does not trigger this policy.
- The session on the other device gets `401` on its next request; the SDK state becomes `reauthRequired`. Your game can show a screen such as "signed in from another device" in this case.

## CSRF double-submit

A session carried in a cookie is also added automatically by the browser to other sites' requests. To prevent this, **double-submit** CSRF protection is applied to state-changing requests: the same token must arrive both in the cookie and in the header.

**Scope.** It is required on these requests: all non-`GET` requests under `/v1/auth/*` (including the sign-in endpoints); plugin commands called with a player session (and queries called with POST); player store purchases (only in a cookie session; in an `Authorization: Bearer` session only the Origin and Fetch Metadata checks apply); the realtime ticket request. `GET` requests are exempt. Calls made **with a server key** are not subject to CSRF.

**Flow.**

1. `GET /v1/auth/csrf` is called. The response: body `{"token":"<hex>"}`, header `x-csrf-token: <the same token>`, and `Set-Cookie: __Secure-crx.csrf=<sealed grant>`.
2. Every state-changing request sends the **cookie** (`__Secure-crx.csrf`) and the **header** (`x-csrf-token`) together. The browser adds the cookie itself; your code adds the header.
3. On every successful request the token **rotates**: the response carries a new `x-csrf-token` header and a new `Set-Cookie`. Use **the new one** on the next request.
4. The token is **single-use.** A request sent again with the old token gets `403` (replay protection).

```bash
# Get a token
TOKEN="$(curl -sS -c "$JAR" "$OPEN_PLAY_URL/v1/auth/csrf" | jq -r .token)"

# Use it; keep the new token from the response header for the next request
curl -sS -D headers.txt -b "$JAR" -c "$JAR" -X POST "$OPEN_PLAY_URL/v1/auth/logout" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" -H "x-crx-env: $OPEN_PLAY_ENV" -H "x-csrf-token: $TOKEN" -d '{}'
TOKEN="$(grep -i '^x-csrf-token:' headers.txt | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '\r')"
```

Things to watch out for:

- **Do not send two concurrent mutations with the same token;** when one succeeds, the other gets `403`. Put the requests in a queue. The SDKs do this with a single lock.
- The CSRF cookie lives for 15 minutes; when it expires you get `403`. Get a fresh token and retry **once**. The `403` is plain text and does not distinguish between a CSRF rejection and an authorization rejection; if no new `x-csrf-token` header came in the response, you know it was a CSRF layer rejection.
- The Origin check is the first layer of CSRF: the `Origin` domain of a browser request must be bound to the environment. See [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md#domains-and-trusted-origins).
- Clients without cookies (Bearer) must also carry the CSRF cookie and header on `/v1/auth/*` and plugin endpoints (the Bearer branch of the store purchase is the exception). The Unity SDK does this by managing the cookies itself in a native build and with the browser's cookies in WebGL.

## SDK and session states

TypeScript `session.state.status` values:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `signedOut` | No session |
| `authenticating` | Sign-in or restore in progress |
| `authenticated` | Session open; `playerId`, `sessionId`, `isGuest`, `displayName`, `email` are filled |
| `refreshing` | Refresh in progress |
| `reauthRequired` | The session was lost or could not be refreshed; sign-in is needed again |
| `signingOut` / `logoutUncertain` | Sign-out in progress / its outcome is uncertain (can be retried) |
| `banned` | The account is banned; terminal |

In Unity the equivalent is the `SessionStatus` values (`SignedOut`, `Authenticating`, `Authenticated`, `Refreshing`, `ReauthRequired`, `SigningOut`, `LogoutUncertain`, `Banned`, `Disposed`); state changes arrive through the `Session.StateChanged` event.

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/sdk-session-state.ts -->
```ts
import { CrxError, ErrorKind, createPlayerClient, type PlayerClient, type SessionState } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";

/** Oturum durumunu arayüze bağlar; `state.status` değerleri kapalı bir kümedir. */
export function watchSession(client: PlayerClient, render: (label: string) => void): () => void {
  const label = (state: SessionState): string => {
    switch (state.status) {
      case "authenticated": return state.isGuest === true ? "Misafir" : (state.displayName ?? "Oyuncu");
      case "banned": return "Hesap askıya alındı";
      case "reauthRequired": return "Yeniden giriş gerekiyor";
      case "signedOut": return "Giriş yapılmadı";
      default: return "…"; // authenticating, refreshing, signingOut, logoutUncertain
    }
  };
  render(label(client.session.state));
  return client.session.subscribe((state) => render(label(state))); // dönen işlev aboneliği kapatır
}

/** Sayfa kapanırken: sunucu oturumunu kapatmak için `logout`, yalnız yerel kaynakları bırakmak için `dispose`. */
export async function leave(client: PlayerClient, signOut: boolean): Promise<void> {
  try {
    if (signOut) await client.session.logout();
  } catch (error) {
    if (!(error instanceof CrxError && error.kind === ErrorKind.UnknownOutcome)) throw error;
    // Yanıt kaybolduysa sunucu oturumu kapanmamış olabilir (durum `logoutUncertain`); gerekirse logout'u yeniden deneyin.
  } finally {
    await client.dispose();
  }
}

export function createClient(environmentId: string): PlayerClient {
  return createPlayerClient({ baseUrl: window.location.origin, environmentId });
}
```

`dispose()` only releases local resources; to close the server session, call `logout()` first. `AuthenticatedSession.email` is only for the player's own screen; do not write it to logs or analytics.

docs.title: Using AI tools (MCP)
docs.description: Explains how to set up the MCP server that connects AI assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code to the Open Play docs and SDK API, and what its tools do.
docs.body:
# Using AI tools (MCP)

The Open Play MCP (Model Context Protocol) server lets your AI assistant answer questions such as "how do I sign in a guest", "how do I save player data" or "how do I call a plugin" from the official documentation on this site and from the SDK API, instead of guessing. The server is **read-only**: it never touches your Open Play server, your keys or the network; the docs and the SDK index are bundled into the package at build time, so no internet access is needed while it runs.

## Installation

The package name is `@ferdiunal/open-play-mcp` (source: `sdks/mcp`). Like the TypeScript SDK it is published on GitHub Packages; the repository is private, so installing it requires an authorized GitHub token. Until the package is published you can build it from the repository:

```bash
cd sdks/mcp
npm ci
npm run build        # produces dist/cli.js and dist/index.json
```

In the examples below, use `node /path/sdks/mcp/dist/cli.js` instead of `npx -y @ferdiunal/open-play-mcp` to run the local build. For the `npx` route your user `.npmrc` needs the line `@ferdiunal:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` and a token for that registry (never write the token into docs or the repository).

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add open-play -- npx -y @ferdiunal/open-play-mcp
```

### Cursor and VS Code

Add this to `.cursor/mcp.json` for Cursor, or to `.vscode/mcp.json` for VS Code (use the key `servers` instead of `mcpServers` there):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "open-play": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@ferdiunal/open-play-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### HTTP mode

The same server also runs over Streamable HTTP, which is useful when you want to put one shared address in front of a team:

```bash
npx -y @ferdiunal/open-play-mcp --http 8787     # http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp
```

By default it binds only to `127.0.0.1` (change with `--host`). There is no public `https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/mcp` address yet.

## Tools

Tool names and descriptions are in English; pass `lang: "tr"` to get the Turkish page content (the default is `en`).

| Tool | What it does | Example input |
|---|---|---|
| `search_docs` | Searches the docs; scoring runs title, then headings, then body; returns the page id, description and public URL | `{"query": "guest sign in"}` |
| `read_doc` | Returns the full markdown of one page (at most 40,000 characters) | `{"page": "auth/guest"}` |
| `list_docs` | Lists page ids and titles; `section` limits it to one section | `{"section": "auth"}` |
| `search_sdk` | Searches type, function and member names in the TypeScript and Unity SDKs | `{"query": "signInGuest", "sdk": "typescript"}` |
| `get_sdk_symbol` | Returns the signature, summary and members of a type; the `Type.Member` form is supported | `{"name": "PlayerSession", "sdk": "unity"}` |

Every doc page is also a **resource** at `open-play-docs://<lang>/<page>` (for example `open-play-docs://en/auth/guest`), and a **prompt** named `integrate_open_play` (`platform`: `web`, `unity` or `server`) returns integration steps and the right page links.

> **Limit:** The Unity API index is extracted from the C# source by a lightweight parser; details such as inheritance and generic type parameters may be missing. For an exact reference use the generated reference linked from the [Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md) page. SDK summaries are in Turkish for now, because they come from the Turkish comments in the source code.

## Example questions

- "How do I sign a player in as a guest?" → `search_docs` + `read_doc` (`auth/guest`).
- "How do I save player data?" → `guides/player-data`.
- "How do I call a plugin?" → `plugins/calling-plugins`.
- "Which methods does `PlayerSession` have in Unity?" → `get_sdk_symbol`.

For a first look, start from the [Quickstart](quickstart.md).

docs.title: Architecture and hosting
docs.description: Explains what runs where in the Open Play stack, direct CORS calls and the reverse-proxy option for browser games, and domain binding.
headings: Calling from the browser: direct CORS or reverse proxy
docs.body:
# Architecture and hosting

This page explains how to position your game with Open Play: the parts of the stack, how browser games call Open Play directly (CORS) or through a reverse proxy, binding a domain to an environment, and cookie/TLS requirements. If you will publish a browser or WebGL game, read this page from start to finish.

## What runs where

The reference deployment is a Docker Compose stack:

| Part | Role | Exposed externally? |
|---|---|---|
| **api** | REST, WebSocket, and the realtime surface; all business logic | Only through the gateway |
| **worker** | Background jobs: event queue (outbox), webhook delivery, scheduled jobs, ranking projections | No |
| **PostgreSQL** | Persistent data | No |
| **Redis** | Rate limits, CSRF usage records, realtime keys | No |
| **converter** | 3D model conversion (`amd64` only) | No |
| **public-gateway** | The Caddy gateway opened to players and to the game server; cuts `/v1/panel/*` off with `404` | Yes (the layer in front terminates TLS) |
| **admin-gateway** | The admin panel | Loopback only by default |
| **grpc-proxy** | gRPC for trusted services | Loopback only by default |

```text
Player browser ──HTTPS──▶ game.example.com ─┬─ /            ▶ your game's static files
                                            └─ /open-play/* ▶ Open Play public-gateway ▶ api
Your game server ───────HTTPS───────────────────────────────▶ Open Play public-gateway ▶ api
Open Play worker ──signed webhook───────────────────────────▶ your server
```

Public TLS is not terminated inside this stack; you need Cloudflare, a load balancer, or a Caddy/nginx entry point. Because the panel cookie is `Secure`, the panel also requires HTTPS. For installation, resource budgets, and network details, see the [production deployment guide](../../../production-and-adapters.tr.md).

> [!NOTE]
> The gRPC interface is not a public channel for game developers; by default it listens on loopback only and the SDKs do not use it.

## Calling from the browser: direct CORS or reverse proxy

**If your game's domain is in the environment's domain list, your browser game can call Open Play directly.** On the public API (panel and setup endpoints excluded) the server sends CORS (cross-origin resource sharing) headers. The allowed set is the union of the domains written to all environments under **Game settings › Environments and domains** in the panel and the operator's global allowed list (`CRX_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`); there is no game-specific setting. For example, if the game runs at `https://game.example.com`, Open Play at `https://open-play.example.com`, and `game.example.com` is an environment domain, the game talks to it directly with `baseUrl: "https://open-play.example.com/open-play"`.

Rules:

- The allowed origin is exactly `https://<domain>` (no path, no non-default port). The response reflects that origin verbatim in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and adds `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`; `*` is never used and unknown origins get no headers.
- A preflight (`OPTIONS`) returns `204` for an allowed origin and `403` for a disallowed one; `Access-Control-Max-Age` is 600 s.
- In non-production environments (`CRX_ENV` development or test), if `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` is in the list, `http://localhost:<port>` and `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` are allowed too.
- A domain newly added in the panel takes effect within a few seconds (the server snapshot refreshes every 5 s).
- **CORS is not authorization.** The `Origin`/CSRF/environment checks run unchanged; CORS only lets the browser read the response. The panel path (`/v1/panel/*`) never gets CORS headers. The realtime WebSocket handshake is unchanged: `Origin` is checked per environment.

> [!WARNING]
> **The session cookie needs the same site.** Cookies are written with `__Secure-`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`. If the game is on a **different registrable domain** than Open Play (for example `game.example.com` and `open-play.other.dev`), the browser does not attach the session cookie to cross-site `fetch` requests; even with correct CORS headers a session cannot be established. Subdomains of the same registrable domain (for example `game.example.com` and `open-play.example.com`) are the same site and work. A different site is not supported; use the reverse proxy below in that case.

**A reverse proxy is still an option.** If you want to serve the game and the API from the same origin (or the game is on a different site), set up a reverse proxy on the game's own gateway that routes the API path to Open Play; CORS then does not come into play. Example (Caddy):

```caddyfile
game.example.com {
  # Strips the /open-play/ prefix and forwards to the Open Play public-gateway.
  handle_path /open-play/* {
    reverse_proxy open-play-gateway:8080
  }
  # Everything else is your game's static files.
  handle {
    root * /srv/game
    try_files {path} /index.html
    file_server
  }
}
```

With a reverse proxy, the client-side configuration is:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| TypeScript `baseUrl` | `https://game.example.com/open-play` (the SDKs accept a path prefix), or `window.location.origin` if you do not use a prefix |
| Unity `BaseUrl` | the same address; today the Unity WebGL SDK requires the same origin as the page, otherwise you get the `webgl_cross_origin_unsupported` configuration error (server CORS does not lift this; see [Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md)) |
| `x-crx-env` | the environment ID (the SDKs send it from the `environmentId` setting) |

Watch out for these on the reverse proxy:

- **The WebSocket upgrade** (`Upgrade`/`Connection`) must pass through; the realtime connection is on `/v1/realtime/ws`. Caddy's `reverse_proxy` does this on its own; on nginx, set `proxy_http_version 1.1` and the `Upgrade` headers explicitly.
- **The `Origin` and `Cookie` headers** must be forwarded as they are.
- **Client IP:** set the `X-Forwarded-For` header correctly. If there is an extra proxy in front and the proxy addresses the server should trust have not been declared, all players fall into a single IP bucket; the symptom is different players getting `429` at the same time. Resolve this with your operator team (see [Rate limits](../reference/rate-limits.md)).
- **Do not open the panel path.** The `/v1/panel/*` path is `404` on the public-gateway; do not give the panel a route through your game domain.

### Cookie behavior

| Cookie | Purpose | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| `__Secure-crx.session` | Player session | `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/` |
| `__Secure-crx.refresh` | Session refresh | same |
| `__Secure-crx.csrf` | CSRF double-submit cookie | same; 15-minute lifetime |

`Secure` cookies require HTTPS. In local development, the SDKs allow plain `http` only on loopback addresses (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`); check whether your browser accepts `Secure` cookies for `localhost`, and if it does not, use HTTPS locally as well.

## Domains and trusted origins

The browser adds an `Origin` header to state-changing (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) requests. The server checks whether this origin is a domain bound to the relevant environment:

- **Domain bound to the environment:** the names you enter in the panel under **Game settings › Environments and domains › Domains**. Each line is one full domain (for example `game.example.com`); there are no wildcards, IPs, or ports; at most 10 domains can be bound per environment. The same domain cannot be bound to two environments (`409`).
- **Global allowed list:** the operator's server setting (`CRX_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`: a full domain or `*.domain`). If the environment has no domain of its own, this list applies.
- **If a domain is bound to another environment**, a browser coming from that domain cannot write to this environment and cannot read this environment (`403`).
- **Clients that do not send `Origin`** (your game server, non-browser clients such as `curl`) are not caught by the origin check; if they use cookies, the CSRF double-submit protection checks them.
- If `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` and `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate` arrive together, the state-changing request is rejected.

The realtime ticket is also bound to the same origin rule: a ticket is single-use and bound to the origin it was obtained from.

> [!NOTE]
> Unity native builds send a fixed `Origin` derived from configuration on ticket and WebSocket requests (the scheme, domain, and non-default port of `BaseUrl`; can be changed with `NativeOrigin`). This origin must be in the environment's domains or in the global allowed list. See [Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md).

Domain binding steps: [Environments and domains](../panel/game-settings-environments.md).

## Calling from your game server

Your game server connects **directly** (HTTPS) to Open Play with a server key. No reverse proxy, CORS, or domain binding is needed (CORS concerns only the browser); the environment comes from the key. Keep the key only in the server environment (an environment variable or secret management).

To verify a player's identity on your server, you can verify the access JWT offline: [Server-side verification](../auth/server-verification.md).

## Webhooks (Open Play → your server)

The worker sends events to your address as signed HTTPS requests. Your address must be publicly reachable and must verify the signature. See [Webhooks](../guides/webhooks.md) and [Security](../operations/security.md).

## Pre-release check

The [Production checklist](../operations/production-checklist.md) gathers the items for domain binding, key management, TLS, and monitoring.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.description: Defines the concepts of studio, game, environment, module, API key types, player session, and plugin.
docs.body:
# Core concepts

Everything in Open Play revolves around a few concepts: the **environment** that data belongs to, the **modules** that turn features on and off, two kinds of **API key**, the player's **session**, and the **plugin** that carries game-specific logic. Read this page once; the other pages assume you know these words.

## Studio, game, environment

Open Play uses a three-level hierarchy. In the panel you manage this tree on the **Studios and games** screen (visible only to the super admin).

| Level | Meaning | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Studio** | The organization that holds your games together | A server can have more than one studio |
| **Game** | A single product | When a new game is created, the `dev` and `prod` environments are opened automatically |
| **Environment** | An isolated copy of the game: `dev`, `prod`, and `staging` if you want it | Players, characters, wallets, and keys belong to an environment |

**The environment is the data boundary.** A player, character, wallet, or key in one environment is not visible from another environment. Every API call runs against a single environment:

- In calls made **with an API key**, the environment comes from the key; you do not send an extra header.
- In calls made **with a player session**, you declare the environment with the `x-crx-env: <environment-id>` header. The ID is a UUID. The SDKs send it from the `environmentId` setting.

> [!NOTE]
> Today the panel does not show the environment ID (UUID) in a readable field. Ask your operator team for the ID, or read it from the `environmentId` field in the response to the `GET /v1/panel/modules` request that the **Game settings › Modules** tab makes in a panel session. This gap is on record.

For the panel steps, see [Quickstart](quickstart.md#1-create-a-game-and-an-environment) and [Game settings](../panel/game-settings-environments.md).

## Modules

Most features are modules: `characters`, `economy`, `items`, `trading`, `store`, `rewards`, `social`, `chat`, `competition`, `notifications`, `webhooks`, `scenes`, `plugins` (13 modules). Modules are turned on and off **per environment**; at installation the wizard has you choose a starter set, and afterwards you use the **Game settings › Modules** tab (super admin only).

- The endpoints of a disabled module do not work: HTTP `404` with the body `{"code":"module_disabled","message":"…","module":"<name>"}`. A caller with invalid credentials gets `401` and cannot find out that the module is disabled.
- Disabling does not delete data, it only stops the surface; when you enable it again the data is still there.
- Some modules depend on others (for example `trading` relies on `economy` and `items`), and a module that an active plugin needs cannot be disabled.
- Core surfaces (player sign-in, content groups, API keys) are not modules and cannot be disabled.

For error details, see [Errors](../reference/errors.md).

## API keys: server and client

An API key is a secret string bound to an **environment**, sent with the `Authorization: Bearer` header. Its format:

```text
crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

The panel shows only the `crx_live_<prefix>` part (the prefix); the secret is shown **once, at the moment it is created** and cannot be recovered. If you lose it, you create a new key or rotate the key: the old secret becomes invalid and the new one is shown once.

| | Server key | Client key |
|---|---|---|
| Where is it used? | Your game server, your backend code | The game client (browser, mobile) |
| Can it be embedded? | **No**, keep it secret | Yes |
| What can it do? | All operations: creating definitions, granting money, minting items, registering webhooks, administration | Only permitted, non-sensitive operations |
| Example | the `add_xp` command, granting money, minting items | reading a character, the `set_flag` command |

The exact rule changes **per endpoint** and is tested per endpoint in code. Which endpoint accepts which key type is listed in the [endpoint reference](../reference/endpoints.md). If the key type is insufficient, the call gets `403`.

To create a key in the panel: **Game settings › API keys › New API key** (see [API keys](../panel/game-settings-api-keys.md)). When you create one, you enter a name, the type (Server key or Client key), the validity period, and a note written to the audit log (8–500 characters).

> [!WARNING]
> **Advanced settings** (scope labels, permissions, extra information) are for record-keeping only today; they do not restrict what the key can access. Only the key type determines access. Do not treat a server key as "restricted".

For managing keys and secret values, see [Security](../operations/security.md).

## Player session

Players talk to the server not with an API key but with their own **sessions**. A session is opened in these ways: guest sign-in, email and password, Google. On a successful sign-in the server writes a session cookie (`__Secure-crx.session`) and a refresh cookie (`__Secure-crx.refresh`); the same tokens are also returned in the response body, so clients without cookies (the Unity native build, command-line tools) can use `Authorization: Bearer <session-token>`.

Every request made with a player session carries the `x-crx-env` header. In a cookie-based (browser) session, state-changing requests additionally require **CSRF** protection (the `x-csrf-token` header). The SDKs manage these details for you; with raw REST you implement them yourself:

- [Authentication overview](../auth/overview.md)
- [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)

The player session can also be carried to **your game server**: the player's short-lived **access JWT** (EdDSA) is verified offline with a shared JWKS. See [Server-side verification](../auth/server-verification.md).

## Plugin

A plugin is a package **compiled into the server** that carries game-specific server logic (commands, queries, realtime modules). Plugin calls are made under `/v1/plugins/{plugin}/...`; state-changing commands carry an idempotency key and, if the schema requires it, a version check with `expectedVersion`. A plugin's schema is an artifact (`<plugin>.plugin.schema.json`), and the TypeScript/Unity bindings are generated from this schema.

> [!NOTE]
> Loading third-party plugins (from the panel or the API) is not supported today. Plugins come with the Open Play server release. See [Plugins overview](../plugins/overview.md).

## Common call rules

The same three rules apply to many endpoints; you will find the details in the reference pages:

- **Idempotency-Key:** for state-changing commands, the same key and the same body replay the result; the same key with a different body returns `422`. See [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md).
- **If-Match / expectedVersion:** by declaring the version of the resource that you read, you catch a concurrent write conflict (`409`).
- **Numbers:** large integers (`i64`) become `bigint` in JavaScript; in the plugin protocol they are carried as decimal strings. See [Numbers and encoding](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md).

For short definitions of terms, see the [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md).

docs.title: Open Play overview
docs.description: Explains what Open Play gives your game, which surfaces you talk to, and where to start.
headings: What does it offer? The module map
Which channel do you talk through?
docs.body:
# Open Play overview

This page summarizes which ready-made building blocks Open Play offers your game and which channel you use to talk to each of them. Read it before you start integrating; follow the links at the end of each section for details.

## What is Open Play?

Open Play covers a game's backend needs as a single server: player identity and sessions, characters, inventory, economy, store, rewards, social features, leaderboards, notifications, webhooks, and realtime connections. You connect your game to this server over HTTP (REST) and WebSocket; the team that runs the game configures the same server from the **admin panel**.

> [!NOTE]
> Today Open Play is a Docker Compose stack and runs on your or your team's infrastructure. For installation and deployment, see the [production deployment guide](../../../production-and-adapters.tr.md); this document describes the game developer's point of view.

## What does it offer? The module map

Most features are turned on and off as **modules**. The endpoints of a disabled module do not work and return `404` with the code `module_disabled` (see [Concepts](concepts.md#modules)). Modules are managed in the panel under **Game settings › Modules**.

| Module | What it gives your game | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| `characters` | Character definitions, characters, commands, rules, traits, level curves | [Characters](../guides/characters.md) |
| `economy` | Currencies, wallets, transfers, ledger | [Economy](../guides/economy.md) |
| `items` | Item definitions, item instances, inventory | [Inventory and items](../guides/inventory-items.md) |
| `trading` | Merchants and player-to-player trading | Raw REST: [endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md) |
| `store` | Store catalog, purchasing, in-app purchase (IAP) verification | [Store and IAP](../guides/store-iap.md) |
| `rewards` | Reward tables, quests, NPC rewards, VIP, daily login reward | [Rewards](../guides/rewards.md) |
| `social` | Clans and parties | [Social](../guides/social.md) |
| `chat` | Chat | [Chat](../guides/chat.md) |
| `competition` | Leaderboards and tournaments | [Competition](../guides/competition.md) |
| `notifications` | Notification channels, templates, player inbox, web push | [Notifications](../guides/notifications.md) |
| `webhooks` | Delivering game events to your own server, signed | [Webhooks](../guides/webhooks.md) |
| `scenes` | Scenes and visual assets | [Scenes, assets, models](../guides/scenes-assets-models.md) |
| `plugins` | The plugin platform and the realtime surface | [Plugins](../plugins/overview.md), [Realtime](../realtime/overview.md) |

**Core** surfaces that have no module switch are always on:

- **Player identity and sessions:** guest, email/password, Google. See [Authentication](../auth/overview.md).
- **Content groups and catalog:** data managed from the panel and read by the game. See [Content groups](../guides/content-groups.md).
- **Game rules and automations.** See [Game rules](../guides/game-rules.md).
- **API keys, environments, and domains.** See [Concepts](concepts.md).

## Which channel do you talk through?

| Channel | Who uses it? | Credential | What for? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **REST** (`/v1/...`) + server key | Your game server (trusted backend) | `Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>` | Administration and operations that change money or items |
| **REST** + client key | Your game client | a client key in the same format | Limited, non-sensitive operations |
| **REST** + player session | The player's own client (browser, Unity) | cookie or session token + `x-crx-env` | The player's own data: sign-in, catalog, store, rankings, plugin commands |
| **WebSocket** (`/v1/realtime/ws` etc.) | The player's client | single-use ticket | Plugin state, live input, uninterrupted streaming |
| **Webhook** (Open Play → your server) | Your server | `X-Crx-Signature` signature | Event notification |
| **SDK** | TypeScript and Unity | a wrapper over the channels above | Typed use of REST and WebSocket |

> [!WARNING]
> A server key is a secret. Do not put it in the browser, in a mobile app, or in the game bundle. On the client side, use only the player session and (if needed) a client key.

A gRPC interface exists on the server side, but it is not a public channel for game developers; by default it listens on loopback only and the SDKs do not use it. This document does not cover it.

## Where to start

1. [Concepts](concepts.md): studio, game, environment, module, key types, player session.
2. [Quickstart](quickstart.md): your first server call and your first player sign-in.
3. [Architecture and hosting](architecture-and-hosting.md): direct CORS or reverse proxy, domains, what runs where.
4. [Authentication](../auth/overview.md) and the [SDKs](../sdk/typescript.md).

## Current limits

The following are written honestly on purpose; plan your roadmap accordingly.

- **CORS is open only to origins in the environment's domain list, and the cookie needs the same site.** A browser game can call Open Play directly if its domain is bound to an environment; if the game is on a different registrable domain than Open Play, the `SameSite=Lax` session cookie is not sent (use a reverse proxy). See [Architecture and hosting](architecture-and-hosting.md#calling-from-the-browser-direct-cors-or-reverse-proxy).
- **Loading third-party plugins is not supported.** Plugins ship compiled into the server; you cannot upload a plugin from the panel. See [Plugins](../plugins/overview.md).
- **SDK coverage is partial.** Modules that have no typed client in the TypeScript SDK are used through raw REST. See [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md#scope-which-modules-have-a-typed-client).
- **On Unity, only Unity 6000.6.7f1 is verified.** See [Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md#verified-platforms).
- **Error bodies are mostly plain text.** Only a few places have a JSON error envelope. See [Errors](../reference/errors.md).

docs.description: Describes character templates, creating characters, commands, level curves and the version rule.
headings: Where it lives in the panel
docs.body:
# Characters

This page explains how the character a player plays is defined, created and changed in Open Play. Read it if you want to keep character state (attributes, resources, XP, level, abilities, flags) on the server and change it with cheat-proof commands.

## What it does

The character module (`characters`) keeps player-bound character state in one trustworthy place. State changes only through **commands**, and every change is recorded as an immutable event. This lets you read back a character's state at any point in time and undo a faulty change with a new event.

If the module is disabled, every endpoint on this page returns `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"characters"}`. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| Define a character template, a trait and a level curve | [Character templates](../panel/character-templates.md) |
| List characters, open one and see its state and history | [Characters](../panel/characters.md), [Character profile](../panel/character-profile.md) |
| See a player's account and characters together | [Players](../panel/players.md), [Player profile](../panel/player-profile.md) |
| Write event-driven automation | [Game rules](game-rules.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Trait:** A reusable bundle of fields. For example, a "warrior" trait brings strength and health fields. A template combines several traits.
- **Template (definition):** A character type identified by a key (`warrior`). It says which traits it uses, the defaults of the fields, how the character is created (`defaults`, `point_buy`, `roll`) and which level curve it follows. A template becomes **a new version** on every publish; existing characters stay bound to the version they were born with.
- **Level curve:** Describes how many XP a level corresponds to. The level is not stored; it is derived from cumulative XP, so changing the curve does not require migrating character data. There are three kinds: `table` (a list of thresholds), `piecewise` (XP per level range) and `formula` (a quadratic formula, with `max_level`).
- **Character:** An instance born from a template. You can write your game's own player ID into `external_id`; two characters in the same environment cannot have the same `external_id`.
- **State:** `attributes` (trait values), `resources` (consumed resources such as health/mana), `progression` (`level`, `xp`, `highest_level`), `abilities`, `flags` (yes/no flags) and the free-form `custom` field.
- **Version (`version`):** A number that grows with every command on the character. It is used to prevent concurrent writes (see below).

Numbers are integers (`i64`); there are no decimals. Percentages are written in basis points, `10000` = 100%. Details: [Numbers and encoding](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md).

## Calls your game makes

Character endpoints are called with an **API key**; a player session (cookie or session token) is not valid on these endpoints. Request header:

```
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

The key type matters (see [Concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)): a **server key** runs every command, a **client key** can only run the `set_flag` command. Do not embed a server key in your game.

| Method and path | Key | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/definitions` | any (see note below) | Saves a template as a new version |
| `GET /v1/definitions/{key}` | any | Reads the current template and the resolved schema |
| `POST /v1/traits` | any (note) | Saves a trait |
| `POST /v1/level-curves` | any (note) | Saves a level curve |
| `GET /v1/level-curves/{key}` | any | Reads a curve |
| `POST /v1/characters` | any | Creates a character from a template |
| `GET /v1/characters` | any | Lists characters (`definition`, `cursor`, `limit`) |
| `GET /v1/characters/{id}` | any | Reads a character with its state |
| `DELETE /v1/characters/{id}` | any | Deletes a character (soft delete, `204`) |
| `POST /v1/characters/{id}/commands` | depends on the command | Runs a command |
| `GET /v1/characters/{id}/stats` | any | Returns effective values and the calculation breakdown |
| `GET /v1/characters/{id}/events` | any | Event log (`cursor`, `limit`) |
| `GET /v1/characters/{id}/timeline` | any | Human-readable timeline |
| `GET /v1/characters/{id}/state?at=` | any | Reconstructs the state at a past moment |

Identity and module rules and error bodies: [Errors](../reference/errors.md). Pagination: [Pagination](../reference/pagination.md) (`limit` 1–200, default 50; when `next_cursor` is `null`, it is the last page).

> [!NOTE]
> Error bodies on these endpoints are plain text (`text/plain`). Only `module_disabled` and `account_banned` return JSON.

> [!WARNING]
> **Known limitation:** The endpoints that write templates, traits, level curves and rules, and the endpoints that read or delete characters, do not look at the key type; a valid **client key** can call them too. A client key is scoped to the environment, not to the player: with a key embedded in the game, any character in that environment can be read or deleted. So make management calls and character deletion only from your own server, and apply an ownership check on your server to any character ID that comes from a player. A gate by key type does not exist yet.

### Creating a character

```
POST /v1/characters
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "definition": "warrior", "external_id": "player-1234" }
```

```json
{
  "id": "0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f",
  "definition": "warrior",
  "definition_version": 3,
  "external_id": "player-1234",
  "version": 1,
  "level": 1,
  "state": {
    "attributes": { "strength": 10 },
    "resources": { "hp": 100 },
    "progression": { "level": 1, "xp": 0, "highest_level": 1, "granted_rewards": [] },
    "abilities": [],
    "flags": {},
    "custom": {}
  },
  "created_at": "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z"
}
```

The body can also contain `allocation` (for point-buy creation: field → points spent), `seed` (required for dice-roll creation, a deterministic seed) and `custom` (free-form JSON, at most 64 KB). The mode is defined in the template; the request only carries the input the mode asks for.

> [!WARNING]
> The create and delete endpoints do not accept an idempotency key and are not retried automatically. A second create with the same `external_id` returns `409`; this also prevents duplicate characters. After a network error, do not blindly resend; first look the character up by `external_id`.

### Running a command

```
POST /v1/characters/{id}/commands
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: quest-17-player-1234
If-Match: 1

{ "type": "add_xp", "amount": 250 }
```

```json
{
  "id": "0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f",
  "version": 2,
  "state": { "...": "current state" },
  "events": [
    { "id": "…", "seq": 2, "type": "xp_added", "payload": { "...": "…" }, "created_at": "2026-11-03T09:01:00Z" }
  ],
  "replayed": false
}
```

The command type is chosen with the `type` field:

| `type` | Body fields | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `set_flag` | `key`, `value` (bool) | client or server |
| `set_attribute` | `key`, `value` (integer) | server |
| `add_resource` | `key`, `delta` (integer, can be negative) | server |
| `add_modifier` | `stat`, `operation` (`flat_add`, `flat_sub`, `percent_add`, `percent_mul`, `clamp`), `value`, `priority`, `source_kind` (`item`, `buff`, `skill`, `curse`, `quest`), `source_id`, `expires_at` | server |
| `remove_modifier` | `source_kind`, `source_id` | server |
| `add_xp` | `amount` | server |
| `rollback` | `to_version` | server |

If you send any command other than `set_flag` with a client key, you get `403` and your idempotency key is not burned.

One command can produce several events: for example, if `add_xp` causes a level up, the response contains `xp_added` and `level_up` together; defined rules produce additional events as well.

## Concurrency and replay safety

- **`Idempotency-Key` (optional, 1–200 characters):** If the same key and the same body arrive a second time, the command does not run again; the first response is returned with `replayed: true`. The same key with a different body is `422`. The key is "burned" only when the command succeeds; a rejected command does not consume the key. The same key in flight at the same time gets `409`.
- **`If-Match` (optional):** The `version` value you read, as `3` or `"3"`. If the character is not at that version, the command is rejected with `409` and nothing changes. `*` and the weak `W/` form are not accepted (`400`). `If-Match` is not processed on the `rollback` command.

General rules: [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md).

### Rollback

The `rollback` command does not delete history. It writes **a new event** (`character_rolled_back`) that returns the character to the state at `to_version`; the event log is append-only.

## Events and webhooks

Character events (`flag_set`, `attribute_set`, `resource_changed`, `modifier_added`, `modifiers_removed`, `xp_added`, `level_up`, `ability_unlocked`, `event_emitted`, `character_rolled_back`) can also be delivered as webhooks. The envelope contains `event_id`, `type`, `character_id`, `environment_id`, `seq` and `data`. Registration and verification: [Webhooks](webhooks.md).

## Limits

- The `custom` field is at most 64 KB; it cannot contain decimal numbers.
- `limit` on list endpoints is 1–200.
- A level cannot be below 1; the maximum is 65535.
- `GET …/state?at=` returns `400` for a future or negative time. `at` is a Unix millisecond timestamp or an RFC 3339 time.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `403 permission denied` | A command other than `set_flag` with a client key | Send the command from your server with a server key |
| `409 version conflict: expected 3, actual 4` | `If-Match` is stale | Re-read the character and resend with the new version |
| `409 already exists` | The same `external_id` already exists | Find the existing character with `GET /v1/characters` |
| `422 idempotency mismatch` | The same key, a different body | Generate a new key; use the same key only for network retries |
| `400 If-Match tam sürüm numarası olmalı` | `*` or a weak tag was sent | Send only the number |
| `404` + `module_disabled` | The `characters` module is disabled | Enable the module |

> [!NOTE]
> The `400` message text is returned by the server in Turkish, exactly as shown; match on the status code, not on the text.

## Working example

The example below creates a character and safely grants XP. The template (`warrior`) must already be defined, from the panel or with `POST /v1/definitions`.

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/characters-server.ts -->
```ts
/** Güvenilir backend örneği: karakter oluşturur, XP verir. Server anahtarı yalnız sunucu ortamından gelir. */
import { CrxClient, CrxError } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";

/** Oyuncunun karakterini açar ve ilk XP'yi güvenle (idempotent) verir. */
export async function createAndReward(baseUrl: string, serverApiKey: string, playerId: string): Promise<bigint> {
  const crx = new CrxClient({ baseUrl, apiKey: serverApiKey });

  // 1) Karakteri tanımdan oluştur. `external_id` oyunun kendi oyuncu kimliğidir.
  const character = await crx.createCharacter({
    body: { definition: "warrior", external_id: playerId },
  });

  // 2) XP ver: aynı Idempotency-Key ile tekrar denemek ikinci XP vermez.
  //    If-Match, karakterin okuduğunuz sürümüdür; araya başka komut girdiyse 409 döner.
  try {
    const result = await crx.executeCommand({
      path: { id: character.id },
      body: { type: "add_xp", amount: 250n },
      headers: {
        "Idempotency-Key": `quest-1-${playerId}`,
        "If-Match": character.version.toString(),
      },
    });
    return result.version;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof CrxError && error.status === 409) {
      // Sürüm çakışması: karakteri yeniden okuyup komutu yeni sürümle gönderin.
      throw new Error("Karakter bu arada değişti; yeniden okuyup tekrar deneyin.");
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Related pages

- [Concepts: key types and sessions](../getting-started/concepts.md)
- [Game rules and automation](game-rules.md)
- [Inventory and items](inventory-items.md)
- [Errors](../reference/errors.md), [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md)

docs.body:
# Chat

This page describes channel chat between players (global, world, clan, party and direct). Read it if you want to send messages with a player session, read history and receive live messages.

## What it does

The chat module (`chat`) provides channel-based text chat. Messages are written to a durable archive; live delivery is done separately over a WebSocket. The same message can be sent over REST or over the WebSocket, and both apply the same rules (mute, rate limit, profanity filter, replay protection).

It works with the player's own session. **Chat endpoints cannot be called with an API key.**

If the module is disabled, the endpoints return `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"chat"}`; the chat socket first sends an `error` frame (`code: "module_disabled"`) and then closes. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| Enable or disable the module | [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) |
| Read the chat of the city (scene) plugin, delete a message, mute a player | [City chat](../panel/scene-chat.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source. The panel's "City chat" screen manages the chat of the **scene plugin**; for the channel chat on this page there is no panel screen yet for reading, deleting or muting messages.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Channel:** Distinguished by `kind`:

  | `kind` | `reference_id` | Who can join |
  |---|---|---|
  | `global` | none | Everyone in the environment |
  | `world` | required (world/map UUID) | Players who know the reference |
  | `clan` | required (clan UUID) | Members of the clan |
  | `party` | required (party UUID) | Members of the party |
  | `direct` | none; `direct_player_id` is required | Only the two players |

  A channel of the same kind and the same reference is created once; asking again returns the existing channel. In a `direct` channel the other player cannot be yourself.
- **Message:** `id`, `channel_id`, `sender_player_id`, `client_message_id`, `body`, `sent_at_ms`.
- **`client_message_id`:** A replay key generated by the client (cannot be empty, at most 200 characters). A second send with the same value in the same channel does not create a new message; it returns the existing message with `duplicate: true`.
- **Mute:** Muting a player in the scope `all`, `global`, `world`, `clan`, `party` or `direct`. A send by a muted player returns `403`.

## Calls your game makes

All chat endpoints are called with a **player session**: the session cookie or an opaque session token (`Authorization: Bearer <session token>`), plus the environment header:

```
x-crx-env: <environment uuid>
```

On these endpoints the `x-csrf-token` double-submit and the `Origin` check are **not applied**; the session cookie or session token is enough (unlike the store purchase endpoint). Session rules: [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md).

| Method and path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/chat/channels` | Creates a channel or returns the existing one |
| `GET /v1/chat/channels` | Lists the channels the player is authorized for |
| `POST /v1/chat/channels/{channel_id}/messages` | Sends a message |
| `GET /v1/chat/channels/{channel_id}/messages` | Reads the archive backwards (`before_ms`, `limit` 1–100, default 50) |
| `GET /v1/chat/ws` | Live chat WebSocket |

> [!NOTE]
> The TypeScript and Unity SDKs have no ready-made client for chat; call the endpoints with raw REST and WebSocket. See [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md).

### Creating a channel

```
POST /v1/chat/channels
x-crx-env: <environment uuid>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "kind": "clan", "reference_id": "0192f0aa-…" }
```

```json
{ "channel": { "id": "0192f2bb-…", "environment_id": "…", "kind": "clan", "reference_id": "0192f0aa-…", "participant_a": null, "participant_b": null, "created_at_ms": 1790000000000 } }
```

A player who is not a member of the clan or party is rejected when creating or reading that channel.

### Sending a message

```
POST /v1/chat/channels/0192f2bb-…/messages
x-crx-env: <environment uuid>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "client_message_id": "c-0001", "body": "Hello!" }
```

```json
{ "message": { "id": "…", "channel_id": "0192f2bb-…", "sender_player_id": "…", "client_message_id": "c-0001", "body": "Hello!", "sent_at_ms": 1790000000123 }, "duplicate": false }
```

The rules, in order:

1. `400` if `client_message_id` is empty or longer than 200 characters.
2. The body must be 1–2000 Unicode characters and contain at least one non-whitespace character; otherwise `400`.
3. `403` if the player is muted for that channel.
4. **Rate limit:** at most 20 messages per player per 10 seconds; exceeding it returns `429`.
5. **Profanity filter:** if the message contains a banned word (a whole word separated by whitespace, case-insensitive), `422` is returned.
6. The message is written to the archive, then delivered to live subscribers. Even if delivery fails, the archived message is not deleted.

### Reading the archive

`GET /v1/chat/channels/{channel_id}/messages?before_ms=1790000000000&limit=50` returns `{ "messages": [ … ] }`. `before_ms` asks for messages **older** than this Unix millisecond timestamp; for the next page, pass the `sent_at_ms` of the oldest message.

## Live chat (WebSocket)

When connecting to `GET /v1/chat/ws`, `x-crx-env` and the session identity (cookie or `Authorization: Bearer`) are sent **as headers**. The upgrade is not performed without authentication (`401`); `404` if the module is disabled.

> [!WARNING]
> The browser `WebSocket` API cannot send custom headers (`x-crx-env`); therefore the chat socket cannot be connected directly from a browser. Browser games can poll with REST; native clients (for example Unity desktop/mobile) can connect by adding headers. A query parameter or subprotocol instead of a header is not supported yet.

Client frames (JSON; the `type` field is lower camelCase, the other fields are snake_case):

| `type` | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `subscribe` | `channel_id` | Subscribe to the channel's live stream |
| `unsubscribe` | — | Drop the subscription |
| `send` | `channel_id`, `client_message_id`, `body` | Send a message, as in REST |
| `ping` | `nonce` | Liveness probe |

Server frames:

| `type` | Fields |
|---|---|
| `subscribed` | `channel_id` |
| `unsubscribed` | — |
| `message` | `message`, `duplicate` |
| `pong` | `nonce` |
| `error` | `code` (`invalid_frame`, `invalid_payload`, `forbidden_channel`, `unavailable`, `message_rejected`, `module_disabled`) |

A socket is subscribed to a single channel at a time. A frame with an unrecognized field gets `invalid_frame`. If the module is disabled later, the open socket is closed too. For the general realtime surface, see [Realtime: overview](../realtime/overview.md).

## Versioning and replay safety

- Message sending has **no** `Idempotency-Key` header; replay safety is provided by `client_message_id`. After a network error, resend with the same value: the message appears once (`duplicate: true`).
- `If-Match` is not used.

## Events

A chat event is not delivered as a webhook; **chat is not among the webhook event types**. Use the WebSocket for the live stream.

## Limits

- Message body 1–2000 characters; `client_message_id` at most 200 characters.
- Send rate: 20 messages per player per 10 seconds.
- An archive page is 1–100 messages.
- A WebSocket can be subscribed to a single channel at a time.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `401` | No session, expired, or `x-crx-env` missing | Refresh the session; add the header |
| `403` (send) | The player is muted or has no permission in the channel | Inform the user |
| `400` | Empty or too long body / `client_message_id` | Fix the input |
| `422` | The profanity filter rejected the message | Change the message |
| `429` | 20 messages per 10 seconds exceeded | Wait and retry |
| `error: forbidden_channel` (WS) | No permission for the channel | Create the channel with REST first / verify the permission |

## Working example

Writing to a channel over REST with a session cookie (`cookies.txt`) and reading the history:

```
curl -X POST "$API/v1/chat/channels/$CHANNEL/messages" \
  -H "x-crx-env: $ENV" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -b cookies.txt \
  -d '{"client_message_id":"c-0001","body":"Hello!"}'

curl "$API/v1/chat/channels/$CHANNEL/messages?limit=20" \
  -H "x-crx-env: $ENV" -b cookies.txt
```

## Related pages

- [Clans and parties](social.md) · [Realtime: overview](../realtime/overview.md)
- [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md) · [Errors](../reference/errors.md)
