Working example: write a score, read the board
docs.body:
# Leaderboards and tournaments

This page describes leaderboards, where players compete on score, and elimination-style tournaments. Read it if you want to write scores from a trusted server and show the ranking in your game.

## What it does

The competition module (`competition`) provides two things:

- **Leaderboard:** A ranking that keeps each player's **best score** and can be split into seasons.
- **Tournament:** A single-elimination, double-elimination or round-robin bracket with player or clan participants, with a final prize.

Writing scores and managing boards is done with a **server key**. The game client reads the board with a **player session** and does not need a server key.

If the module is disabled, the endpoints return `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"competition"}`. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| Define a board; set season, unit and visibility | [Leaderboard](../panel/leaderboards.md) |
| See a board's top entries and season history | [Leaderboard detail](../panel/leaderboard-detail.md) |
| The prize currency for a tournament | [Currencies](../panel/currencies.md) |

There is no panel screen for tournaments; they are managed only with REST.

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Board definition:** `key`, `name`, `metric_expr`, `order` (`asc`: a smaller score is better, `desc`: a larger score is better), `season`, `tie_policy`, `player_visible`, `unit` and `unit_suffix`. A definition is versioned.
- **Season (`season`):** `none` (never reset), `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly` (aligned to the UTC calendar: a day turns over at 00:00 UTC, a week on Monday at 00:00 UTC, a month on the first of the month) or `custom` (a period of `custom_period_ms` length). When a season closes, its ranking is stored as an immutable record.
- **Score:** An integer (`i64`). A player's **best score** in the season counts (the highest for `desc`, the lowest for `asc`). Sending a worse score does not change the ranking.
- **Tie-break (`tie_policy`):** For now the only option is `score_achieved_player_id`: score first, then whoever **reached that score first**, then the player ID.
- **Rank (`rank`):** Starts at 1.
- **Unit (`unit`):** `points`, `money` (smallest currency unit) or `duration_ms`; `unit_suffix` is a 1–8 character suffix (`$`, `ms` …). The unit is for display only.
- **`player_visible`:** If `true`, a player session can read the board; the default is `false`.
- **`metric_expr`:** A CEL expression compiled at registration (required, cannot be empty). Boards that plugins create on their own use `event.score`; write the same expression when you create one with REST.

## Calls your game makes

| Method and path | Credential | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/leaderboards` | server key | Creates a board definition |
| `GET /v1/leaderboards`, `GET /v1/leaderboards/{key}` | server key | Lists / reads definitions |
| `POST /v1/leaderboards/{key}/scores` | server key | Writes a player score (`Idempotency-Key` required, `202`) |
| `GET /v1/leaderboards/{key}/entries?limit=&cursor=` | server key | Top ranks (paginated) |
| `GET /v1/leaderboards/{key}/around-me?player_id=&radius=` | server key | Ranks around a player |
| `GET /v1/player/leaderboards/{key}?limit=` | player session | The first page of the board and the player's own row |
| `POST /v1/tournaments` | server key | Creates a tournament |
| `GET /v1/tournaments/{id}` | server key | Reads the tournament state |
| `POST /v1/tournaments/{id}/participants` | server key | Registers a participant (`Idempotency-Key`) |
| `POST /v1/tournaments/{id}/start` | server key | Generates the bracket and starts |
| `POST /v1/tournaments/{id}/matches/{match_id}/result` | server key | Reports a match result or resolves a dispute (`Idempotency-Key`) |

Server endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`; a client key and a player session are rejected. The player endpoint works with a cookie or session token and `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>`; a developer key is not accepted.

> [!NOTE]
> The TypeScript SDK has `player.leaderboard(key, { limit })` for player reads; there is no typed client for the server endpoints (writing scores, definitions, tournaments), which are called with raw REST. See [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md).

### Board definition

```
POST /v1/leaderboards
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "key": "daily-earnings", "name": "Daily earnings",
  "metric_expr": "event.score", "order": "desc",
  "season": "daily", "tie_policy": "score_achieved_player_id",
  "player_visible": true, "unit": "money", "unit_suffix": "$"
}
```

Returns `201` with `{ id, key, name, metric_expr, order, season, custom_period_ms, tie_policy, season_key }`. For `season: "custom"`, `custom_period_ms` must be positive.

### Writing a score

```
POST /v1/leaderboards/daily-earnings/scores
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Idempotency-Key: score-player-1234-2026-11-03
Content-Type: application/json

{ "player_id": "0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f", "score": 4200 }
```

```json
{ "entry": { "rank": 7, "player_id": "0192f0f2-…", "score": 4200, "achieved_at_ms": 1790000000000 }, "replayed": false }
```

The response is `202`: the score has been durably accepted; the ranking projection is updated after a short delay, so a board read immediately afterwards can lag by a few seconds. `Idempotency-Key` is required: the same key and the same body return the same result with `replayed: true`.

### Reading the board with a player session

```
GET /v1/player/leaderboards/daily-earnings?limit=10
x-crx-env: 0192f000-0000-7000-8000-00000000e001
```

```json
{
  "leaderboard": { "key": "daily-earnings", "name": "Daily earnings", "order": "desc", "season": "daily", "seasonKey": "2026-11-03", "seasonEndsAtMs": 1790121600000, "unit": "money", "unitSuffix": "$" },
  "entries": [ { "rank": "1", "playerId": "…", "displayName": "Ayşe", "score": "9800", "achievedAtMs": 1790000000000 } ],
  "me": { "rank": "7", "playerId": "…", "displayName": "You", "score": "4200", "achievedAtMs": 1790000000000 }
}
```

- Only `player_visible` boards can be read; otherwise `404`. `404` also if the module is disabled.
- `limit` is 1–50 (default 20).
- `rank` and `score` are **decimal strings** in JSON (lossless `i64`); the SDK turns them into `bigint`. Field names on this endpoint are camelCase.
- Banned and deleted players are filtered out and ranks are numbered densely within the page; `me` is your rank among visible players. If you have no score this season, `me` is `null`.
- The first page is cached for a short time (at most a few seconds).

## Tournaments

```
POST /v1/tournaments
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Winter Cup", "format": "single_elimination", "participant_type": "player",
  "capacity": 16,
  "registration_opens_at_ms": 1790000000000, "registration_closes_at_ms": 1790086400000,
  "seeding_source": "registration_order",
  "prize_table": { "currency_key": "gold", "amount": 5000 }
}
```

- `format`: `single_elimination`, `double_elimination`, `round_robin`. `participant_type`: `player` or `clan`.
- `capacity` is 2–1024; the registration close must be after the open; `name` is 1–200 characters.
- `seeding_source`: `registration_order` (registration order; `leaderboard_id` is not given) or `leaderboard` (player tournaments only; `leaderboard_id` is required).
- `prize_table`: an object with `currency_key` (no whitespace, at most 200 characters) and a positive `amount`.
- Flow: create → register with `participants` (`{ "participant_id" }`) → generate the bracket with `start` → report `result` for each match (`reporter_id`, `reported_side`: `home` `away` `admin`, `outcome`: `home_win` `away_win` `draw`, `score`). The `admin` side is for resolving a dispute.
- Responses carry the tournament's current view (`{ "tournament": { … } }`).

## Versioning and replay safety

- Writing a score, registering a participant and a match result require `Idempotency-Key` (the same key + the same body: does not run again; a different body: `422`).
- A board definition is versioned; list and ranking reads do not need a version header.
- General rules: [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md).

## Events

Accepting a score produces the `score_submitted` event, and a season rollover produces `season_closed`/`season_opened`; these can be used in quest objectives and rule automation. **Among the types you can select as a webhook filter there is no leaderboard or tournament event**; endpoints registered without a filter receive all events, and leaderboard events are included, but the envelope format is not a documented contract. For the final prize, use the reward granting flow on the [Rewards](rewards.md) page.

## Limits

- `limit` is 1–50 on player reads; pagination on the server `entries` endpoints is cursor-based.
- Tournament `capacity` is 2–1024.
- `season: custom` needs a positive `custom_period_ms`.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `404` (player read) | The board is not `player_visible`, does not exist, or the module is disabled | Check the definition |
| `403` | A server endpoint called with a client key or a player session | Use the server key from your server |
| `400` (`Idempotency-Key`) | The header is missing when writing a score | Send a key |
| The score was written but the ranking did not change | The player's best score this season is better | Only a better score changes the ranking |
| The score was written but the board did not update right away | Projection delay | Wait a few seconds and read again |
| `400` (tournament) | `capacity`, the registration window, `prize_table` or the seeding rule is wrong | Fix the body |

## Working example: write a score, read the board

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/competition-leaderboard.ts -->
```ts
/** Skor tablosu: sunucu puan yazar (ham REST), oyun istemcisi tabloyu oyuncu oturumuyla okur. */
import type { PlayerClient } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";

/** Sunucu: `POST /v1/leaderboards/{key}/scores`. Sunucu anahtarı gerekir; Idempotency-Key zorunludur. */
export async function submitScore(baseUrl: string, serverApiKey: string, board: string, playerId: string, score: number, requestKey: string): Promise<number> {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/v1/leaderboards/${encodeURIComponent(board)}/scores`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${serverApiKey}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "Idempotency-Key": requestKey,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ player_id: playerId, score }),
  });
  if (response.status !== 202) throw new Error(`Puan yazılamadı: HTTP ${response.status} ${await response.text()}`);
  const body = (await response.json()) as { entry: { rank: number }; replayed: boolean };
  return body.entry.rank;
}

/** Oyun istemcisi: tablonun ilk sayfası ve oyuncunun kendi satırı (`player_visible` tablolar). */
export async function showBoard(player: PlayerClient, board: string): Promise<void> {
  const view = await player.leaderboard(board, { limit: 10 });
  for (const row of view.entries) console.log(`${row.rank}. ${row.displayName} — ${row.score}`);
  if (view.me !== null) console.log(`Siz: ${view.me.rank}. sıra, ${view.me.score} puan`);
}
```

## Related pages

- [Rewards](rewards.md) · [Clans and parties](social.md) · [Characters](characters.md)
- [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md) · [Numbers and encoding](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md)

docs.title: Content groups
docs.description: Describes the game-data groups defined in the panel, field types, the publish flow and how your game reads this data from the catalog.
headings: Where it lives in the panel
docs.body:
# Content groups

This page describes **content groups**, which let you change game data such as tools, weapons, NPCs or police units without shipping code. Read it to learn how the data is defined and published in the panel and how your game reads it.

## What it does

A content group is a typed table you define: the group has **fields** (for example `speed`, `damage`, `color`, `model`), and every **entry** (for example `sedan`) carries a value for those fields. An operator edits the values in the panel and **publishes** them; the game reads only the current published state. This way you do not have to redeploy the game to change a value.

Content groups are part of the core: there is no separate module switch, and they work in every environment.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| Create a group, add fields, start from a template | [Content](../panel/content.md), [Edit group](../panel/content-group-edit.md) |
| Add an entry, edit values, publish or archive an entry | [Edit entry](../panel/content-entry-edit.md) |
| See the publish history and the diff, send changes to the game | [Content](../panel/content.md) › Publish |
| Attach a 3D model to a model field | [3D models](../panel/models.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source, and the panel itself is shown in Turkish.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Group:** A `key` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,47}$`, that is 2–48 characters), a name and fields. The key does not change after creation.
- **Field:** A `key` (the same rule) and a **kind**. There are ten kinds:

  | Kind (`kind`) | What it holds | Settings |
  |---|---|---|
  | `integer` | An integer (with an optional decimal display scale) | `min`, `max`, `scale` (0–3), `unit` (at most 12 characters), `default` |
  | `percent` | A percentage in basis points (10000 = 100%) | `min_bp`, `max_bp`, `default_bp` |
  | `text` | Text | `max_chars` (at most 512), `multiline` |
  | `bool` | Yes/no | `default` |
  | `select` | Option(s) | `options` (at most 64), `multiple` |
  | `color` | A color | `#rrggbb` |
  | `model` | A 3D model | model library ID |
  | `image` | An image | the asset's `sha256` value |
  | `reference` | A link to another entry | target: another group, a built-in item or a built-in character |
  | `table` | A matrix with repeated rows | `columns` (1–8), `min_rows`, `max_rows` (at most 100) |
- **Visibility (audience):** Each field can be `player` (goes to the player) or `server` (only a server key sees it).
- **Entry:** A `key` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`) and field values. Its status is one of: Published (`Yayında`), Has draft changes (`Taslak değişikliği var`), Archived (`Arşivli`), Not published yet (`Henüz yayınlanmadı`); the panel shows these labels in Turkish.
- **Publish:** Done in the panel with "Değişiklikleri oyuna gönder" (send changes to the game); it takes a note of at most 280 characters and produces a sequential publish counter (`seq`). The next publish does not change the previous one, it adds a new one; the history and the diff are visible in the panel. If someone published while you were looking, the panel refreshes the diff and asks for confirmation again.
- **Numbers:** Integers; fractional or exponent notation (`40.0`, `1e2`) is rejected. Display a scaled integer in the game with `formatScaled`.

> [!NOTE]
> Item and character templates also appear in the panel as **built-in groups**; they behave as "live in the game as soon as you save" and need no publish step. User-defined groups need a publish.

Limits: at most 64 groups per environment, 48 fields per group and 1000 entries; one entry's table data cannot exceed 128 KiB, and the publish snapshot for a server audience cannot exceed 1 MiB.

## Catalog: items and characters

The game reads item and character definitions (key, name, typed data rows and the 3D model address) from the **catalog** endpoints:

| Method and path | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/catalog/items`, `GET /v1/catalog/items/{key}` | Item manifests |
| `GET /v1/catalog/characters`, `GET /v1/catalog/characters/{key}` | Character manifests |

These depend on the `items` and `characters` modules; `404` if the module is disabled. The list is paginated (`limit` 1–100, default 50; `cursor`). Each manifest carries `kind`, `key`, `name`, `definition_version`, `data` (typed rows), `model` (`null` if none) and `content_sha256`. For details, watching with ETag and showing models with `three`: [Game catalog integration](../../../oyun-katalog-entegrasyonu.md) (Turkish) and [Scenes, assets and 3D models](scenes-assets-models.md).

## Calls your game makes (content groups)

Content groups are exposed through a **read-only** surface; the game cannot reach drafts. There are two credential types:

- **Player session** (cookie or session token + `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>`): sees only fields with `visibility = player` and their values.
- **Server key** (`Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`): sees all fields with their visibility and with `seq`. An invalid `Bearer crx_…` key gets `401` even with a valid cookie; it does not fall back to the cookie.

| Method and path | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/catalog/groups` | The key and name of published groups and a `content_sha256` per audience |
| `GET /v1/catalog/groups/{group}` | The group's current publish: `group`, `fields`, `entries`, `seq` |
| `GET /v1/catalog/groups/{group}/entries/{key}` | The same shape, only that entry |

Headers:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x-crx-env` | Required on a player session; with a server key the environment comes from the key |
| `If-None-Match` | The `ETag` you hold; if it matches, `304` and no body |

Responses carry an audience-specific `ETag`. The player `ETag` and the `content_sha256` value are computed from the **filtered** body; so changing a server-only field shows no change on the player side. A group that was never published, or does not exist, returns `404`.

> [!NOTE]
> Server-only rows are not a secret store: operators in the panel and holders of a server key can see them. Do not put passwords, keys or personal data in them.

### Table field

A `table` field holds rows repeated within an entry (a weapon's level → damage table, an NPC loot list). Column kinds are `integer`, `percent`, `text`, `bool`, `select` and `reference`. The value is an array of objects that **preserves row order**; changing the order means a new publish digest. A server-only table is absent from the player body entirely.

### Reading from the game

The TypeScript SDK provides a typed reader for both audiences (`player.catalog.groups`, and `CrxClient.catalog.groups` on the server; `list`, `get`, `entry`). There are `watchCatalogGroup` for watching and `formatScaled` for displaying a scaled number. The Unity SDK has no catalog; use raw REST.

## Versioning and replay safety

- The read endpoints have no `Idempotency-Key` or `If-Match`; you do conditional reads with `If-None-Match`.
- The publish counter (`seq`) grows with every publish; if `seq` has not changed, the content has not changed.
- Group, field and entry keys do not change after creation; a field kind change is checked, and the panel lists the problems before publishing.

## Events

Publishing a content group does not write an event to the outbox (only an audit record is made), so it does not produce a webhook. To catch a change in the game, poll with `ETag`: a change reaches the player at most one polling interval later; a one-minute interval is enough.

## Limits

- 64 groups / 48 fields / 1000 entries; a table has at most 8 columns and 100 rows; an entry's table data 128 KiB; the server publish snapshot 1 MiB.
- A text field is at most 512 characters; a select field at most 64 options.
- A publish note is at most 280 characters.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `404` (group) | The group was never published or does not exist | Publish the group in the panel |
| `401` | No credential or an invalid `Bearer crx_…`; `x-crx-env` missing on a player session | Fix the credential and the header |
| Publish rejected in the panel | A reference (`reference`) target is missing; the table or publish size is exceeded | Fix the problems the panel lists |
| I changed the value but the game does not see it | The draft was not published, or the field has `server` visibility | Publish; check the visibility |
| `304` | The `ETag` matched | Expected behavior; your copy is current |

## Working example

Reading the current publish of the `weapons` group with an `ETag`:

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/catalog-groups-read.ts -->
```ts
/** İçerik grubunu (panelde yayınlanan oyun verisi) oyuncu oturumuyla okur; ETag ile değişmediyse 304 döner. */
import type { PlayerClient } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";

/** `weapons` grubunun güncel yayınındaki kayıt anahtarlarını döndürür; değişmediyse boş liste. */
export async function readWeapons(player: PlayerClient, previousEtag?: string): Promise<readonly string[]> {
  const result = await player.catalog.groups.get("weapons", previousEtag === undefined ? {} : { ifNoneMatch: previousEtag });
  if (result.status === 304) return [];
  return result.value.entries.map((entry) => entry.key);
}
```

## Related pages

- [Content groups as a reward source](rewards.md) · [Inventory and items](inventory-items.md) · [Characters](characters.md) · [Scenes, assets and 3D models](scenes-assets-models.md)
- [Game catalog integration (detailed guide, Turkish)](../../../oyun-katalog-entegrasyonu.md) · [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md)

headings: Where it lives in the panel
How to give a player money
Working example: grant money, then buy a product
docs.body:
# Economy

This page describes how in-game money is held and moves in Open Play: currency definitions, wallets, the ledger, player-to-player transfers, NPC merchants and player trading. Read it if you are looking for the safe way to give players money, let them spend it and monitor the economy.

## What it does

The economy spans two modules:

- `economy`: currencies, wallets, the ledger, transfers and reports.
- `trading`: NPC merchants (`merchants`) and player-to-player trading (`trades`).

Every money movement is **double-entry**: the amount leaving one wallet enters another wallet or a system account, and both sit in the ledger under the same transaction ID (`tx_id`). The ledger is append-only; no row is updated or deleted. To correct a mistake, a reversing entry is written.

If a module is disabled, the endpoints return `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"economy"}` (or `trading`).

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| Create a currency; set the icon, decimal places and supply cap | [Currencies](../panel/currencies.md), [Currency profile](../panel/currency-profile.md) |
| See the daily summary, balance ranking, trades and wallet lookup | [Economy reports](../panel/economy.md) |
| See a player's wallet and movements | [Player profile](../panel/player-profile.md) |
| Set up a reward table | [Reward tables](../panel/reward-tables.md) |
| Tie a product to money and sell it | [Store](../panel/store.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Currency:** Has a key (`gold`), a name, `transferable` (whether player-to-player transfer is allowed), `max_supply` (the total supply cap; unlimited if absent) and an icon. Registering again with the same key produces **a new version**; old versions do not change. The decimal places (`display_decimals`) and the icon image are set in the panel; a REST registration leaves them at `0`/empty.
- **Wallet:** An owner's balance in one currency. The owner has the form `<kind>:<uuid>` (`player`, `character`, `clan`, `system`). **There is no wallet write endpoint**; a wallet is born by itself on its first movement and is bound to the currency version it was born with.
- **Balance:** An integer in the smallest unit (`i64`). There are no decimals: to display "12.50 gold", apply the decimal places set in the panel in your client.
- **Ledger row:** `direction` (in/out), `amount`, `reason` (`transfer`, `grant`, `burn`, `merchant_purchase`, `merchant_sale`, `iap`, `iap_revoke`, `party_reward`, `clan_treasury`, `quest`, `login`, `npc_reward`, `reward_table`, `trade_lock`, `trade_refund`, `trade_settle` …) and `reference` (context).
- **Merchant:** An NPC with a key, a name and per-item buy/sell price overrides (`price_overrides`). The item's own `npc_buy_price`/`npc_sell_price` is the default.
- **Trade:** A state machine between two players: `draft` → `offered` → `locked` → `completed` or `cancelled`/`expired`.

## How to give a player money

There is no REST endpoint that directly "adds this much to a wallet". Money enters a player's account through these routes:

| Route | When |
|---|---|
| **Reward table grant** (`POST /v1/reward-tables/{key}/grant`) | Money the game gives, such as quests, tournaments and login rewards — see [Rewards](rewards.md) |
| **Daily login reward, quest, NPC reward** | [Rewards](rewards.md) |
| **In-app purchase** (IAP) | Game money bought with real money — see [Store](store-iap.md) |
| **Selling an item to a merchant** (`POST /v1/merchants/{key}/sell`) | A player sells an item to an NPC |
| **Party reward distribution, clan treasury** | [Social](social.md) |
| **Manual grant from the panel** | An operator; the operation is written to the audit trail |

Each shows up in the ledger with its own `reason` value.

## Calls your game makes

Endpoints are called with `Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`. Currency and merchant **management** needs a server key (`403` otherwise); reads and player operations can be done with any API key.

| Method and path | Key | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/currencies` | server | Saves a currency as a new version |
| `GET /v1/wallets?owner=player:<uuid>` | API key | The owner's wallets (one row per currency) |
| `POST /v1/transfers` | API key | Wallet-to-wallet transfer (`Idempotency-Key` required) |
| `GET /v1/ledger?wallet_id=<uuid>` | API key | A wallet's ledger stream (`cursor`, `limit`) |
| `POST /v1/merchants` | server | Saves a merchant as a new version |
| `GET /v1/merchants/{key}` | API key | The merchant's current content |
| `POST /v1/merchants/{key}/buy` | API key | A player buys an item from the merchant |
| `POST /v1/merchants/{key}/sell` | API key | A player sells an item to the merchant |
| `POST /v1/trades` | API key | Opens a trade draft |
| `GET /v1/trades/{id}?actor_id=` | API key | Views a trade (only the two parties) |
| `POST /v1/trades/{id}/offer` | API key | Locks the legs |
| `POST /v1/trades/{id}/accept` | API key | Final confirmation; atomic exchange |
| `POST /v1/trades/{id}/cancel` | API key | Cancels; locks are released and money is refunded |
| `GET /v1/economy/faucet-sink`, `/flags`, `/merchant-gap`, `/top-holders` | server | Daily economy reports |
| `GET /v1/auth/admin/player-wallet-movements?player_id=` | server | A player's recent wallet movements (`limit` 1–100, default 20) |

> [!NOTE]
> The TypeScript SDK has no typed client for these modules; call them with raw REST. See [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md).

> [!WARNING]
> **Known limitation:** The transfer, merchant buy/sell and trade endpoints do not look at the key type; a valid **client key** can call them too, and the wallet/player IDs are given freely in the request. A client key is scoped to the environment, not to the player. Make money movements only from your own game server and verify the ID coming from the player there.

### Currency registration

```
POST /v1/currencies
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "key": "gold", "name": "Gold", "transferable": true, "max_supply": 1000000000 }
```

```json
{ "id": "0192f0aa-1000-7000-8000-000000000001", "key": "gold", "version": 1, "name": "Gold", "transferable": true, "max_supply": 1000000000, "icon": null }
```

`key` and `name` cannot be empty; if `max_supply` is given it must be greater than 0 (`400`). A currency with `transferable: false` returns `422` on a player-to-player transfer (in-game spending still works).

### Transfer

```
POST /v1/transfers
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: transfer-2026-11-03-0001

{ "from_wallet": "0192f1…", "to_wallet": "0192f2…", "amount": 500, "reference": { "reason": "gift" } }
```

```json
{ "tx_id": "0192f3…", "from": { "id": "0192f1…", "balance": 1500, "version": 7 }, "to": { "id": "0192f2…", "balance": 500, "version": 3 }, "replayed": false }
```

(The `from` and `to` in the response contain the full fields of the wallet records; they are abbreviated above.) Rejected cases: an amount of 0 or negative `400`; different currencies `400`; wallet not found `404`; insufficient balance, `transferable: false`, or the same key with a different body `422`; the same key in flight `409`.

### Merchant buy and sell

```
POST /v1/merchants/blacksmith/buy
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: buy-player-1234-17

{ "player_id": "0192f0f2-…", "item_key": "iron_sword", "currency_key": "gold", "quantity": 1 }
```

Response: `{ "event": {…}, "wallet_balance": 900, "wallet_version": 8, "inventory_id": "…", "inventory_version": 5, "replayed": false }`.

A purchase, in one transaction, deducts from the wallet, creates the item as a **new instance**, places it in the first empty slot and reduces the stock. `422` if the price is undefined, the balance is insufficient or the inventory is full; `409` if the stock is insufficient. For a sale (`sell`), the body carries `{ "player_id", "item_instance_id", "currency_key" }` and **the whole stack** is sold; for a partial sale, apply `split` first. `Idempotency-Key` is required on both.

### Player trading

1. `POST /v1/trades` — open a draft with `{ "initiator_player_id", "counterparty_player_id", "ttl_ms" }` (`ttl_ms` > 0; when the time runs out the trade becomes `expired`).
2. Both parties lock their legs with `POST /v1/trades/{id}/offer`: `{ "actor_id", "legs": [ {"type":"item","item_instance_id":"…"}, {"type":"currency","currency_id":"…","amount":100} ] }`. An item must be in an inventory, tradable and not locked in another trade (`409` if locked); money is taken into escrow (a holding account).
3. When both parties have locked, the trade becomes `locked`. `POST /v1/trades/{id}/accept` (`{ "actor_id" }`) works only with the **initiating** player and exchanges all legs in one transaction. If the recipient's inventory has no room, `422` is returned and the trade stays locked.
4. `POST /v1/trades/{id}/cancel` can be called by either party; locks are released and money is refunded.

If someone who is not a party calls `GET /v1/trades/{id}`, they get `404` (the trade's existence is hidden); the `actor_id` query parameter is required.

## Versioning and replay safety

- All of the `transfers`, `merchants/{key}/buy|sell` and `trades` commands **require** `Idempotency-Key` (`400` if absent). The same key and the same body do not repeat the operation and return `replayed: true`; a different body is `422`. The key is burned only on success.
- Currency and merchant registration writes a new version each time; old versions are untouchable.
- Ledger reads are cursor-based (`limit` 1–200, default 50).

## Reports

The report endpoints (`faucet-sink`, `flags`, `merchant-gap`, `top-holders`) are computed over **closed days** in UTC: `from` and `to` are inclusive and a range of at most 366 days can be given. Missing days are listed in the response as `missing_dates`; they are not counted as zero. `iap_net` is game money, not real money. `flags` is a review signal; no automatic sanction is applied.

## Events

Money movements write events to the outbox. **Among the types you can select as a webhook filter there is no economy-specific type**; endpoints registered without a filter receive all events and so receive money events too, but the envelope format of these events is not a documented contract. Store and reward events are selectable types: [Webhooks](webhooks.md).

## Limits

- Balances and amounts are `i64` smallest units; an amount must be greater than 0.
- Production that exceeds the currency's `max_supply` cap (reward, IAP, sale) returns `422`.
- At most 366 days in reports.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `400` (`Idempotency-Key`) | The header is missing | Send a key on every write |
| `403` | Currency/merchant registration with a client key | Use a server key |
| `404` wallet | The wallet ID given in the transfer does not exist | Read the ID with `GET /v1/wallets`; if the owner has never had a movement in that currency, the wallet is not born yet and the list comes back empty |
| `422` insufficient balance | The balance is less than the amount | Read the balance with `GET /v1/wallets` |
| `422` `transferable=false` | The currency cannot be transferred | Enable transfer on the currency or use another route |
| `409` stock | The merchant's stock is not enough | Reduce the quantity |

## Working example: grant money, then buy a product

The server gives the player money from a reward table; the player buys a product from the store with their own session. The first step runs on the server, the second in the game client. The `welcome_pack` table must already be set up from the panel ([Reward tables](../panel/reward-tables.md)) or with `POST /v1/reward-tables`.

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/economy-grant-and-buy.ts -->
```ts
/** Ekonomi akışı: sunucu ödül tablosundan para verir, oyuncu kendi oturumuyla mağazadan ürün alır. */
import { CrxClient, StoreBuyErrorCode, storeBuyErrorCode, type PlayerClient } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";

/** 1. adım (güvenilir sunucu): oyuncuya tablodan ödül verir. Aynı `requestKey` ile tekrar ödeme yapmaz. */
export async function grantWelcomeReward(baseUrl: string, serverApiKey: string, playerId: string, requestKey: string): Promise<void> {
  const crx = new CrxClient({ baseUrl, apiKey: serverApiKey });
  const grant = await crx.grantRewardTable("welcome_pack", {
    playerId,
    source: { type: "manual", operatorId: "game-server" },
    idempotencyKey: requestKey,
  });
  // `rewards` verilen birleşik ödüllerdir; `replayed: true` ikinci çağrının aynı sonucu geri verdiği anlamına gelir.
  console.log(grant.rewards, grant.replayed);
}

/** 2. adım (oyun istemcisi): oyuncunun gördüğü ilk ürünü satın alır. */
export async function buyFirstListing(player: PlayerClient, pageKey: string, idempotencyKey: string): Promise<string> {
  const catalog = await player.store.catalog({ page: pageKey });
  const listing = catalog.pages[0]?.listings[0];
  if (listing === undefined || listing.version === null) return "Vitrinde ürün yok.";
  try {
    // Gördüğünüz sürümü geri gönderin: fiyat arada değiştiyse sunucu satmaz (409 listing_changed).
    const result = await player.store.buy(listing.id, { expectedVersion: listing.version, quantity: 1, idempotencyKey });
    return `Satın alındı. Kalan bakiye: ${result.balanceAfter}`;
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    switch (storeBuyErrorCode(error)) {
      case StoreBuyErrorCode.InsufficientFunds: return "Bakiye yetmiyor.";
      case StoreBuyErrorCode.OutOfStock: return "Stok tükendi.";
      case StoreBuyErrorCode.ListingChanged: return "Ürün değişti; mağazayı yenileyin.";
      default: throw error;
    }
  }
}
```

## Related pages

- [Rewards](rewards.md) · [Store and IAP](store-iap.md) · [Inventory and items](inventory-items.md) · [Social](social.md)
- [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md) · [Numbers and encoding](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md)

docs.title: Game rules and automations
docs.description: Describes game rule values set from the panel, event-driven automations, the REST rule endpoints and the limits of CEL rules.
headings: Where it lives in the panel
docs.body:
# Game rules and automations

This page describes the two parts of the panel's "Rules" screen: the **game rule values** that the game's plugin reports (for example police thresholds) and the **automations** that do work automatically when an event happens. Read it if you want to tune the game's behavior without shipping code or react automatically to an event.

## What it does

- **Game rule values:** The game's plugin reports which numbers are adjustable (name, unit, lower and upper bound, step, default). An operator changes these values in the panel and **publishes** them; the new values take effect in the game shortly (in about 6 seconds at the latest). Every publish becomes a new version and you can return to old values with one click.
- **Automations:** Rules of the form "when this event happens, if this condition is true, do this". A rule attaches to character events (`level_up`, `xp_added` …) and gives the character a stat, resource, flag, modifier or reward. Conditions are written as a CEL expression; in the panel a structured builder generates the CEL for you.

Game rule values are a panel surface: your game server does **not** write them with a REST endpoint; the plugin reads the values on the server. Automations are managed both from the panel and with REST (they are part of the `characters` module).

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| An overview of the Rules screen, topics and cards | [Rules](../panel/rules.md) |
| Edit, publish and preview a game rule card | [Rule card](../panel/rules-game-card.md) |
| See the publish history and the diff, roll back | [Rule history](../panel/rules-history.md) |
| Create, edit, enable and disable an automation | [Automation editor](../panel/rules-automation-editor.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source, and the panel itself is shown in Turkish.

## Game rule values

### Model

- **Catalog:** Reported by the game's plugin. There are topics, cards and each card's parameters; every parameter comes with a unit (for example seconds, meters, percent) and bounds. If there is no catalog or the plugin does not report one, only Automations appear in the panel.
- **Version:** The effective values are the latest version. If there has been no publish, the plugin's code defaults are used ("Kod varsayılanı", the code default). Publishing and rolling back write a new version; history is not deleted.
- **Apply time:** If a parameter is `canlı` (live), it is applied shortly after the publish; if it is `yeniden başlatmada` (on restart), the old value stays until the game server restarts, and the panel shows both together as "Yayında / Bekliyor" (Published / Pending).
- **Validation:** Values are validated on the server against the catalog bounds, step and cross-field constraints; an invalid field is reported per field. The plugin re-validates with the same bounds; an invalid value does not break the game, and the plugin falls back to its code defaults.
- **Permission:** Reading is open to the four panel roles; publishing and rolling back only to the `super_admin` and `game_manager` roles. Publishing and rolling back require a justification of 8–500 characters and are written to the audit log.
- **Concurrency:** A publish carries the version you saw (`expectedVersion`); if someone else published while you were looking, `409` is returned and you need to refresh the tab.
- **Preview:** The panel runs a scenario (for example a continuous speed violation) with the plugin's real logic using today's and the proposed values and shows the event timeline; it saves nothing.
- **Client warning:** If a parameter is `clientVisible`, the game client reads it from the plugin's query. If the client does not read that value yet, the panel warns you while publishing.

### Effect on the game

Your game code does not read game rule values with REST. The plugin takes the values from a single snapshot at every step on the server; the values the client needs come through the plugin's own query. This behavior is plugin-specific; today only the `package-ride` plugin reports a catalog. Third-party plugins reporting a catalog and being loaded is **not supported yet**; see [Plugins: overview](../plugins/overview.md).

## Automations

### Model

- **Rule:** `key` (a unique key), `trigger_type` (the trigger event), `condition` (a CEL expression), `actions` (a list of actions) and `priority`. A rule is versioned; every publish is a new version.
- **Trigger:** `flag_set`, `attribute_set`, `resource_changed`, `modifier_added`, `modifiers_removed`, `xp_added`, `level_up`, `ability_unlocked`, `event_emitted`, `character_rolled_back`. An unknown type is rejected. The panel builder does not offer the `character_rolled_back` option.
- **Actions:** `add_stat` (`key`, `delta`), `add_resource` (`key`, `delta`), `set_flag` (`key`, `value`), `add_modifier`, `remove_modifier` and `grant_reward` (`what`: a fixed amount of money `{ "type": "currency", "key", "amount" }` or a reward table `{ "type": "table", "key" }`).
- **CEL context:** The condition has the variables `character`, `event`, `now` and `seed`; the functions `has_ability`, `base_stat` and `clamp` can be used. The context carries time and seed, a rule cannot read its own clock; there is no `now()` or `random()`. Rules are compiled at registration, not at run time.
- **Budget (fixed):** In one command chain at most 50 rules are evaluated and 200 actions are produced, the chain depth cannot exceed 5, and a condition expression cannot exceed 500 nodes. Exceeding it is **fail-closed**: the command is rejected with `429` and which limit was exceeded is stated. Two rules that trigger each other are cut off by this limit.

### Panel builder

The builder produces CEL from a "When → Conditions → Do" structure: condition rows (field, operator, value) are combined with **all** (`&&`) or **any** (`||`); at most 20 conditions and 10 actions can be added. Text values are escaped; line breaks and control characters are rejected. When the builder is used, the server recompiles the rule (the CEL text the client sends is not read for a builder rule). A new rule starts **disabled**; the "enable right away" option is unchecked. Before publishing you can do a **dry run** with a sample event; it is not required.

### Calls your game makes

Rule endpoints are called with an **API key**:

```
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

| Method and path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/rules` | Saves a rule (`201`) |
| `GET /v1/rules` | Lists rules (`cursor`, `limit`) |
| `GET /v1/rules/{key}` | Reads the rule's current version |
| `POST /v1/rules/{key}/enable`, `POST /v1/rules/{key}/disable` | Enables / disables the rule (`204`) |
| `DELETE /v1/rules/{key}` | Deletes the rule (`204`) |
| `POST /v1/rules/dry-run` | Tries a rule against a character without writing |

> [!WARNING]
> **Known limitation:** The endpoints that write rules do not look at the key type; a valid **client key** can also save or delete a rule. If you embed a client key in the game, manage rules from your own server and do not call these endpoints from the client.

The TypeScript SDK exposes these endpoints in a typed way: `createRule`, `listRules`, `getRule`, `deleteRule`, `enableRule`, `disableRule`, `dryRunRule` (see [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md)). These endpoints take raw CEL text; the panel builder's structured model exists only on the panel surface.

#### Saving a rule

```
POST /v1/rules
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "key": "lvl10_reward",
  "trigger_type": "level_up",
  "condition": "event.to == 10",
  "actions": [
    { "type": "grant_reward", "what": { "type": "currency", "key": "gold", "amount": 1000 } },
    { "type": "set_flag", "key": "reached_level_10", "value": true }
  ],
  "priority": 0
}
```

```json
{ "key": "lvl10_reward", "current_version": 1, "enabled": true, "created_at": "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z" }
```

A rule saved with REST starts **enabled right away** (`enabled: true`); unlike the panel builder, to start it disabled call `POST /v1/rules/{key}/disable` after saving. `event.to` is the new level of the level-up event; event fields vary by trigger. The registration is rejected if the condition cannot be compiled, the trigger is unknown or a budget limit is exceeded.

#### Dry run

```
POST /v1/rules/dry-run
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "condition": "character.progression.level >= 10", "actions": [ { "type": "set_flag", "key": "veteran", "value": true } ], "character_id": "0192f0f2-…" }
```

```json
{ "condition_result": true, "node_cost": 7, "would_produce_events": [ { "...": "…" } ], "would_grant": [], "warnings": [] }
```

A dry run writes no events and grants no rewards.

## Versioning and replay safety

- Publishing and rolling back game rules: done by the panel with `Idempotency-Key` and `expectedVersion`; the same key returns the same version again and writes a single audit record.
- Automation publishing: every publish is a new version; old versions are not deleted, and "roll back" rewrites the old version as a new version.
- The REST rule endpoints have no `Idempotency-Key` or `If-Match`.

## Events

The actions a rule runs produce normal character events (`flag_set`, `xp_added` …); these can be delivered through [webhooks](webhooks.md). A reward produced by a rule also produces the `reward_granted` event.

## Limits

- In a command chain: 50 rules, 200 actions, depth 5, 500 nodes per condition.
- In the panel builder: at most 20 conditions and 10 actions.
- A game rule justification is 8–500 characters.
- Game rule integer values are limited to ±(2^53−1) in the panel.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `429` (command) | The rule chain exceeded the budget | Simplify the rules that trigger each other |
| `400`/`422` on registration | The CEL could not be compiled, unknown trigger or field | Try the condition with a dry run first |
| `409` in the panel (publish) | Someone else published while you were looking | Refresh the tab and publish again |
| Field error in the panel (`422`) | The value is outside the bound, step or constraint | Respect the bound the field shows |
| I published the value but the game behaves the old way | The parameter is applied `yeniden başlatmada` (on restart), or the 6 seconds have not passed | Look at the panel's "Bekliyor" (Pending) indicator |

## Working example

The two requests above (the `lvl10_reward` registration and the dry run) together form a complete flow: first try the condition with a dry run, then save it with `POST /v1/rules`, then make a character level up with an `add_xp` command and verify that the rule ran, following the flow on the [Characters](characters.md) page.

## Related pages

- [Characters](characters.md) · [Rewards](rewards.md) · [Webhooks](webhooks.md) · [Notifications](notifications.md)
- [Plugins: overview](../plugins/overview.md) · [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md)

headings: Where it lives in the panel
docs.body:
# Inventory and items

This page describes how to define your game's items (potions, weapons, cosmetics…), give them to players, consume them, transfer them and place them in the inventory. Read it if you want inventory state to be held safely on the server.

## What it does

The items module (`items`) manages two separate things:

- **Item definition:** A kind such as "Small health potion". Its key, kind, whether it is stackable, whether it is tradable and the NPC buy/sell price live here.
- **Item instance:** The real item in a player's hands. It carries the definition version it was born with, its owner, its quantity and its customization data (`metadata`).

An **inventory** is the placement of an owner's items. The inventory only holds *which item is in which slot*; quantity and customization live on the item instance.

If the module is disabled, the endpoints return `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"items"}`. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| Edit item definitions and game data (the built-in item group) | [Content](../panel/content.md) |
| Attach a 3D model to an item | [3D models](../panel/models.md), [Model profile](../panel/model-profile.md) |
| See a player's inventory and wallet | [Player profile](../panel/player-profile.md) |
| Sell an item in the store | [Store](../panel/store.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Kind (`kind`):** `consumable`, `equipment`, `material`, `cosmetic`, `vip_card`.
- **Stackable (`stackable`) and `max_stack`:** For a stackable item, instances from the same definition version with empty `metadata` merge into a single row. If `stackable: true`, `max_stack` is required (between 1 and `2147483647`).
- **`tradeable`:** If `false`, the item cannot be transferred to another owner (`422`). The default is `true`.
- **`npc_buy_price`, `npc_sell_price`:** An integer in the smallest unit. If `null`, buying/selling with a merchant is closed.
- **Version pinning:** Each instance carries the definition version it was born with (`definition_version`). Changing a definition later does not change the rules of old instances.
- **Owner (`owner`):** The form `<kind>:<uuid>`; the kind can be `player`, `character`, `clan` or `system`. Example: `player:0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f`.
- **Inventory:** Opened by itself on the first command (default capacity 32). The capacity is the upper bound on the **number of occupied slots**; a slot number can be any number 0 or greater. Reading an inventory that has never been opened returns `404` and does not open it.
- **`version`:** Both the item instance and the inventory have their own version; it grows with every change and is used with `If-Match`.

## Calls your game makes

Item and inventory endpoints are called with an **API key**:

```
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

The player side offers two read endpoints; they are called with a **player session** (a cookie or session token, with the `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>` header):

| Method and path | Credential | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/item-definitions` | server key | Saves a definition as a new version (game data can also be written with the `content` field) |
| `GET /v1/item-definitions/{key}` | API key | Reads the current definition version |
| `POST /v1/items` | server key | Creates (mints) an item |
| `GET /v1/items?owner=player:<uuid>` | API key | Lists the owner's items (`cursor`, `limit`) |
| `GET /v1/items/{id}` | API key | Reads a single instance |
| `POST /v1/items/{id}/consume` | API key | Consumes quantity |
| `POST /v1/items/{id}/destroy` | server key | Destroys the item |
| `POST /v1/items/{id}/transfer` | API key | Transfers ownership |
| `GET /v1/inventories/{owner}` | API key | Reads the inventory and the occupied slots |
| `POST /v1/inventories/{owner}/move` | API key | Places or moves an item into a slot |
| `POST /v1/inventories/{owner}/split` | API key | Splits a quantity off a stack into a new slot |
| `POST /v1/inventories/{owner}/stack` | API key | Merges two stacks |
| `POST /v1/inventories/{owner}/equip` | API key | Puts an item into an equip slot |
| `POST /v1/inventories/{owner}/unequip` | API key | Moves an equipped item down to another slot |
| `GET /v1/player/inventory` | player session | The player's own inventory (read-only) |
| `GET /v1/player/items` | player session | The player's own items (read-only) |
| `GET /v1/catalog/items`, `GET /v1/catalog/items/{key}` | server key or player session | The item catalog ([below](#item-catalog)) |

> [!NOTE]
> The TypeScript SDK has no typed client for items and inventory; these endpoints are called with raw REST. There is no SDK helper yet for reading with a player session (`/v1/player/*`) either. Coverage table: [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md).

> [!WARNING]
> **Known limitation:** The `consume`, `transfer`, `move`, `split`, `stack`, `equip` and `unequip` endpoints do not look at the key type; a valid **client key** can call them too, and `owner` or the item ID is given freely in the request. A client key is scoped to the environment, not to the player. Verify **on your own server** that a player touches only their own items; against the risk of cheating, make these calls from the game server. `mint` and `destroy` work only with a server key.

### Minting an item

```
POST /v1/items
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: quest-17-potion-player-1234

{
  "definition_key": "health_potion",
  "owner": "player:0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f",
  "quantity": 3,
  "source": "quest"
}
```

```json
{
  "instance": {
    "id": "0192f1aa-1111-7222-8333-944455556666",
    "definition_id": "0192f0aa-0000-7000-8000-000000000001",
    "definition_version": 2,
    "owner_type": "player",
    "owner_id": "0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f",
    "quantity": 3,
    "metadata": {},
    "version": 1,
    "created_event_id": "0192f1aa-2222-7333-8444-955566667777",
    "created_at": "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z"
  },
  "event": { "type": "item_instance_created" },
  "replayed": false
}
```

- `quantity` is between 1 and `2147483647`.
- `source` can be `mint`, `craft`, `purchase`, `quest` or `grant`; if not given, `mint`.
- If `metadata` is non-empty, the item does not stack and is always a single row.
- For a stackable definition, if the owner already holds a stack of the same version with empty `metadata`, no new row is opened and the quantity is added to that stack. If `max_stack` is exceeded, `422`.

### Consuming, destroying, transferring

| Endpoint | Body | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/items/{id}/consume` | `{"amount": 1}` | `amount` is between 1 and the current quantity; exceeding it is `422`. If the quantity drops to zero, the row is deleted and the next `GET` returns `404`. The item kind is not checked. |
| `POST /v1/items/{id}/destroy` | `{"amount": 1}` | Server key only. The same rule applies; past events are not deleted. |
| `POST /v1/items/{id}/transfer` | `{"to_owner": "player:<uuid>"}` | `422` if `tradeable: false`. |

`Idempotency-Key` is required on all three of these endpoints (`400` if absent). `If-Match` is optional and is the item instance's `version` value.

### Inventory placement

Placement commands have the same shape:

```
POST /v1/inventories/player:0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f/move
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: move-1
If-Match: 4

{ "item_instance_id": "0192f1aa-1111-7222-8333-944455556666", "to_slot": 5 }
```

| Endpoint | Body |
|---|---|
| `move` | `item_instance_id`, `to_slot` |
| `equip`, `unequip` | `item_instance_id`, `to_slot` |
| `split` | `from_instance_id`, `amount`, `to_slot` |
| `stack` | `from_instance_id`, `to_instance_id` |

The response has the form `{ "inventory": {…}, "slots": [{ "slot_idx": 5, "item_instance_id": "…", "created_at": "…" }], "event": {…}, "replayed": false }`.

Rules:

- Placing into an occupied slot is `422`. When placing a new item, exceeding the capacity is also `422`; moving an already placed item does not consume capacity.
- `If-Match` is the **inventory's** version. If you send `If-Match` on the first open (while the inventory does not exist yet), you get `400`.
- If the same item is already placed in another inventory, `409` (double-placement lock).
- `split`: `amount` is between 1 and one less than the source quantity; the item must be stackable. The new instance's ID is returned in the event in the response (`new_instance_id`).
- `stack`: both stacks must be placed; they must be of the same definition version and have empty `metadata`.
- `equip`: if the definition's `metadata` has an `equip_condition` (a CEL expression), equipping depends on this condition. If the condition or its evaluation errors, equipping is **rejected** (`422`). In the condition the `character` context is empty for now, and `now` and `seed` are a constant `0`.

## Item catalog

The game client reads the item definition, the **typed data rows** and the model address from the catalog. There are two audiences: a **player** sees only rows with `player` visibility; a **server key** sees all rows, with each row's visibility and with `content_revision`. Responses carry an `ETag`; with `If-None-Match`, `304` is returned if nothing changed. Details and a watching example: [Content groups](content-groups.md#catalog-items-and-characters) and [Scenes, assets and 3D models](scenes-assets-models.md).

## Versioning and replay safety

- `Idempotency-Key` is **required** on mint, consume, destroy, transfer and all inventory commands. If the same key and the same body arrive a second time, the operation does not run again; the response returns with `replayed: true`. The same key with a different body is `422`. The key is burned only on success.
- `If-Match` prevents concurrent writes (a mismatch is `409`).
- General rules: [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md).

## Events

Item events (`item_instance_created`, `item_ownership_changed`, `item_consumed`, `item_stacks_merged`, `item_stack_split`) can be used in rule automation and quest objectives. **There is no item event among the event types you can select as a filter for a webhook endpoint.** An endpoint registered without a filter (empty `event_types`) receives all events and so receives item events too; the envelope format of these events is not a documented contract, so do not rely on it. If you need to announce an item change to the outside, read it from your own server. Selectable types: [Webhook events](../reference/webhook-events.md).

## Limits

- `limit` is 1–200 on list endpoints; pagination is cursor-based.
- The default inventory capacity is 32 occupied slots.
- `quantity`, `amount` and prices are integers; there are no decimals.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `400` (no key) | The `Idempotency-Key` header is missing | Send a key on every write |
| `403` | `mint`/`destroy`/definition registration with a client key | Use a server key |
| `404` (inventory) | The inventory was never opened | The first inventory command (for example `move`) opens it; a read does not |
| `409` | `If-Match` is stale or the item is in another inventory | Re-read and try again |
| `422` insufficient quantity | `amount` is greater than the current quantity | Reduce the quantity |
| `422` trade | `tradeable: false` | Enable trading on the definition |
| `422` slot occupied | The target slot is occupied | Choose an empty slot |

## Working example

An example that gives a potion and consumes it with raw REST (it uses `fetch` because the SDK has no typed client):

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/inventory-raw-rest.ts -->
```ts
/** Envanter ve eşya uçları için SDK'da tipli istemci yoktur; ham REST ile çağrılır (sunucu anahtarı). */

/** Küçük yardımcı: Bearer + Idempotency-Key ile JSON POST. */
async function post(baseUrl: string, key: string, path: string, idempotencyKey: string, body: unknown, ifMatch?: number): Promise<unknown> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Idempotency-Key": idempotencyKey,
  };
  if (ifMatch !== undefined) headers["If-Match"] = String(ifMatch);
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, { method: "POST", headers, body: JSON.stringify(body) });
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${path}: HTTP ${response.status} ${await response.text()}`);
  return response.json();
}

/** Oyuncuya bir iksir verir (mint, yalnız server anahtarı) ve 1 adedini tüketir. */
export async function grantAndDrink(baseUrl: string, serverKey: string, playerId: string): Promise<void> {
  const minted = (await post(baseUrl, serverKey, "/v1/items", `mint-${playerId}-potion-1`, {
    definition_key: "health_potion",
    owner: `player:${playerId}`,
    quantity: 3,
  })) as { instance: { id: string; version: number } };

  await post(
    baseUrl,
    serverKey,
    `/v1/items/${minted.instance.id}/consume`,
    `drink-${minted.instance.id}-1`,
    { amount: 1 },
    minted.instance.version, // If-Match: okuduğunuz sürüm; uyuşmazlık 409
  );
}
```

## Related pages

- [Economy: wallets, currencies, merchants and trading](economy.md)
- [Store and in-app purchases](store-iap.md)
- [Content groups](content-groups.md)
- [Errors](../reference/errors.md)

Sending a notification from the server
Rules: automatic notifications when an event happens
docs.body:
# Notifications

This page describes how to send players in-game (inbox) and push notifications: provider, template and rule setup in the panel; the game's device registration, inbox reading and direct sending from the server. Read it if you want to use notification infrastructure without writing it yourself.

## What it does

The notifications module (`notifications`) first **writes a notification to a queue**, then a background worker sends it to the provider (FCM, APNs or OneSignal). The API has no synchronous push send: when your request is written to the queue you get `200`; delivery happens afterwards.

The notification text comes from a **template**. A template is written in the panel; the game sends only the template key and the fill data. You can produce a notification in two ways:

- **Sending from the server:** Your game server calls `POST /v1/notifications`.
- **Rule:** A rule you set up in the panel produces a notification automatically when a game event happens (for example a level up, quest completion or store purchase).

If the module is disabled, the endpoints return `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"notifications"}`. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| Enter push provider (FCM, APNs, OneSignal) credentials | [Notifications](../panel/notifications.md) › Providers |
| Write a template (title and body per language, placeholders) | [Notifications](../panel/notifications.md) › Templates |
| Set up an event-driven rule, preview the rule live | [Notifications](../panel/notifications.md) › Rules |
| Send a test notification to a player, see the send history and devices | [Notifications](../panel/notifications.md) › History, Devices |

Provider credentials are entered in the panel only by an authorized role and are stored sealed on the server; the panel shows only the fingerprint.

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source, and the panel tabs are shown in Turkish.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Provider:** `fcm`, `apns`, `one_signal`. Each is switched on and off separately per environment.
- **Device:** A player's registered token (`token`) at a provider and its platform (`ios`, `android`, `web`). The same (environment, provider, token) can be registered again; the response says which branch handled it (`created`, `revived`, `refreshed`).
- **Template:** A key, a title and body per language, `{{placeholder}}` fields. If the requested language is missing, English (`en`) is used. Each notification is bound to the template version at the moment it was sent.
- **Channel:** `in_game` (inbox only), `push` (push only), `both`.
- **Notification (inbox row):** `id`, `template_key`, `title`, `body`, `data`, `channel`, `status`, `created_at`, `sent_at`, `read_at`. Status: `queued`, `sent`, `delivered`, `failed`, `read`.
- **Dedup key (`dedup_key`):** The same (environment, player, key) is not written a second time.

## Calls your game makes

There are two credential types: a **player session** (cookie or session token + `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>`) and a **server key** (`Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`).

| Method and path | Credential | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/notifications` | server key | Writes a notification for a player to the queue |
| `GET /v1/notifications` | player session | Inbox (`status`, `cursor`, `limit`) |
| `POST /v1/notifications/{id}/read` | player session | Marks as read |
| `POST /v1/devices` | player session | Registers a push device |
| `DELETE /v1/devices/{token}?provider=` | player session | Revokes a device registration (`204`) |
| `GET /v1/push/config` | no credential (`x-crx-env` required) | Settings exposed to the client for web push |
| `GET /v1/ws` | player session | Live notification push socket (server to player only; the environment is given with the `x-crx-env` **header**, so it cannot be connected with the browser `WebSocket` API; frames arrive at most once, the durable surface is the inbox) |

On the player endpoints the `x-csrf-token` and `Origin` checks are **not applied**; the session cookie or session token is enough.

The player side is ready in the TypeScript SDK: under `player.notifications` there are `getPushConfig`, `registerDevice`, `unregisterDevice`, `enableWebPush`, `disableWebPush`, `inbox` and `markRead`. There is no typed client for sending from the server; use raw REST. See [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md).

### Sending a notification from the server

```
POST /v1/notifications
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "player_id": "0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f",
  "template_key": "daily_reward_ready",
  "locale": "en",
  "data": { "amount": 250 },
  "channel": "both",
  "dedup_key": "daily-2026-11-03"
}
```

```json
{ "id": "0192f400-…", "duplicate": false }
```

- `locale`: a short language code (`tr`, `en` …). If the requested language is not in the template, `en` is used.
- `dedup_key` (optional, 1–256 characters): if the same key arrives a second time, no new row is written; `200` and `duplicate: true` are returned with **the ID of the first notification**.
- `403`: a client key or a player session. `404`: the template does not exist in any language. `400`: `template_key` is empty or longer than 128 characters, the `locale` format is invalid, or a placeholder in the template is missing from `data`.

### Reading the inbox

```
GET /v1/notifications?status=queued&limit=20
x-crx-env: 0192f000-0000-7000-8000-00000000e001
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    { "id": "0192f400-…", "template_key": "daily_reward_ready", "template_version": 2, "title": "Your daily reward is ready", "body": "250 gold is waiting for you.", "data": { "amount": 250 }, "channel": "both", "status": "sent", "created_at": "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z", "sent_at": "2026-11-03T09:00:02Z", "read_at": null }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

The list is ordered newest to oldest (`created_at`, `id`). `limit` is 1–100; when `next_cursor` is `null`, it is the last page. Rows whose delivery **failed** are listed too. `POST /v1/notifications/{id}/read` makes the row `read`; a second call returns the same row and produces no new event.

### Registering a push device

```
POST /v1/devices
x-crx-env: 0192f000-0000-7000-8000-00000000e001
Content-Type: application/json

{ "provider": "fcm", "platform": "android", "token": "<device token>", "device_meta": { "model": "Pixel 8" } }
```

```json
{ "id": "…", "registration": "created", "provider": "fcm", "platform": "android", "created_at": "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z" }
```

`provider` is `apns`, `fcm` or `one_signal`; `platform` is `ios`, `android` or `web`. The token cannot be empty. The player ID comes from the session, not from the body. `app_key` separates the app in multi-app environments.

> [!NOTE]
> The generated OpenAPI document writes the device provider as `onesignal`; the server and the SDK use `one_signal`. This is a known documentation deviation; send `one_signal`.

For web push, `player.notifications.enableWebPush` runs the browser permission flow with the settings it gets from `GET /v1/push/config`; on sign-out, `session.logout()` automatically revokes the web device registered from this page.

## Rules: automatic notifications when an event happens

In the panel, a rule consists of a **trigger** (a game event from a closed list; for example `level_up`, `quest_completed`, `store_purchase_completed`, `vip_tier_up`), an optional **condition**, a **template**, a **language**, a **channel** and the recipient player path. Rule versions appear on the panel's history tab. A notification itself does not trigger a new rule. The rule editor offers a "live preview" and a test send. For the detailed fields, see the panel page.

## Versioning and replay safety

- Sending: replay safety with `dedup_key`; there is **no** `Idempotency-Key` header.
- Device registration and the read mark are naturally idempotent.
- The template version is bound to the notification; changing the template later does not affect an old notification.

## Events

When a notification is written to the queue, a `notification_queued` event is produced and the send worker consumes it. **Among the types you can select as a webhook filter there is no notification type**; endpoints registered without a filter receive this internal event too, but the envelope format is not a documented contract.

## Limits

- `dedup_key` is 1–256 characters; inbox `limit` is 1–100.
- Push delivery is best-effort: if the provider rejects it, the row becomes `failed`. If a device is permanently invalid (for example the app was uninstalled), the device is revoked automatically.
- If provider credentials are not defined, the notification waits in the queue and the provider status in the panel shows a warning.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `403` (send) | A client key instead of a server key | Use the server key |
| `404` (send) | `template_key` does not exist in any language | Create and publish the template in the panel |
| `duplicate: true` | The same `dedup_key` was already written | Expected behavior; use a new key for a new notification |
| The notification stays `queued` | The provider is disabled or the credential is wrong | Check the provider status in the panel |
| `400` (device) | Empty token or unknown provider/platform | Fix the input |

## Working example

Draining the inbox on the player side:

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/notifications-inbox.ts -->
```ts
/** Oyuncu tarafı: gelen kutusunu okur ve okunmamış bildirimleri okundu işaretler. */
import type { PlayerClient } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";

/** İlk sayfadaki okunmamış bildirimleri yazdırır ve okundu yapar. */
export async function drainInbox(player: PlayerClient): Promise<number> {
  const page = await player.notifications.inbox({ limit: 20 });
  let marked = 0;
  for (const item of page.items) {
    if (item.readAt !== null) continue;
    console.log(item.title, item.body, item.data);
    await player.notifications.markRead(item.id);
    marked += 1;
  }
  return marked;
}
```

The curl example for sending from the server is above.

## Related pages

- [Characters](characters.md) · [Rewards](rewards.md) · [Store and IAP](store-iap.md) · [Game rules](game-rules.md)
- [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md) · [Errors](../reference/errors.md)
