docs.body:
# Player data (cloud save)

This page describes how to store a player's progress (level, settings, game save) in Open Play and resume it on another device. Read it if your game carries its own save format and you want to attach it to the player account.

## What it does

Player data is a **per-player key-value** store. The value is **an opaque JSON object that the server does not interpret**: Open Play stores it, measures its size and returns it unchanged; it does not query its fields or compute anything from them. Your game decides the save format and its version.

This feature is **part of the core**: it is not tied to a product module and cannot be turned off on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it is in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| See a player's keys, sizes and value; delete one if needed | [Players](../panel/players.md) › player profile › "Game data" section |

Values **cannot be written** from the panel; they appear only as read-only formatted JSON. An operator deletion requires a reason (8–500 characters) and is written to the audit log.

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` (lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; at most 64 characters) |
| Value | Top-level **JSON object**; its serialized (compact) size is at most **65,536 bytes** |
| Number of keys | At most **16** per player |
| Write rate | At most **60** writes per minute per player (PUT and DELETE; reads are not counted) |

**Floating-point numbers are allowed in the value**: the value is opaque data and the server does no arithmetic on it. There are two caveats: the order of object keys is not preserved, and integers larger than 2^64 and decimals beyond double precision may be rounded; store large numbers as strings.

## Versioned writes (CAS)

Every key has a **version**: `1` on the first write, increased by 1 on every successful write. The version is an i64 and is carried in JSON as a **decimal string** (`"3"`); in the HTTP header it takes the form `ETag: "3"`.

**There is no unconditional write.** Every `PUT` carries exactly one of:

- `If-None-Match: *` — create only if the key **does not exist**.
- `If-Match: "<version>"` — update only if the current version is this one.

Sending both headers, sending neither, or sending a malformed value returns `428 precondition_required`. If the version does not match (another device wrote at the same time) the response is `409 version_conflict` together with the current version; **read the remote record, merge it with your own rule and retry**. Source: `crx-domain::player_data`.

## Calls your game makes

Player endpoints work with a player session: the `__Secure-crx.session` cookie or an opaque session token (`Authorization: Bearer`) and `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>`. **Writes** (`PUT`, `DELETE`) carry the same browser protection as the store purchase endpoint: Origin check and, for a cookie session, `x-csrf-token` (see [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)). A developer key is not accepted on player endpoints (`401`).

| Method and path | Identity | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/player/data` | player session | Lists a summary of the player's own keys |
| `GET /v1/player/data/{key}` | player session | Reads one key (`ETag: "<version>"`) |
| `PUT /v1/player/data/{key}` | player session | Creates or updates with a precondition |
| `DELETE /v1/player/data/{key}` | player session | Deletes with `If-Match` (`204`) |
| `GET /v1/players/{player_id}/data` | **server key** | Key summaries of one player (read only) |
| `GET /v1/players/{player_id}/data/{key}` | **server key** | One key of one player (read only) |

Server endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`; a **client key gets `403`** and a player session gets `401`. Responses carry `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

### List

```
GET /v1/player/data
x-crx-env: 0192f000-0000-7000-8000-00000000e001
```

```json
{ "items": [ { "key": "my-game.save", "version": "3", "size": 214, "updatedAt": "2026-11-03T10:15:30.120Z" } ] }
```

### Create

```
PUT /v1/player/data/my-game.save
x-crx-env: 0192f000-0000-7000-8000-00000000e001
x-csrf-token: <csrf token>
If-None-Match: *
Content-Type: application/json

{ "value": { "level": 4, "stars": 17, "playTimeSeconds": 913.5 } }
```

```json
{ "key": "my-game.save", "version": "1", "updatedAt": "2026-11-03T10:15:30.120Z" }
```

The response also carries the `ETag: "1"` header. The body must be exactly `{ "value": <object> }`; any other field returns `422 invalid_value`.

### Update and delete

```
PUT /v1/player/data/my-game.save
If-Match: "1"
{ "value": { "level": 5, "stars": 21 } }
```

```
DELETE /v1/player/data/my-game.save
If-Match: "2"
```

Delete returns `204`. A player deletion is conditional too; an operator deletion is done from the panel.

### Read

```
GET /v1/player/data/my-game.save
```

```json
{ "key": "my-game.save", "value": { "level": 5, "stars": 21 }, "version": "2", "updatedAt": "2026-11-03T10:16:02.004Z" }
```

If the key does not exist the response is `404` with `{"code":"not_found"}`.

## Error codes

Unlike the rest of the core, the errors of these endpoints are **JSON**: `{ "code": "…", "message": "…" }`.

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | The key does not exist (on server endpoints also when the player is not in this environment) |
| 409 | `version_conflict` | The version did not match, or `If-None-Match: *` on an existing key; `currentVersion` carries the current version (`null` if the key does not exist) |
| 413 | `value_too_large` | The value exceeded 64 KiB; the `limit` field gives the limit |
| 422 | `invalid_key` | The key does not match the pattern |
| 422 | `invalid_value` | The value is not an object, the body is not `{ "value": … }`, or it is not JSON |
| 422 | `too_many_keys` | The player already has 16 keys; the `limit` field gives the limit |
| 428 | `precondition_required` | `If-Match` / `If-None-Match: *` is missing, doubled or malformed |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | The 60 writes per minute limit was exceeded; `Retry-After` gives the wait in seconds |
| 401 | — | No session, an invalid session, or a banned player (the identity layer does not leak the ban distinction) |
| 403 | — | Origin, Fetch Metadata or CSRF rejection; on server endpoints, a client key |

A write by a banned player ends with `401` in the identity layer; as a defence the store also rejects the write with `403` and `{"code":"account_banned"}`.

## TypeScript SDK

`PlayerClient.data` is the typed counterpart of these endpoints: `list()`, `get(key)`, `create(key, value)`, `update(key, value, version)`, `delete(key, version)`. Versions are `bigint`; the value is a plain JS object (safe integers are `number`, out-of-range integers are `bigint`, decimals are `number`). The SDK manages the CSRF token and the cookie. A `409` conflict is thrown as `PlayerDataConflict` (+ `currentVersion: bigint | null`); other rejections are `CrxError` and are told apart with `playerDataErrorCode(error)`. See [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md).

## Working example: save, merge on conflict

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/player-data-save.ts -->
```ts
/** Oyuncu verisi (bulut kaydı): kaydı oku, değiştir, sürümlü yaz; çatışmada uzak kayıtla birleştirip yeniden dene. */
import { PlayerDataConflict, type PlayerClient, type PlayerDataValue } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";

const KEY = "my-game.save";

/** İki kaydı oyunun kendi kuralıyla birleştirir: burada her bölümde en iyi yıldız sayısı kalır. */
function merge(remote: PlayerDataValue, local: PlayerDataValue): PlayerDataValue {
  const best = (a: unknown, b: unknown): number => Math.max(typeof a === "number" ? a : 0, typeof b === "number" ? b : 0);
  return { ...remote, ...local, stars: best(remote.stars, local.stars) };
}

/** Kaydı buluta yazar; sürüm çatışırsa (başka cihaz yazmıştır) uzak kaydı okur, birleştirir ve en çok 3 kez dener. */
export async function saveToCloud(player: PlayerClient, local: PlayerDataValue): Promise<void> {
  let value = local;
  let current = await player.data.get(KEY).catch((error: unknown) => {
    if (error instanceof Error && "status" in error && error.status === 404) return null;
    throw error;
  });
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt += 1) {
    try {
      if (current === null) await player.data.create(KEY, value);
      else await player.data.update(KEY, value, current.version);
      return;
    } catch (error: unknown) {
      if (!(error instanceof PlayerDataConflict)) throw error;
      current = error.currentVersion === null ? null : await player.data.get(KEY);
      if (current !== null) value = merge(current.value, value);
    }
  }
  throw new Error("Kayıt üç denemede birleştirilemedi");
}
```

## Retention and deletion

- The player row is never deleted; when an abandoned guest account is closed (anonymization), that account's player data is **deleted in the same transaction**.
- An operator can delete a key from the panel with a reason; a player deletes their own key with `If-Match`.
- Data is isolated per player and **environment**: a player of one environment cannot be read from another environment.

## Common situations

- **I keep getting 409.** Another device is writing, or you are passing a stale version to `update`. Keep the `version` returned after every write; on a conflict, read the remote record and merge it, do not just increment the raw version and send again.
- **I get 429.** The 60 writes per minute limit is per player. Write with a debounce and at meaningful points, not on every keystroke; wait for `Retry-After`.
- **The 16-key limit.** Use one key per save type instead of many small keys (for example `my-game.save`, `my-game.settings`).

## Related pages

- [Guest sign-in](../auth/guest.md)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.description: Describes reward tables, granting rewards from a table, the daily login reward, quests, NPC rewards and VIP status.
headings: Where it lives in the panel
Granting a reward from a table
docs.body:
# Rewards

This page describes how the rewards your game gives players are defined and granted in Open Play: chance-based reward tables, the daily login reward, quests, NPC rewards and VIP cards. Read it if you want a reward to be granted on the server, cheat-proof and only once.

## What it does

The rewards module (`rewards`) does the job of "give the player money or an item" through a single trustworthy line. Every reward grant is **a single database transaction**: money is written to the wallet, the item is put into the inventory and the event is recorded. If the inventory is full or the currency would exceed its supply cap, **nothing is granted** (`422`).

Table rewards are **deterministic**: the same seed gives the same result. The seed is kept on the server; it does not appear in the response, the webhook event or the ledger record.

If the module is disabled, the endpoints return `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"rewards"}`. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| Set up a reward table, edit row chances and guaranteed rewards, see versions | [Reward tables](../panel/reward-tables.md), [Reward table profile](../panel/reward-table-profile.md) |
| Define the currency to use in a reward | [Currencies](../panel/currencies.md) |
| Define the item to use in a reward | [Content](../panel/content.md) |
| Grant rewards with event-driven automation | [Game rules](game-rules.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Reward table:** `key`, `name`, `rolls` (how many draws are made, 1–10), `entries` (rows) and `guaranteed` (rewards given every time). Every registration becomes **a new version**; the current version is used at grant time and the version number is returned in the result.
- **Row (entry):** `chance_bp` (basis points, 1–10000) and `drop`. The row chances of one draw must **add up to exactly 10000** (100%); "no reward" can be a row.
- **Reward (`drop`):** `currency` (`key`, `min`, `max`), `item` (`key`, `min`, `max`) or `nothing`. The quantity is always chosen from between `min` and `max` with a uniform distribution; quantities are between 1 and 1,000,000. A table has at most 50 rows and 10 guaranteed rewards.
- **Guaranteed reward:** Given independently of the draw; it cannot be `nothing`.
- **Source (`source`):** Writes, in a typed way, why the reward was given: `content_entry`, `tournament`, `leaderboard_season`, `quest`, `npc_reward`, `rule` or `manual`.

## Calls your game makes

All reward endpoints are called with a **server key** (or a key of the admin type); a client key and a player session are rejected. The player ID is carried in the body by the trusted server component:

```
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

| Method and path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/reward-tables` | Saves a reward table as a new version |
| `GET /v1/reward-tables/{key}` | Reads the current version |
| `POST /v1/reward-tables/{key}/grant` | Grants a reward from the table, idempotently |
| `GET /v1/login-rewards/{player_id}` | Reads today's login reward status |
| `POST /v1/login-rewards/{player_id}/claim` | Grants the daily login reward |
| `POST /v1/quests` | Saves a quest definition |
| `GET /v1/quests`, `GET /v1/quests/{key}` | Lists / reads quests |
| `POST /v1/quests/{key}/claim` | Grants the quest period's reward |
| `GET /v1/npc-rewards/{key}/eligibility` | Reads NPC reward eligibility (does not write) |
| `POST /v1/npc-rewards/{key}/claim` | Grants the NPC reward |
| `GET /v1/vip/{player_id}` | Reads the VIP tier |
| `POST /v1/vip/{player_id}/cards/{item_instance_id}/use` | Uses a VIP card |

> [!NOTE]
> In the TypeScript SDK only the reward **table** has a typed client (`CrxClient.createRewardTable`, `getRewardTable`, `grantRewardTable`). The login reward, quest, NPC and VIP endpoints are called with raw REST. See [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md).

### Saving a reward table

```
POST /v1/reward-tables
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "key": "welcome_pack",
  "name": "Welcome pack",
  "rolls": 1,
  "entries": [
    { "chance_bp": 7000, "drop": { "type": "currency", "key": "gold", "min": 100, "max": 300 } },
    { "chance_bp": 2500, "drop": { "type": "item", "key": "health_potion", "min": 1, "max": 3 } },
    { "chance_bp": 500,  "drop": { "type": "nothing" } }
  ],
  "guaranteed": [ { "type": "currency", "key": "gold", "min": 50, "max": 50 } ]
}
```

The response is `201` with `{ id, version, key, name, rolls, entries, guaranteed, created_at_ms }`; the draw seed is not present in any response. If the chances do not add up to 10000, the table is empty or the limits are exceeded, the registration is rejected with `422` and a plain-text message. The `validate` key is reserved and cannot be used as a table key.

### Granting a reward from a table

```
POST /v1/reward-tables/welcome_pack/grant
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Idempotency-Key: welcome-player-1234
Content-Type: application/json

{ "player_id": "0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f", "source": { "type": "manual", "operator_id": "game-server" } }
```

```json
{
  "grant_id": "…", "tx_id": "…", "event_id": "…",
  "table_key": "welcome_pack", "table_version": 1,
  "rewards": [ { "drop": "currency", "key": "gold", "quantity": 250 }, { "drop": "item", "key": "health_potion", "quantity": 2 } ],
  "replayed": false
}
```

`Idempotency-Key` is **required**. The same key and the same body do not grant the reward a second time; the first result is returned with `replayed: true`. The same key with a different body is `422`. The `source` variants:

| `type` | Additional fields |
|---|---|
| `manual` | `operator_id` |
| `content_entry` | `group`, `entry` |
| `quest` | `quest_key` |
| `npc_reward` | `npc_key` |
| `tournament` | `tournament_id`, `placement` |
| `leaderboard_season` | `leaderboard_key`, `season` |
| `rule` | `rule_key`, `event_id` |

Money and items are granted in one transaction: if the inventory is full or the currency supply cap would be exceeded, the whole grant is rolled back and `422` is returned. An NPC reward cannot be granted for a character that is not bound to a player.

### Daily login reward

`GET /v1/login-rewards/{player_id}` returns today's status: `period_date`, `claimed`, `streak_day`, `current_streak`, `config_version`. `POST /v1/login-rewards/{player_id}/claim` grants the reward and returns `{ period_date, streak_day, rewards, event_id, tx_id, replayed }`; **a second call on the same day returns the same receipt** with `replayed: true` and grants no second reward.

The day is computed according to the environment's time zone (`timezone`, [Environments and domains](../panel/game-settings-environments.md)). The reward schedule (the number of days, each day's money reward) and the missed-day policy (`reset_on_miss`: the streak returns to 1; `freeze`: the streak is preserved) are a versioned configuration.

> [!NOTE]
> There is no public endpoint or panel screen yet that writes the login reward configuration (the schedule and the streak policy); for now the configuration is set up by the Open Play operator.

### Quests

`POST /v1/quests` saves a quest definition as a new version:

```json
{
  "key": "kill_10_wolves",
  "name": "Hunt ten wolves",
  "objectives": [ { "key": "wolves", "event_type": "event_emitted", "count": 10, "filter_cel": "event.event_key == \"wolf_killed\"" } ],
  "rewards": [ { "type": "currency", "key": "gold", "amount": 500 }, { "type": "table", "key": "welcome_pack" } ],
  "recurrence": "daily"
}
```

- `objectives[].event_type`: the event type that advances the quest (character events, `score_submitted`, `login`, item and money events and so on); `count` is how many times it is required; `filter_cel` is an optional condition.
- `rewards[].type`: `currency` (`key`, `amount`) or `table` (a reward table key).
- `recurrence`: `none`, `daily`, `weekly`. `window` and `prerequisite_cel` (compiled at registration) are optional.
- The body of `POST /v1/quests/{key}/claim` is `{ "player_id": "…", "period_key": "…" }` (`period_key` at most 160 characters). The response is `{ status: "claimed" | "already_claimed", reward_count, event_id }` — claiming the same period a second time returns `already_claimed` and the reward is not repeated.
- `GET /v1/quests` lists with `search`, `limit`, `offset` (it returns an in-page `total`).

> [!NOTE]
> There is no public REST endpoint yet that reads quest **progress** (which quest a player is at and how far). Progress is computed on the server from events; for this reason your game server itself must know the `period_key` value.

### NPC rewards

`GET /v1/npc-rewards/{key}/eligibility?character_id=…&period_key=…` reports eligibility without writing: `{ eligible, reason }` (`reason`: `cooldown`, `daily_limit`, `condition`). `POST /v1/npc-rewards/{key}/claim` (`Idempotency-Key` required, body `{ "character_id", "period_key" }`) either grants the reward or returns `rejected`: `{ status: "claimed" | "rejected", reward_count, claim_count, tx_id, reason }`. There is no public endpoint yet that registers the NPC rule (cooldown, daily limit, CEL condition, reward).

### VIP

The VIP tier is derived from cumulative points. `GET /v1/vip/{player_id}` returns `{ player_id, cumulative_points, tier, config_version }`. `POST /v1/vip/{player_id}/cards/{item_instance_id}/use` (`Idempotency-Key` required) consumes a `vip_card` item and adds points; if the card does not meet the condition of the next tier up (`current tier + 1`), `422` is returned. A client key and a server key can use the same VIP surface.

## Versioning and replay safety

- Table grant, NPC claim and VIP card use: `Idempotency-Key` is **required**.
- Login reward: a second claim on the same day returns the same receipt; no header is needed.
- Quest claim: the period key is the natural replay safety (`already_claimed`).
- Table and quest registrations are a new version each time; old versions do not change.
- General rules: [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md).

## Events and webhooks

Every reward granted from a table or as a fixed amount of money produces the `reward_granted` event and can be delivered as a webhook. The envelope contains `event_id`, `environment_id`, `player_id`, `type` and `data` (`source_kind`, `table_key`, `table_version` and what was granted); there is no seed. Registration and verification: [Webhooks](webhooks.md).

## Limits

- At most 50 rows, 10 guaranteed rewards and 10 draws (`rolls`) in a table; quantities 1–1,000,000.
- The `chance_bp` total is exactly 10000.
- Quest `period_key` and `claim` fields are at most 160 characters.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `403` | A call with a client key or a player session | Make the call with a server key, from your server |
| `422` (table registration) | The chances do not complete to 10000 or a limit was exceeded | Fix the rows; complete them with a `nothing` row |
| `422` inventory full | There is no empty slot for the item to be granted | Have the player make room; nothing was written, so it can be retried |
| `422` supply cap | The currency's `max_supply` limit | Raise the cap in the panel |
| `422 idempotency mismatch` | The same key, a different body | Use a new key |
| `404` table not found | `key` is wrong or the table has not been saved yet | Verify with `GET /v1/reward-tables/{key}` |

## Working example

The flow of granting money from the welcome table and then buying from the store is on the [Economy](economy.md#working-example-grant-money-then-buy-a-product) page. In TypeScript, the call `crx.grantRewardTable("welcome_pack", { playerId, source, idempotencyKey })` goes to the same endpoint; if `idempotencyKey` is not given, the SDK generates one per call, so on a network retry you must supply the same key **yourself**.

## Related pages

- [Economy](economy.md) · [Inventory and items](inventory-items.md) · [Characters](characters.md) · [Game rules](game-rules.md)
- [Errors](../reference/errors.md) · [Webhooks](webhooks.md)

docs.description: Describes scene provisioning, the content-addressed image store, the 3D model library and how your game reads them.
headings: Where it lives in the panel
Bringing a 3D model into the game
docs.body: # Scenes, assets and 3D models This page describes the three parts that make up your game's world: real-time **scene** (stage/room) registration, **images** uploaded from the panel and the server, and **3D models** uploaded by an operator. Read it if you want to open city rooms from the server, manage icon and banner images, or serve models to the game. ## What it does - **Scene:** The room where the real-time plugin gathers players. The game server registers the scenes it needs at startup; registration is idempotent. - **Image (asset):** PNG, JPEG or WebP. It is content-addressed: the address is the file's `sha256` digest, and the same file is stored once. Store banners, currency icons and content group `image` fields use this store. - **3D model:** A `glb` (or a converted source file) uploaded by an operator in the panel. Once published it is bound to an item or a character and the game gets it from the catalog. The scene and image write endpoints depend on the `scenes` module; if the module is disabled, `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"scenes"}` is returned. The image and model **read** endpoints are core and work even when the module is disabled. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page. ## Where it lives in the panel | What you want to do | Panel page | |---|---| | Upload, preview, publish and archive a 3D model, add a clip | [3D models](../panel/models.md), [Model profile](../panel/model-profile.md) | | Bind a model to an item or a character | [Content](../panel/content.md) (built-in item/character groups) | | Upload store banners and product images, currency icons | [Store](../panel/store.md), [Currencies](../panel/currencies.md) | | Moderate city chat (scene plugin) | [City chat](../panel/scene-chat.md) | | See that the scene plugin is installed, and its permissions | [Plugins](../panel/plugins.md) | > [!NOTE] > Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source. ## Data model (in plain words) **Scene** - The ID is derived from three parts: `plugin_id` (the plugin), `module_id` (the real-time module) and `key` (at most 96 characters). The same triple always resolves to the same scene. - `capacity`: The room's player capacity; at most 10,000. - `state`: `open`, `draining` (emptying) or `closed`. - `partition_id`: The ID of the partition the scene runs on in the distributed setup (generated by the server). **Image** - The type is derived from the first bytes of the file; the `Content-Type` header is only advisory. Accepted types are `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`. - At most **2 MiB**; width and height are each at most 4096 pixels. - The response gives `sha256`, `contentType`, `byteSize` and `created` (whether it was written in this call). **3D model** - An upload can be `glb`, or it is converted from source formats such as `fbx`, `obj`, `usdz`, `stl`, `blend`, `3mf`, `dxf`. The conversion status is `queued`, `converting`, `ready`, `failed`; the reason for a failure appears in the panel as a sentence in Turkish (for example an external resource reference, a budget overrun, a 2D DXF). - Every model is versioned; the published version appears in the catalog. The lifecycle is `active`, `archived`, `purged`. - Default limits: uploaded file 50 MiB, environment quota 1 GiB, 200 models per environment, 20 versions per model, 10 uploads per operator per 10 minutes. - The converter runs only on the amd64 architecture; on other architectures only `glb` can be uploaded. ## Calls your game makes | Method and path | Credential | What it does | |---|---|---| | `PUT /v1/scenes` | server key | Provisions a scene idempotently | | `PUT /v1/assets` | server key | Uploads an image as a raw body | | `GET /v1/assets` | server key | Lists the environment's images (`cursor`, `limit`) | | `DELETE /v1/assets/{sha256}` | server key | Deletes an image row (`204`) | | `GET /v1/assets/{sha256}` | no credential | Reads the image bytes | | `GET /v1/model-files/{sha256}` | no credential | Reads a published model's `glb` file | Management endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer crx_live__`; a client key gets `403`. ### Provisioning a scene ``` PUT /v1/scenes Authorization: Bearer crx_live__ Content-Type: application/json { "plugin_id": "package-ride", "module_id": "package-ride.presence", "key": "istanbul-1", "capacity": 200 } ``` ```json { "scene_id": "…", "plugin_id": "package-ride", "module_id": "package-ride.presence", "key": "istanbul-1", "partition_id": "…", "capacity": 200, "state": "open", "created": true } ``` - If the scene does not exist, it is written (`201`, `created: true`); if it exists, it is returned **unchanged** (`200`, `created: false`). `Idempotency-Key` is not needed. - `400`: the ID, key or capacity is invalid (body errors are `400` too). `403`: a client key. `409`: a scene with a different ID on the same key. `422`: the plugin is not enabled in this environment. For a plugin's real-time modules and the player-side flow, see [Realtime: overview](../realtime/overview.md) and [Plugins](../plugins/overview.md). ### Uploading an image ``` PUT /v1/assets Authorization: Bearer crx_live__ Content-Type: image/png ``` ```json { "sha256": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08", "contentType": "image/png", "byteSize": 18234, "created": true } ``` `201` with `created: true` is the first write; if the same bytes already exist, `200` and `created: false` are returned and the row does not change, so the upload is idempotent. An empty body, an unrecognized type, a size over 2 MiB or a width/height over 4096 pixels is rejected with `400` (error codes `asset_empty`, `asset_unsupported_type`, `asset_too_large`, `asset_dimensions_too_large`). To show the image in the game, use ``: the endpoint is **unauthenticated**, and it takes the environment from the `x-crx-env` header or (for ``/texture loaders that cannot send headers) from the `env` query parameter. The response carries the `sha256` as its `ETag` and can be cached indefinitely (`immutable`); if `If-None-Match` matches, `304` is returned. A new image means a new `sha256`, that is a new address. > [!NOTE] > The image and model read endpoints send cross-origin readable response headers so that a browser's texture loader can use them. The other public endpoints grant CORS only to origins in the environment's domain list; see [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md). > [!WARNING] > `DELETE /v1/assets/{sha256}` deletes only the row; the store does not know whether other records (a product, an icon, content) refer to this image. Make sure the image is unused before deleting it. ### Bringing a 3D model into the game Upload and publish the model in the panel and bind it to an item or a character. The game reads the model's address and computed facts (triangle count, bones, clips, bounding box) **from the catalog**; `model.glb.url` has the form `/v1/model-files/?env=`. Details: [Content groups › Catalog](content-groups.md#catalog-items-and-characters) and [Game catalog integration](../../../oyun-katalog-entegrasyonu.md) (Turkish). `GET /v1/model-files/{sha256}` is unauthenticated and content-addressed: - The environment is given with the `x-crx-env` header or the `env` query; if both are given and differ, or neither is present, `400`. - Only the `glb` file of a model that is ready, whose files are retained and which is not deleted is returned; `404` for a deleted model. - A matching `If-None-Match` gives `304` without opening the file. A `200` response carries `Content-Length`, the `model/gltf-binary` type and indefinite cache headers. `Range` is not supported. - The same `sha256` is always the same bytes: cache the file by `sha256` and do not download it again. > [!NOTE] > Model upload and publishing are done only from the panel; there is no public write endpoint for models. The Unity SDK has no catalog and model read helpers; use raw REST. ## Versioning and replay safety - `PUT /v1/scenes` and `PUT /v1/assets` are naturally idempotent (a derived ID, a content address); they do not ask for `Idempotency-Key`. - A model file and an image are content-addressed: the same address never gives different bytes. - Model versions are tracked in the panel; the game always sees the current published version from the catalog. ## Events These surfaces produce no webhook events. A model change is reflected in the catalog as a new `sha256`; poll with `ETag`. ## Limits - An image is at most 2 MiB and 4096×4096 pixels; only PNG, JPEG, WebP. - Scene `key` is at most 96 characters, `capacity` at most 10,000. - The model default limits are above (50 MiB, 1 GiB quota, 200 models, 20 versions). - The `GET /v1/assets` page size is at most 200 (default 50). ## Common errors | Symptom | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | `422` (scene) | The plugin is not enabled in this environment | Enable the plugin ([Plugins](../panel/plugins.md)) | | `409` (scene) | A scene with a different ID on the same key | Change the key | | `400` (image) | The type was not recognized, or 2 MiB or 4096 pixels was exceeded | Upload PNG/JPEG/WebP under 2 MiB and 4096 pixels | | `` does not load | `env` or `x-crx-env` is missing | Add `?env=` to the address | | `404` (model file) | The model was deleted or is not ready yet | Check the `model` field in the catalog | | The model is `failed` in the panel | A conversion error | Fix the file according to the reason the panel shows | ## Working example Uploading and reading an image: ``` curl -X PUT "$API/v1/assets" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: image/png" \ --data-binary @banner.png curl "$API/v1/assets/?env=$ENV" -o banner.png ``` ## Related pages - [Content groups](content-groups.md) · [Inventory and items](inventory-items.md) · [Store and IAP](store-iap.md) - [Realtime: overview](../realtime/overview.md) · [Plugins](../plugins/overview.md)

docs.title: Clans and parties
docs.description: Describes the clan and party model, membership flows, the clan treasury, party reward distribution and server calls.
headings: Where it lives in the panel
docs.body:
# Clans and parties

This page describes how to set up and manage persistent player communities (clans) and temporary teams (parties) in Open Play. Read it if you want to manage membership, invites, the clan treasury, clan XP and party reward distribution from a trusted server.

## What it does

The social module (`social`) manages two structures:

- **Clan:** A persistent community. It has leader, officer and member roles, an invite and application flow, a shared treasury (a currency) and XP/level.
- **Party:** A temporary team. It has a capacity, a loot rule and reward splitting; it ends when it disbands.

**Important:** All of these endpoints are called with a **server key**. A player client cannot call a clan or party endpoint directly; the player's identity is written in the request body (as `actor_player_id` and similar) by your trusted server. Verifying that a player "can manage their own clan" is your server's job; Open Play enforces the role rules inside the clan (who can kick whom, who can withdraw from the treasury).

If the module is disabled, the endpoints return `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"social"}`. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| List clans; see membership, invites, applications, the vault and command history | [Clans](../panel/clans.md) |
| See parties, their members, the loot rule and reward distributions | [Parties](../panel/parties.md) |
| Clan and party chat | [Chat](chat.md), [City chat](../panel/scene-chat.md) |
| The currency used in the clan treasury | [Currencies](../panel/currencies.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source.

## Data model (in plain words)

**Clan**

- `name` (3–64 characters), `tag` (2–8 characters), `leader_player_id`, `xp`, `highest_level_reached`, `state` (`active` or `disbanded`) and `members`.
- **Roles:** `leader`, `officer`, `member`.
- **Environment settings** (`/v1/clan-settings`): `max_members` (the member limit), `request_ttl_seconds` (the lifetime of invites and applications), `officer_can_withdraw` (whether an officer can withdraw from the treasury) and `level_curve_key` (the [level curve](characters.md) for the clan level).
- **Invite:** A call the clan sends to a player. Its statuses are `pending`, `accepted`, `declined`, `revoked`, `expired`.
- **Application:** A player's application to a clan. Its statuses are `pending`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `expired`.
- **Treasury:** The clan's wallet; currency movement is done with `deposit` and `withdraw` and appears in the [ledger](economy.md) as `clan_treasury`.

**Party**

- `leader_player_id`, `capacity` (positive), `loot_rule` (`equal`: equal shares, `weighted`: basis-point shares), `state` (`active`, `disbanded`) and `members`.
- **Invite:** Carries `share_bp` (the member's basis-point share; under the `weighted` rule the shares must add up to exactly 10000) and is valid for 24 hours. Its statuses are `pending`, `accepted`, `expired`.
- **Reward distribution:** Splits a single currency amount among the members. With equal distribution the leftover minor units are distributed in `player_id` order; the result is always deterministic. The distribution record carries the member snapshot, the legs, `delivery_mode` (`inline` or `outbox`) and the status (`processing`, `queued`, `completed`).

## Calls your game makes

All with a server (or admin) key:

```
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

A client key and a player session are rejected (`403`).

### Clan

| Method and path | Body | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/clan-settings`, `PATCH /v1/clan-settings` | `max_members`, `request_ttl_seconds`, `officer_can_withdraw`, `level_curve_key` | Reads / updates the environment settings |
| `GET /v1/clans` | — | Lists clans |
| `POST /v1/clans` | `leader_player_id`, `name`, `tag` | Creates a clan |
| `GET /v1/clans/{clan_id}` | — | Reads a clan with its members |
| `PATCH /v1/clans/{clan_id}` | `actor_player_id`, `name`, `tag` | Updates the name and tag |
| `POST /v1/clans/{clan_id}/invites` | `inviter_player_id`, `invitee_player_id` | Sends an invite |
| `GET /v1/clan-invites/{invite_id}`, `POST …/respond` | `actor_player_id`, `decision` (`accept`, `decline`, `revoke`, `expire`) | Reads / responds to an invite |
| `POST /v1/clans/{clan_id}/applications` | `applicant_player_id` | Opens an application |
| `GET /v1/clan-applications/{application_id}`, `POST …/resolve` | `actor_player_id`, `decision` (`accept`, `reject`, `cancel`, `expire`) | Reads / resolves an application |
| `POST /v1/clans/{clan_id}/leave` | `actor_player_id` | A member leaves |
| `POST /v1/clans/{clan_id}/members/kick` | `actor_player_id`, `target_player_id` | Removes a member |
| `POST /v1/clans/{clan_id}/members/role` | `actor_player_id`, `target_player_id`, `role` | Changes a role |
| `POST /v1/clans/{clan_id}/leadership` | `actor_player_id`, `target_player_id` | Transfers leadership |
| `POST /v1/clans/{clan_id}/disband` | `actor_player_id` | Disbands the clan |
| `POST /v1/clans/{clan_id}/treasury/deposit`, `…/withdraw` | `actor_player_id`, `currency_id`, `amount` | Deposits to / withdraws from the treasury |
| `POST /v1/clans/{clan_id}/xp` | `amount` | Adds XP to the clan |

`Idempotency-Key` is **required** on all clan write commands. The response is always in the same envelope: `{ "type": "clan" | "invite" | "application" | "settings" | "treasury" | "xp", "<kind>": { … }, "replayed": false }`. For example, creating a clan:

```
POST /v1/clans
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Idempotency-Key: create-clan-player-1234
Content-Type: application/json

{ "leader_player_id": "0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f", "name": "Wolf Pack", "tag": "WLF" }
```

Returns `201` and the clan record comes inside a `type: "clan"` envelope. The TypeScript SDK exposes these endpoints in a typed way (`createClan`, `getClan`, `createClanInvite`, `respondClanInvite`, `depositClanTreasury`, `addClanXp` …); see [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md).

### Party

| Method and path | Body | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/parties` | `leader_player_id`, `capacity`, `loot_rule` | Creates a party |
| `GET /v1/parties?player_id=` | — | Lists a player's parties |
| `GET /v1/parties/{party_id}` | — | Reads a party with its members |
| `PATCH /v1/parties/{party_id}` | `actor_player_id`, `capacity` | Updates the capacity |
| `POST /v1/parties/{party_id}/invites` | `inviter_player_id`, `invitee_player_id`, `share_bp` | Sends an invite |
| `POST /v1/party-invites/{invite_id}/accept` | `actor_player_id` | Accepts an invite |
| `POST /v1/parties/{party_id}/leave` | `actor_player_id` | A member leaves |
| `POST /v1/parties/{party_id}/disband` | `actor_player_id` | Disbands the party |
| `POST /v1/parties/{party_id}/rewards` | `currency_key`, `amount` | Splits a reward among the members |

`Idempotency-Key` is **required** on party reward distribution; the same key returns the same distribution again with `replayed: true` and does not distribute a second time. The other party commands do not ask for `Idempotency-Key`.

> [!NOTE]
> The TypeScript SDK has no typed client for the party endpoints; call them with raw REST.

## Versioning and replay safety

- Clan commands and party reward distribution ask for `Idempotency-Key`: the same key and the same body do not run again (`replayed: true`); the same key with a different body is `422`; the same key in flight is `409`.
- `If-Match` is not used in this module.
- General rules: [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md).

## Events

Clan and party events (`ClanMemberJoined`, `ClanXpAdded`, `PartyMemberJoined`, `RewardDistributed` …) can be used in rule automation and quest objectives. **Among the types you can select as a webhook filter there is no clan or party event**; endpoints registered without a filter receive all events and clan/party events are included, but the envelope format is not a documented contract. Selectable types: [Webhook events](../reference/webhook-events.md).

## Limits

- A clan name is 3–64 characters, its tag 2–8 characters.
- A party capacity must be positive; exceeding the capacity is rejected. A party invite is valid for 24 hours.
- The clan member limit and the invite/application lifetime are in the environment settings.
- In a party reward the `weighted` shares must add up to 10000; `amount` must be positive.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `403` | A call with a player session or a client key; or the `actor_player_id` has no permission for this operation inside the clan (for example a member cannot kick another member) | Make the call with a server key; check the role of `actor_player_id` |
| `400` | `Idempotency-Key` is missing; the clan name/tag violates the length or character rule; XP or an amount is not positive; the party capacity is not positive | Fix the input |
| `409` | A clan with the same name or tag exists; the player is already in another active clan/party; a pending invite or application already exists; the same key is in flight | Read the conflicting record and leave the decision to the game |
| `422` | Party capacity/share rules (capacity exceeded, `weighted` share total is not 10000, a duplicate player) or the same key with a different body | Fix the input; use a new key |
| `404` | The clan, invite or party does not exist | Verify the IDs with `GET` |

## Working example

Creating a clan and sending an invite in TypeScript (with the SDK's typed clan client):

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/social-clan-server.ts -->
```ts
/** Güvenilir backend örneği: klan kurar ve bir oyuncuya davet gönderir. Server anahtarı yalnız sunucuda durur. */
import { CrxClient } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";

/** Lider için klan kurar, ardından davet gönderir; her yazma kendi `Idempotency-Key`'iyle tekrar güvenlidir. */
export async function foundClanAndInvite(baseUrl: string, serverApiKey: string, leaderId: string, friendId: string): Promise<string> {
  const crx = new CrxClient({ baseUrl, apiKey: serverApiKey });
  const created = await crx.createClan({
    body: { leader_player_id: leaderId, name: "Kurt Sürüsü", tag: "KRT" },
    headers: { "Idempotency-Key": `clan-kur-${leaderId}` },
  });
  if (created.type !== "clan") throw new Error("Beklenmeyen yanıt zarfı");
  await crx.createClanInvite({
    path: { clan_id: created.clan.id },
    body: { inviter_player_id: leaderId, invitee_player_id: friendId },
    headers: { "Idempotency-Key": `davet-${created.clan.id}-${friendId}` },
  });
  return created.clan.id;
}
```

## Related pages

- [Chat](chat.md) · [Economy](economy.md) · [Characters](characters.md) · [Game rules](game-rules.md)
- [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md) · [Errors](../reference/errors.md)

docs.description: Describes the store showcase, a player's purchase with their own session, the server-side reservation flow and in-app purchase (IAP) verification.
headings: Where it lives in the panel
docs.body:
# Store and in-app purchases

This page describes the store showcase the player sees, the flow of buying with game money and the verification of in-app purchases (IAP) made with real money. Read it if you want to build a showcase, sell products and complete payment safely on the server.

## What it does

The store module (`store`) ties three things together:

- **Showcase (page) and product (listing):** The catalog an operator sets up in the panel and that is shown to the player.
- **Payment:** A product is sold either with **game money** (`currency`: through a merchant, money in exchange for an item) or with **real money** (`iap`: an App Store or Google Play receipt).
- **Reservation:** A purchase first reserves an entitlement (stock and the per-player limit), then completes the payment in one transaction. Payment and delivery either both happen or neither does.

If the module is disabled, the endpoints return `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"store"}`. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| Create showcases and products; set price, stock, visibility window and per-player limit | [Store](../panel/store.md), [Product](../panel/store-product.md) |
| Define the currency for a price | [Currencies](../panel/currencies.md) |
| Define the item to be sold | [Content](../panel/content.md) |

In the panel, IAP products and receipts are **only listed**. For attaching an IAP product to the store and for the platform credentials (App Store / Google Play), see [Limits and known limitations](#limits-and-known-limitations).

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Showcase (page):** `key` (lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `-`; at most 64), `title`, `sort_order` and visibility. Showcase fields such as the description, the banner image, the product title, the badge and the image are entered in the panel; the server-key REST draft does not carry them.
- **Product (listing):** Attached to a showcase. The payment form is `currency` (merchant + item definition + currency + `price_amount`) or `iap` (an IAP product ID). `limit_per_player` (at least 1) is the lifetime per-player quantity limit.
- **Visibility:** `active`, a date window (`starts_at`/`ends_at`, Unix ms) and an optional CEL `visibility_rule` (a player-specific condition; compiled at registration, at most 8192 bytes). The player showcase is recomputed on **every read**: the condition, the time and the remaining limit are evaluated against the state at that moment.
- **Catalog version (`version`):** Every change made to a showcase increases the catalog version; on management commands `If-Match` is this version.
- **Product version:** The `version` field of the product the player sees; it is sent back as `expected_version` on purchase.
- **Reservation:** Its status is `reserved`, `processing`, `completed`, `cancelled`. `reserved` and `processing` **do not count as payment**.
- **Price:** An integer in the smallest unit; it comes with `display_decimals` (0–4) in the showcase. Build the display with integer/string operations; do not convert it to a decimal number.

## Calls your game makes

There are two credential types:

- **Player session** (cookie or session token + `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>`): reads the showcase and buys on its own behalf. With a cookie session, mutations require the CSRF double-submit (`x-csrf-token`) and the `Origin` check; see [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md).
- **Server key** (`Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`): catalog management, player preview, reservation and payment completion.

| Method and path | Credential | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/store/pages[?page=<key>&at=now]` | player session | The showcases the player can see; `page` narrows to one showcase |
| `POST /v1/player/store/listings/{listing_id}/buy` | player session | The player buys on their own behalf |
| `GET /v1/store/catalog` | server key | The raw management catalog (visibility is not filtered) |
| `GET /v1/store/preview/{player_id}[?at=now]` | server key | Previews the showcase a player would see |
| `POST /v1/store/pages`, `PUT/DELETE /v1/store/pages/{id}`, `POST /v1/store/pages/reorder` | server key | Showcase management |
| `POST /v1/store/pages/{page_id}/listings`, `PUT/DELETE /v1/store/listings/{id}`, `POST …/listings/reorder` | server key | Product management |
| `POST /v1/store/listings/{listing_id}/reserve` | server key | Reserves an entitlement for a player (not a payment) |
| `POST /v1/store/reservations/{id}/checkout/currency` | server key | Completes payment with game money |
| `POST /v1/store/reservations/{id}/checkout/iap` | server key | Completes payment with a verified IAP |
| `POST /v1/store/reservations/{id}/cancel` | server key | Cancels a `reserved` reservation (not a refund) |
| `POST /v1/iap/verify` | API key | Verifies an IAP receipt and grants the reward |
| `POST /v1/webhooks/iap/{platform}/{environment_id}` | no key (signature) | Receives the platform's refund notification |

Error envelopes: errors from the management and reservation endpoints are `text/plain`; the player purchase endpoint returns JSON with a typed `code` (below). General list: [Errors](../reference/errors.md).

### Reading the showcase

```
GET /v1/store/pages?page=garage
x-crx-env: 0192f000-0000-7000-8000-00000000e001
```

```json
{
  "version": 12,
  "pages": [
    {
      "id": "…", "key": "garage", "title": "Garage",
      "listings": [
        {
          "id": "0192f111-…", "version": 3,
          "title": "Fast Car", "badge": "sale",
          "price": { "currency_key": "gold", "currency_name": "Gold", "amount": 1250, "display_decimals": 0, "icon_url": null },
          "item": { "key": "fast_car", "name": "Fast Car" },
          "remaining": 40
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The response carries `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. A `page` key that is not visible or unknown returns `404`. The player identity, the time and the CEL result are **not taken from the client**; adding `player_id` or any other field to the query returns `400`.

### A player's purchase

```
POST /v1/player/store/listings/0192f111-…/buy
x-crx-env: 0192f000-0000-7000-8000-00000000e001
x-csrf-token: <csrf>
Idempotency-Key: buy-player-1234-0001
Content-Type: application/json

{ "quantity": 1, "expected_version": 3 }
```

```json
{
  "reservation_id": "…",
  "payment_reference": "…",
  "item_instance_ids": ["…"],
  "balance_after": 750,
  "replayed": false
}
```

The body contains only `quantity` (positive) and `expected_version`; **a player ID, a price or a payment claim is not accepted**, and an unknown field returns `400`. The identity comes from the session. Reservation and charging are **in a single transaction**. `Idempotency-Key` is required: the same key and the same body repeat the durable result with `replayed: true` and make no second charge; the same key with a different body is `422`. An IAP product cannot be bought on this endpoint (`422`).

Rejected purchases carry a typed JSON code, `{"code": "...", "message": "..."}`:

| `code` | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `not_visible` | 404 | The product is not visible to this player or does not exist |
| `listing_changed` | 409 | The product changed while you were looking (`expected_version` is stale); refresh the showcase |
| `out_of_stock` | 422 | Out of stock |
| `limit_reached` | 422 | The per-player limit is full |
| `insufficient_funds` | 422 | The balance is insufficient |
| `inventory_full` | 422 | The inventory is full; the operation is rolled back completely |

Other errors (`401`, `403` CSRF/Origin, `400`, `429` budget, `500`) follow the general rules.

### Server-side flow: reservation and payment

In cases where the game server manages the payment (for example, when your server receives the real-money receipt), use two steps:

```
POST /v1/store/listings/{listing_id}/reserve
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Idempotency-Key: reserve-player-1234-0001
If-Match: 12
Content-Type: application/json

{ "player_id": "0192f0f2-…", "quantity": 1 }
```

The response has the form `{ catalog_version, entity_id, event_id, event, reservation, replayed }`; `reservation.status` is `reserved`. Then:

```
POST /v1/store/reservations/{id}/checkout/currency
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "player_id": "0192f0f2-…" }
```

```json
{ "reservation_id": "…", "payment_reference": "…", "kind": "currency", "replayed": false }
```

`Idempotency-Key` and `If-Match` are **not sent** on the `checkout` endpoints (`400` if sent); the durable reservation ID is the anchor of replay safety. If there is an error when paying with a currency, the operation is rolled back and the reservation stays `reserved`; you can retry or cancel. If the outcome of an IAP payment is uncertain, the reservation becomes `processing` and the player limit is preserved; retry **with the same `credential`**. In an IAP payment `quantity` is 1.

`Idempotency-Key` is required on `reserve` and the catalog management commands; `If-Match` is the catalog version and is optional (a mismatch is `409`). A failed command does not burn the key.

### IAP verification

```
POST /v1/iap/verify
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Idempotency-Key: iap-player-1234-tx-abc
Content-Type: application/json

{ "platform": "app_store", "product_sku": "gems_500", "credential": "<transactionId>", "player_id": "0192f0f2-…" }
```

```json
{ "receipt_id": "…", "status": "granted", "product_sku": "gems_500", "transaction_id": "…", "grants": [ … ], "replayed": false }
```

- `platform`: `app_store` or `google_play`. `credential`: the `transactionId` for the App Store, the `purchaseToken` for Google Play. The server queries the platform **itself**; the client is not trusted.
- Verifying the same transaction twice does **not** grant a second reward (`200`, `replayed: true`).
- `status` can be `verified`, `granted`, `revoked` or `failed`; the happy path is `granted`.
- Errors: a forged receipt `403`; the product is not in the catalog or the transaction is not recognized on the platform `404`; a `product_sku` mismatch, a platform that is not configured or a supply cap overrun `422`; another request in flight with the same key `409`.
- Refund notification: App Store (ASN V2) and Google Play (RTDN) notifications arrive at `POST /v1/webhooks/iap/{platform}/{environment_id}`; the endpoint is keyless and authentication is the signature. On a refund of a known receipt the reward is taken back **with reversing entries** and the receipt becomes `revoked`; cases that can only be partially reversed are marked `flagged` (the default policy; it does not touch the consumed part). Non-refund notifications and unknown transactions get `200` and are ignored.

## Versioning and replay safety

- Player purchase: `expected_version` (the product version) + `Idempotency-Key`.
- Catalog management and reservation: `Idempotency-Key` required, `If-Match` = the catalog version.
- Payment completion: the durable reservation ID; no header.
- General rules: [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md).

## Events and webhooks

Store events can be delivered as webhooks: `store_page_created`, `store_page_updated`, `store_page_deleted`, `store_pages_reordered`, `store_listing_created`, `store_listing_updated`, `store_listing_deleted`, `store_listings_reordered`, `store_purchase_initiated`, `store_payment_started`, `store_purchase_completed`, `store_reservation_cancelled`. The envelope contains `event_id`, `environment_id`, `type`, `seq`, `now_ms`, `actor_api_key_id` and `data`. Registration and verification: [Webhooks](webhooks.md).

## Limits and known limitations

- A showcase key is `^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`; at most 2000 entries in a reorder request.
- An IAP product is not supported on the player purchase endpoint; IAP products are bought with `checkout/iap` or `iap/verify`.
- **IAP product registration:** In the panel, IAP products and receipts are read-only, and there is no public HTTP endpoint yet to save a product. For now, adding an IAP product is done through the Open Play operator.
- **Platform credentials:** The App Store and Google Play verification credentials are defined by the operator at deployment. If they are not defined, `iap/verify` and `checkout/iap` return `422`.
- Read the showcase when the player opens or refreshes it; changes are recomputed at read time.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `409 listing_changed` | The product version you read in the showcase went stale | Re-read the showcase and try with the new `version` |
| `404 not_visible` | The product is not visible to the player (window, condition, inactive) | Refresh the showcase; check the condition in the panel |
| `422 insufficient_funds` | The balance is insufficient | Show the balance; give money through a reward or IAP |
| `400` (unknown field) | An extra field was added to the purchase body | Send only `quantity` and `expected_version` |
| `400` (checkout) | `Idempotency-Key`/`If-Match` was sent | Remove these headers on the checkout endpoints |
| `403` (purchase) | The CSRF pair or the `Origin` was rejected | Refresh the CSRF token; see [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md) |
| `403` (iap/verify) | A forged receipt or one with an invalid signature | Get the receipt again from the platform |
| `422` (iap) | The platform is not configured or `product_sku` does not match | Contact the operator; check the sku |

## Working example

An example that reads the showcase and buys the first product is on the [Economy](economy.md#working-example-grant-money-then-buy-a-product) page; it shows a separate message per error code (`storeBuyErrorCode`). The TypeScript SDK provides the `player.store.catalog()` and `player.store.buy()` helpers; if `Idempotency-Key` is not given, it generates one per call, and after a network interruption you must supply the same key yourself.

## Related pages

- [Economy](economy.md) · [Inventory and items](inventory-items.md) · [Rewards](rewards.md) · [Webhooks](webhooks.md)
- [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md) · [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)

docs.body:
# Webhooks

This page describes how Open Play forwards game events to your own server with an HTTP POST: endpoint registration, event types, signature verification, retries and coping with repeated deliveries. Read it if you want to trigger your own backend system on a character, store or reward event.

## What it does

When an event occurs (for example `level_up`, `store_purchase_completed`, `reward_granted`), Open Play sends a signed POST to your registered endpoints. Delivery is **at-least-once**: the same event can arrive more than once because of network errors, so your receiver must drop repeats using `X-Crx-Event-Id`.

If the module is disabled, the endpoints return `404` with `{"code":"module_disabled","module":"webhooks"}`. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| See registered endpoints, delivery attempts, failed (DLQ) deliveries and the event queue | [Webhooks and event queue](../panel/webhooks.md) |
| Enable the module | [Game settings › Modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md) |

The panel is **read-only** on this page: endpoint registration is done with REST; there is no button in the panel to resend or to rescue a failed delivery. The panel does not show secrets, the raw body or the raw error text.

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source.

## Data model (in plain words)

- **Endpoint:** `url`, an optional `event_types` filter, `enabled` and `created_at`.
- **Secret:** Generated by the server (`whsec_` + 64 lowercase hex characters), returned **once** only in the registration response and stored encrypted. No endpoint gives it again afterwards. There is no endpoint to rotate the secret: to renew it, delete the endpoint and register it again.
- **Event envelope:** The JSON body that is sent. Every envelope contains `event_id`, `type`, `environment_id` and `data`.
- **Delivery:** The sending of one event to one endpoint. Its statuses are pending, delivered and failed (DLQ).

### Selectable event types

If `event_types` is empty, the endpoint receives **all** events (see the note below). If it is non-empty, you can choose only from these types:

| Area | Types |
|---|---|
| Character | `flag_set`, `attribute_set`, `resource_changed`, `modifier_added`, `modifiers_removed`, `xp_added`, `level_up`, `ability_unlocked`, `event_emitted`, `character_rolled_back` |
| Store | `store_page_created`, `store_page_updated`, `store_page_deleted`, `store_pages_reordered`, `store_listing_created`, `store_listing_updated`, `store_listing_deleted`, `store_listings_reordered`, `store_purchase_initiated`, `store_payment_started`, `store_purchase_completed`, `store_reservation_cancelled` |
| Reward | `reward_granted` |

An unknown type returns `400`. Full list and data fields: [Webhook events](../reference/webhook-events.md).

> [!WARNING]
> If you leave the filter **empty**, the endpoint is not limited to the list above: it receives all events written to the outbox (such as item, wallet, clan, party, score and notification queue events). The envelope format of these extra events is not a documented contract and may change without notice. In production, always give the `event_types` filter explicitly.

### Envelope format

Character events:

```json
{
  "event_id": "0192f500-1111-7222-8333-944455556666",
  "type": "level_up",
  "character_id": "0192f0f2-5b1a-7c3e-9d11-4a5b6c7d8e9f",
  "environment_id": "0192f000-0000-7000-8000-00000000e001",
  "seq": 12,
  "data": { "...": "event-specific fields" }
}
```

Store events have no `character_id`; together with `seq` they carry `now_ms` (the moment the event was processed) and `actor_api_key_id`. The `reward_granted` event has `player_id`, and `data` contains `source_kind`, `table_key`, `table_version` and what was granted; **the draw seed is in no event.**

## Calls your game makes

All management endpoints are called with a **server key**; a client key gets `403`:

```
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

| Method and path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/webhooks` | Registers an endpoint (`201`; the secret only here) |
| `GET /v1/webhooks` | Lists endpoints (`cursor`, `limit` 1–200, default 50) |
| `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}` | Reads a single endpoint (without the secret) |
| `DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id}` | Deletes an endpoint (soft delete, `204`) |

The TypeScript SDK exposes these four endpoints in a typed way: `createWebhook`, `listWebhooks`, `getWebhook`, `deleteWebhook` (see [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md)).

### Registering an endpoint

```
POST /v1/webhooks
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "url": "https://hooks.example-game.com/open-play",
  "event_types": ["level_up", "store_purchase_completed"]
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "0192f600-…",
  "url": "https://hooks.example-game.com/open-play",
  "event_types": ["level_up", "store_purchase_completed"],
  "enabled": true,
  "created_at": "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z",
  "secret": "whsec_<64 hex characters>"
}
```

Write the `secret` value to a safe place (a secrets management service) right away; it cannot be read again.

Registration rules:

- The URL must be `https`; it must not carry user information (`user:password@`); it must not contain non-letter control characters or whitespace. Loopback, private and link-local **IP addresses** are rejected at registration (`400`).
- In addition, on every send the IP that the name resolves to is re-checked; a name that resolves to a private or loopback address cannot be sent to. Redirects are **not followed**.
- A second registration while the same URL is active returns `409`.

## Delivery

For every event, this request arrives at your endpoint:

```
POST /open-play
Content-Type: application/json
X-Crx-Signature: t=1790000000,v1=9c1f…e2
X-Crx-Event-Id: 0192f500-1111-7222-8333-944455556666
X-Crx-Event-Type: level_up

{ …envelope… }
```

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-Crx-Signature` | `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>` |
| `X-Crx-Event-Id` | The event ID; your dedup key |
| `X-Crx-Event-Type` | The `type` value in the envelope |

### Verifying the signature

The signature is the HMAC-SHA256 digest (lowercase hex) of the text `"{t}.{raw body}"`, computed with **the whole secret returned at registration** (with the `whsec_…` prefix) as the key. Verification steps:

1. Separate the `t` and `v1` values from the `X-Crx-Signature` header.
2. Take the **raw** body bytes. Do not parse the JSON and re-serialize it; the signature is for the exact bytes on the wire.
3. Compute `HMAC-SHA256(secret, t + "." + raw_body)` and compare it with `v1` in **constant time**.
4. Compare `t` with your own clock; reject requests that are too old (for example older than 5 minutes). `t` is refreshed on every retry, so a genuine retry stays within this window.
5. If `X-Crx-Event-Id` has already been processed, return `2xx` without repeating the work.

### Response and retry rules

- Only **`2xx`** is success. Every other response, a timeout and a connection error trigger a retry.
- 5 seconds are waited for the connection and 10 seconds in total, including DNS.
- If the body exceeds 64 KB, it is not sent and counts as an error.
- The delay is `min(1 s × 2^attempt, 5 min)` and includes ±20% randomness. At most **10 attempts** are made; after the 10th failed attempt the delivery is moved to the failed (DLQ) state and is not repeated automatically.
- When you delete the endpoint, pending deliveries are also moved to the failed state.
- There is **no** ordering guarantee: events can be ordered with `seq` for a character, but the delivery order can change.
- Events that occur while there is no endpoint are not sent afterwards; there is no retroactive delivery.

## Versioning and replay safety

- Receiver side: dedup with `X-Crx-Event-Id` is mandatory. The same event arrives on a retry with the **same** `event_id`; the signature time (`t`) is refreshed.
- The registration endpoint has no `Idempotency-Key`; registering the same URL a second time returns `409`.
- There is no event version field in the envelope; ignore fields you do not recognize and do not reject the body with a strict schema.

## Limits

- Body 64 KB; total wait 10 seconds; 10 attempts.
- `limit` on the list endpoint is 1–200.
- Redirects are not followed; `https` only.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `400` on registration | The URL is not `https`, is an IP address, has user information, or an unknown event type | Fix the URL and `event_types` values |
| `403` on registration | A client key | Use a server key |
| `409` on registration | The same URL is already active | Delete or use the existing one |
| The signature does not verify | The body was re-serialized; the `whsec_` prefix of the secret was dropped; clock skew | Compute with the raw bytes and the whole secret |
| The same event arrives twice | At-least-once delivery | Drop it with `X-Crx-Event-Id` |
| Deliveries stopped | The 10 attempts were used up (DLQ) or the endpoint was deleted | Fix the receiver; for missed events, read from your own source |
| No delivery ever arrives | The endpoint name resolves to a private/loopback IP, or the response exceeds 10 seconds | Use a public address; respond quickly |

## Working example: a receiver with Node

The server below verifies the signature, drops a repeated event and returns `2xx`. The secret comes from an environment variable; in production, do the dedup with a durable store.

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/webhook-receiver.ts -->
```ts
/** Webhook alıcısı (Node 22): imzayı doğrular, tekrar eden teslimatı `X-Crx-Event-Id` ile eler. */
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
import { createServer } from "node:http";

const SECRET = process.env["OPEN_PLAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET"] ?? ""; // uç noktayı kaydederken bir kez dönen sır
const TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 300; // eski teslimatı (replay) reddetme penceresi: alıcının kendi politikası
const seen = new Set<string>(); // örnek amaçlı bellek; üretimde kalıcı depo kullanın

/** `X-Crx-Signature: t=<unix-sn>,v1=<hex>` değerini ham gövdeye karşı doğrular. */
export function verifySignature(secret: string, header: string, rawBody: Buffer, nowSeconds: number): boolean {
  const parts = new Map(header.split(",").map((part) => part.split("=", 2) as [string, string]));
  const t = parts.get("t");
  const v1 = parts.get("v1");
  if (t === undefined || v1 === undefined) return false;
  if (Math.abs(nowSeconds - Number(t)) > TOLERANCE_SECONDS) return false;
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.`).update(rawBody).digest("hex");
  const a = Buffer.from(expected, "utf8");
  const b = Buffer.from(v1, "utf8");
  return a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b);
}

createServer((req, res) => {
  const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
  req.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => chunks.push(chunk));
  req.on("end", () => {
    const rawBody = Buffer.concat(chunks); // imza ham bayt üzerindendir: JSON'u yeniden serileştirmeyin
    const signature = req.headers["x-crx-signature"];
    if (typeof signature !== "string" || !verifySignature(SECRET, signature, rawBody, Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000))) {
      res.writeHead(401).end();
      return;
    }
    const eventId = String(req.headers["x-crx-event-id"] ?? "");
    if (!seen.has(eventId)) {
      seen.add(eventId);
      const event = JSON.parse(rawBody.toString("utf8")) as { type: string; data: unknown };
      console.log("olay", event.type, event.data);
    }
    res.writeHead(200).end(); // yalnız 2xx başarıdır; başka kod yeniden denemeyi tetikler
  });
}).listen(8080);
```

## Related pages

- [Webhook events](../reference/webhook-events.md) · [Characters](characters.md) · [Store and IAP](store-iap.md) · [Rewards](rewards.md)
- [Security](../operations/security.md) · [Errors](../reference/errors.md)

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.description: The most frequently asked questions during integration and their short answers; key types, CORS, numbers, replay safety, plugins, and realtime.
docs.body:
# Frequently asked questions

This page gathers the questions that come up most often in integration with short answers. For details, go to the linked pages.

## Getting started and topology

**Can I put the server key inside the game?**
No. The server key is only on your server. The game client works with the player session; if you need a key embedded in the client there is a client key, but the endpoints it can call are limited, and on some endpoints there is no key-type gate ([security](security.md), [endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md)).

**Why am I getting a CORS error?**
The server does not send CORS headers to an origin that is not in an environment's domain list (or the operator's global allowed list). Add the domain in the panel; the origin must be exactly `https://<domain>`. If the game is on a different registrable domain than Open Play, the session cookie (`SameSite=Lax`) is not sent; use a same-origin reverse proxy then. Do not add extra CORS headers to your own proxy ([architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md)).

**My game is a mobile app or Unity desktop; do the browser restrictions apply?**
The CORS and same-site rule concerns only the browser. Non-browser clients can use a Bearer session token instead of a cookie; but rules such as the CSRF pair on plugin commands and `Origin` on the realtime ticket request still apply ([calling plugins](../plugins/calling-plugins.md), [protocol](../realtime/protocol.md)). For Unity, see the [Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md).

**Can I use Open Play's gRPC interface?**
It is not supported as a public surface. Game integrations go through REST, WebSocket, and the SDKs.

**Which SDKs are there?**
TypeScript (`@ferdiunal/open-play-ts`) and Unity (`com.openplay.sdk`). For modules that have no typed `CrxClient`, you use raw REST ([endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md)). Details are on the [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md) and [Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md) pages.

## Identity

**How does the server verify who a player is?**
Your game server verifies the access JWT returned at player sign-in offline with the JWKS ([server verification](../auth/server-verification.md)). It is not the session token or the cookie.

**How long does a session live?**
It slides for 30 days (one request a day is enough), and the absolute ceiling is 180 days. An open realtime socket does not keep the session alive ([security](security.md)).

**What happens to a banned player?**
On sign-in endpoints, after ownership is proven, they get `403` and `account_banned`; on other endpoints it looks like `401`. On plugin endpoints `403 forbidden` (`message: account banned`) ([errors](../reference/errors.md)).

## Replay safety, version, numbers

**When is a new `Idempotency-Key` generated?**
For every **new operation**. The same key is used on retries of the same operation; repeating a command with an uncertain outcome with a new key leads to double application ([idempotency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md)).

**I got `409`. Can I repeat the same request?**
There are two different `409`s: on a version conflict (`version conflict`) first re-read the state; on an "in progress" (`idempotent request in progress`) response repeat shortly with the same key.

**Why is the balance a big integer?**
Money is a minor-unit integer; floating point is used nowhere. You compute the display decimals yourself ([numbers and encoding](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md)).

**Why do some numbers come as text?**
Plugin and realtime `int64` fields can exceed the safe range of the JavaScript `number`; so they are carried as decimal text. The TypeScript SDK turns them into `bigint`.

**Why are percentage fields out of 10000?**
Basis points: 10000 = 100% ([numbers and encoding](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md)).

**Why is the error body sometimes plain text and sometimes JSON?**
Core REST returns plain text (a few JSON exceptions), plugin endpoints always return JSON. For the decision, look at the status code and, if present, the `code` field ([errors](../reference/errors.md)).

## Rate limits

**Is there a per-key request limit?**
No; there is no general quota. Certain operations (sign-in, sign-up, chat, plugin commands, socket connection) have limits. In big bulk jobs, apply your own concurrency limit ([rate limits](../reference/rate-limits.md)).

**Hundreds of guests will be opened at the same time at launch. Will it be a problem?**
Opening a guest is 30 per minute per IP. If the players are on separate IPs it is not a problem; but if your reverse proxy does not forward the client IP, they all gather in one bucket. Verify IP forwarding and do a load test ([production checklist](production-checklist.md)).

## Plugins

**Can I upload my own plugin?**
No, not yet. Plugins are trusted code compiled into the server; there is no third-party loading or isolation. Today's paths: rules, webhooks, and your own server ([plugins overview](../plugins/overview.md)).

**The plugin schema changed; will my client break?**
Plugin schemas are pinned by digest (`schemaSha256`). If the server changes the schema, the old binding sees a mismatch and you must regenerate it from the current document ([bindings](../plugins/bindings.md)).

**A plugin call returned `403 forbidden`. Why?**
Mostly the plugin is not enabled in your environment or the grant version does not match the server's; or a CSRF/Origin rejection. Look at the plugin's state in the panel ([Plugins](../panel/plugins.md)).

## Realtime

**What should I do when the socket drops?**
Get a new ticket, reconnect, and rejoin durable streams with the last cursor; if `ResyncRequired` arrives, join without a cursor. The TypeScript SDK does this on its own ([reconnect](../realtime/reconnect-and-limits.md)).

**Why does the socket close every 5 minutes?**
Because no player activity arrived on a subscription that accepts input, the server does an idle close (`4100`). Show a "Continue" screen or send a keep-alive input.

**Can I use a socket for notifications and chat?**
Not directly from the browser: `/v1/ws` and `/v1/chat/ws` require the `x-crx-env` header on the upgrade and the browser cannot add it. In the browser, read the inbox with REST and use the REST endpoints for chat ([realtime overview](../realtime/overview.md)).

## Webhooks

**Can I accept webhooks without a signature?**
No. Verify every request's signature over the raw body and deduplicate with `X-Crx-Event-Id` ([security](security.md)).

**Can I resend an event I missed?**
There is no resend action in the panel; deliveries are only monitored. Make up for it by reading the state of the relevant resource with REST.

## Administration

**I lost the key; can I get it back?**
No; the secret value is shown only at creation time. Generate a new key and revoke the old one ([security](security.md)).

**What can I do in the panel, and what should I do with the API?**
The panel is for managing the game (content, store, economy reports, rules, settings). In-game flows are done with the API and the SDK. For the panel screens, see the relevant [panel help pages](../panel/plugins.md).

**There is something I cannot find in the documentation.**
First look at [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) and the [glossary](../reference/glossary.md); if you cannot find it, send your question with the status code, path, and time information.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.description: A list to tick off under the headings of network, identity, keys, replay safety, realtime, and monitoring before taking your game live with Open Play.
docs.body:
# Production checklist

This page gathers the items you will tick off one by one before going live. Each item comes with a short reason and links to the relevant page. Review the list once before launch and again after every major change.

## 1. Network and hosting

- [ ] **Everything is HTTPS.** Session cookies have the `__Secure-` prefix and carry the `Secure` flag; a session cannot be established over plain HTTP. Sockets are opened with `wss://`. If you use `http://localhost` in local development, verify your browser's `localhost` exception.
- [ ] **Browser call path chosen.** Either the game's domain is in an environment's domain list and the game calls Open Play directly (the server sends CORS headers; the game and Open Play must be subdomains of the same registrable domain, otherwise the `SameSite=Lax` session cookie is not sent), or the game calls the API from under its own domain through a reverse proxy ([architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md)).
- [ ] **The proxy forwards these headers as they are:** `Authorization`, `Cookie` (and `Set-Cookie` in the response), `Origin`, `x-crx-env`, `x-csrf-token`, `Idempotency-Key`, `If-Match`, `x-crx-schema-version`, `Sec-WebSocket-*` (including subprotocol and extension negotiation). It does not strip the response headers (`x-csrf-token`, `Deprecation`, `Retry-After`, `ETag`).
- [ ] **The WebSocket upgrade** is open on the proxy, the `Upgrade`/`Connection` headers are forwarded, and the connection can stay **idle for at least 5 minutes** (the server does the idle close itself: [limits](../realtime/reconnect-and-limits.md)).
