- [ ] **The request body limit is at least 2 MiB.** The server rejects anything above 2 MiB with `413`; your proxy should not set a lower limit.
- [ ] **Timeout:** the proxy's response-header wait time does not cut off long operations (Open Play's own gateway uses 65 s).
- [ ] **The client IP is forwarded.** The rate limits on the identity endpoints depend on the client IP. If the proxy does not add `X-Forwarded-For`, **all players gather in a single bucket** (for example guest opening is 30 per minute). If multiple proxies are chained, the operator must define the trusted proxy blocks.
- [ ] **The panel path is closed to the internet.** The `/v1/panel/*` path returns `404` on the public gateway; the panel is reached only from the management network or from a separate domain.
- [ ] **Caching:** API responses that carry a cookie or `Authorization` are not put in a shared cache (CDN). Only public, content-addressed responses (`/v1/assets/{sha256}`, `/v1/model-files/{sha256}`) and catalog responses that carry an `ETag` are subject to an appropriate caching rule.

## 2. Environments and domains

- [ ] You use **separate environments** for development, staging, and live; data is not shared.
- [ ] Each environment's **domain** is defined in the panel ([Game settings: environments](../panel/game-settings-environments.md)); this is the allowed `Origin` list.
- [ ] The correct environment ID (the `x-crx-env` value) is in the client configuration; the live client does not point to the staging environment.
- [ ] Only the needed **modules are on** ([modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md)). A disabled module returns `404 module_disabled`; every module you leave on is an attack surface.
- [ ] Sign-in methods are configured in the panel (guest, email, Google); the methods you do not use are off ([Sign-in methods](../panel/game-settings-sign-in.md)).

## 3. Keys and secrets

- [ ] **Server keys are only on the server.** They are not in the client bundle, the mobile app, the WebGL build, or the repository ([security](security.md)).
- [ ] A **separate key per environment and service**; the keys have been given an expiry date.
- [ ] If you use a **client key**, you have verified that you know which endpoints it can call; player operations are done with the player session ([endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md)).
- [ ] A **key rotation rehearsal** was done: second key, rollout, revoke the old one.
- [ ] Keys and tokens are not in the logs; `Authorization`, `Cookie`, and `x-csrf-token` are filtered.
- [ ] The webhook secret is in your receiver's secret manager; because it is shown only once at registration, it has a backup.

## 4. Replay safety and concurrency

- [ ] **Every call** that grants money, items, rewards, or sends a command **carries an `Idempotency-Key`**; the key is generated once and used exactly on repeats ([idempotency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md)).
- [ ] On an uncertain outcome (timeout, network drop), the command is completed **with the same key**, not a new one, or with the result query.
- [ ] Calls that write a shared resource send `If-Match`/`expectedVersion`; on `409` the state is re-read.
- [ ] There is exponential backoff + jitter on `429`, `503`, and network errors; `Retry-After` is respected ([rate limits](../reference/rate-limits.md)).
- [ ] Error handling is by **status code**; the plain-text message is not parsed ([errors](../reference/errors.md)).

## 5. Player identity

- [ ] The session-loss flow is set up: session refresh when `401` arrives, otherwise sign in again; a separate screen for a banned account ([sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)).
- [ ] The guest identity's storage behavior and the upgrade flow to email or Google are set up (guest progress is kept with the upgrade).
- [ ] Your game server verifies the access JWT **with the JWKS**, checking the expiry and environment fields ([server verification](../auth/server-verification.md)).
- [ ] The identity rate limits (guest 30/min, email sign-in 5/min, sign-up 10/min, per IP) can carry your expected launch traffic; a load test was done if needed.

## 6. Realtime

- [ ] The client uses the SDK or implements the protocol (ticket, `Origin`, subprotocol) completely ([protocol](../realtime/protocol.md)).
- [ ] **Reconnect:** a new ticket on every connection, exponential backoff, `Join` with the last cursor on durable streams, `Join` without a cursor on `ResyncRequired` ([reconnect](../realtime/reconnect-and-limits.md)).
- [ ] There is a "Continue" screen for **idle close (`4100`)**; a keep-alive input is sent on pause screens.
- [ ] The frame rate is **below 40/s**; the limit of 4 tabs/sockets per player is known.
- [ ] The notification and chat sockets cannot be opened directly from the browser (header restriction); inbox polling or the REST endpoints are used ([realtime overview](../realtime/overview.md)).

## 7. Plugins

- [ ] The **schema digest** (`schemaSha256`) of the plugin you use is written into your release manifest and the bindings were generated with this digest ([bindings](../plugins/bindings.md)).
- [ ] A digest comparison (at startup or in CI) is done after a server update.
- [ ] The plugin's state in the environment is **enabled** ([Plugins](../panel/plugins.md)); this is the first place to look for an unexpected `403 forbidden`.
- [ ] A migration task was opened for calls that carry the `Deprecation` header ([versioning](../reference/versioning.md)).

## 8. Webhooks

- [ ] The endpoint is `https`; **the signature is verified on every request**, the timestamp window is checked, and deduplication is done with `X-Crx-Event-Id` ([security](security.md)).
- [ ] The receiver returns a fast `2xx` (queues the work); there is a monitoring plan for deliveries that end up `failed` (DLQ) after 10 attempts ([Webhooks and event queue](../panel/webhooks.md) offers only monitoring, there is no resend); you have a way to make up for missed events by reading the relevant resource with REST.

## 9. Observability and operations

- [ ] Your request log has the status code, duration, called path, and (on plugin endpoints) `x-request-id`; there are no secret values.
- [ ] You have an alert for the `5xx` and `429` rate; it was verified that `503` + `Retry-After` responses are retried.
- [ ] Panel admin accounts are personal and two-factor authentication is on ([Panel operators](../panel/operators.md)).
- [ ] The [operation history](../panel/audit.md) is reviewed regularly; the [safety switches](../panel/safety-switches.md) are in their default position (if you changed them deliberately, the reason is recorded).
- [ ] The SDK version is pinned **exactly** (no `^`); upgrades are followed from the changelog ([versioning](../reference/versioning.md)).

## 10. Final rehearsal before launch

1. Run the **end-to-end flow** in a staging environment similar to the live one: sign-in, reward, purchase, socket connection, connection drop, and reconnect.
2. Deliberately send the same request twice with the same `Idempotency-Key`; verify that the second response returns the same result.
3. Revoke a server key once and observe the switch to the second key.
4. Send a request with a wrong signature to your webhook receiver; verify that it rejects it.
5. Do a trial on the identity endpoints that imitates your launch traffic; look at the `429` rate.

If problems come up, see the [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) page.

docs.title: Security
docs.description: A security guide for API key management and rotation, player sessions and CSRF, CORS and the same-origin rule, and webhook signature verification.
headings: 5. What not to write to logs
docs.body:
# Security

This page gathers what you need to know to operate a game integrated with Open Play securely: where to keep keys, how to rotate them, how the browser session is protected, and how to verify webhook requests. Read it together with the [production checklist](production-checklist.md) before going to production.

## 1. API keys

There are two key types, and both are bound to a single **environment**:

| Type | Where it is kept | What it can do |
|---|---|---|
| **Server key** (`server`) | Only on your server (a secret manager or an environment variable) | All server endpoints |
| **Client key** (`client`) | Can be embedded in the client | Sensitive commands (for example `add_xp`, `set_attribute`) do not work; but some endpoints have no key-type gate ([endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md)) |

> [!WARNING]
> **A client key is not "harmless".** On endpoints such as character creation/deletion, inventory movements, trading, merchant buy-sell, and wallet transfer, there is no key-type gate in code; a key embedded in the client can call them. Call these endpoints only from your server, and for the player use the endpoints that work with a player session (`/v1/player/...`, plugins, `PlayerClient`).

### Key format and storage

- Format: `crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`. The server stores only the key's **digest** (argon2id); it cannot regenerate the secret part.
- The secret value is shown **only once, at creation time**. If you lose it, it cannot be recovered; you generate a new key.
- Do not put the key in the repository, logs, error reports, the client bundle, or screenshots. Filter the `Authorization` header out of logs.
- Use a **separate key per environment and per service** (for example the live API server, a batch job, an admin script); in a leak you revoke only one.
- Give the key an **expiry date**. `expiresAt` can be set when creating it in the panel; an expired key is rejected.

### Lifecycle

Keys are managed in the panel on the **Game settings: API keys** screen ([API keys](../panel/game-settings-api-keys.md)):

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| Create | A new key; the secret value is shown once |
| Disable / enable | Temporary and reversible |
| Rotate | Creates a new key with the same name and **immediately revokes the old one in the same operation** |
| Revoke | Permanent; cannot be undone |
| Delete | Soft delete + revoke |

The key state is **re-read from the database on every request**: a revoke or disable takes effect on the next request (only the verification result of the secret value is cached for 60 s, the state is not). A reason is written for every operation and it goes into the [operation history](../panel/audit.md).

### Rotation without downtime

The **Rotate** action in the panel revokes the old key immediately; until you roll out the new key, your calls get `401`. To rotate without downtime:

1. In the panel, create a second key **with a different name** (there can be only one active key with the same name and owner at a time).
2. Write the new key into your secret manager and roll it out by restarting your services.
3. Verify that no service uses the old key (the operation history and your own logs).
4. **Revoke** the old key.

### If a leak happens

1. **Revoke** the leaked key immediately (the effect is on the next request).
2. Roll out the new key in the order above.
3. In the operation history and your own logs, look for unexpected operations after the moment of the leak (wallet transfers, item minting, webhook registration).
4. In the environments the key could access, review the webhook endpoints; an attacker may have registered an endpoint (registered secrets are shown once, but a new registration generates a new secret).

## 2. Player session and browser security

- After player sign-in the server writes three cookies: `__Secure-crx.session` (session), `__Secure-crx.refresh` (refresh), and `__Secure-crx.csrf` (CSRF). All three carry `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `Path=/`, and `SameSite=Lax` (scripts cannot read them); the plain value of the CSRF token given to the script is not in the cookie but in the response header and body. The `__Secure-` prefix **requires HTTPS**: a session cannot be established over plain HTTP.
- The session **slides for 30 days**: it is extended if the player makes a request at least once a day. **The absolute ceiling is 180 days**: no matter how active, a new sign-in is needed after 180 days. An open realtime socket does not keep the session alive. The durations are fixed in server code.
- The environment can turn on a **single active session** rule if it wants (a new sign-in drops the old one); this is among the sign-in settings in the panel.
- The access JWT (EdDSA) is not the session token; your game server verifies it offline with `GET /v1/auth/jwks` ([server verification](../auth/server-verification.md)).

### CSRF

In a cookie session, every modifying (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) request passes two protections:

1. **Origin check:** the host in the `Origin` (or `Referer`) header must be one of the environment's allowed origins. A host bound to an environment can target only that environment. It is blocked if `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` and `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate` are together. Clients that send no `Origin` at all (curl, server-to-server) pass this check; the layer that protects them is double submit.
2. **Double submit:** the `__Secure-crx.csrf` cookie and the `x-csrf-token` header must arrive together and match. The token is **single-use** and rotates on every successful verification: store the new `Set-Cookie` and `x-csrf-token` value in the response for the next request. `GET /v1/auth/csrf` for a new token.

The TypeScript SDK manages this automatically; if you write HTTP by hand, see the [sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md) page. The failure case: `403` and the plain text `permission denied`.

### CORS and same origin

The server sends CORS headers **only to `https://<domain>` origins in the environment domain list** (and the operator's global allowed list), and only on the public API: the allowed origin is reflected verbatim, `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` is added, `*` is never used, and the panel path (`/v1/panel/*`) never gets CORS. **CORS is not authorization:** `Origin`, the CSRF double submit, and the environment checks run unchanged; CORS only lets the browser read the response. Do not add extra CORS headers to your own proxy: duplicate headers cause a browser error.

Because the session cookie is `SameSite=Lax`, a direct call works only if the game and Open Play are on the **same site** (subdomains of the same registrable domain); on a different site, use a reverse proxy. Topology: [architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md#calling-from-the-browser-direct-cors-or-reverse-proxy).

The allowed origins are **your environment domains**. The domain you define for the environment in the panel is the basis both for routing to that environment and for the `Origin` check ([Game settings: environments](../panel/game-settings-environments.md)). A modifying request from an unknown host is rejected.

## 3. Webhook verification

Open Play sends the events you subscribe to your endpoint with a signed `POST`. **You must verify every request**; do not process an unsigned request.

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-Crx-Signature` | `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` |
| `X-Crx-Event-Id` | The event ID (UUID); the deduplication key |
| `X-Crx-Event-Type` | The event type ([webhook events](../reference/webhook-events.md)) |

The signature: `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{t}.{raw body}")`, lowercase hexadecimal. The key is the `whsec_…` text you received at registration itself (as bytes). Rules:

1. Sign/verify the **raw body**: if you decode the JSON and rewrite it, the bytes change and the signature does not match.
2. Use a **constant-time** comparison (`timingSafeEqual`, `hmac.compare_digest`).
3. Compare the `t` value with your own clock and reject anything outside the window (5 minutes is recommended; this is a receiver policy, the server does not enforce it).
4. **At-least-once:** the same event may arrive more than once. Deduplicate with `X-Crx-Event-Id` and make the operation replay-safe.
5. Only a `2xx` response is success. Respond quickly (queue the work); other statuses are retried.

Delivery behavior:

| Behavior | Value |
|---|---|
| Retry | Exponential backoff: starts at 1 s, grows by powers of 2, capped at 5 minutes, ±20% jitter |
| Maximum attempts | 10; after that the delivery becomes `failed` (dead-letter queue, DLQ) |
| Redirect | Not followed |
| Body limit | A body above 64 KiB is not sent |
| Endpoint address | `https` only; private, loopback, and link-local IP addresses and addresses containing user info (`user:password@`) are rejected at registration (SSRF protection) |
| Secret key | Returned in the registration response **only once**; rotation = deleting the endpoint and registering it again |

> [!NOTE]
> There is no in-place "rotate" for the webhook secret. For a seamless transition: register the new endpoint (with the new secret), have your receiver verify both, and delete the old endpoint.

Verification example (Node, `node:crypto`):

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/security-webhook-verify.ts -->
```ts
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

/** İmzalı webhook isteğinin doğrulama sonucu. */
export type WebhookCheck = { ok: true; eventId: string; eventType: string } | { ok: false; reason: string };

const TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 300; // yeniden oynatma penceresi: alıcı politikasıdır, 5 dakika önerilir

/**
 * Open Play webhook isteğini doğrular. `rawBody`, ayrıştırılmamış HAM bayt dizisi olmalıdır:
 * JSON'u çözüp yeniden yazarsanız imza tutmaz.
 * İmza: HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{t}.{ham gövde}"), başlık biçimi `t=<unix saniye>,v1=<hex>`.
 */
export function verifyWebhook(
  secret: string,
  rawBody: Buffer,
  headers: { signature: string | undefined; eventId: string | undefined; eventType: string | undefined },
  nowSeconds: number = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
): WebhookCheck {
  const parts = Object.fromEntries((headers.signature ?? "").split(",").map((part) => part.trim().split("=", 2) as [string, string]));
  const timestamp = Number(parts["t"]);
  const received = parts["v1"];
  if (!Number.isInteger(timestamp) || received === undefined) return { ok: false, reason: "imza başlığı bozuk" };
  if (Math.abs(nowSeconds - timestamp) > TOLERANCE_SECONDS) return { ok: false, reason: "zaman damgası pencere dışında" };
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${timestamp}.`).update(rawBody).digest("hex");
  const a = Buffer.from(expected, "utf8");
  const b = Buffer.from(received, "utf8");
  if (a.length !== b.length || !timingSafeEqual(a, b)) return { ok: false, reason: "imza uyuşmuyor" };
  if (headers.eventId === undefined || headers.eventType === undefined) return { ok: false, reason: "olay başlıkları eksik" };
  return { ok: true, eventId: headers.eventId, eventType: headers.eventType };
}
```

Monitor delivery status and the DLQ in the panel: [Webhooks and event queue](../panel/webhooks.md). For registration and endpoint management, see the [webhooks guide](../guides/webhooks.md).

## 4. Rotating secrets: summary

| Secret | How it is rotated |
|---|---|
| Server/client API key | Create a second key, roll it out, revoke the old one (above) |
| Webhook secret | Register a new endpoint, update the receiver to accept both, delete the old one |
| Player password | The player changes their own password (all sessions drop) or the password reset flow ([email and password](../auth/email-password.md)) |
| Player sessions | The user signs out; an admin revokes the player's sessions (panel or `POST /v1/auth/admin/revoke-player-sessions`) |

## 5. What not to write to logs

The API key, session and refresh tokens, the CSRF token, the realtime ticket, the webhook secret, OAuth `state` and `code` values, passwords, and the guest secret value. The SDKs do not include these in error objects; in your own logging code, too, do not print the request raw.

## 6. Other notes

- **Error detail is not leaked:** the server gives no internal detail in a `500` response; account existence is also not leaked (a wrong password and an unknown address get the same response).
- **Banned account:** on sign-in endpoints, `403 account_banned` after ownership has been proven; no distinction is made on other endpoints ([errors](../reference/errors.md)).
- **Safety switches:** in the panel you can loosen or force back some protection rules per environment; every change is recorded with a reason ([Safety switches](../panel/safety-switches.md)).
- **Plugins** are trusted code compiled into the server; running third-party plugins and isolation do not exist yet ([plugins](../plugins/overview.md)).
- **Panel admin accounts** have a separate identity line and two-factor authentication; there is no two-factor authentication for player accounts.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.description: Tables that go from symptom to cause to fix; identity, network, plugin, realtime, and webhook problems by real error codes and status codes.
headings: If it is still not resolved
docs.body:
# Troubleshooting

This page lists the problems you will encounter in integration as a **symptom, cause, fix** triple. Find the symptom from the error code or the status code. For the full code tables, see the [error reference](../reference/errors.md).

> [!NOTE]
> When reporting a problem, include: the path and method called, the status code and body (with secret values removed), the request time (UTC), and on plugin endpoints the `x-request-id`/`requestId`. The server does not leak error detail outward; this information speeds up the investigation.

## Identity and session

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Server call `401 unauthorized` | The `Authorization: Bearer crx_live_…` header is missing or its format is wrong; the key was revoked, disabled, or expired; the key belongs to another environment | Check the header and the key; look at the key's state and environment in the panel ([API keys](../panel/game-settings-api-keys.md)). The server does not distinguish "wrong key" from "revoked" |
| Server call `403 permission denied` | You are calling a server endpoint with a client key | Use a server key ([endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md): the endpoints marked "Server key") |
| Player call `401` | The `x-crx-env` header is missing or not a UUID; the session is missing, expired, or revoked; the environment does not match | Add the header; refresh the session or sign in again. A banned account also looks like `401` (no distinction is made) |
| Player `403 permission denied` (POST) | The CSRF pair is missing/does not match; the token was already used; `Origin` is not allowed | See the CSRF rows below |
| `403` and `{"code":"account_banned"}` at sign-in | The account is banned | Show the player a suspension screen; do not build a retry loop; do not open a new guest |
| The session ends earlier than expected | No request was made for 30 days; or the 180-day absolute ceiling was reached; the password changed (all sessions drop); "single active session" is on in the environment and a sign-in was made from another device | Build a sign-in-again flow; the behavior is on the [security](security.md) page |
| The session cookie is never set in the browser | You are working over HTTP (`Secure` + the `__Secure-` prefix); the API is on another domain (the cookie becomes third-party, `SameSite=Lax`); the browser blocks cookies | Use HTTPS and **the same origin** ([architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md)) |
| `429 rate limited` on sign-in/sign-up | The per-IP rate limit is full (guest 30/min, email sign-in 5/min…) | Wait; if many players come from one IP or the proxy does not forward the client IP, see [rate limits](../reference/rate-limits.md) and the [production checklist](production-checklist.md) |
| Email sign-in fails, the password is correct | Failed-attempt lock (10 per 15 min per address + IP) | Wait 15 minutes or reset the password |

### CSRF and Origin

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every POST `403` | The `x-csrf-token` header or the `__Secure-crx.csrf` cookie is not being sent | Get a token with `GET /v1/auth/csrf`; send the cookie and the header together. The SDK does this automatically |
| The first POST passes, the second `403` | The CSRF token is **single-use** and renewed with every successful response; you did not store the response's new value, or you sent two requests **in parallel** with the same token | Use the new `x-csrf-token` and `Set-Cookie` value in each response; put modifying requests in a queue |
| `403` only in the browser, works in curl | `Origin` is not in the environment's allowed origins; a navigation request with `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` | Define the game's domain as an environment domain ([Game settings: environments](../panel/game-settings-environments.md)); call the API from the same origin |
| A "CORS policy" error in the browser console | The game's domain is in no environment's domain list or the global allowed list (the server sends no CORS to that origin); or the origin is not `https://<domain>` (`http`, a port, `null`) | Add the domain as an environment domain ([Game settings: environments](../panel/game-settings-environments.md)); if that is not possible, set up a same-origin reverse proxy. Do not add extra CORS headers to your proxy |

## Call errors

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `404` and JSON `module_disabled` (the `module` field) | The product module is disabled in the environment | Enable the module in the panel ([modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md)) |
| `404 not found` | The resource does not exist, was deleted, or the wrong environment | Check the ID and the environment |
| A `400` message like "Idempotency-Key required" | The header is missing on an endpoint where the key is required, or it is empty/200+ characters | Add the header ([idempotency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md)) |
| `400` "must be a valid UUID" | On a clan, group, or tournament endpoint the key is not a UUID | Generate a UUID v4 |
| `400` `If-Match` error | `*`, `W/"3"`, a negative or non-numeric value | Send the exact version number (`3` or `"3"`) |
| `409 version conflict` | The resource changed after you read it | Re-read, repeat with the new version |
| `409 idempotent request in progress` | The request with the same key is still being processed | Repeat shortly **with the same key** |
| `422 idempotency mismatch` | You used the same key with a different body | A new key for every different operation; do not change the body when repeating the same operation (remember that the key is unique across the environment) |
| `422 unprocessable: …` | A business rule rejection (balance, stock, limit) | Read the state and show it to the user; do not repeat the same request |
| `410` | The key's 24-hour record retention expired | Read the state and, if the operation was not applied, restart it with a new key |
| `413` | The body is above 2 MiB | Shrink the body; for images use the image upload endpoint |
| `429` | Rate limit or rule budget | Wait and repeat with the same key; for the rule budget simplify the rule |
| `503` and `Retry-After: 30` | The environment's placement is temporarily unavailable | Wait for `Retry-After` and repeat |
| A big number is corrupted (`9007199254740992` instead of `9007199254740993`) | You read the JSON with `JSON.parse`; `int64` did not fit in a JS `number` | Use the SDK's `bigint` reading or `lossless-json` ([numbers](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md)) |
| An SDK error of type `Contract` | The response does not conform to the schema the SDK knows (the server is newer) or the response is above 2 MiB | Update the SDK; match the server and SDK versions |

## Plugins

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `403` and `forbidden` | The plugin is not enabled in the environment (read-only, draining, disabled) or the environment's plugin version does not match the server's; CSRF/Origin rejection | Look at the plugin's state and version in the panel ([Plugins](../panel/plugins.md)) |
| `400` and `invalid_argument` ("x-crx-schema-version is required") | The `x-crx-schema-version` header is missing or the schema version is wrong; the payload does not conform to the schema; the same parameter twice in a query | Verify the operation's `schemaVersion` value and the input schema from the schema document |
| `404` and `not_found` | The plugin ID or the message type is wrong; you confused the message type with the operation **name** | Write the `requestMessageType` value in the schema document into the path |
| `409` `idempotency_in_flight` | The command with the same key is being processed | `retryable: true`; wait and repeat with the same key |
| `422` `unprocessable` + `reason` | A plugin business rule rejection | `reason` is a plugin-specific code; see the plugin's documentation; repeating does not help |
| The command result is uncertain | The network dropped | Query with `…/result?idempotency_key=…` or repeat with the same key ([calling plugins](../plugins/calling-plugins.md)) |
| SDK `upgrade_required` (`plugin_binding_mismatch`) | The binding's pin does not match the expectation you hold or the document on the server | Get the current document and regenerate the binding ([bindings](../plugins/bindings.md)) |
| `Cannot find module '@open-play/sdk/player'` in the generated binding | The generator writes the import with the name `@open-play/sdk`; the published package's name is `@ferdiunal/open-play-ts` | Define an alias in `package.json`: `"@open-play/sdk": "npm:@ferdiunal/open-play-ts@<version>"` |
| `crx plugins generate` error: `CRX TYPES FAIL` | The digest does not match, the output file already exists, the output folder does not exist, or there is a symbolic link in the path | Match the digest with the `schemaSha256` in the document; delete the existing output; create the folder |

## Realtime

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Ticket request `403` | An identity, CSRF, `Origin`, or `x-crx-env` error (all get the same response) | Check CSRF and `Origin`; the game's domain must be in the environment domain list |
| Upgrade `401` | There is a query string, the `openplay.realtime.v1` subprotocol was not requested, or `Origin` is not allowed | [Protocol: open the socket](../realtime/protocol.md) |
| An immediate `AuthenticationFailed` and close | The ticket was used (single-use), 30 s expired, or it was obtained from a different `Origin`; `Authenticate` did not arrive within 5 s | A new ticket on every connection; send `Authenticate` right after the socket opens |
| `UnexpectedFrame` | A frame in the wrong phase (`Join` before authentication, a second `Authenticate`) | Set the order according to the [protocol](../realtime/protocol.md) |
| `InvalidPayload` | Broken JSON, unknown field, a payload that does not conform to the schema, `int64` was sent as a number | Send counters as decimal text; validate the payload against the schema |
| `CapacityExceeded` and close | Frame rate above 40/s; 4 sockets per player or 8 per address | Reduce sending; close old tabs |
| The socket closes in 5 minutes (`4100`) | Idle close | A "Continue" flow; keep-alive input ([limits](../realtime/reconnect-and-limits.md)) |
| Inputs get `Ack: Stale` | A newer socket of the same player was opened | Close the old socket; work with a single socket |
| A `ResyncRequired` loop | Insisting on an expired or gapped cursor | Discard the cursor, `Join` without a cursor |
| `/v1/ws` or `/v1/chat/ws` `401` in the browser | These two sockets require the `x-crx-env` header on the upgrade; the browser cannot add headers | Use REST in the browser ([realtime overview](../realtime/overview.md)) |

## Webhooks

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No request ever arrives at my endpoint | The endpoint is not registered, was deleted, or is disabled; the event type is not in the subscription list; the `webhooks` module is disabled (deliveries wait in place, data is not deleted); the endpoint is not publicly reachable | Check the endpoint and the module in the panel ([Webhooks and event queue](../panel/webhooks.md)) |
| Registration `400` | The address is not `https`; it contains a private/loopback IP or user info | Provide a publicly reachable `https` address ([security](security.md)) |
| The signature does not match | You parsed and reserialized the body (raw bytes are needed); the secret is wrong (the `whsec_…` text itself, not base64); you forgot the `t.` prefix | Verify the raw body; example: [security](security.md) |
| Timestamp rejection | Your server's clock has drifted | Sync the clock with NTP; keep the window at 5 minutes |
| The same event arrived twice | Delivery is at-least-once | Deduplicate with `X-Crx-Event-Id` |
| Deliveries are `failed` | No `2xx` was received in 10 attempts | Fix the receiver error. The panel's deliveries are only for **monitoring** (there is no resend/replay action); make up for the effect of missed events by reading the relevant resource with REST |
| A large event did not arrive | A body above 64 KiB is not sent | Shrink the event size |

## Unity

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The package does not install | `~/.upmconfig.toml` or the scoped registry configuration is missing; the token lacks `read:packages` | The [Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md) installation steps |
| Requests are blocked in WebGL | The game and the API are not on the same origin; the Unity WebGL SDK requires the same origin today | Set up a same-origin reverse proxy ([Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md)) |
| `UpgradeRequired` (`plugin_binding_mismatch`) | The `package-ride` binding embedded in the package does not match the server's | Update the SDK |
| The session is not restored at runtime | The default secret storage is not secure (`PlayerPrefs`) | [Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md): attach your own secure storage |

## If it is still not resolved

1. Repeat the same request with `curl` (keeping secret values safe); tell apart whether the problem is in the SDK, the network, or the server.
2. Find the status code in the [error reference](../reference/errors.md).
3. Review the network items in the [production checklist](production-checklist.md) (header forwarding, client IP, HTTPS).
4. Add the information above to your support request.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.description: See the unchangeable record of changes admins made; check who changed what, when and why.
docs.body:
# Audit log

## Purpose

Every change made from the panel leaves an unchangeable record: which admin did which action, on which record, when, and for what reason. This page shows those records as a table. Records are append-only; none is ever deleted or edited.

## When to use

- To find out who changed a setting, when and why.
- To answer "what had changed?" after an incident.
- To compare the state of an operation before and after.

## Step by step

1. The newest records are at the top of the table. Each row shows the time, admin, action, target type, target and reason.
2. Narrow the list with the filters and search: action, target, admin, player and time range. The request ID, environment and player columns are hidden by default; you can turn them on from the column menu.
3. Press **İncele** (Inspect) on a row. The panel that opens shows the admin, target, environment, request ID, reason and the **Önce** (Before) and **Sonra** (After) states of the operation.
4. If the record is tied to a player, the panel shows a link that opens the player's page.

Super admins see two tabs: **Ortam kayıtları** (Environment records: operations tied to the selected environment) and **Operatör işlemleri** (Operator operations: operations not tied to any environment, such as display name, password, session, sign-in and admin management).

> [!NOTE]
> Records in the Operator operations tab are not tied to a player; the player filter returns no results in this tab.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Filters and search | No | Action, target, admin, player and time range; applied on the server |
| Columns | No | Can be hidden and pinned; the record time cannot be hidden |
| Page size | No | 15, 25, 50, 100 or 500 |
| Scope tab | No | Super admin only: environment records or operator operations |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| There is no Operator operations tab | Only a super admin sees these records. |
| I cannot see the record I am looking for | Check the selected environment and the time range. Environment records belong to the selected environment; environment-independent operations are in the Operator operations tab. |
| I want to delete or fix a record | Not possible; records are unchangeable. |

## Related docs

- [Security](../operations/security.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Character profile
docs.description: Inspect a character's attributes, wallet and history; if needed, run a command or roll back to an earlier version.
headings: Rolling back to an earlier version
docs.body:
# Character profile

## Purpose

This page shows the details of a single character: level, XP, record version, which player it belongs to, its attributes, its wallet and its event history. At most six key facts are at the top, with section tabs below. You get here by clicking a row in the [Player characters](characters.md) list.

## When to use

- To look into a complaint about a player's character state.
- To see how and when a change happened from the event history.
- To run a command to fix a wrong change, or to roll back to an earlier version.

## Step by step

### Inspecting

1. Pick one of the tabs: **Genel** (General), **İstatistikler** (Statistics), **Cüzdan ve envanter** (Wallet and inventory), **Geçmiş** (History), **Gelişmiş** (Advanced). A section you have no permission for, or whose module is disabled, is either hidden or shows a "yetki gerekir" (permission required) note.
2. To go to the player, use the **Oyuncu profiline git** (Go to the player profile) link in the key facts.

### Running a command

1. On the **Gelişmiş** tab, press **Komut çalıştır** (Run command). Only admins with command permission see this button.
2. Choose the command from the **Komut** (Command) list; the matching fields appear depending on your choice.
3. Enter the values, write an **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason) and apply the command.
4. The command runs on the character's current version. If the character is changed from somewhere else while you fill in the form, the action is rejected with a version conflict; refresh the profile and try again.

### Rolling back to an earlier version

1. On the **Gelişmiş** tab, press **Geri al** (Roll back). Only admins with rollback permission see this button.
2. Write the version number you want to return to in the **Hedef sürüm** (Target version) field (at least 1) and add the reason.

> [!WARNING]
> Rolling back does not delete history. A new event is written that brings the character to the state of that version; the old events stay in place.

### Viewing a past state

1. On the **Gelişmiş** tab, enter the time in the "Geçmişteki hâli" (State in the past) section and press **Hâlini göster** (Show the state). The character's state at that moment is recalculated from the event history.

## Fields and options

### Command window

| Field | Which commands | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Komut (Command) | All | Bayrak ayarla (Set flag), Özellik değeri ata (Set attribute value), Kaynak ekle ya da çıkar (Add or remove resource), Değiştirici ekle (Add modifier), Değiştirici kaldır (Remove modifier), Deneyim puanı (XP) ekle (Add experience points), Önceki sürüme dön (Roll back to an earlier version) |
| Bayrak anahtarı, Bayrak değeri (Flag key, Flag value) | Set flag | The flag's name and its on/off state |
| Anahtar (Key) | Set attribute value, Add or remove resource | The attribute's or resource's key |
| Değer / Miktar / XP miktarı / Hedef sürüm (Value / Amount / XP amount / Target version) | Commands other than flag (except Remove modifier) | An integer |
| Etkilenen istatistik, Değiştirici türü (Affected stat, Modifier type) | Add modifier | Which stat, and how it is affected |
| Kaynak türü, Kaynak kimliği (Source kind, Source ID) | Add and remove modifier | The modifier's source |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | All | At least 8 characters |

### State in the past

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Tarih ve saat (Date and time) | Yes | An RFC 3339 time; a time in the future or an invalid time is rejected |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The "Komut çalıştır" button is disabled | The character's data could not be loaded; refresh the profile. |
| The command was rejected with a version conflict | The character was changed from somewhere else; refresh the profile and run the command again. |
| "tanımsız attribute" or "tanımsız resource" error (undefined attribute or resource) | The key does not exist in the character's definition; it must match the definition's spelling exactly. Computed fields also cannot be set by hand. |
| A "min altında" or "max üstünde" error (below the minimum or above the maximum) | You are going past the lower or upper limit in the definition; choose a value within the limits. When adding a resource, the amount cannot be 0. |
| A tab is not visible | Your role has no permission to see that section, or the related module is disabled. |
| History is empty | It says "Bu karakter için olay kaydı yok." (There is no event record for this character.); the character has not received a command yet. |

## Related docs

- [Characters](../guides/characters.md)
- [Economy](../guides/economy.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Character templates
docs.description: The templates of characters and items in the game. Changing a template releases a new version; the old version is not deleted.
headings: Release a new version for a character definition
docs.body:
# Character templates

## Purpose

This page holds the game's character and item **templates**. It has four sections: character definitions, item definitions, level curves and traits. A character definition decides which traits and which level curve a character is born with; an item definition is the template of every item that can be given in the game. When you change a template the old version is not deleted; a new version is released.

## When to use

- To define a new item (weapon, consumable, cosmetic...).
- To change which traits characters are born with.
- To set the XP needed per level.
- To try whether a definition is valid before releasing it.

## Step by step

### Add a new item

1. In the **Eşya tanımları** (Item definitions) section press **Yeni silah** (New weapon). Only admins with the related write permission see the button. Weapon is not a separate kind: it is the "Weapon / equipment" kind; you can change the kind in the form.
2. **Temel bilgiler** (Basic information): name, key, kind; the max stack if the item is stackable.
3. **Ticaret** (Trade): tradeability and NPC buy and sell prices.
4. **Görünüm (3D)** (Appearance (3D)): if you wish, choose a published model.
5. **Oyun verisi** (Game data): add the extra values the game will read, row by row.
6. **Kayıt** (Save): write a reason and save. The item's system information and details open when you press the row.

### Release a new version for a character definition

1. In the **Karakter tanımları** (Character definitions) section press **Yeni sürüm yayınla** (Release new version); or open a definition and choose **Bu tanımla yeni sürüm hazırla** (Prepare a new version with this definition).
2. Write the key and choose at least one trait.
3. If needed, change the values coming from the traits for this definition with **Üzerine yazılacak değerler** (Values to overwrite).
4. Set the display name, the model and the game data.
5. Write a reason and release. The panel states the work to be done in one sentence before saving.

> [!NOTE]
> The trait order and values are merged at release time and become a new version. The display name, model and game data are independent of the version; they take effect immediately when saved.

### Try without releasing

With **Doğrula / önizle** (Validate / preview) you can see whether the definition is valid and its merged form without saving anything. **Önizle** (Preview) in the level curve section also computes on the server the curve's highest level and the total XP for that level.

### Release a level curve

1. In the **Seviye eğrileri** (Level curves) section press **Yeni sürüm yayınla**.
2. Write the curve key and the curve's JSON definition; check the result first with **Önizle**.
3. Write a reason and press **Yayınla** (Release). The new version does not replace the old one.

## Fields and options

### Item form

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Yes | The name the player will see |
| Key | Yes | Lowercase letters, digits, underscores; fixed after saving |
| Kind | Yes | Consumable, Weapon / equipment, Material, Cosmetic, VIP card |
| Stackable | Yes | Yes or No |
| Max stack | If stackable | 1 to 2147483647 |
| Tradeable | Yes | Yes or No |
| NPC buy price, NPC sell price | No | If empty, trade in that direction is off; 0 is free |
| 3D model | No | A published model |
| Values | No | Game data rows |
| Action reason | Yes | At least 8 characters |

### Character definition form

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Definition key | Yes | Fixed after saving |
| Trait keys | Yes | At least one; order matters |
| Values to overwrite | No | Section, name, field and value rows |
| Display name | No | The name shown in the game |
| 3D model | No | A published model |
| Game data | No | Extra values |
| Action reason | Yes | At least 8 characters |

In overwrite rows the **Bölüm** (Section) is one of: Nitelikler (Attributes; fields: Default value, Min, Max), Kaynaklar (Resources; Default value, Max (expression), Regeneration per minute, When it reaches zero) and Türetilmiş değerler (Derived values; Expression). System fields used by a plugin are locked.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Yayın için en az bir özellik anahtarı yazın" (Write at least one trait key to release) | A version with no traits empties the definition; choose at least one trait. |
| The "Yeni sürüm yayınla" or "Yeni silah" button is missing | Your account's role has no related write permission; the page is read-only. |
| Someone else changed the same record and a conflict warning appeared | See the latest state with **Güncel hâli yükle** (Load the current state); or deliberately overwrite with **Yine de kaydet** (Save anyway). |
| "Bu anahtar zaten var" (This key already exists) | You cannot write an existing key in the new version form; edit the definition from its detail with **Bu tanımla yeni sürüm hazırla**. |
| I cannot delete a record with a "Sistem" (System) badge | It is a system record used by a plugin; it is not deleted, changes become a new version. |
| I cannot change traits from this page | Traits are only inspected on this screen. |
| There is no "weapon" in the item kind list | Weapon is not a separate kind; it is the "Weapon / equipment" kind. |

## Related docs

- [Content](content.md)
- [3D models](models.md)
- [Characters guide](../guides/characters.md)
- [Inventory and items guide](../guides/inventory-items.md)

docs.title: Player characters
docs.description: Find the characters players play in the game, open their profile and, if needed, create a new character from a definition.
docs.body:
# Player characters

## Purpose

This page lists the characters in the selected environment. A character is the entity a player plays in the game; its state (level, attributes, resources) changes through commands, and every change is recorded. Use it to find a character, open its profile and, if needed, create a new character by hand. Character templates (definitions) are not on this page; they are on the Content page.

## When to use

- To check the state of a player's character.
- To filter characters of a given type, such as drivers.
- To create a character by hand for testing or support.

> [!NOTE]
> If the characters module is disabled, this page does not appear in the menu. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Step by step

### Finding a character

1. Make sure you selected the right game and environment; the list shows only the selected environment.
2. Narrow by type with the **Tümü** (All), **Sürücüler** (Drivers) and **Diğer** (Other) buttons at the top.
3. Use the table's search box and filter menu to narrow by name, type, level or date.
4. Click the row to open the profile. For the profile page, see [Character profile](character-profile.md).

### Creating a new character

1. Press **Yeni karakter** (New character). Only admins with permission to create characters see this button.
2. Choose the character's type from the **Tanım** (Definition) list. If there is no definition, first publish one on the Content page.
3. If you like, write the ID from your game server in the **Dış kimlik** (External ID) field.
4. Write an **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason) and press **Oluştur** (Create). The character is created immediately and you are taken to its profile.

## Fields and options

### New character form

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Tanım (Definition), or Tanım anahtarı (Definition key) | Yes | The definition the character is created from; its current version is used |
| Dış kimlik (External ID) | No | An ID to match your game server; a second character cannot be created with the same ID |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | Yes | The reason written to the audit log, 8-500 characters |

### Columns in the list

The columns Oyuncu (Player), Tür (Type), Seviye (Level), Puan (Score), Teslimat (Deliveries), Son değişiklik (Last change) and Oluşturulma (Created) are shown by default. You can turn on the Dış kimlik (External ID) and Oyuncu kimliği (Player ID) columns from the column menu. Old placeholder driver records that have no player carry a "Taşınmamış" (Not migrated) badge.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The list looks empty | Check that you selected the right environment and that no filters are active. |
| It says "Bu ortamda henüz tanım yok" (There is no definition in this environment yet) | A character is created from a definition. Publish a definition on the Content page and come back. |
| "Bu anahtarla yayınlanmış bir tanım yok" error (There is no published definition with this key) | The definition key is wrong or the definition is not published. Pick it from the list or publish the definition. |
| "Bu dış kimlikle zaten bir karakter var" error (A character with this external ID already exists) | Enter another external ID or leave the field empty. |
| The "Yeni karakter" button is missing | Your account's role cannot create characters; ask an admin. |

## Related docs

- [Characters](../guides/characters.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)
- [Authentication overview](../auth/overview.md)

docs.title: Clans
docs.description: Inspect, read-only, the clans players have created, their members, invites and applications, clan treasury movements and command history.
docs.body:
# Clans

## Purpose

This page lists the clans in the selected environment and shows the details of the clan you select: clan settings, members, invites, applications, clan treasury (vault) transfers and completed command records. The page is **read-only**; you cannot create a clan, add a member or take money out of the treasury from the panel. Clan actions are done from the game, through server calls.

## When to use

- To see a clan's members, leader and level.
- To verify the amount a player paid into or took out of the clan treasury.
- To check the state of an application or invite.

## Step by step

1. Make sure you selected the right game and environment. The list shows only the selected environment.
2. In the "Klan atlası" (Clan atlas) table, search and filter by name, tag, status, level or date.
3. Click the clan's name, or open the row, to see the details. When the page first opens, the newest clan is selected automatically.
4. In the "Klan detay ve ilişkiler" (Clan details and relations) card you see members, invites, applications, treasury transfers and command records. Long tables are paginated.
5. To go to a player's profile, use the player link in the table.

## Fields and options

There is no form to fill in on this page.

### Columns in the list

Klan (Clan; the name and the tag in square brackets), Durum (Status), Seviye (Level), XP, Üye (Members) and Oluşturulma (Created) are shown by default. You can turn on the Etiket (Tag), Lider (Leader) and Güncellenme (Updated) columns from the column menu. The status is "active" or "disbanded".

### Detail cards

| Card | Contents |
|---|---|
| Klan ayarları (Clan settings) | The environment's clan rules; read-only |
| Üyeler (Members) | Player, role, join time and leave time. Members who left are also listed and marked with an "Ayrıldı" (Left) badge |
| Davetler (Invites) | The invited player, the status and the expiry |
| Başvurular (Applications) | The applying player, the status and the creation time |
| Kasa transferleri (Treasury transfers) | Deposit or withdrawal, amount, the player who did it, balances and currency. Amounts are shown as text |
| Komut geçmişi (Command history) | The type of the completed command, the request digest (hash) and the time; the response body is not shown |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The list looks empty | Check that you selected the right environment and that no filters are active. |
| The member count does not match the row count | Members who left are also listed; rows with the "Ayrıldı" badge are not counted in the active member count. |
| I cannot edit the clan from the panel | The page is read-only; clan actions are done from the game or through server calls. |
| A warning like "Bu sayıyı görme yetkiniz yok" (You do not have permission to see this number) appears | Your role has no clan read permission; ask an admin. |

## Related docs

- [Clans and parties](../guides/social.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Content
docs.description: Manage your game content such as vehicles, characters and items in groups. The game sees only the version you published.
headings: Go back to an older release
docs.body:
# Content

## Purpose

This page gathers your game's content in **groups**: vehicles, NPCs, weapons and so on. Each group has a schema made of fields you define (number, text, color, 3D model...) and entries filled in with that schema. The game sees content only as you **published** it; a change you make in the draft does not reach the player until you publish.

## When to use

- When you set up the first group to add a new kind of content (for example vehicles) to your game.
- To change a group's entries and send them to the game (publish).
- To go back to a version you published earlier.

## Step by step

### Create a new group

1. Press **Yeni grup** (New group). Only admins with content write permission see the button.
2. You can start with an empty group or choose one of the ready templates; a template only fills in a field suggestion, it does not create entries.
3. Write the group name, icon and description and set up the fields with **Devam: alanlar** (Continue: fields). See [Edit group](content-group-edit.md) for details.

### Change entries and publish

1. Click the group card; the list of entries opens. You can switch between cards and the table view.
2. Open an entry, change it with **Düzenle** (Edit) and say **Taslağı kaydet** (Save draft). The change is only in the draft. See the [Entry](content-entry-edit.md) page for details.
3. Press **Yayınla** (Publish) at the top of the list. The window that opens shows, entry by entry, what will go to the game; if there are **Engelleyici** (Blocking) rows you must fix them first, **Uyarı** (Warning) rows do not stop the release.
4. If you wish, write the "Ne değişti?" (What changed?) note and publish.

### Go back to an older release

1. Press **Geçmiş** (History) in the entry list.
2. Look at what will change with **Farkı gör** (See the difference) next to the release you want to return to.
3. Say **Bu hale geri dön** (Go back to this state). This creates a new release; it does not touch your draft.

### Suggested groups

If a plugin offers its own content ready-made, a **Önerilen** (Suggested) section appears at the top of the page. The **Kur** (Set up) button creates that group with today's values; you can then edit it as you like.

## Fields and options

| Field | Where | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Ara (Search) | Entry list (card view) | Searches by entry name or key |
| Taslak değişikliği olanlar (With draft changes) | Entry list (card view) | Shows only entries with unpublished changes |
| Ne değişti? | Publish window | Optional release note, at most 280 characters |

### Sections on the page

- **Önerilen:** Ready-made groups offered by plugins.
- **Gruplarınız** (Your groups): Groups you created; the card shows the entry count, last release time and an "N unpublished changes" badge.
- **Yerleşik içerik** (Built-in content): The system's own groups such as character and item definitions. They have no release step: as soon as you save, it is valid in the game. The cards go to the [Character templates](character-templates.md) page.
- **3D model kütüphanesi** (3D model library): A link to the [3D models](models.md) page. If the Scenes module is off, the reason is written instead of the link.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The "Yeni grup" button is missing | Your account's role has no content write permission; ask an admin. |
| The Publish button does not work, I see "Engelleyici" | Open the related entry with the link on the blocking row and fix the missing or wrong value. |
| Players do not see the change I made | The change stayed in the draft; **Yayınla** the group. |
| The 3D model library link is not visible | The Scenes module is off in this environment; turn it on from the Modules tab in Game settings. |

## Related docs

- [Edit group](content-group-edit.md)
- [Entry](content-entry-edit.md)
- [Character templates](character-templates.md)
- [3D models](models.md)
- [Content groups guide](../guides/content-groups.md)

docs.title: Content entry
docs.description: See a content entry's values, edit its draft or create a new entry.
docs.body:
# Content entry

## Purpose

This screen shows and edits a single entry in a content group. The group's schema decides the entry's fields; that is, the fields in the form change from group to group. A change you make here is a **draft**: it reaches the game only with **Yayınla** (Publish) in the group's entry list.

## When to use

- To update an entry's values (for example a vehicle's speed).
- To add a new entry to the group.
- To archive or unarchive the entry.

## Step by step

### Edit an entry

1. Open the group from the [Content](content.md) page, then the entry from the list.
2. Press **Düzenle** (Edit). Only admins with content write permission see the button.
3. Change the values. Required fields are marked "(zorunlu)" ("(required)") next to their names.
4. Press **Taslağı kaydet** (Save draft) at the bottom of the page. The change is written to the draft; "Taslak değişikliği var" (Has draft changes) shows in the list and on the entry.
5. To send it to the game, use **Yayınla** in the entry list.

### Create a new entry

1. Press **Yeni kayıt** (New entry) in the group's entry list.
2. Write the **Kayıt adı** (Entry name); the key is suggested from the name, change it if you wish.
3. Fill in the fields and say **Taslağı kaydet**. The entry is added to the draft.

> [!NOTE]
> In closed groups used by a plugin (for example Package & Ride vehicles) a new entry cannot be added; the panel writes the reason on the page.

### Archive

From the **Daha fazla** (More) menu choose **Arşivle** (Archive) or **Arşivden çıkar** (Unarchive). Archiving is also a draft change; it reaches the game when published.

## Fields and options

### Fields on every entry

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Entry name | Yes | The name shown in the panel |
| Key | On a new entry | The ID in the game; fixed after the entry exists |

### The group's fields

The remaining fields come from the group's schema. The gray text under each field is the help text written by whoever set the group up. Input by type is as follows:

| Field type | Input |
|---|---|
| Number, Percent | A number within limits; decimal places depend on the group's setting |
| Text | Free text; the upper character limit is in the group's setting |
| Yes / No | Checkbox |
| Option list | Single or multiple choice |
| Color | Color picker |
| 3D model | Choice from the model library; a preview appears above the entry |
| Image | Image upload |
| Another entry | Choice of an entry from the target group |
| Table | Add, delete and move rows; the table data per entry cannot exceed 128 KiB in total |

Fields marked "game server only" do not go to the player; they appear with a badge in the panel.

### Sections

- **Özellikler** (Properties): The values.
- **Bağlantılar** (Links): The entries this entry links to and the entries that link to it.
- **Kullanan** (Used by): If a plugin uses this group, which feature uses it.
- **Geçmiş** (History): The entry's revision count, last change time and latest releases.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "N sorun var; alanların altındaki mesajlara bakın" (N problems; see the messages under the fields) | Fix the fields with red messages; the messages say what is wrong without showing the value. |
| I get a key error | The key must start with a lowercase letter or digit and contain only lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. |
| The price field cannot be edited and says "Mağazada yönetilir" (Managed in the store) | If the vehicle entry has a product in the store, the product is the only source of the price; change it on the [Product](store-product.md) page. |
| It asks for confirmation when leaving the page | There are unsaved changes; save with **Düzenlemeye dön** (Back to editing) or say **Değişiklikleri at** (Discard changes). |
| Someone else changed the entry at the same time | The entry is written with version checking; refresh the page and make the change again. |

## Related docs

- [Content](content.md)
- [Edit content group](content-group-edit.md)
- [Content groups guide](../guides/content-groups.md)

docs.title: Edit content group
docs.description: Set up a content group's name and fields in two steps; every entry is filled in with these fields.
docs.body:
# Edit content group

## Purpose

This screen sets up a content group in two steps: first its name, icon and description; then the group's **fields**. Fields are the values every entry in this group will fill in (top speed, color, 3D model and so on). The same screen is also used to change the schema of an existing group; in that case its title is "Grubu düzenle" (Edit group).

## When to use

- When setting up a new content group.
- To add a field to an existing group, change the field order or update a field's limits.

## Step by step

### Set up a new group

1. On the [Content](content.md) page press **Yeni grup** (New group); if you wish, choose a template.
2. In step **1 / 2** write the group name. In a new group the key is suggested from the name; you can change it as you like, it does not change after saving.
3. Move to the second step with **Devam: alanlar** (Continue: fields).
4. With **Alan ekle** (Add field), enter a name, kind and, if needed, limits for each field. Reorder fields with the up and down arrows.
5. Check how the entry form will look with the live preview on the page and say **Grubu oluştur** (Create group).

### Change an existing group's schema

1. Press **Şemayı düzenle** (Edit schema) in the group's entry list.
2. The key and kind of saved fields are locked. If you need a different kind, open a new field with **Yeni alan olarak ekle** (Add as new field).
3. Press **Kaydet** (Save). A schema change is also a draft, like entries; it goes to the game when you publish.

> [!NOTE]
> If you press **Vazgeç** (Cancel) while there are unsaved changes, the panel asks for confirmation before leaving.

## Fields and options

### Group information

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Group name | Yes | The name shown in the panel |
| Key | Yes | The ID the game finds the group by; fixed after saving |
| Icon | No | The icon shown on the card |
| Short description | No | At most 500 characters |

### Field kinds

| Kind | What it holds | Extra settings |
|---|---|---|
| Number | Whole number | Unit, decimal places, min, max, default |
| Percent | Percentage value | Min, max, default |
| Text | Text | Max characters, multi-line |
| Yes / No | Boolean value | Default |
| Option list | Choice from a list | Options (at most 64), multiple choice possible |
| Color | `#rrggbb` color | None |
| 3D model | A model from the model library | None; cannot be chosen if the Scenes module is off |
| Image | An uploaded image | None |
| Another entry | A link to another entry | Target, target group |
| Table | Repeated rows, for example a level-damage table | Min rows, max rows, columns (at most 8) |

### Settings common to every field

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Field name | Yes | The name shown in the form |
| Key | Yes | The ID the game reads; fixed after saving |
| Kind | Yes | Does not change on a saved field |
| Visibility | Yes | Player can see, or game server only |
| Help text | No | Shown under the field in the form |
| Required | No | If left empty, the entry cannot be saved |
| Show in list | No | Also shows it in the list and summary |

A group has at most 48 fields.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| I wrote the key wrong and saved | The key does not change. Add a new field with the right key; if the old one is no longer needed, remove it from the entries. |
| The "3D model" kind cannot be chosen | The Scenes module is off in this environment; turn the module on. |
| I cannot change a field's kind | A saved field's kind is fixed. Open a separate field for the new kind with **Yeni alan olarak ekle**. |
| Some fields have a lock icon | A plugin (for example Package & Ride) uses that field; it cannot be deleted and its kind does not change. |
| I cannot add a required text column to a saved table | Add it as optional first; a new required column is rejected because existing rows have no value. |
| "Devam: alanlar" does not move to the next step | In step 1 the name or key is missing or invalid; fix the red messages. |

## Related docs

- [Content](content.md)
- [Entry](content-entry-edit.md)
- [Content groups guide](../guides/content-groups.md)
