docs.body:
# Currencies

## Purpose

This page lists your game's currencies. A currency is the unit used to set prices in the store and to give money in reward tables (gold, diamonds, cents and so on). Each card shows the currency's name, icon, key, decimal places, supply cap and whether it can be sent between players.

## When to use

- To create a currency before setting prices in the store or setting up a reward table.
- To open an existing currency's detail (click the card; see [Currency](currency-profile.md)).

## Step by step

1. Choose the right game and environment from the environment selector at the top.
2. Press **Yeni para birimi** (New currency). Only admins with currency write permission see the button.
3. Fill in the form that opens using the instructions on the [Currency](currency-profile.md) page.
4. When you save, the currency is added to the list.

> [!NOTE]
> There is no deleting a currency on this page. Every save with the same key produces a new version; old versions do not change.

## Fields and options

There is no form field to fill in on this page; the create form is described on the [Currency](currency-profile.md) page. The information shown on the card:

| Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Name and icon | The name and image players see |
| Key | The ID the game uses to find the currency |
| Decimal places | How many decimal places the amount is shown with |
| Supply cap | The total amount that can be minted; "Sınırsız" (Unlimited) if none |
| Transferable | Whether players can send it to each other |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Ekonomi bu ortamda kapalı" (Economy is off in this environment) | The Economy module is off; turn it on from the Modules tab in Game settings. |
| "Henüz para birimi yok" (No currency yet) | Create the first one with **Yeni para birimi**. |
| The New currency button is missing | Your account's role has no currency write permission. |

## Related docs

- [Currency](currency-profile.md)
- [Economy reports](economy.md)
- [Store](store.md)
- [Economy guide](../guides/economy.md)

docs.title: Currency
docs.description: Manage a currency's icon, decimal places and supply cap; see its movement over recent days.
docs.body:
# Currency

## Purpose

This page is the detail of a single currency; the same page also works as the form for creating and editing a currency. In the detail view you see the currency's icon, key, version, decimal places, supply cap and transferability, along with the amount minted and burned in the last 30 days, the biggest balances, wallets, movements and the products priced in this currency.

## When to use

- To create a new currency.
- To change the decimal places, the icon, the supply cap or transferability.
- To look at how money circulates in the game.

## Step by step

### Create a new currency

1. On the [Currencies](currencies.md) page press **Yeni para birimi** (New currency).
2. Write the **Ad** (Name). Write the key with lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores; it does not change after saving.
3. If you wish, upload an icon image.
4. Choose the **Kuruş hanesi** (Decimal places). The "Oyunda böyle görünür" (This is how it looks in the game) preview on the right shows a sample amount with these places.
5. Choose the **Arz tavanı** (Supply cap) and tick **Oyuncular arası gönderilebilir** (Transferable between players) as needed.
6. Write a reason and press **Para birimini oluştur** (Create currency).

### Edit the currency

1. On the detail page press **Düzenle** (Edit).
2. Change the fields and press **Yeni sürüm olarak kaydet** (Save as a new version). Each save is a new version; old versions do not change.

> [!WARNING]
> Changing the decimal places changes only the display; stored balances and prices stay the same. So when the places change, the amounts shown to players may look different. Be sure before changing.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Yes | At most 120 characters |
| Key | When creating | Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores; does not change later |
| Icon image | No | PNG, JPEG or WebP |
| Decimal places | Yes | 0 (whole number), 1, 2 (cents), 3 or 4 |
| Supply cap | Yes | Unlimited or limited |
| Total supply at most | If limited | Amount with decimal places |
| Transferable between players | No | If selected, players can send it to each other |
| Action reason | Yes | 8-500 characters |

### Cards on the detail page

- **Son 30 gün** (Last 30 days): Amount minted and burned daily.
- **En çok bakiyesi olanlar** (Biggest balances): Balance ranking as of yesterday's close.
- **Cüzdanlar** (Wallets) and **Hareketler** (Movements): The wallets in this currency (can be sorted by balance) and ledger movements. Not shown if you lack the related read permission.
- **Bu parayla fiyatlanan ürünler** (Products priced in this currency): Products priced in this currency in the store; gives a link to the product page.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Bu anahtarla bir para birimi zaten var" (A currency with this key already exists) | Write another key; to change the existing currency, open it and use **Düzenle**. |
| "İkon görseli bu ortamda bulunamadı" (The icon image was not found in this environment) | Upload the image again. |
| I cannot change the key | The key is written only when creating; if it is wrong, create a new currency. |
| Cards that say "Bunu görme yetkiniz yok" (You do not have permission to see this) | Your account's role has no permission to read that information. |
| I changed the places and amounts look broken | The places are display only; go back to the old places and save as a new version. |

## Related docs

- [Currencies](currencies.md)
- [Economy reports](economy.md)
- [Economy guide](../guides/economy.md)

docs.title: Game overview
docs.description: See the state of the selected game and environment at a glance: players, characters, content, rules, plugin and recent actions.
docs.body:
# Game overview

## Purpose

This is the first screen you see when you open the panel. It summarises the state of the selected game and environment; each card's **Aç** (Open) button takes you to the matching detail page. The page title has the form "game name · environment name" (for example "My Game · Production"), so you always see which environment you are working in.

## When to use

- To check the overall state of the game at the start of the day.
- To confirm that the numbers you expect (players, characters, rules) are in place after a change.
- To see the recent actions and quickly understand who changed what.
- To notice whether one of the safety protections has been left loose.

## Step by step

1. Make sure the selector at the top left shows the right game and environment. Every number on this page covers only the selected environment.
2. Look at the cards. If you see a note under a card, the number could not be fetched (see the table below).
3. Press the card's **Aç** (Open) button for details.
4. The "Son işlemler" (Recent actions) card shows the six newest admin actions. Use the **Tüm kayıtları gör** (See all records) button for the full list.

## Fields and options

There is no form to fill in on this page. The cards show the following:

| Card | What it shows | Open button |
|---|---|---|
| Oyuncular (Players) | The total number of player accounts in the selected environment | [Players](players.md) |
| Oyuncu karakterleri (Player characters) | The number of characters; if the list is long, a "+" appears after the number | [Characters](characters.md) |
| İçerik (Content) | The number of character templates and item definitions | İçerik (Content) |
| Kurallar (Rules) | "enabled rules / total rules" (for example 3/5) | Kurallar (Rules) |
| Eklenti (Plugin) | The state of the plugin attached to the game: Açık (On), Salt okunur (Read-only), Drain (closing, with the seconds left), Yetki yok (No permission) or Eklenti yok (No plugin) | Eklentiler (Plugins) |

The "Son işlemler" card appears only if you have permission to read the audit log. Each row has the action name, the time, who did it, the target and the action reason.

If a safety protection is loose, a yellow banner appears at the top of the page ("N koruma gevşek", N protections are loose); if its state could not be read, an "unknown" banner appears. The **Şalterleri aç** (Open the switches) button takes you to the safety switches page.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| A card says "Bu sayıyı görme yetkiniz yok." (You do not have permission to see this number.) | Your account's role cannot read that area; ask an admin to widen your role. |
| A card says "Sayı alınamadı." (The number could not be fetched.) | It is a temporary read error; refresh the page. If it continues, check the server status. |
| The text "Bu oyunda henüz oyuncu yok" (There are no players in this game yet) appears | Your game client has not signed in yet; the number updates after the first player signs in. |
| The plugin card says "Yetki yok" (No permission) | The plugin has no active grant for this environment; check its state on the Plugins page. |
| The numbers differ from what I expected | You may have selected another environment (for example development instead of live). Check the environment name in the title. |

## Related docs

- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)
- [Open Play overview](../getting-started/overview.md)

docs.title: Economy reports
docs.description: Shows how money circulates in the game.
headings: Add to or deduct from a balance
docs.body:
# Economy reports

## Purpose

This page shows the state of money in your game. It does three jobs: it queries the **wallet, inventory and items** of a player, character, clan or the system; when needed it **adds to or deducts from the balance** of a wallet; and it shows a currency's **daily summary**, the biggest balances and warnings, as well as **trades** between players.

## When to use

- To investigate where a player's money went.
- To fix a wrong balance (support work).
- To watch whether too much money is being minted or burned in the game.
- To look at a trade's status.

## Step by step

### Query a wallet

1. Choose the **Sahip türü** (Owner type): player, character, clan or system.
2. Search for the owner by name and select. For a system owner, write the ID and press **Sorgula**.
3. The result shows that owner's **Cüzdanlar** (Wallets), **Envanter** (Inventory) and **Eşyalar** (Items) sections. The **Hareketler** (Movements) button on a wallet row opens that wallet's ledger movements.

> [!NOTE]
> Game money is in the player's wallet. If you choose a character, the panel resolves the character to the player who owns it and says so on screen; a character without a player stays a character. The real place for a player is the wallet section in the player profile; the "Oyuncu profilinde aç" (Open in player profile) link in the result takes you there.

### Add to or deduct from a balance

1. Press the balance operation button on the wallet row. Only admins with the permission to give or deduct balance see the button.
2. Write the **Tutar** (Amount).
3. Write the **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason).
4. Press **Bakiye ekle** (Add balance) or **Bakiyeden düş** (Deduct from balance).

> [!WARNING]
> A balance operation really changes money and shows permanently in the ledger; it cannot be undone, only corrected with a reverse operation. If the wallet changes through another operation while you are looking, the operation is rejected; refresh the page and try again.

### Daily report

1. Open the **Günlük raporlar** (Daily reports) section.
2. Enter the **Para birimi anahtarı** (Currency key) and the **Başlangıç** (Start) and **Bitiş** (End) days.
3. The **Günlük özet** (Daily summary), **En çok bakiyesi olanlar** (Biggest balances) and **Uyarılar** (Warnings) boxes fill in.

> [!NOTE]
> Daily reports are shown for now as raw data (key and value pairs); there is no chart yet. For a readable summary per currency, see the "Last 30 days" card on the [Currency](currency-profile.md) page.

### Trades

The **Takaslar** (Trades) section lists trades between players with the total count, status, number of parties and legs (money or items given).

## Fields and options

| Field | Where | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Owner type | Owner query | Player, character, clan or system |
| Owner (search) | Owner query | Search by name and select |
| Owner ID | Owner query | Only for a system owner |
| Wallet ID | Owner query | If there is no permission to see wallets; UUID |
| Amount | Balance window | With the currency's decimal places |
| Action reason | Balance window | At least 8 characters |
| Currency key | Daily reports | For example gold |
| Start, End | Daily reports | Closed days |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Henüz bir sahip seçilmedi" (No owner selected yet) | Choose the owner type above and search for the owner. |
| The Wallets section shows a permission warning | Your account's role has no wallet read permission. If you have the balance permission, you can operate by pasting the wallet ID; movements still cannot be listed. |
| "Geçerli bir kimlik (UUID) girin" (Enter a valid ID (UUID)) | The ID must be hyphenated in 8-4-4-4-12 format. |
| The balance operation was rejected | The wallet may have changed while you were looking; refresh the page. Also check that the amount fits the currency's number of decimal places. |
| The report is empty | Make sure you entered the currency key and a closed date range. Only closed days are reported. |
| "Takas yok" (No trades) | No trade record was found in this environment. If the section shows a permission warning, your account's role has no permission to read trades. |

## Related docs

- [Currencies](currencies.md)
- [Currency](currency-profile.md)
- [Economy guide](../guides/economy.md)

docs.title: API keys
docs.description: Create the keys your game uses to connect to Open Play, and manage their expiry and status.
headings: Editing, rotating and revoking a key
docs.body:
# API keys

## Purpose

API keys let your game's server prove its identity to Open Play. This page lists the keys of the selected game and environment, and lets you create new keys and manage their expiry and status. It is the **API anahtarları** (API keys) tab inside **Oyun ayarları** (Game settings).

## When to use

- When you connect your game server to Open Play for the first time.
- To revoke a key that has leaked or is no longer needed.
- To extend a key's expiry or rename it.

## Step by step

### Creating a new key

1. Use the environment selector at the top to choose the game and environment the key will work in.
2. Press **Anahtar oluştur** (Create key). Only admins with key write permission see this button.
3. Give the key a name and choose the **Anahtar türü** (Key type): **Sunucu anahtarı** (Server key) for your game server, **İstemci anahtarı** (Client key) for the game client.
4. Pick a period under **Geçerlilik** (Validity). If you are unsure, a period such as 90 days that you renew regularly is safer.
5. Write a short reason in the **Not** (Note) field.
6. Press **Anahtarı oluştur** (Create the key).
7. Copy the secret value shown on the page right away and store it somewhere safe.

> [!WARNING]
> The secret value is shown only once, when the key is created; it cannot be viewed afterwards. If you lose it, you must rotate the key.

### Using the key

Your game server sends the key in the `Authorization` header with every request:

```bash
curl https://<your-server>/v1/<endpoint> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>"
```

Replace the placeholders with your own values. Do not write the real key into source code or the game client.

### Editing, rotating and revoking a key

1. Click the key's row in the list to open its detail page.
2. Use **Düzenle** (Edit) to change the name, expiry and notes; the secret value does not change.
3. **Rotate** revokes the old secret and shows the new value once.
4. **Devre dışı bırak** (Disable) pauses the key temporarily, **Etkinleştir** (Enable) turns it back on; **Revoke** is permanent.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Anahtar adı (Key name) | Yes | A name to recognise the key in the list; at least 2 characters |
| Anahtar türü (Key type) | Yes | Server (secret) or client (can be embedded in the game) |
| Geçerlilik (Validity) | Yes | No expiry, 30 days, 90 days, 1 year or a custom date; when editing there is also "Değiştirme" (Do not change) |
| Not (Note) | Yes | The reason written to the audit log, 8-500 characters |
| Anahtarın sahibi (Key owner) | No | Default is "Bu ortam" (This environment); it is under "Gelişmiş ayarlar" (Advanced settings) |
| Sahip oyuncu / organizasyon (Owner player / organization) | Depends on the owner type | Required once you pick an owner |
| Kapsam etiketleri (Scope labels) | No | Labels for notes only |
| İzinler (Permissions) | No | Name-value notes; they do not restrict access |
| Ek bilgiler (Extra information) | No | Name-value notes; they do not restrict access |

> [!NOTE]
> Scope labels, permissions and extra information are for your records only for now. What a key can access is decided by the **key type** (server or client).

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| I lost the secret value | Rotate the key with **Rotate**; save the new value and update it on your server. |
| A key stopped working one day | It may have expired, been disabled or been revoked; check its status and end date on the detail page. |
| The "Anahtar oluştur" button is missing | Your role has no key write permission; ask an admin. |
| A server key was embedded in the client | Revoke the key immediately, create a new one and use it only on the server. |

## Related docs

- [Quickstart](../getting-started/quickstart.md)
- [Server-side verification](../auth/server-verification.md)
- [Security](../operations/security.md)

docs.title: Environments and domains
docs.description: See the game's environments, add a new environment, bind each environment to its own domains or archive an environment.
docs.body:
# Environments and domains

## Purpose

A game can have several **environments**: development (dev), staging and live (prod). Each environment has its own players, data and API keys. This tab lists the game's environments as cards; it lets you bind each environment to its own domains, add a new environment and archive an environment. The tab is open only to a super admin.

## When to use

- To bind a new address to an environment when your game will be opened from it in a browser.
- To add a staging or development environment.
- To hide an environment that is not used.

## Step by step

### Bind a domain

1. In the **Alan adları** (Domains) box on the environment's card, write one domain per line (for example `oyun.example.com`). Names are lowercased; empty lines and duplicates are dropped.
2. Write your reason in the **Gerekçe** (Reason) field.
3. Press **Alan adlarını kaydet** (Save domains).

### Add an environment

1. Press **Ortam ekle** (Add environment) at the top of the tab.
2. Choose the environment kind: Development (dev), Staging or Live (prod). The window selects Staging by default.
3. Write your reason and confirm. Domains and Google sign-in are bound separately after the environment is added.

### Archive or reopen an environment

The **Arşivle** (Archive) button under the card hides the environment; no data is deleted. An archived environment shows a **Geri aç** (Reopen) button and its domain fields are disabled.

> [!WARNING]
> Keep the old address in the list until the new address works and the old one redirects. Once an address is removed, a game opened from it cannot sign in or write records at once. When you press Save, the removed addresses are listed in a dialog; the change is not applied until you choose **Yine de kaldır ve kaydet** (the confirm button). If the list becomes empty, the server's general allowlist applies.

> [!NOTE]
> Domains are used as an allowlist in the origin check of requests coming from a browser. Bind every address you serve your game from to the right environment; a domain bound to another environment is not accepted.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Domains | No | One domain per line; at most 10 |
| Reason | Yes | 8-500 characters |
| Environment kind (add window) | Yes | Development, Staging or Live |
| Action reason (in windows) | Yes | 8-500 characters |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Bu alan adı başka bir ortama bağlı" (This domain is bound to another environment) | The same domain cannot be bound to two environments. Remove it from the other environment first. |
| "En fazla 10 alan adı bağlanabilir" (At most 10 domains can be bound) | Shorten the list; at most 10 domains can be bound to one environment. |
| "Önce başka bir ortam seçin" (First select another environment) | The currently selected environment cannot be archived; select another environment from the top bar. |
| The tab says "permission required" | This tab is open only to a super admin. |
| The game on the old address cannot sign in | The address was removed from the list. Add it back and save, then finish moving to the new address. |
| Archiving was rejected | The environment has a live grant or an active API key; the window shows the reason. |

## Related docs

- [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: General
docs.description: See the selected game's name, short name, studio and plugin; rename or archive the game.
docs.body:
# General

## Purpose

The **Genel** (General) tab of the **Game settings** page shows the identity of the selected game: the game name, short name, the studio it belongs to and the plugin it uses. Authorized admins can rename or archive the game from here. This tab sends no request to the server; the information is read from the selected game and environment.

## When to use

- To verify which game and studio are selected.
- To change the game's name (super admin).
- To hide a game that is no longer used from lists and the selector (super admin).

## Step by step

### Rename the game

1. Choose the game from the environment selector at the top.
2. Press the **Yeniden adlandır** (Rename) button. Only a super admin sees the button; the page is read-only for everyone else.
3. Write the new name (1-160 characters), write your reason and press **Adı kaydet** (Save name).

The short name does not change.

### Archive the game

1. In the **Tehlikeli işlemler** (Dangerous operations) box at the bottom of the page, press **Arşivle** (Archive).
2. Write your reason and confirm.

> [!WARNING]
> Archiving hides the game from lists and the selector; no data is deleted. If the game has a live grant or an active API key, archiving is rejected; the window shows the reason. While the selected environment belongs to this game, the **Arşivle** button is disabled; first select another game's environment.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Game name | Read-only | Changes from the rename window |
| Short name | Read-only | Given when the game is set up, does not change |
| Studio | Read-only | The studio the game belongs to |
| Plugin | Read-only | If there is no plugin it says "Eklenti yok" (No plugin); if you have permission, a link to the Plugins page appears |
| New name (rename window) | Yes | Must differ from the current name |
| Action reason (in windows) | Yes | 8-500 characters |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| It says "Ortam seçilmedi" (No environment selected) | Choose a game and environment from the top bar. |
| The Rename and Archive buttons are missing | These operations are open only to a super admin; you see the text "this page is read-only for you". |
| It says "Önce başka bir ortam seçin" (First select another environment) | The environment of the game you want to archive is currently selected. Select another game's environment and try again. |
| Archiving was rejected | The game has a live grant or an active API key. According to the reason in the window, revoke the active [API keys](./game-settings-api-keys.md) or turn the plugin's state off on the [Plugins](./plugins.md) page, then try again. |

## Related docs

- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)
- [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md)

docs.title: Modules
docs.description: See which product modules are on in the selected environment; a super admin can turn a module on or off.
docs.body:
# Modules

## Purpose

Open Play features come as **modules**: characters, economy, store, leaderboards, notifications and so on. This tab shows which modules are on in the selected environment. The screens of an off module disappear from the panel menu and its API returns `404` (`module_disabled`); the module's data is not deleted and comes back when you turn it on again.

## When to use

- When you investigate why a screen or an API is not visible.
- To turn off a feature your game does not use.
- To turn an off module back on.

## Step by step

1. Choose the environment from the environment selector at the top of the tab.
2. On the module's card, see its status (**Açık** (On) or **Kapalı** (Off)), what it depends on and, if any, the reason blocking it.
3. If you have permission, press **Aç** (Turn on) or **Kapat** (Turn off).
4. Write your reason in the window that opens. When turning off, a confirmation is also asked.
5. The change spreads in about two seconds.

The modules are: Characters and rules, Economy, Items and inventory, Trader and trade, Store and purchases, Missions and rewards, Party and clan, Chat, Leaderboard and tournament, Notifications, Webhooks, Scene and assets, Plugin platform.

> [!WARNING]
> API calls to an off module return `404` and `{"code":"module_disabled"}`. If your game depends on a module, make sure the game does not use it before turning it off.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Action reason | Yes | 8-500 characters |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The **Aç** and **Kapat** buttons are missing | Only a super admin can turn modules on and off; the screen is read-only for you. |
| The button is disabled and says "Önce şu modülleri açın" (First turn on these modules) | The module depends on other modules; turn on the listed modules first. |
| The button is disabled and says "Önce şu modülleri kapatın" (First turn off these modules) | Other modules depend on this module; turn them off first. |
| It says "Etkin eklentiler kullanıyor" (Used by active plugins) | A plugin needs this module. Turn those plugins off on the [Plugins](./plugins.md) page, then turn the module off. |
| Is the data of the module I turned off gone? | No. Data is kept; only the screens and the API stop. |

## Related docs

- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)
- [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md)

docs.title: Sign-in methods
docs.description: See which methods players use to get into the game; enter Google sign-in details and set the single active session rule.
headings: Remove information entered from the panel
docs.body:
# Sign-in methods

## Purpose

This tab is where you manage which providers players can sign in with in the selected environment. The provider managed from the panel today is Google; guest sign-in and email sign-in are not set here. The page also has the environment's **session policy** (single active session). Each provider's detail page has its status, scopes, client information and safe extra information.

## When to use

- When turning on Google sign-in for the first time (to enter the client ID, secret and redirect base).
- To temporarily turn Google sign-in off or turn it back on.
- If you want a player's old sessions to close on their new sign-in.

## Step by step

### Configure Google sign-in

1. Choose the environment at the top of the tab and press **Detay** (Detail) on the **Google** row in the list.
2. On the **OAuth istemci bilgisi** (OAuth client information) card press **OAuth bilgilerini düzenle** (Edit OAuth information). Only a super admin sees the button.
3. Enter the client ID, the client secret and the redirect base.
4. Write your reason and the 6-digit code from your authenticator app and press **Kaydet** (Save).
5. In the Google Cloud console, register as the **Authorized redirect URI** your redirect base with `/google` added at the end.
6. If the provider is not **Etkin** (Enabled), press **Etkinleştir** (Enable) on the detail page.

> [!WARNING]
> The client secret is write-only. After saving it never appears in the panel again; the card shows only a "configured" status and a short fingerprint. If you lose it, get a new one from Google and enter it again.

### Single active session

1. Turn the **Tek aktif oturum** (Single active session) switch on the **Giriş ayarları** (Sign-in settings) card on or off. Only admins with sign-in method write permission can change the switch.
2. Write your reason in the window that opens and confirm.

The line under the card shows the value's source: environment setting or server default.

### Remove information entered from the panel

For Google information entered from the panel, a **Kaldır** (Remove) button appears on the detail page. You confirm by typing the provider's ID and enter your reason and verification code. If the server has a default value, the environment returns to it; if not, the provider becomes unconfigured in this environment.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Single active session | No | A switch per environment; does not touch open sessions |
| Client ID | Yes | At most 256 characters, visible characters without spaces |
| Client secret | Yes | At least 8, at most 1024 characters; write-only |
| Redirect base | Yes in live | Starts with https; contains no query, fragment or user info |
| Action reason | Yes | 8-500 characters |
| Verification code | Yes | The current 6-digit code |
| Confirmation text (removal) | Yes | The provider ID exactly |
| Running state enabled (provider settings) | No | Turns the provider on or off |
| Safe extra information (JSON) | No | Field names that contain secrets are rejected |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The Google button does not appear in the game, or the start returns `403` | Google is not configured or is off in this environment. Enter the information and enable the provider. |
| Google says "redirect_uri_mismatch" | The address you registered in the Google Cloud console must be exactly the same as the redirect base + `/google`. |
| The "edit information" button is missing | Only a super admin can write client information. |
| "Kaydet" gives a verification code error | A recovery code is not accepted; enter the current 6-digit code from your authenticator app. The code is cleared after each attempt. |
| Server default appears as the source | The information comes from the server setting. A value you enter from the panel overrides it in this environment. |
| A player cannot stay signed in on two devices at the same time | **Single active session** is on. If you turn it off, players can stay signed in on more than one device at the same time. |

## Related docs

- [Sign in with Google](../auth/oauth.md)
- [Authentication overview](../auth/overview.md)

docs.title: Leaderboard detail
docs.description: See one leaderboard's ranking this season, its past seasons and its settings; change its visibility in the game and its score format.
docs.body:
# Leaderboard detail

## Purpose

This page shows a single leaderboard in a profile-page layout. At the top are the leaderboard's name, its copyable key and four summary boxes (player count this season, leader, last score time, next reset). Below are three tabs: **Bu sezon** (This season), **Geçmiş sezonlar** (Past seasons) and **Ayarlar** (Settings).

## When to use

- To look at the top ranks of the leaderboard and a specific player's place.
- To see the winners of closed seasons and the closing table.
- To change the leaderboard's visibility in the game or its score format.
- To copy the key to read the leaderboard with in your game code.

## Step by step

### See this season's ranking

1. The top ranks are listed in the **Bu sezon** tab. Each row has the rank, player, score and last update time; if you click the player's name, the player's page opens.
2. To see a specific player, write their name or email in the **Oyuncu bul** (Find player) field and select them. The rows around the player are shown in a separate card.

Banned or deleted players are shown faded and labeled "hidden in game"; players do not see these rows in the game.

### Look at past seasons

1. Closed seasons are listed in the **Geçmiş sezonlar** tab; each row shows the date, the player count and the first place.
2. Clicking a row opens the season's closing table (first 100 rows). A closed season cannot be changed.

### Change settings

1. In the **Ayarlar** tab, change the **Oyunda görünsün** (Show in game), **Puan nasıl gösterilsin?** (How should the score be shown?) and **Birim eki** (Unit suffix) fields.
2. Press **Kaydet** (Save). Only the changed fields are sent.

The **Tablo tanımı** (Leaderboard definition) card below shows the key, sort direction, reset interval and source read-only; these are chosen at setup and cannot be changed. The **Geliştirici bilgisi** (Developer info) section shows the player-session read endpoint and the SDK call.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Find player | No | View only; shows the player's surroundings |
| Show in game | No | Turns players seeing the leaderboard on or off |
| How should the score be shown? | Yes | Number, money or time |
| Unit suffix | No | At most 8 characters; not available for the time unit |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Bu sezon henüz puan yok" (No scores yet this season) | Your game server has not sent scores this season. The row appears when the first score arrives. |
| "Tablo bulunamadı" (Leaderboard not found) | There is no leaderboard with this key or it was deleted; reopen it from the [Leaderboards](./leaderboards.md) list. |
| The Settings tab is disabled | Changing fields needs the leaderboard management permission; ask an admin. |
| "Bu tabloya yalnız … eklentisi puan yazar" (Only the ... plugin writes scores to this leaderboard) | A plugin set this leaderboard up. The plugin writes the scores, not your game server. |
| I want to change the sort direction or the reset | These do not change after setup. Set up a new leaderboard from the [Leaderboards](./leaderboards.md) page. |
| The list has only the first rows | The page shows the first rows; the rest is not listed in this version. |

## Related docs

- [Leaderboards and tournaments](../guides/competition.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.body:
# Leaderboards

## Purpose

A leaderboard is a table where players are ranked by their scores. This page lists the leaderboards in your environment as cards: name, reset interval, whether it is visible in the game, the player count this season, the leader and the time left until the next reset. You also set up a new leaderboard from here. Your game server sends the scores; the panel does not write scores.

## When to use

- To set up a leaderboard before your game server sends scores.
- To see which leaderboard is visible, when it will reset and who leads it.
- To move to a leaderboard's detail (ranking, past seasons, settings).

## Step by step

### Set up a new leaderboard

1. Press **Yeni tablo** (New leaderboard). Only admins with the leaderboard management permission see the button.
2. Write a name in the **Tablonun adı** (Leaderboard name) field; the key fills in automatically. If you wish, change the key yourself.
3. Choose **Hangi puan önde?** (Which score comes first?) and **Ne zaman sıfırlansın?** (When should it reset?). If you choose "Özel aralık" (Custom interval), write days and hours.
4. Choose **Puan nasıl gösterilsin?** (How should the score be shown?); write a unit suffix if needed.
5. If you want players to see the leaderboard in the game, turn on the **Oyunda görünsün** (Show in game) switch.
6. Check how the score will look in the preview row below and press **Tabloyu oluştur** (Create leaderboard). On success the leaderboard's detail page opens.

> [!WARNING]
> The key, sort direction and reset interval cannot be changed after the leaderboard is set up. To change them you need to set up a new leaderboard; so choose carefully before setting it up.

### Open a leaderboard

Click the card's name; the detail page opens ([Leaderboard detail](./leaderboard-detail.md)).

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Leaderboard name | Yes | 1-400 characters |
| Key | Yes | Starts with a lowercase letter or digit; lowercase letters, digits, dots, hyphens, underscores; at most 200 characters |
| Which score comes first? | Yes | High score or low score |
| When should it reset? | Yes | Never, every day, every week (Monday), every month or custom interval |
| Days, Hours | Only for a custom interval | At least one of days or hours; total at least 1 hour, whole numbers |
| How should the score be shown? | Yes | Number, money or time |
| Unit suffix | No | At most 8 characters; not available for the time unit |
| Show in game | No | Off by default |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Bu anahtar kullanılıyor ya da bir eklentiye ayrılmış" (This key is in use or reserved for a plugin) | Choose another key. Some key prefixes are reserved for the game's plugin. |
| There is no leaderboard in the list and it says "package-ride eklentisi 'Günlük kazanç' tablosunu ilk teslimatta kendiliğinden kurar" (the package-ride plugin sets up the 'Daily earnings' leaderboard by itself at the first delivery) | The plugin sets the leaderboard up at the first delivery; no delivery has happened yet. You only need to wait. |
| "Sıralama (Competition) modülü bu ortamda kapalı" (The Leaderboard (Competition) module is off in this environment) | Turn the module on from [Game settings › Modules](./game-settings-modules.md). |
| The "Yeni tablo" button is missing | You do not have the leaderboard management permission; ask an admin. |
| I see only the first leaderboards | The list shows at most a certain number of leaderboards; when the limit is reached the page says so. More is not listed in this version. |
| The card says "Kaynak: … eklentisi (otomatik)" (Source: ... plugin (automatic)) | A plugin set the leaderboard up and only that plugin writes scores. |

## Related docs

- [Leaderboards and tournaments](../guides/competition.md)
- [Notifications](../guides/notifications.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Model
docs.description: Preview a 3D model, publish or roll back its versions, add clips and archive it.
docs.body:
# Model

## Purpose

This page is the detail of a single 3D model: the preview, values computed from the file, versions, the definitions that use the model and the release history. You choose here which version of the model goes to the game.

## When to use

- To publish a converted model to the game.
- To roll a wrong release back to a previous version.
- To add animation clips to the model.
- To archive, rename or permanently delete the model.

## Step by step

### Publish a version

1. In the **Sürümler** (Versions) table, press **Yayınla** (Publish) on a version whose status is **Hazır** (Ready).
2. If the release does not bring a big change to the live version's clips or dimensions, it is done immediately.
3. If the version removes a clip that is live or noticeably changes the bounding box, a confirmation window opens. The window shows the removed and added clips and the size difference. Tick **Farkı gördüm, yine de yayınla** (I saw the difference, publish anyway), write a reason and confirm.

### Roll back

On a version older than the live one, the button appears as **Geri al** (Roll back) and always opens a confirmation window. You can roll back only to versions that are still retained.

> [!WARNING]
> Versions that are no longer live are deleted after 14 days in the default setting; you cannot go back to a version whose retention period has expired. The table shows each version's retention date.

### Add clips

1. Press **Klip ekle** (Add clip). The button is disabled if there is no ready version with a skeleton and an fbx or blend source, and the reason is written next to it.
2. Choose the **Taban sürüm** (Base version), choose the clip file or zip package and press **Yükle** (Upload).
3. The server attaches the clips to the base version's skeleton and produces a new version; you can then publish the new version.

### Rename, archive, delete

Done with the buttons at the top; each asks for a reason.

- **Yeniden adlandır** (Rename): The new name shows in the library; existing references are not affected.
- **Arşivle** (Archive): The model closes to new selections; definitions that use it keep working. **Arşivden çıkar** (Unarchive) reopens it.
- **Kalıcı sil** (Delete permanently): Possible only for an archived model that no definition uses. It cannot be undone; all of the model's versions are deleted.

## Fields and options

| Field | Where | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Previewed version | Preview | Which version is shown |
| Base version | Add clip | The version that will receive the clips |
| Clip file or zip | Add clip | fbx or zip |
| New name | Rename | At most 200 characters |
| I saw the difference, publish anyway | Release confirmation | Required checkbox |
| Action reason | Rename, archive, delete, confirmed release | 8-500 characters |

### Sections on the page

- **Önizleme** (Preview): A 3D viewer; you can play the selected version's clips.
- **Olgular** (Facts): Triangle, vertex, bone, material and texture counts, size, glb file size and the clip list. The server computes these itself from the glb file.
- **Uyarılar** (Warnings): Minor problems during conversion (for example a missing texture or a skipped clip). They do not block the release.
- **Sürümler** (Versions): Each version's source, status, source files (downloadable), retention period and release button.
- **Kullanan tanımlar** (Definitions using it): The item, character and content entry definitions that use this model.
- **Yayın geçmişi** (Release history): Which version was released when and for what reason.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The "Kalıcı sil" button is disabled and says "N definitions use this model" | First remove the model from the definitions that use it; then you can delete it. |
| A note "another release was made while you were looking" appeared when publishing | The difference was refreshed; look at the new difference and confirm again. |
| "Klip ekle" is disabled | Clips can be added only to ready versions with a skeleton and an fbx or blend source. |
| I cannot go back to an old version | The version's retention period has expired; upload the model again. |
| The preview does not open | The preview needs a ready, retained version; conversion may not be finished or may have failed. |

## Related docs

- [3D models](models.md)
- [Content](content.md)
- [Scenes, images and 3D models guide](../guides/scenes-assets-models.md)

docs.title: 3D models
docs.description: Upload a model; the server converts it to glb and validates it. Bind a ready model to an item or character; the game sees the change without a redeploy.
docs.body:
# 3D models

## Purpose

This page is the library of 3D models your game will use. You upload a model; the server converts it to the **glb** format the game can read and validates it. You publish the ready model and bind it to an item or a character; the game sees the change without redeploying the game.

## When to use

- To add a new vehicle, weapon or character model to the game.
- To check the status of a model whose conversion is in progress or has failed.
- To inspect a model's published version, the definitions that use it or its version history (click the row; see [Model profile](model-profile.md)).

## Step by step

### Upload a model

1. Press **Model yükle** (Upload model). Only admins with model write permission see the button.
2. Choose the **Yükleme türü** (Upload type): single file or zip package.
3. Choose the file. The file cannot exceed 50 MiB.
4. If you wish, write a name. For obj, stl, 3mf, dxf files and zip packages, **Birim** (Unit) and **Yukarı eksen** (Up axis) also appear; defaults are filled in by file format, check the values.
5. Press **Yükle** (Upload). A progress bar shows during upload; you can stop it with **Yüklemeyi iptal et** (Cancel upload).
6. The model passes through the **Sırada** (Queued) and **Dönüştürülüyor** (Converting) states in the list and becomes **Hazır** (Ready). The list refreshes by itself in the meantime.

### Publish a model

A ready model does not go to the game immediately. Open the model row and **Yayınla** (Publish) the version from the **Sürümler** (Versions) table on the [Model profile](model-profile.md).

> [!NOTE]
> Formats that carry no animation (obj, stl, 3mf, dxf) appear in the list with the note "Bu biçim animasyon taşımaz" (This format carries no animation). Clips cannot be added to these models.

## Fields and options

### Upload form

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Upload type | Yes | Single file or zip package |
| File | Yes | At most 50 MiB |
| Name | No | If empty, the file name is used, at most 200 characters |
| Main file | No | Only in zip mode; the path inside the zip if there is more than one model file |
| Unit | Depends on format | Micron, millimeter, centimeter, inch, foot, meter |
| Up axis | Depends on format | Y up or Z up |

### List columns

The Name, Format, Last version (with status), Published, Versions and Added columns are shown by default. You can turn on the Last version number and Lifecycle columns from the table's column menu. Lifecycle: Active, Archived.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The model is in the "Başarısız" (Failed) state | Open the model's row; under the version the reason is written as a plain sentence (for example a reference to an external file or a 2D dxf). Fix the file and upload again. |
| I uploaded a zip and it does not know which file is the main file | Write the model file's path inside the zip in the **Ana dosya** (Main file) field. |
| The model looks too big or too small | You chose the wrong unit during upload; upload the model again. |
| The Upload model button is missing | Your account's role has no model write permission. |
| Conversion never starts, "glb only" warning | The converter runs only on amd64 servers; in this environment you can upload only glb. |
| The library list is empty | Check the selected game and environment; if the Scenes module is off, the model library cannot be used in this environment. |

## Related docs

- [Model profile](model-profile.md)
- [Content](content.md)
- [Scenes, images and 3D models guide](../guides/scenes-assets-models.md)

docs.title: Notifications
docs.description: Manage the messages sent to players; first connect a push notification provider, then write a template, then add a rule or send a test.
headings: 3. Add a rule or send a test
docs.body:
# Notifications

## Purpose

This page is where you manage the notifications sent to players. Three things are needed for a notification to go out: a **provider** (a push notification service such as Firebase, Apple or OneSignal), a **template** (the message text) and a **rule** or a manual **test send** (when the message goes out). The page has six tabs: Overview, Templates, Rules, Providers, Delivery history and Devices.

## When to use

- When setting up the notification infrastructure for the first time (follow the three steps in the Overview tab).
- To send an automatic notification on an event such as a level up.
- To investigate why a notification did not go out (the Delivery history and Devices tabs).

## Step by step

### 1. Connect a provider

1. In the **Sağlayıcılar** (Providers) tab, press **Bağla** (Connect) on the card of the service you use. This operation is open only to a super admin.
2. Enter the information the service asks for and choose the key file. The key is write-only; after saving it is never shown again, only its fingerprint is shown.
3. Write your reason and the 6-digit code from your authenticator app and press **Kaydet** (Save).
4. The card becomes **Hazır** (Ready) within a few seconds; the server loads the setting. If you see an error, its reason is written on the card in plain language.

### 2. Write a template

1. In the **Şablonlar** (Templates) tab press **Yeni şablon** (New template) (or **İlk şablonu oluştur** (Create the first template) if empty; **Örnekle başla** (Start with an example) brings a ready example).
2. Write the key, display name and language; enter the title and text. For player-specific values write `{{name}}` in the text and add the same name to the **Değişkenler** (Variables) list.
3. In the live preview on the right, look at the phone lock screen and the browser notification, then press **Şablonu oluştur** (Create template).
4. To add another language, use the **+ Dil ekle** (+ Add language) button in the template's detail. Each save is stored as a new **version**; you can go back to an old version from the version history.

> [!NOTE]
> If there is no version in the player's language, the fallback language, the English (en) version, is used. If there is no English version either, the notification is not sent.

### 3. Add a rule or send a test

- **Rule:** In the **Kurallar** (Rules) tab, choose the event, conditions, template, language and channel with **Yeni kural** (New rule); in the **Örnek olayla dene** (Try with a sample event) section try the rule without sending any notification.
- **Test:** In the **Gönderim geçmişi** (Delivery history) tab press **Test gönder** (Send test); choose the player, template, language and channel and send. The page follows the result for 60 seconds at most. Frequent tries are limited (10 tries in 15 minutes).

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Template key, display name, description, language | Key, name, language required | The key does not change; name at most 120, description 500 characters |
| Title, Text | Yes | Soft limit of 65 characters for the title and 240 for the text |
| Variable name, type, example value, required | When a variable is added | At most 32 variables; whole number for a number variable |
| Version note | No | At most 200 characters |
| Rule key, rule name | Yes | The key is at most 64 characters and does not change; name at most 120 |
| When, conditions | When is required | At most 20 condition rows; with no condition the rule runs every time the event happens |
| Template, language, channel | Yes | Channel: in-game, push notification or both |
| Provider information and key file | Yes | Firebase: service account JSON; Apple: Team ID, Key ID, Bundle ID, environment and .p8; OneSignal: App ID and REST API key |
| Action reason, verification code | Yes | Reason 8-500 characters; code 6 digits |

An environment can have at most 50 notification rules.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Bu oyunda bildirimler kapalı" (Notifications are off in this game) | Turn on the Notifications module from [Game settings › Modules](./game-settings-modules.md). |
| The card says "Bağlı değil" (Not connected) | The provider is not connected in this environment; enter the information with **Bağla**. Connecting needs super admin permission. |
| "Sağlayıcı anahtarı reddetti" (The provider rejected the key) | Renew the service account file for Firebase, the .p8 key and the Team ID, Key ID, Bundle ID values for Apple, the REST API key for OneSignal. |
| "Anahtar dosyası biçimi tanınmadı" (The key file format was not recognized) | A service account JSON file is needed for Firebase and a .p8 file for Apple; a Google OAuth client file or a .p12 certificate will not do. |
| The test says "oyuncunun ulaşılabilir cihazı yok" (the player has no reachable device) | The player has not turned on notifications in the game. Choose the in-game channel or look in the Devices tab at whether the player has a device. |
| The rule cannot be saved: "Şablon arşivlenmiş" (Template archived) or "bu dilde şablon yok" (no template in this language) | Unarchive the template or add the language you chose to the template. |
| Rules coming from the server setting are running | When you add the first rule in the panel, panel rules replace them in this environment. |
| A rule or template cannot be edited | You do not have the notification management permission; the view is read-only. Ask an admin. |

## Related docs

- [Notifications guide](../guides/notifications.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Background jobs
docs.description: See the records of plugins' scheduled background jobs, and inspect, read-only, a player's linked sign-in accounts and devices.
docs.body:
# Background jobs

## Purpose

This page shows two things, read-only: (1) the background job records of plugins' scheduled commands, and (2) the linked sign-in accounts and device information of a player you select. From this page you cannot start or retry a job, close a session or change a password. For those actions, use the [Player profile](player-profile.md) page.

## When to use

- To see whether a plugin's scheduled job is running or has failed.
- To see which sign-in methods (Google, password and so on) a player is linked to the account with.
- To check which devices a player signed in from.

## Step by step

### Job records

1. Make sure you selected the right game and environment.
2. In the "Worker job runs" table, filter jobs by status: pending (not yet picked up, or released for a retry), claimed (a worker picked it up), done (completed), dead (closed because of a permanent error or the retry limit).
3. For a specific time range, use the "Oluşturulma" (Created) column in the filter menu with "arasında" (between).
4. The "Failure" column shows the error code of the failed job. The job content and the raw error text are not shown.

### Player sign-in relations

1. In the "Player auth relations" card, type and select the player in the **Oyuncu** (Player) field.
2. Press **İlişkileri getir** (Fetch relations).
3. The "Provider accounts" table shows the player's linked sign-in accounts, and the "Devices" table shows device information and status. Revoked records are also listed. Long lists are paginated.

> [!NOTE]
> The job runner's health is not shown on this page: there is no persistent health signal source yet, so values such as "online" or lag are not made up. The "Worker health: gözlemlenemiyor" (Worker health: cannot be observed) card on the page says so.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Oyuncu (Player) | Yes (for İlişkileri getir) | The player whose relations will be seen |

### Job records table

Plugin / mesaj (Plugin / message; the plugin ID, the message and the schedule ID), Durum (Status), Attempt (the number of attempts), Deadline (the last time), Failure (the error code) and Oluşturulma (Created) are shown by default. Sonraki deneme (Next attempt), Bitiş (End) and Zamanlama kimliği (Schedule ID) are turned on from the column menu.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| It says "Operations yüzeyi yetki gerektiriyor" (The operations surface needs permission) | Your role has no job record read permission; ask an admin. |
| Player relations do not load | Player read permission is needed for this card; if you do not have it, you see a note. |
| A job is "dead" | The job closed with a permanent error or by reaching the retry limit. Look at the code in the Failure column together with the plugin's owner; it cannot be restarted from the panel. |
| Job records are empty | There is no scheduled plugin job in the selected environment, or the filter is too narrow. |
| I want to close a device | This page is read-only; close sessions from the [Player profile](player-profile.md) page. |

## Related docs

- [Account linking](../auth/account-linking.md)
- [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Panel admins
docs.description: Create the admin accounts that sign in to the panel; set their roles and the environments they can access, disable an account, and reset their sessions and two-step verification.
docs.body:
# Panel admins

## Purpose

This page lists and manages the admin accounts that sign in to the admin panel. An admin is the person who uses the panel, not a game player; for player accounts, see the [Players](players.md) page. Every admin has a role and a list of environments they can access. The page is open only to accounts that have permission to read admins.

## When to use

- To add a new admin to the team.
- To change an admin's role or environment access.
- To close the account of an admin who is leaving and end their sessions.
- To reset the two-step verification of an admin who lost their phone.

## Step by step

### Creating an admin

1. Press **Operatör oluştur** (Create operator). Only accounts with admin write permission see this button.
2. Enter at least one of email or username, the display name, the role and the temporary password.
3. Choose the environments they can access. By default, the environment currently selected comes preselected.
4. Write an **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason) and save. The admin's page opens.

### Changing the role and environments

1. Open the admin from the list and press **Düzenle** (Edit).
2. Change the display name, the role and the environments; write the reason and save. The email, username and password cannot be changed from this form.

### Disabling the account, sessions and 2FA

1. Use the "Güvenlik eylemleri" (Security actions) card on the admin's page.
2. **Devre dışı bırak** (Disable) rejects new sign-ins; open sessions must also be closed separately with **Oturumları revoke et** (Revoke sessions). **Etkinleştir** (Enable) opens the account again.
3. **2FA'yı sıfırla** (Reset 2FA) deletes the admin's authenticator and recovery codes and closes all their sessions. The admin signs in with the password only and must set up two-step verification again. To confirm, you type **your own** password.

> [!WARNING]
> You cannot disable your own account, close your own sessions or reset your own 2FA; this is blocked for security.

## Fields and options

### Roles

| Role | What it can do |
|---|---|
| super_admin | Has access to all environments and all admin actions; only this role manages admin accounts, studios, plugins and safety switches |
| game_manager | Manages game and player resources in the assigned environments; does most actions except admin accounts, studios, plugin management, safety switches, sign-in provider credentials and the admin details in the audit log |
| support | Does support in the assigned environments: reads players, sessions and chat; updates player information, bans, closes sessions, mutes in chat |
| read_only | Only reads in the assigned environments |

### Create and edit form

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| E-posta (Email) | No* | *At least one of email or username; only when creating |
| Kullanıcı adı (Username) | No* | 3-32 characters; only when creating |
| Görünen ad (Display name) | Yes | The name shown in the panel |
| Rol (Role) | Yes | One of the four roles |
| Geçici parola (Temporary password) | Yes (when creating) | At least 12 characters |
| Ortamlar (Environments) | Yes | The environments to be accessed |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | Yes | 8-500 characters |

### Columns in the list

Operatör (Operator), Rol (Role), Durum (Status; Etkin (Active) or Devre dışı (Disabled)), 2FA (Açık (On) or Kapalı (Off)), Scope (the number of environments that can be accessed), Son giriş (Last sign-in) and Oluşturulma (Created) are shown by default. You can turn on the E-posta (Email), Kullanıcı adı (Username) and Güncellenme (Updated) columns from the column menu.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| I cannot see the page | The permission to read admin accounts belongs only to the widest role; ask a super admin. |
| An environment is missing from the environment list | The list shows only environments you are also authorised for; widen your own access first. |
| An "E-posta ya da kullanıcı adı gerekli" error (Email or username required) | You cannot leave both empty. |
| A "Parola en az 12 karakter olmalı" error (The password must be at least 12 characters) | Write the temporary password with 12 or more characters. |
| The "2FA'yı sıfırla" button is missing | The admin's two-step verification is off, or you are looking at your own account. |
| An admin I disabled is still in the panel | Disabling blocks new sign-ins; close the open session with **Oturumları revoke et**. |

## Related docs

- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)
- [Authentication overview](../auth/overview.md)

docs.title: Player organizations
docs.description: Manage the organizations players have created (not studios), their members, invites, teams and dynamic roles; this screen is being retired.
docs.body:
# Player organizations

## Purpose

This page lists the organizations players have created and lets you manage the members, invites, teams and roles of the organization you select. An organization is not a studio; for studios, use the [Studios and games](tenancy.md) page.

> [!WARNING]
> This screen is being retired. It keeps working and is hidden in the menu by default; for new work, use [Clans](clans.md) for player groups.

## When to use

- To add members, invites, teams or roles to existing organizations.
- To fix or remove an organization.
- To inspect the organization data of an old setup.

## Step by step

### Creating an organization

1. Press **Organizasyon oluştur** (Create organization). Only admins with organization write permission see this button.
2. Fill in the **Ad** (Name) and **Plan** fields.
3. Write an **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason) and save. The organization's page opens.

### Inviting a member

1. On the organization page, on the **Üyeler** (Members) or **Davetler** (Invites) tab, press **Davetle üye ekle** (Add a member by invite) or **Davet oluştur** (Create invite).
2. Enter the email, the role and the expiry date; write the reason and save.
3. The invite appears on the **Davetler** tab. You can renew an expired or pending invite with a new expiry using **Yeniden gönder** (Resend), and make a pending invite unusable with **İptal** (Cancel).

> [!NOTE]
> The panel only creates and manages the invite record; it does not send the invite email.

### Changing a member's role

1. On the **Üyeler** tab, press **Düzenle** (Edit) in the member's row.
2. Choose the built-in role, add dynamic roles if needed, write the reason and save.
3. To remove the member, use **Çıkar** (Remove) in the row; to confirm, you type the member's name (or their email if there is no name).

### Managing teams and roles

1. On the **Takımlar** (Teams) tab, add a team with **Takım oluştur** (Create team); add one of the organization's members to the team with the **Üye** (Member) button.
2. On the **Roller** (Roles) tab, add a new role with **Dinamik rol oluştur** (Create dynamic role). Built-in roles (marked "Built-in") cannot be deleted or renamed.

## Fields and options

| Field | Window | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Ad, Plan (Name, Plan) | Organization | The name and the plan text (the plan is at most 64 characters) |
| Built-in rol, Dinamik roller (Built-in role, Dynamic roles) | Edit member | The built-in role and extra dynamic roles |
| E-posta, Rol, Son geçerlilik (Email, Role, Expiry) | Invite | The role is admin or member; validity is at most 30 days |
| Yeni son geçerlilik (New expiry) | Resend invite | The new expiry date |
| Takım adı (Team name) | Team | The team's name |
| Oyuncu (Player) | Add team member | One of the organization's members |
| Rol adı, Permissions JSON (Role name, Permissions JSON) | Dynamic role | The role name and the permissions object |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | All | 8-500 characters |
| Onay metni (Confirmation text) | Delete and remove | Type the record's name exactly; if there is no name, type "SİL" (DELETE) |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| I cannot see the page in the menu | It is hidden by default because it is being retired; turn on the "Gizlenen eski ekranları göster" (Show hidden legacy screens) switch in your account menu, or use the address directly. |
| The invite gives a validity error | The expiry date must be in the future and no more than 30 days away. |
| A "Permissions JSON" error | The permissions object must have the form `{ "resource": ["action"] }`; actions cannot be empty or repeated. |
| I cannot add a player to a team | Only the organization's members can be added to a team; add them as a member first. |
| I cannot delete a built-in role | Built-in roles cannot be deleted; only dynamic roles can. |

## Related docs

- [Clans and parties](../guides/social.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Parties
docs.description: Inspect, read-only, the parties players have created, their members, invites and the results of reward distributions.
docs.body:
# Parties

## Purpose

This page lists the parties in the selected environment; it shows the members and invites of the party you select, and the result of a reward distribution. The page is **read-only**: you cannot form a party, remove a member or distribute a reward from the panel. Party actions are done from the game, through server calls.

## When to use

- To see a party's members, leader and loot rule.
- To understand, from the invite status, why a player could not join a party.
- To verify the amount, status and delivery mode of a reward distribution.

## Step by step

### Inspecting a party

1. Make sure you selected the right game and environment.
2. In the "Party roster" table, filter by status, capacity, loot rule or date. When the page opens, the newest party is selected automatically.
3. To select another party, click its name or open the row.
4. In the "Party detay ve ilişkiler" (Party details and relations) card you see the leader, the loot rule, the capacity, the members and the invites.

### Looking up a reward distribution

1. Have a party selected.
2. In the "Reward distribution lookup" card, paste the distribution's UUID into the **Dağıtım kimliği** (Distribution ID) field.
3. Press **Yükle** (Load). If the ID is not a valid UUID, no request is sent and an error appears next to the field.
4. The result shows the amount, the status and the delivery mode. The raw reward content is not shown.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Dağıtım kimliği (Distribution ID) | Yes (for Yükle) | The reward distribution's UUID; it belongs to the selected party, and the field resets when the party changes |

### Columns in the list

Party (a shortened ID), Durum (Status), Üye (Members; "member count/capacity"), Ganimet kuralı (Loot rule), Lider (Leader) and Oluşturulma (Created) are shown by default. You can turn on the Kapasite (Capacity) and Güncellenme (Updated) columns from the column menu. The status is "active" or "disbanded", and the loot rule is "equal" or "weighted". In the member and invite tables, the "Pay" (Share) column shows each record's reward share as a percentage.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The list looks empty | Check that you selected the right environment and that no filters are active. |
| "Dağıtım kimliği 8-4-4-4-12 biçiminde olmalı" error (The distribution ID must be in 8-4-4-4-12 form) | Copy the ID completely, with its dashes, and make sure there are no extra characters at the start or end. |
| The distribution cannot be found | The ID may belong to another party or environment; make sure you selected the right party. |
| I cannot change the party from the panel | The page is read-only; party actions are done from the game or through server calls. |

## Related docs

- [Clans and parties](../guides/social.md)
- [Rewards](../guides/rewards.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Player profile
docs.description: Inspect a player's account, sessions, sign-in history and bans; edit the profile, manage the password, ban or delete the player.
docs.body:
# Player profile

## Purpose

This page shows a single player's account: status, account type, last sign-in, open session count, total play time and main currency balance. In the tabs below you see the player's characters, wallet, sessions, sign-in history, bans, linked accounts and action history. You get here from the [Players](players.md) list.

## When to use

- To check an account's status while looking into a player's help request.
- To fix the player's name, email or extra information.
- To reset the password or convert a guest to a permanent account.
- To ban a player who broke the rules, lift a ban or delete the account.
- To close a player's open sessions or remove a linked sign-in method.

## Step by step

### Inspecting

1. Pick one of the tabs: **Genel** (General), **Karakterler** (Characters), **Cüzdan ve envanter** (Wallet and inventory), **Oyun süresi** (Play time), **Oturumlar** (Sessions), **Giriş geçmişi** (Sign-in history), **Yasaklar** (Bans), **Hesaplar** (Accounts), **Geçmiş** (History). Tabs your role cannot see, or whose module is disabled, are hidden or show a "yetki gerekir" (permission required) note.
2. On the **Genel** tab you see the profile information, recent security events and extra information (metadata).

### Editing the profile

1. Press **Profili düzenle** (Edit profile). Only admins with edit permission see this button.
2. Change the display name, the email, the email verification state, the image and the extra information. Only the fields you changed are saved.
3. Fill in the **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason) field at the bottom of the page and save. If you try to leave the page without saving, the panel warns you.

### Managing the password

1. On a registered account, from the **Diğer işlemler** (More actions) menu, give a new password with **Parola yönet** (Manage password) (at least 12 characters), or ask the system to generate one with **Rastgele parola üret** (Generate a random password).
2. On a guest account, the **Hesaba çevir** (Convert to account) action gives the guest an email and a one-time random password.
3. The generated password is shown **only once** and cannot be retrieved again. Pass it to the player through a secure channel; the **Gizle** (Hide) button, or changing the tab or page, wipes the password from memory. Generating a password and converting close the open sessions.

### Banning and lifting a ban

1. From the **Diğer işlemler** menu, choose **Banla** (Ban) (if the player is already banned, **Yasağı düzenle** (Edit ban) and **Banı kaldır** (Lift ban) appear).
2. Choose the duration, write the optional ban reason and the action reason, and press **Banla**.
3. All the player's sessions are closed and they cannot sign in again. When you lift the ban, the player can sign in again, but the sessions that were closed do not come back.

### Sessions, account links and deletion

1. On the **Oturumlar** tab you can revoke a single session, and from the **Diğer işlemler** menu you can choose **Tüm oturumları kapat** (Close all sessions).
2. On the **Hesaplar** tab you can remove the link to a sign-in method. If you remove the last sign-in method, the player cannot sign in; check the other methods first.
3. The **Oyuncuyu sil** (Delete player) action marks the account as deleted and closes it to access; the record is not destroyed completely. There is no button in the panel that undoes a deletion. To confirm, you type the player's name (or their email if there is no name).

> [!WARNING]
> All these actions are written to the immutable audit log. Deleting and closing sessions affect the player immediately.

## Fields and options

### Profile edit form

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Görünen ad (Display name) | Yes | The player's display name |
| E-posta (Email) | No | If empty, the email is removed; needs a separate permission |
| E-posta doğrulandı (Email verified) | No | The address counts as verified; needs a separate permission |
| Görsel URL (Image URL) | No | The address of the player's image |
| Metadata JSON | No | A JSON object |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | Yes | 8-500 characters |

### Ban window

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Süre (Duration) | Yes | 1, 3, 7, 30 days, permanent or a custom date and time (at most 365 days) |
| Yasak gerekçesi (Ban reason) | No | At most 200 characters; visible only on admin screens |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | Yes | 8-500 characters |

### Password windows

| Field | Window | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Yeni parola (New password) | Parola yönet | At least 12 characters |
| E-posta (Email) | Hesaba çevir | The account's sign-in email |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | All | At most 200 characters in the password and convert windows |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The email field is disabled | Your role has no permission to change the email and verification; ask an admin. You can still change the display name. |
| "Profili düzenle", "Banla" or "Parola yönet" is missing | The matching permission is not in your role. The buttons are visible only to authorised admins. |
| I lost the generated password | The password is not shown again; start the action again and generate a new password. |
| A "Parola daha önce gösterildi" (The password was shown before) note appeared | The same action had already been completed; start the action again for a new password. |
| A player I banned still shows a session | A ban closes all sessions; refresh the **Oturumlar** tab and check their status. |
| A metadata error | Enter a valid JSON object; an array or plain text is not accepted. |

## Related docs

- [Authentication overview](../auth/overview.md)
- [Account linking](../auth/account-linking.md)
- [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)
