docs.description: Search, filter and inspect your game's player accounts, and create a new account by hand if you need to.
docs.body:
# Players

## Purpose

This page lists the player accounts of the selected game and environment. Use it to find a player, check an account's status, open a profile and, if needed, create a new account by hand. In the left menu this page appears as "Oyuncular" (Players).

## When to use

- To find a player's account when they ask for help.
- To filter banned or suspicious accounts.
- To create a player account by hand for testing.

## Step by step

### Finding a player

1. Make sure the environment selector at the top of the page shows the right game and environment. The list shows only the selected environment.
2. Type the player's name or email in the table's search box.
3. Use the table's filter menu to narrow the list by status, sign-in method or date.
4. Click the row, or press **Detay** (Details), to open the profile.

### Creating an account by hand

1. Press **Kullanıcı oluştur** (Create user). Only admins who are allowed to create accounts see this button.
2. Enter the display name. Email, password and extra information are optional.
3. Write a short reason in the **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason) field.
4. Save with the **Kullanıcı oluştur** button. The account appears in the list.

> [!NOTE]
> Players usually sign in from the game on their own. Use this form only for testing and support.

## Fields and options

### Account creation form

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Görünen ad (Display name) | Yes | The player's display name; at least 2 characters |
| E-posta (Email) | No | The player's email address |
| E-posta doğrulandı (Email verified) | No | Makes the address count as verified |
| Geçici parola (Temporary password) | No | At least 12 characters; if empty, no password account is created |
| Metadata JSON | No | Extra information, a JSON object |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | Yes | The reason written to the audit log, 8-500 characters |

### Columns in the list

The columns Kullanıcı (User), Durum (Status), Giriş yöntemi (Sign-in method), Aktif oturum (Active sessions), Son giriş (Last sign-in) and Oluşturulma (Created) are shown by default. You can turn on the columns E-posta (Email), Oyuncu kimliği (Player ID), Hesap türü (Account type), Güncellenme (Updated) and E-posta doğrulandı (Email verified) from the table's column menu.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The list looks empty | Check that you selected the right environment and that no filters are active. |
| I cannot find the player | Guest accounts have no email; search by name or ID, or use the sign-in method. |
| The "Kullanıcı oluştur" button is missing | Your account's role cannot create accounts; ask an admin. |
| The form shows a "metadata" error | Enter a valid JSON object; an array or plain text is not accepted. |

## Related docs

- [Authentication overview](../auth/overview.md)
- [Account linking](../auth/account-linking.md)
- [Security](../operations/security.md)

docs.title: Plugin page
docs.description: Explains how the screens a game's plugin defines in the panel work, how actions are performed and what the status warnings mean.
docs.body:
# Plugin page

## Purpose

A game's plugin can define its own admin screens in the panel: player lists, filtered tables, detail pages, charts and action buttons. This page is the shared help for all of those screens; plugin-specific content comes from the plugin's own definition and is not described here.

## When to use

- To understand what will happen when you search, paginate or perform an action on a plugin screen.
- To learn what the status warnings at the top of the screen mean.

## Step by step

### Getting to know the screen

1. The page title is the plugin's name; the second heading below it is the screen's name. The plugin's screens are listed in tabs under the title.
2. The **Yenile** (Refresh) button re-reads only this screen's data.
3. The **Son okuma** (Last read) line under the title shows when the data was read.

### Moving around lists and tables

- The list narrows as you type in the search box; the search text and page number stay in the address bar, so you can share the link.
- In the paginator you can choose 12, 25 or 50 rows from the **Sayfa başına** (Per page) list.
- If there is a **CSV indir** (Download CSV) button, it downloads the rows loaded on the screen as a file; in a paginated table it contains only the loaded page.

### Performing an action

1. Press the action button on the screen; a window opens. Only admins with the plugin operation permission see or can use the button.
2. Fill in the fields, write your reason in the **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason) field and confirm.
3. The result appears on screen; the action is written to the audit log.

> [!NOTE]
> The plugin's state appears as a warning at the top of the screen. In the **Salt okunur** (Read-only) state data is visible but changes cannot be made; in the **Boşaltılıyor** (Draining) state new operations are not accepted and open operations finish. An admin changes the state on the [Plugins](./plugins.md) page.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Search | No | Searches in the fields the plugin defines |
| Per page | No | 12, 25 or 50 |
| Action reason (action window) | Yes | Limits are written under the field |
| Action fields | Depends on the action | Defined by the plugin; each field's description is written in the window |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "This plugin is read-only in this environment" | The plugin is open for reading only. If you need changes, ask an admin to set the state to on on the [Plugins](./plugins.md) page. |
| "This plugin is being drained" | Before a version change the plugin accepts no new operations; it will return to the on state when draining ends. |
| The action button is missing or disabled | You do not have the plugin operation permission, or the plugin is read-only. |
| There is a "being deprecated" banner at the top of the screen | The screen is being replaced by a new screen; the link in the banner takes you to the replacement. |
| The action says "another change was made" | The record changed while you were looking. See its current state and confirm again. |

## Related docs

- [Plugins overview](../plugins/overview.md)
- [Calling plugins](../plugins/calling-plugins.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Plugins
docs.description: See the game's plugin and the other plugins authorized in the selected environment; an authorized admin can change a plugin's state.
headings: Bind a plugin to the game and move to a new version
docs.body:
# Plugins

## Purpose

A plugin is the module that runs the game's server-side logic: it offers game-specific commands, queries and panel screens. This page shows the game's plugin, the other plugins authorized in the selected environment and the state of each. You reach a plugin's admin screens from here and from the sidebar.

## When to use

- To see whether a plugin is on in this environment.
- To make a plugin temporarily read-only, drain it or turn it off (authorized admin).
- To inspect a plugin's version, permissions, operations and dependencies.
- To bind a plugin to the game or move to a new version.

## Step by step

### See a plugin's details

The card's **Ayrıntılar** (Details) button lists the version, permissions, dependencies and the operations the plugin offers (query or command, who can access). The information is read from the plugin's own declaration; it cannot be changed from here.

### Change a plugin's state

1. Press the card's **Durumu değiştir** (Change state) button. Only admins with the plugin management permission see the button.
2. Choose the target from the **Yeni durum** (New state) list; the player and admin effect of the state you choose is written in the window.
3. Write your reason and press **Durumu değiştir**. If you choose **Kapalı** (Off), a confirmation is also asked.

Transitions are limited: from On you can go to read-only, draining or off; from read-only and draining to on or off; from off to read-only or on.

### Bind a plugin to the game and move to a new version

The game plugin card at the top of the page is for these operations:

1. If no plugin is bound, choose the plugin from the list with **Eklenti bağla** (Bind plugin) and bind it.
2. To move to a newly built version, first drain players with **Drain başlat** (Start drain); type the plugin ID to confirm.
3. When the countdown ends, deploy the new version, then press **Sürüme geç** (Switch to version). The button is disabled until the countdown ends.

> [!WARNING]
> In the **Kapalı** (Off) state, players and admins cannot use the plugin in this environment and the plugin disappears from the sidebar. To turn it back on you must change the state separately.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| New state | Yes | On, Read-only, Draining or Off |
| Action reason | Yes | 8-500 characters |
| Plugin (bind window) | Yes | One of the plugins installed on the server |
| Plugin ID (drain window) | Yes | The ID must be typed exactly |

The badge at the top of the card shows the plugin's state in this environment. If it says "Bu ortamda yetkisiz" (Not authorized in this environment), the plugin is installed but there is no grant row for this environment; the plugin cannot be used here.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Kurulu eklenti yok" (No plugin installed) | The server was started without plugins. Plugins are added to the server build and activated by the operator. |
| The card has a warning "Yetki sürümü ... kurulu sürüm ..." (Grant version ... installed version ...) | The environment's grant does not match the installed version; version activation is pending. In this case only draining and turning off can be chosen. |
| "Bu durum geçişine izin verilmiyor" (This state transition is not allowed) | The state may have changed while you were looking; refresh the page and try again. |
| The **Durumu değiştir** button is missing | You do not have the plugin management permission; ask an admin. |
| The **Ekranları aç** (Open screens) button is missing | The plugin defines no panel screen, or it is off in this environment. |
| A "Kullanımdan kalkan sorgular" (Deprecated queries) box appears | Some of the plugin's queries have been replaced by a new surface. In the box you see the old name, its replacement and since which version it was deprecated; move your game code to the new surface. |

## Related docs

- [Plugins overview](../plugins/overview.md)
- [Calling plugins](../plugins/calling-plugins.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Reward table
docs.description: See and edit a reward table's rows and chances, try it without saving or create a new table.
docs.body:
# Reward table

## Purpose

This page shows a single reward table; the same page also works as the form for creating and editing the table. A table has two parts: **chance rows** (one is picked in each draw) and **always given** rewards (given every time, independent of the draw). You can try the table before saving it.

## When to use

- To set up a new reward table for an NPC, creature, tournament or mission.
- To change chances or amounts.
- To see where the table is used and the latest rewards given.

## Step by step

### Create a new table

1. On the [Reward tables](reward-tables.md) page press **Yeni ödül tablosu** (New reward table).
2. Write the **Ad** (Name) and the **Anahtar** (Key); the key does not change after saving.
3. Choose **Kaç çekiliş** (How many draws).
4. Enter the reward rows with **Satır ekle** (Add row): kind, what it gives, minimum and maximum amount and chance. You can reorder rows with the up and down arrows.
5. Complete the sum of the chances to 100%. The total is shown live under the rows; with **Kalanı 'Ödül yok' yap** (Make the rest 'No reward') you can give the remainder to a "no reward" row.
6. If you wish, add draw-independent rewards to the **Her zaman verilenler** (Always given) section.
7. Try the table without saving from the **Dene** (Try) panel on the right.
8. Write a reason and press **Ödül tablosunu oluştur** (Create reward table).

### Edit the table

1. On the table's page press **Düzenle** (Edit).
2. Change the rows and press **Yeni sürüm olarak kaydet** (Save as a new version). Each save is a new version; old versions are not deleted and appear in the version history.

### Try the table

The **Dene** button runs 100 sample draws with the table without saving and summarizes which reward came up how many times. No reward is given and the result changes with every try. If the form is incomplete (for example the chances are not 100%) the button is disabled.

### Delete the table

Press **Sil** (Delete) and write a reason. If the table is used by an NPC rule, mission or content entry it cannot be deleted; the window lists the places that use it. Rewards given in the past are not deleted.

## Fields and options

### Table information

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Yes | At most 120 characters |
| Key | When creating | Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores; does not change later |
| How many draws | Yes | 1-10 |

### Chance rows (at most 50)

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Reward kind | Money, Item or No reward |
| What | Currency or item |
| Min, Max | Amount range; if max is empty it is the same as min |
| Chance % | The row's chance of coming up; the total must be exactly 100% |

### Always given (at most 10)

Made of the Reward kind (Money or Item), What, Min and Max fields; there is no chance.

### Cards on the profile page

- **Şans çubukları** (Chance bars), **Her zaman verilenler** (Always given), **Kaç çekiliş** (How many draws).
- **Nerede kullanılıyor** (Where it is used): NPC rules, missions and content entries that use the table.
- **Son verilen ödüller** (Latest rewards given): The latest rewards given from the table; player, source and reward.
- **Sürüm geçmişi** (Version history): Each version's date and row count; the current one has a badge.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Kaydetmek için toplam %100 olmalı" (The total must be 100% to save) | Bring the sum of the chances to exactly 100%; for the missing remainder you can use a "No reward" row. |
| "Kaydetmek için en az bir ödül ekleyin" (Add at least one reward to save) | At least one chance row or one "always given" reward is needed. |
| "Bu anahtarla bir ödül tablosu zaten var" (A reward table with this key already exists) | Choose another key; to change the existing table, open it and use **Düzenle**. |
| I cannot delete the table | The table is in use; detach it from the places that use it first. The delete window shows where it is used. |
| I get an amount error | Write a money amount in the currency's decimal format; the minimum is 1 and the maximum is 1,000,000 of the smallest unit. |
| "Dene" is disabled | Complete what is missing in the form; the chances must be 100%. |

## Related docs

- [Reward tables](reward-tables.md)
- [Currencies](currencies.md)
- [Rewards guide](../guides/rewards.md)

docs.title: Reward tables
docs.description: Tables that tie NPC, creature, tournament and mission rewards to chance.
docs.body:
# Reward tables

## Purpose

A reward table defines which reward an NPC, creature, tournament or mission gives and with what chance. This page lists all the tables in the environment as cards: name, key, row count, the number of "always given" rewards and how many places the table is used in.

## When to use

- To create a new reward table.
- To quickly look at where a table is used or how many rows it has.
- To open, edit, try or delete a table (click the card; see [Reward table](reward-table-profile.md)).

## Step by step

1. Choose the right game and environment from the environment selector at the top.
2. Press **Yeni ödül tablosu** (New reward table). Only admins with reward table write permission see the button.
3. Fill in the form using the instructions on the [Reward table](reward-table-profile.md) page.
4. When you save, the table is added to the list.

> [!NOTE]
> A table does not give rewards by itself. A reward is given when an NPC, mission or rule calls the table by its key; see the [Rewards guide](../guides/rewards.md) for details.

## Fields and options

There is no form field to fill in on this page; the create form is described on the [Reward table](reward-table-profile.md) page. The information shown on the card:

| Information | Description |
|---|---|
| Name and key | The table's name and the ID the game calls it with |
| Rows | The number of chance-based reward rows |
| Always given | The number of rewards given every time, independent of the draw |
| Usage | How many places the table is used in; "Kullanılmıyor" (Not used) if it is not used at all |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Ödüller bu ortamda kapalı" (Rewards are off in this environment) | The Rewards module is off; turn it on from the Modules tab in Game settings. |
| "Henüz ödül tablosu yok" (No reward table yet) | Create the first one with **Yeni ödül tablosu**. |
| The New table button is missing | Your account's role has no reward table write permission. |

## Related docs

- [Reward table](reward-table-profile.md)
- [Currencies](currencies.md)
- [Rewards guide](../guides/rewards.md)

docs.title: Rules
docs.description: Set how the game reacts to events from here. Changes reach the game when you release them; every release can be rolled back.
headings: Turn an automation on and off
docs.body:
# Rules

## Purpose

This page is where you tune your game's behavior without writing code. You see two kinds of things: **game rule cards** offered by the game's plugin (for example police or city crowd values) and **automations** you write (such as "add power to the character when it reaches level 10"). Changes do not reach the game until you release them; every release can be rolled back.

## When to use

- To tune the game's built-in settings (speed, duration, density and so on) without changing code.
- To automatically give a character a reward, points or a flag when a game event happens.
- To return a wrongly released setting to the previous version ([Rule history](./rules-history.md)).

## Step by step

### Change a game rule

1. Click a card in the list; the card's settings page opens ([Rule card](./rules-game-card.md)).
2. Change the value. The change does not reach the game yet; an "N changes not released" bar appears at the bottom of the page.
3. You can move to other cards and change their settings too. All pending changes go into a single release.
4. Press **Gözden geçir ve yayınla** (Review and release), write your reason and confirm.

### Add an automation

1. Press **Yeni kural** (New rule), or use **Şablondan başla** (Start from a template) if the list is empty.
2. In the automation editor choose the event, the conditions and the action ([Automation editor](./rules-automation-editor.md)).
3. Release. The rule is saved **off** by default; when it is ready, you turn it on with the **Aç** (Turn on) button in the list.

### Turn an automation on and off

The **Aç** or **Kapat** (Turn off) button on the right of the card opens a confirmation window. Write your reason and confirm; a rule that is turned off stops running in the game, it is not deleted.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Kural ara (Search rules) | No | Searches the card title, description and automation key |
| Topic buttons | No | Narrow the list to the topics you choose; if none is selected, all are shown |
| Action reason (on/off window) | Yes | 8-500 characters; written to the audit log |

The status strip at the top shows the live version, who released it and the reason they wrote. If nothing has been released yet, it says "the game runs with today's (code) values".

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| It says "this game's plugin does not offer rules adjustable from the panel" | The game's plugin does not declare any rule card. You can still add automations from this page. |
| It says "you do not have permission to see rules" | Your role has no rule read permission; ask an admin. |
| The **Yeni kural** button is missing | Only admins with rule write permission see the button. |
| A card has an "Gözlemde" (Under observation) badge | The rule's protection is loosened; the rule is not applied to the game, only recorded. See [Safety switches](./safety-switches.md). |
| A card has a "Yeniden başlatınca" (On restart) badge | The value is released but the live world takes the new value when the server restarts. |
| Where are the notification rules? | Notification rules are on a separate screen; open it from the **Bildirimler** (Notifications) card at the bottom of the page. |

## Related docs

- [Game rules guide](../guides/game-rules.md)
- [Notifications guide](../guides/notifications.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Automation editor
docs.description: An optional note saying what the rule is for (at most 500 characters). It is only a reminder for other admins on the team; it does not affect the game.
docs.body:
# Automation editor

## Purpose

An automation is a rule in the form "when this event happens, if this condition is true, do this". This page lets you set the rule up in three steps: **Ne zaman** (When: which event), **Koşullar** (Conditions: in which situation) and **Ne yap** (What to do: what to do to the character). You do not need to write code; the panel prepares the rule behind the scenes for you.

## When to use

- To define automatic results such as a reward on level up, or a permanent boost when a certain ability opens.
- To change an existing rule's condition or action and release a new version.
- To try the rule with a character and a sample event before releasing it.

## Step by step

1. On the [Rules](./rules.md) page press **Yeni kural** (New rule). For a new rule you can first choose a ready example from the **Şablondan başla** (Start from a template) section, or start with **Boş kural** (Empty rule).
2. Write a name in the **Kural** (Rule) section; the key is generated automatically.
3. Choose the event in the **Ne zaman** section.
4. In the **Koşullar** section add a condition with **Koşul ekle** (Add condition). If you add no condition, the rule runs every time the event happens. With more than one condition, choose "all" or "any".
5. Leave at least one action in the **Ne yap** section; you can add one with **Eylem ekle** (Add action) and change the order with the arrow.
6. If you wish, with the **Kuralı dene** (Try the rule) button choose a character and a sample event and see the result. The try creates no record.
7. In the **Dene ve yayınla** (Try and release) section write your reason. For a new rule, optionally tick the **Hemen açılsın** (Turn on immediately) box and press **Yayınla** (Release).

When you edit an existing rule, a **Yeni sürüm yayınla** (Release new version) button appears; the key does not change.

> [!NOTE]
> A released rule is saved **off** by default. The **Aç** button in the Rules list or the **Hemen açılsın** box makes it run.

> [!WARNING]
> The trait, resource, flag and ability names you write in conditions and actions must be exactly the same as the game's own names. A wrongly written name prevents the rule from working as you expect; before releasing, see the result on a real character with **Kuralı dene**.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Rule name | Yes | 1-120 characters |
| Key | Yes | Generated from the name, at most 64 characters; does not change after release |
| Description | No | At most 500 characters |
| When | Yes | Event choice (level up, resource change, flag change and so on) |
| Conditions join | With more than one condition | All / any |
| What is looked at, which information, name, comparison, value, state | When a condition is added | At most 20 conditions; whole numbers in number fields |
| What to do, name, amount, state | Yes (at least one action) | At most 10 actions; the amount cannot be zero |
| Operation, value, source kind, source name | In boost actions | In percentage operations the value is 100 times the percentage |
| Priority | Yes | A whole number from 1 to 1000, default 100; in the "Gelişmiş" (Advanced) section |
| Character, sample event information | In the try | Affects only the try |
| Why are you changing it? | Yes | 8-500 characters |
| Turn on immediately | No | Shown only on a new rule |

The **Gelişmiş** section shows the CEL (condition language) equivalent of the rule's condition read-only; the panel generates it itself from the condition rows and it is not edited here.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| A "Yayınlamadan önce tamamlayın" (Complete before releasing) list appears | Fill in the missing fields in the list; the release button stays disabled until they are done. |
| "Bu anahtarla bir kural zaten var" (A rule with this key already exists) | Change the rule name or the key. |
| "Bu arada başka bir değişiklik yayınlandı" (Another change was released in the meantime) | Your edits are kept. Press **Son durumu yükle** (Load the latest state) and release again. |
| "Kural kabul edilmedi" (The rule was not accepted) | The server rejected the rule; fix it according to the messages in the list. The values you entered are kept. |
| I cannot change the rule's condition, it says "written in code (CEL)" | The rule was written in code outside the panel. It is displayed in the panel, turned on and off and rolled back to an old version but cannot be edited. |
| The edit fields are disabled | You do not have the rule write permission; ask an admin. |
| The try says "choose a character" | To try you must choose a character from the character search. |

## Related docs

- [Game rules and automations](../guides/game-rules.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Rule card
docs.description: See when a game rule you chose runs and change its settings; a change does not reach the game until it is released.
docs.body:
# Rule card

## Purpose

This page shows the detail of a single game rule: **when** the rule runs, which **conditions** it has, **what it does** and which values you tune. Changes you make here do not reach the game immediately; they pile up at the bottom of the page and are applied together with a single release. What the rule is for is written by the game's plugin; the page's title and texts come from the plugin.

## When to use

- To change a rule's value (duration, distance, speed threshold and so on).
- To see the result of a change before releasing with the **Ne değişir?** (What changes?) preview.
- To temporarily put the rule's protection under observation or turn it back on.

## Step by step

1. On the [Rules](./rules.md) page click a card.
2. Read the **Ne zaman** (When), **Koşullar** (Conditions) and **Ne yap** (What to do) sections. Conditions with a lock icon cannot be changed.
3. In the **Ne yap** section change a value. The field shows the value with its unit (for example seconds or km/h); you can write a decimal number with a comma. Under it the allowed range and default value are written; the **Varsayılana dön** (Reset to default) button returns the value to its old state.
4. If you wish, in the **Ne değişir?** card on the right, choose a scenario and press **Önizle** (Preview). The card shows the order of events side by side with the "now" and "new" values.
5. In the bar at the bottom of the page press **Gözden geçir ve yayınla** (Review and release). In the window that opens, check the list of changes, write your reason and press **Yayınla** (Release).

> [!NOTE]
> Pending changes stay only in this browser tab. If you refresh the page or close the tab, unreleased changes are lost. Moving to other cards does not delete them.

> [!WARNING]
> Some values are applied right after release, others when the server restarts. If you see a "Yayında: … · Bekliyor: …" (Live: ... · Pending: ...) line on the card, the value is released but the live world is still using the old value.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Setting value | No | A row for each of the card's settings; a value outside the range is not accepted |
| Rule switch ("Bu kural açık", This rule is on) | No | Shown only on cards that have a switch; needs write permission |
| Scenario (preview) | No | One of the sample situations the card offers |
| Scenario numbers (preview) | No | Vary by scenario; limits are written under the field |
| Neden değiştiriyorsunuz? (Why are you changing it?) (release window) | Yes | 8-500 characters |

Badges on the card: **Açık** (On: the protection is applied), **Gözlemde** (Under observation: the rule is not applied to the game), **Değiştirildi** (Changed: the live value differs from the default), **Yayınlanmadı** (Not released: there is a pending edit), **Yeniden başlatınca** (On restart: the live world takes the value on restart).

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The setting fields are disabled and say "no permission" | You can read the values but changing them needs the game rules publish permission; ask an admin. |
| The release says "another change was released" | Someone else released while you were looking. Press **Son durumu yükle** (Load the latest state); your edits are kept and the difference is recomputed. |
| The release says "some values were not accepted" | Click the setting name in the list; the page goes to that field. Fix it according to the limit in the message and release again. |
| It says "Bu kural bulunamadı" (This rule was not found) | The card ID is not in this game's catalog; reopen it from the [Rules](./rules.md) page. |
| The preview says "none" | This card has no preview scenario; check the values carefully before releasing. |

## Related docs

- [Game rules and automations](../guides/game-rules.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Rule history
docs.description: See the full list of game rule releases, check what each version changed and go back to an older version if needed.
headings: Go back to an older version
docs.body:
# Rule history

## Purpose

Every game rule release is a new **version**. This page lists versions from newest to oldest: who released, when, for what reason and which settings changed. Going back to an older version also writes a new version; history is never deleted.

## When to use

- To quickly undo a wrongly released setting.
- To find out when and by whom a setting was changed.
- To return all settings to the game's built-in (code) values.

## Step by step

### See what a version changed

1. Click the **Değişen ayarlar** (Changed settings) line under the version.
2. For each setting you see "previous value → new value". A version that changed no setting says so explicitly.

### Go back to an older version

1. Press **Bu sürüme dön** (Go back to this version) on the row of the version you want to return to. This button is not shown on the live version.
2. In the window that opens, write your reason and press **Geri al** (Roll back).
3. That version's values are released as a new version. Police settings take effect within 6 seconds at most.

### Return to the built-in (code) values

1. Press **Bugünkü (kod) değerlere döndür** (Reset to today's code values) at the top of the page.
2. Write your reason and confirm with **Kod değerlerine döndür** (Reset to code values). All settings return to the game's defaults; this is also a new version.

> [!NOTE]
> A rollback appears in the list with a badge such as "rolled back to version 7". No version is deleted; only a new version is added.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Action reason (rollback window) | Yes | 8-500 characters |

Badges on a row: **Yayında** (Live: the version in effect now), **Geri alındı** (Rolled back) or **Sürüm N'e geri alındı** (Rolled back to version N), **Kod değerlerine döndürüldü** (Reset to code values).

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| There are no rollback buttons | Rolling back needs the game rules publish permission; you can still read the history. Ask an admin. |
| It says "Henüz yayın yok" (No release yet) | Settings are at the game's default values; versions appear here after the first release. |
| The rollback was rejected with "another change was released" | Someone else released while you were looking. The page re-reads the current state; look at the current version and confirm again. |
| I cannot see older versions | The list loads page by page; press **Daha eski sürümler** (Older versions) at the end. |

## Related docs

- [Game rules and automations](../guides/game-rules.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Safety switches
docs.description: Loosen or force back the game's protection rules in this environment without a deploy; every change is written to the audit log with a reason.
docs.body:
# Safety switches

## Purpose

A safety switch lets you loosen one of the game's protection rules. In the **Zorla** (Enforce) position the rule is applied to the game. In the loose position the rule is not applied to the game or is only recorded; its raw setting reads "put under observation", "off" or "disabled". You change a switch per environment and reversibly, without redeploying the server.

## When to use

- To loosen a protection rule temporarily when it blocks players unfairly.
- To see that a rule is only being recorded (under observation) and enforce it again.
- To audit which protections are loose.

## Step by step

1. On each row you see the switch's name, what it does, its position (**Zorla** (Enforce), **Gözleme alındı** (Under observation), **Kapalı** (Off), **Devre dışı** (Disabled)), its source and its last change.
2. To loosen a protection that is in the Enforce position, press **Gevşet** (Loosen). In the window that opens, read the effect, write your reason and confirm with **Gevşet**.
3. To turn a loose protection back on, press **Zorla**; it does not ask for confirmation.
4. To return a switch changed from the panel to the deployment default, press **Varsayılana dön** (Reset to default).

The source badge on the row shows where the switch's value comes from: **panel** (you changed it), **dağıtım varsayılanı** (deployment default) or **yalnız dağıtım** (deployment only: settings that cannot be changed from the panel). Deployment-only rows are shown read-only.

> [!NOTE]
> A change is applied on every server replica within a few seconds at most (the time stated on the page); there is no instant effect or instant push.

> [!WARNING]
> A loose protection means the related rule is not applied to the game or is only recorded. The warning banner at the top of the page says how many protections are loose. A read error never loosens a protection; the page shows an error.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Action reason (loosen window) | Yes | 8-500 characters |

The counter card at the bottom of the page shows runtime counters; only admins with that permission see it.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| There are no buttons and it says "read-only" | Only a super admin can change switches; you can read the values. |
| "Güvenlik şalterleri okunamadı" (Safety switches could not be read) | The list could not be loaded. Protections are not treated as loosened; read again with **Tekrar dene** (Try again). |
| I see an "Gözlemde" (Under observation) badge on a rule card | That card's switch is loose. Turn it back on with **Zorla** from this page or from the card page on the [Rules](./rules.md) page. |
| It changed without asking for a reason | The Force and Reset to default buttons do not ask for a reason; a fixed reason such as "operator set the switch to Enforce (panel)" is written to the audit record. |

## Related docs

- [Game rules and automations](../guides/game-rules.md)
- [Security](../operations/security.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: City chat
docs.description: Read the city chat, delete a harmful message and mute its author for a set time; every action is written to the audit log with a reason.
docs.body:
# City chat

## Purpose

This page shows the messages written to the game's city chat and lets you moderate: you can delete the text of a harmful message, mute the player who wrote it for a set time and lift active mutes. Message text is shown as plain text. Messages are kept for 30 days and then deleted automatically.

## When to use

- To find and inspect a message when a complaint about a player comes in about chat.
- To delete a swear word, spam or a harmful message.
- To mute a player who broke the rules for a while.

> [!NOTE]
> This page works only if the plugin attached to the selected game provides scene chat. If it does not, the text "Bu oyunda sahne sohbeti yok" (There is no scene chat in this game) appears. In the menu it appears only for such games.

## Step by step

### Deleting a message

1. Find the message on the **Aktarım** (Transcript) tab. You can filter the table by room, author, account type, deleted or not, and time; the newest message is at the top.
2. Press **Sil** (Delete) in the row.
3. Write an **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason) and confirm with **Mesajı sil** (Delete the message). The message text is deleted; its length stays in the record and the row shows "Silindi · N karakter" (Deleted · N characters). This cannot be undone.

### Muting a player

1. Press **Yazarı sustur** (Mute the author) in the message's row.
2. Choose the duration from the **Süre** (Duration) list. If you choose "Özel bitiş…" (Custom end…), enter the end time.
3. Write an **İşlem nedeni** and press **Sustur** (Mute). The player's messages are rejected; the player is not told the reason and their session is not dropped.

### Lifting a mute

1. Open the **Aktif susturmalar** (Active mutes) tab. Mutes that have run out leave the list automatically.
2. Press **Susturmayı kaldır** (Lift the mute) in the row, write the reason and confirm. The player can write again immediately.

> [!WARNING]
> A guest account can get around a mute by creating a new guest. The lasting fix is to ban the account; for that, use the "Banla" (Ban) action on the [Player profile](player-profile.md) page.

## Fields and options

### Mute window

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Süre (Duration) | Yes | 5 minutes, 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days or Özel bitiş (Custom end) |
| Bitiş anı (End time) | Only for a custom duration | Must be in the future, at most 30 days away |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | Yes | 8-500 characters |

The message delete and lift-mute windows have only the **İşlem nedeni** field.

### Table columns

Transcript: Zaman (Time), Yazar (Author, with an account type badge: Misafir (Guest) or Kayıtlı (Registered)), Oda (Room), Mesaj (Message) and Eylemler (Actions). The Hesap türü (Account type), Silindi (Deleted), Uzunluk (Length) and Oyuncu kimliği (Player ID) columns are turned on from the column menu. Active mutes: Oyuncu (Player), Bitiş (End, with the time left), Gerekçe (Reason), Susturan (Muted by) and Eylem (Action).

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| It says "Bu oyunda sahne sohbeti yok" | The selected game's plugin does not provide scene chat; the page works once a plugin that declares a scene is attached. |
| The Sil and Sustur buttons are not visible | Your role has no chat write permission; you can only read. |
| The custom end gives an error | The end must be in the future and no more than 30 days away. |
| I cannot find an old message | Messages are deleted automatically after 30 days. |
| A muted player is writing again | A guest account may have opened a new guest; consider banning the account. |

## Related docs

- [Chat](../guides/chat.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Session center
docs.description: See players' open session counts and last sign-ins; to close sessions, go to the player's security page.
docs.body:
# Session center

## Purpose

This page lists the players in the selected environment together with their open session counts. A session is a device or browser a player signed in on. Here you see only a summary; to see device details and close sessions, you go to the player's profile. The page is not in the menu; it opens from the session center link on the [Players](players.md) page.

## When to use

- To see which players have open sessions.
- To find accounts with many open sessions or that have not signed in for a long time.
- To go to a player's profile in order to close their sessions.

## Step by step

1. Make sure you selected the right game and environment.
2. Sort or filter the table by status and open session count.
3. To see and close the player's sessions, press **Oturumları yönet** (Manage sessions) in the row. The [Player profile](player-profile.md) opens; on the **Oturumlar** (Sessions) tab you find the individual sessions, and in the **Diğer işlemler** (More actions) menu you find the "Tüm oturumları kapat" (Close all sessions) action.

## Fields and options

There is no form to fill in on this page. Columns: Kullanıcı (User), Durum (Status), Aktif oturum (Active sessions), Son giriş (Last sign-in) and Güvenlik (Security). You can turn on the Oluşturulma (Created) column from the column menu.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| I cannot close the session from this page | The page is only a summary; closing is done on the player profile. |
| The option to close sessions is not visible | Your role has no session revoke permission; ask an admin. |
| The player was able to sign in again | Closing sessions does not block sign-in; to block sign-in, ban the account. |

## Related docs

- [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)
- [Authentication overview](../auth/overview.md)

docs.title: Store
docs.description: Products players buy in the game. Manage their image, price and stock from here.
docs.body:
# Store

## Purpose

This page manages the products players buy in the game. Products are divided into **showcases**: a showcase is a store screen in your game (for example Garage or Armory). Each product sells an item for game money or real money; you set its price, stock, badge and when it will be on sale from here.

## When to use

- To add a new store screen (showcase) to your game.
- To put a product in a showcase and change its price or stock (the [Product](store-product.md) page).
- To filter products by status and to sort showcases and products.

## Step by step

### Preparation

To sell a product you first need a [currency](currencies.md) you can price in and an item to sell (under Content or [Character templates](character-templates.md)). If something is missing, the page says so in a warning box and links to the related page.

### Create a showcase

1. Press **Yeni vitrin** (New showcase), or **İlk vitrini oluştur** (Create the first showcase) if there is no showcase. Only admins with store write permission see the button.
2. Write the name; the key is suggested from the name. The key is the ID the game uses when opening the showcase.
3. If you wish, add a description and a banner, and choose the status and the sale time.
4. Write a reason (the panel fills in a suggestion) and press **Vitrini oluştur** (Create showcase).

To edit a showcase, choose the showcase tab and press **Vitrini düzenle** (Edit showcase). You can delete the showcase from the edit window; when it is deleted, the products in it are deleted too, past sales are kept.

### View and sort products

1. Choose the showcase from the showcase tabs at the top.
2. Change the view with the **Izgara** (Grid) and **Liste** (List) buttons. The list view searches and filters the table with its own toolbar.
3. While **Sırala** (Sort) is on, you can move a product up or down with the buttons next to it, and move the showcase itself with **Vitrini sola/sağa taşı** (Move showcase left/right). Filters are disabled while sorting is on.
4. To go to a product's detail, click its card or row; for a new product press **Yeni ürün** (New product).

### Add vehicles to the store

If the vehicles content group has been published, the **Araçları mağazaya ekle** (Add vehicles to the store) button appears. It prepares the Garage showcase and a locked product for each vehicle in one step; the result is summarized on the page.

## Fields and options

### Showcase form

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Yes | At most 120 characters |
| Key | Yes | Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores; at most 64 characters |
| Description | No | At most 500 characters |
| Showcase banner | No | PNG, JPEG or WebP image |
| Status | Yes | Draft or Live |
| When on sale? | Yes | Immediately or a date range |
| Start, End | In a range | An empty end is unlimited |
| Action reason | Yes | 8-500 characters |

### Filters

Search, Status and (on a narrow screen) Showcase. Statuses: Live, Draft, Scheduled, Expired, Sold out.

### Sections

- **Ürünler** (Products): Showcases and products.
- **NPC tüccarları** (NPC traders): A read-only list. Store products use the automatic "Store" trader in the background; you do not need to do anything here.
- **Uygulama içi ürünler** (In-app products): A read-only list; App Store and Google Play products. You can bind a store product to one of them.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Mağaza bu ortamda kapalı" (The store is off in this environment) | The Store module is off; turn it on from the Modules tab in Game settings. |
| "Fiyat vermek için önce bir para birimi oluşturun" (Create a currency first to set prices) | Add a currency from the [Currencies](currencies.md) page. |
| "Satacak bir eşya yok" (There is no item to sell) | First add an item from the Content page. |
| The product is not visible in the game | Check that the product's and the showcase's status is **Yayında** (Live) and that the sale time has come. |
| "Bu sırada başka biri mağazayı değiştirdi" (Someone else changed the store in the meantime) | The store catalog is written with version checking; press **Yeniden yükle** (Reload) and make the change again. |
| I changed the showcase key and the game cannot find the showcase | The game opens the showcase with its key; update the call in the game with the new key too. |

## Related docs

- [Product](store-product.md)
- [Currencies](currencies.md)
- [Store and in-app purchases guide](../guides/store-iap.md)
- [Economy guide](../guides/economy.md)

docs.title: Store product
docs.description: See and change a product's image, price, stock and sale time, or add a new product.
docs.body:
# Store product

## Purpose

This page shows the detail of a single store product; it is also used to edit that product or create a new one. A product is a record that sits in a showcase and sells an item. Price, stock, per-person limit, badge and sale time are set here.

## When to use

- To add a new product to a showcase.
- To change a product's price, stock or image.
- To take a product off sale, bring it back or delete it.
- To look at a product's sales history and change history.

## Step by step

### Add a new product

1. On the [Store](store.md) page choose the showcase and press **Yeni ürün** (New product).
2. In the **Ne satılıyor?** (What is being sold?) field, search for the item by name and select it.
3. If you wish, write the name in the showcase, the description and the image.
4. In the **Nasıl ödenir?** (How is it paid?) section choose game money or real money; enter the price and currency, or the in-app product to bind.
5. Set the badge, the stock and the per-person limit.
6. Choose the status (draft or live), the sale time and the showcase.
7. Write a reason (the panel fills in a suggestion after the change) and press **Ürünü oluştur** (Create product). On the right there is a preview showing how the product will look in the game.

### Change the product

1. On the product's page press **Düzenle** (Edit).
2. Change the fields and press **Değişiklikleri kaydet** (Save changes).

Other buttons on the product page:

- **Yayından kaldır** (Take off sale) and **Yayına al** (Put on sale): Immediately turns the product into a draft or puts it live.
- **Sil** (Delete): Deletes the product; it asks for a reason. Past sales are kept.

> [!NOTE]
> You do not need to delete the product to change the price, stock or time; editing updates the existing product.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| What is being sold? | Yes | The item to sell |
| Name in showcase | No | At most 120 characters; if empty, the item name |
| Description | No | At most 2000 characters |
| Product image | No | PNG, JPEG or WebP |
| How is it paid? | Yes | Game money or real money |
| Currency and Price | For game money | Price greater than 0 |
| In-app product | For real money | App Store or Google Play product |
| Badge | No | None, New, Sale, Limited, Popular |
| Stock | Yes | Unlimited or limited; the quantity if limited |
| How many can one player buy at most? | No | Unlimited if empty |
| Status | Yes | Draft or Live |
| When on sale? | Yes | Immediately or a date range |
| Showcase | Yes | Does not change after creation |
| Action reason | Yes | 8-500 characters |

### Tabs on the product page

- **Ayrıntılar** (Details): Sale (price, stock, per-person limit, badge), publication status and time, "Ne verir" (What it gives: the item sold).
- **Satışlar** (Sales): The sales table with total quantity and revenue; filtered by status, source (store or in-game) and player.
- **Geçmiş** (History): The product's change events, newest on top.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Satılacak bir eşya seçin" (Choose an item to sell) | Choose the item first; if the list is empty, add an item from the Content page. |
| "Fiyat 0'dan büyük bir sayı olmalı" (The price must be a number greater than 0) | Write the price to fit the currency's decimal places; it cannot be zero or empty. |
| "Stok, ayrılmış N adetten az olamaz" (Stock cannot be less than the N reserved units) | This many units are already reserved for purchases; you cannot lower the stock below that. |
| "Bitiş, başlangıçtan sonra olmalı" (The end must be after the start) | Fix the date range; you must write at least one end. |
| "Bu ürünün API ile verilmiş bir görünürlük koşulu var" (This product has a visibility condition given through the API) | The condition cannot be changed from the panel; it is preserved as it is when you save. |
| I cannot change a vehicle product's price from Content | For a vehicle that has a product in the store, the product is the only source of the price; change the price here. |

## Related docs

- [Store](store.md)
- [Currencies](currencies.md)
- [Store and in-app purchases guide](../guides/store-iap.md)

docs.title: Studios and games
docs.description: See studios, games and environments; create a new studio or game, rename them and archive them.
docs.body:
# Studios and games

## Purpose

This page shows the studios in the installation and each studio's games with their environments. From here you create new studios and games, rename them, archive records and go to a game's settings. The page is open only to admins who have permission to manage studios. For the concepts of studio, game and environment, see the [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md) page.

## When to use

- To create a new studio or game.
- To fix the name of a studio or a game.
- To remove (archive) a game or studio that is no longer used from the list.
- To switch to the settings of another game.

## Step by step

### New studio

1. Press **Yeni stüdyo** (New studio).
2. Fill in the studio name and the **Gerekçe** (Reason) field and press **Stüdyo oluştur** (Create studio).

### New game

1. Press **Yeni oyun** (New game) on the studio's card.
2. Write the game name. If you like, also write the short name (slug); if you leave it empty, it is generated from the name.
3. Write the reason and press **Oyun oluştur** (Create game). The game is set up together with its development and live environments.

### Renaming and archiving

1. From the three-dot menu on the studio or game row, choose **Yeniden adlandır** (Rename) or **Arşivle** (Archive).
2. Write the new name, or only the reason, and confirm.
3. You can bring an archived record back into the lists with **Geri aç** (Restore) from the same menu.

> [!NOTE]
> Archiving only hides; no data is deleted. A game or studio that contains the selected environment cannot be archived; select another environment first. For records that have live permission or an active API key, the server refuses to archive.

### Opening a game's settings

1. Press **Oyun ayarları** (Game settings) on the game's row. If the game has no active environment, the button is disabled.
2. If another game's environment is selected, the panel switches to that game's active environment and opens the [Game settings](game-settings-general.md) page.

## Fields and options

| Field | Window | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stüdyo adı (Studio name) | New studio | Yes | 1-160 characters |
| Stüdyo (Studio) | New game | Yes | The studio the game will belong to (preselected if you opened it from the studio card) |
| Oyun adı (Game name) | New game | Yes | 1-160 characters |
| Kısa ad (Short name) | New game | No | Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; at most 48 characters |
| Yeni ad (New name) | Rename | Yes | 1-160 characters |
| Gerekçe (Reason) | All | Yes | 8-500 characters |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| I cannot see the page | The permission to manage studios belongs only to the widest role; ask a super admin. |
| "Arşivle" is disabled and there is a "Seçili ortam" (Selected environment) note | The environment you are working in right now is inside this record; switch to another game's environment and try again. |
| It says "Bu oyunun etkin ortamı yok" (This game has no active environment) | The game has no active (non-archived) environment left; restore the environment first. |
| A short name error | Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; a hyphen cannot be at the start, at the end or repeated. |
| Archiving was refused | The game may have live permission or an active API key; turn those off first. |

## Related docs

- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)
- [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md)

docs.title: Webhooks and event queue
docs.description: Inspect, read-only, the registered webhook endpoints, delivery attempts and the event queue; see why failed deliveries failed.
docs.body:
# Webhooks and event queue

## Purpose

A webhook is a signed HTTP request Open Play sends to your own server when an event happens. This page shows the registered endpoints, the attempts to send each event to an endpoint, and the event queue (outbox) waiting to be sent. The page is **read-only**: there is no button in the panel to add or delete an endpoint, resend a failed delivery or see the secret. Endpoints are registered over REST; for details, see the [Webhooks](../guides/webhooks.md) guide.

## When to use

- To verify that your server is receiving webhooks.
- To understand why an event did not arrive (is it waiting, did it fail, which error).
- To see whether an endpoint is enabled and which event types it listens to.

> [!NOTE]
> If the webhooks module is disabled, the webhook endpoints do not respond (`404`, `module_disabled`). Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](game-settings-modules.md) page. To see the page, your role also needs webhook read permission.

## Step by step

1. Make sure you selected the right game and environment.
2. In the "Webhook endpoints" table, check your endpoint's address (URL), the event types it listens to and its status. If the filter is empty, it says "tümü" (all), which means the endpoint receives all events.
3. In the "Delivery attempts / DLQ" table, filter deliveries by status. Those that are failed have used up their retries (DLQ, dead letter queue).
4. In the "Hata" (Error) column you see the class of the error and, if there is one, the HTTP code your server returned. The raw error text is not shown.
5. In the "Outbox" table you see the events waiting to be sent or being attempted.
6. Press **Yenile** (Refresh) to see new data.

## Fields and options

There is no form to fill in on this page.

### Tables

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| Webhook endpoints | URL, Event filtreleri (Event filters), Durum (Status; enabled or disabled), Oluşturulma (Created); the Endpoint kimliği (Endpoint ID) column is turned on from the column menu |
| Delivery attempts / DLQ | Endpoint (URL, delivery ID and event ID), Durum (Status; pending, delivered, failed), Attempt (the number of attempts), Hata (Error), Oluşturma (Created), Teslim (Delivered); the delivery order and outbox ID columns are turned on from the column menu |
| Outbox | Event (the type and the event ID), Durum (Status), Attempt, Retry (the time of the next attempt), Oluşturma (Created) |

For a published (completed) outbox record, the next attempt time shows "—". If the event type is a hidden internal event, it says "redacted/private". The panel never shows secrets, the raw body or the raw error text.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| It says "Webhook yüzeyi yetki gerektiriyor" (The webhook surface needs permission) | Your role has no webhook read permission; ask an admin. |
| The tables are empty | You may not have registered an endpoint yet; also check that you selected the right environment. |
| A delivery is "failed" | Your server is not returning 2xx or cannot be reached. Look at the class and code in the Hata column; fix your receiver. There is no resend from the panel. |
| The same event arrived more than once | Delivery happens at least once; your receiver should drop repeats by the event ID. For details, see the guide. |
| I cannot see an endpoint's secret | The secret comes back only once, in the registration response; it is not shown anywhere afterwards. To renew it, delete the endpoint and register it again. |

## Related docs

- [Webhooks](../guides/webhooks.md)
- [Webhook events](../reference/webhook-events.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.title: Calling plugins
docs.description: Describes the rules for calling plugin commands, queries, the result query, and the schema endpoint over HTTP, and the error envelope.
headings: Example: calling a command safely against an uncertain outcome
docs.body:
# Calling plugins

This page describes how to call a plugin's commands and queries over HTTP: headers, version checks, replay safety, the result query, and the error envelope. If you use an SDK, the SDK does most of this for you; still, knowing what happens makes debugging easier.

> [!NOTE]
> For plugins there is **no shared `/openapi.json`**; the plugin's own schema document (artifact) is obtained from the `GET /v1/plugins/{plugin_id}/schema` endpoint. The list of operations you can use is there ([bindings](bindings.md)).

## Endpoints

| Method and path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/plugins/{plugin_id}/commands/{message_type}` | Runs the command |
| `GET /v1/plugins/{plugin_id}/commands/{message_type}/result` | Queries the command's result with the idempotency key |
| `GET /v1/plugins/{plugin_id}/queries/{message_type}` | Runs the query (parameters in the query string) |
| `POST /v1/plugins/{plugin_id}/queries/{message_type}` | Runs the query (parameters in the body) |
| `GET /v1/plugins/{plugin_id}/schema` | Returns the plugin's schema document |

`{plugin_id}` is the plugin ID (for example `package-ride`). `{message_type}` is the operation's **request message type** (for example `package-ride.progression-missions.login-bonus.input`); it is not the operation's name (`claimLoginBonus`). The full path and message type are written in the `path` and `requestMessageType` field of each operation in the schema document. Which method (GET or POST) to use is also stated by the operation's `method` field: some server queries are called with `POST`.

## Identity

| Caller | What to send |
|---|---|
| Player (cookie) | `Cookie` (`__Secure-crx.session`) + `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>`; on modifying (POST) requests also `x-csrf-token` + the `__Secure-crx.csrf` cookie |
| Player (Bearer) | `Authorization: Bearer <session token>` + `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>`. On modifying requests the plugin endpoint requires the CSRF pair (the `__Secure-crx.csrf` cookie + `x-csrf-token`) **with Bearer too**; a client without cookies gets the pair with `GET /v1/auth/csrf` and carries it itself ([sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)) |
| Server | `Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>` (a server key). If you send `x-crx-env` it must be the same as the key's environment, otherwise `401`. CSRF and Origin checks are not applied |
| Public query | Only `x-crx-env`; only `GET`, and only queries that have `access: public` in the schema document |

A key that starts with `crx_` but is not of the server type (a client key) gets `401 unauthorized`. In player requests, if there is an `Origin` header it must be one of the environment's allowed origins (the browser adds it itself); otherwise `403 forbidden`. When a modifying call succeeds, the response returns the new CSRF pair (`Set-Cookie` and the `x-csrf-token` header); use it on the next modifying request.

## Calling a command

```http
POST /v1/plugins/package-ride/commands/package-ride.progression-missions.login-bonus.input HTTP/1.1
Host: game.example.com
Origin: https://game.example.com
Cookie: __Secure-crx.session=<session>; __Secure-crx.csrf=<csrf-cookie>
x-crx-env: 0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-000000000001
x-csrf-token: <csrf-token>
x-crx-schema-version: 1
Idempotency-Key: 5d1f2c88-4f0b-4c8f-9f1e-9a3f6b0c1d22
If-Match: "3"
Content-Type: application/json

{"expectedVersion":"3"}
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
x-crx-message-type: package-ride.progression-missions.login-bonus.output
x-crx-schema-version: 1

{"version":"4","rewardMinor":"250","streak":"2","day":"19300","walletBalanceMinor":"1250","claimEventId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-0000000000c1","ledgerCorrelationId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-0000000000c2"}
```

| Header | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | yes on commands | The logical replay key; cannot be empty. [Rules](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md) |
| `x-crx-schema-version` | yes | The schema version of the payload you send (a positive integer); must match the operation's `schemaVersion` value. It is required on queries too |
| `If-Match` | no | The expected resource version (**optimistic lock**). A decimal integer, quoted or unquoted; values with `*` and the `W/` prefix get `400`. If the real version differs, `409` |
| `Content-Type: application/json` | yes | The body is JSON and conforms to the operation's request schema |

> [!NOTE]
> `int64` values in body fields go as **decimal text** (`"expectedVersion":"3"`), not as a JSON number; the response has the same form. Details: [numbers and encoding](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md). `int32` and `uint32` fields are JSON numbers.

The body of a successful response is JSON that conforms to the operation's response schema; the `x-crx-message-type` and `x-crx-schema-version` response headers indicate the output message.

### Repeating with the same key

If the network drops or you cannot get the response, resend with **the same** `Idempotency-Key` and **the same** body; the server does not apply the operation a second time and returns the recorded result.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| First request | Processed, `200` |
| Same key, same body | The recorded result is returned |
| Same key, **different** body | `422` and `idempotency_mismatch` |
| A request with the same key is still being processed | `409` and `idempotency_in_flight` (`retryable: true`); try again shortly |
| The record expired (the operation's `receiptRetentionSeconds` value, 86,400 s in the example) | `410` and `idempotency_expired` |

Generating a new key means **a new operation**; do not resend a command with an uncertain outcome with a new key.

## Result query

Find out the result of a command whose response you never received, without resending it:

```http
GET /v1/plugins/package-ride/commands/package-ride.progression-missions.login-bonus.input/result?idempotency_key=5d1f2c88-4f0b-4c8f-9f1e-9a3f6b0c1d22&output_message_type=package-ride.progression-missions.login-bonus.output&output_schema_version=1 HTTP/1.1
x-crx-env: 0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-000000000001
Cookie: __Secure-crx.session=<session>
```

All three query parameters are required: `idempotency_key`, `output_message_type`, and `output_schema_version`. The path is the same as the operation's `resultPath` field.

| Response | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `200` + body | The command had been committed; the body is the output | Use the result |
| `202` (empty body) | Still being processed | Query again shortly |
| `404` | There is no record with this key: the command was never applied | Only in this case can you send the command **with the same key and body** |
| `422` + `reason` | The command was processed and rejected by a business rule | Do not send; `reason` is a machine code |
| `410` | The record expired | The result is unknown; re-read the state with a query |

## Calling a query

With `GET`, the parameters go in the query string. Each value is first parsed as JSON; if that fails, it is treated as text; the value `null` becomes `null`. Giving the same parameter twice gets `400`.

```http
GET /v1/plugins/package-ride/queries/package-ride.delivery-trip.active.input HTTP/1.1
x-crx-env: 0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-000000000001
x-crx-schema-version: 1
Cookie: __Secure-crx.session=<session>
```

With `POST`, the same fields go in the JSON body. `POST` is suitable for complex or long inputs; read which method is valid from the operation's `method` field. A public query example:

```http
GET /v1/plugins/package-ride/queries/package-ride.world-catalog.get.input HTTP/1.1
x-crx-env: 0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-000000000001
x-crx-schema-version: 1
```

## Schema endpoint

`GET /v1/plugins/{plugin_id}/schema` returns the plugin's schema document (JSON) (`Cache-Control: no-store`). A player session or a server key is required. If the plugin is not enabled for your environment or the grant version does not match, it is `404`. You find the document's fields and how to use the `schemaSha256` value on the [bindings](bindings.md) page.

## Error envelope

Plugin endpoints return a **JSON** error envelope (unlike the plain-text errors of the core REST endpoints; for a comparison see [errors](../reference/errors.md)):

```json
{"code":"conflict","message":"version conflict: expected 3, actual 5","retryable":false,"requestId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-0000000000d1"}
```

The response also has an `x-request-id` header; give this ID in a support request.

| `code` | HTTP | `retryable` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unauthorized` | 401 | no | Session/key missing, invalid, a client key, or an environment mismatch |
| `forbidden` | 403 | no | CSRF or Origin rejection; the plugin is not enabled or the version does not match; a banned account (`message: account banned`) |
| `module_disabled` | 404 | no | The `plugins` module is disabled (the `module` field carries the module name) |
| `not_found` | 404 | no | Unknown plugin or message type; no record |
| `invalid_argument` | 400 | no | Missing/broken header, unknown schema version, a payload that does not conform to the schema, a duplicate query parameter |
| `conflict` | 409 | no | The `If-Match` version does not match the real one |
| `idempotency_in_flight` | 409 | yes | A request with the same key is still being processed |
| `idempotency_mismatch` | 422 | no | Same key, different body |
| `unprocessable` | 422 | no | A business rule rejection; the `reason` field carries the machine code |
| `idempotency_expired` | 410 | no | The record expired |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | yes | Rate limit; `Retry-After: 60` ([rate limits](../reference/rate-limits.md)) |
| `tenant_unavailable` | 503 | yes | The environment's placement is temporarily unavailable; `Retry-After: 30` |
| `internal` | 500 | yes | Server error |

The `reason` field exists only on a business rule rejection (`unprocessable`) (for example `street_reset_too_early`) and is plugin-specific; its meaning is in the plugin's documentation. On a version mismatch (`conflict`) the message contains the expected and the real version: re-read the state and try again with the new version.

> [!WARNING]
> On plugin endpoints a banned account does **not** come with the `account_banned` code: `403` and `code: "forbidden"`, `message: "account banned"` is returned. The `account_banned` code belongs to the player identity endpoints (sign-in, sign-up) ([errors](../reference/errors.md)). If your client will distinguish these two cases, look at the session state, not at the message.

## Example: calling a command safely against an uncertain outcome

The TypeScript example below prepares the command with an SDK binding (a single `Idempotency-Key` is generated), sends it; if the outcome is uncertain it queries the result **without generating a new command** and resends with the same key only on a `notFound` response. The `demo-game` plugin is a scenario prepared for this example: in your real plugin you take the operation names and fields from your own schema document ([bindings](bindings.md)).

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/plugin-call.ts -->
```ts
import { CrxError, ErrorKind, type PlayerClient } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";
import { DemoGameBinding } from "./generated/demo-game.js";

/**
 * Günlük hediyeyi alır. `prepare` tek `Idempotency-Key` üretir; ağ hatasında sonuç belirsizse yeni komut üretilmez:
 * önce sonuç sorgulanır, yalnız "kayıt yok" yanıtında AYNI anahtarla yeniden gönderilir.
 */
export async function claimDailyGift(client: PlayerClient, expectedVersion: bigint): Promise<bigint> {
  const demo = client.plugin(DemoGameBinding);
  const command = await demo.commands.claimDailyGift.prepare({ giftKey: "daily" }, { expectedVersion });
  try {
    const output = await command.send();
    return output.walletBalanceMinor; // int64 alanlar bigint gelir
  } catch (error) {
    if (!(error instanceof CrxError) || error.kind !== ErrorKind.UnknownOutcome) throw error;
    const outcome = await command.lookup();
    if (outcome.status === "committed") return outcome.result.walletBalanceMinor;
    if (outcome.status === "notFound") return (await command.resume()).walletBalanceMinor; // aynı anahtar, aynı gövde
    throw error; // pending, rejected ya da expired: kör tekrar yok
  }
}

/** Salt-okunur sorgu: tekrar güvenlidir, anahtar gerekmez. */
export async function hasClaimedToday(client: PlayerClient): Promise<boolean> {
  const demo = client.plugin(DemoGameBinding);
  const status = await demo.queries.getGiftStatus({ includeHistory: false });
  return status.claimedToday;
}
```

## Next step

- Typed client and schema pinning: [bindings](bindings.md).
- Rules for replay safety and version checks: [idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md).

headings: Today's state: only trusted, compiled plugins
docs.body:
# Plugins overview

This page explains the **plugin** concept in Open Play: packages that offer game-specific commands, queries, and realtime modules without adding a game name to the core. Here you see how you connect to a game's logic beyond the core modules (character, economy, store…) and what is not supported today.

## What is a plugin

A plugin is a package that runs inside the Open Play server and defines these three surfaces:

| Surface | What it gives | How it is called |
|---|---|---|
| **Command** | A state-changing, durable, replay-safe operation (for example claim a reward, complete a delivery) | HTTP `POST` or the realtime `Command` frame: [calling plugins](calling-plugins.md) |
| **Query** | A read-only read (for example the active delivery, the catalog) | HTTP `GET` or `POST` |
| **Realtime module** | Live input and state broadcast (movement, room, scene) | `/v1/realtime/ws`: [realtime protocol](../realtime/protocol.md) |

Every plugin publishes a **schema document** (artifact): it describes which commands, queries, and modules exist with which input and output schemas, which identity can call them, and the retry rule. The SDKs' typed bindings are generated from this document: [bindings](bindings.md).

Commands are committed in a single database transaction: the command's effect, its result, its event, and the replay record are written together or not at all. Realtime transient state, on the other hand, is kept only for speed and is not the authority for durable outcomes such as payment, XP, items, or rewards.

## Today's state: only trusted, compiled plugins

> [!WARNING]
> **Loading third-party plugins is not available yet.** Plugins are code (Rust) compiled into the Open Play server itself and are considered trusted code. As a game developer you cannot upload your own plugin from the panel or the API; sandboxed execution, resource metering, and signed distribution are a future design and do not work today.

You connect your own game logic today in these ways:

- **Rules** (the Rules screen in the panel): automations bound to character events. See [game rules](../guides/game-rules.md).
- **Webhooks**: Open Play notifies your own server of events. See the [webhooks guide](../guides/webhooks.md).
- **Your own server + a server key**: run your own logic on your own server and call the core REST endpoints. See the [endpoint reference](../reference/endpoints.md).

Plugins that ship in the repository:

| Plugin | Version | What for | Surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package-ride` | 1.44.0 | A delivery game: driving, quests, race bets, scene | 36 commands, 33 queries, 3 realtime modules |
| `arena` | 1.0.0 | A minimal example: a single movement module | 0 commands, 0 queries, 1 realtime module |

These come with the server; you can see which ones are enabled in your environment on the **Plugins** screen in the panel ([Plugins](../panel/plugins.md)).

## Per-environment state

A plugin is in a separate state for each environment:

| State | Commands | Queries |
|---|---|---|
| Enabled (`Enabled`) | accepted | accepted |
| Read-only (`ReadOnly`) | rejected | accepted |
| Draining (`Draining`) | new commands rejected, running work finishes | accepted |
| Disabled (`Disabled`) | rejected | rejected |

A rejected call gets `403` and `forbidden` ([errors](../reference/errors.md)). The same result is also seen when the plugin version granted to the environment does not match the version on the server: if the server was updated with a new plugin version, the environment's plugin grant must also be moved to that version. If you get an unexpected `403 forbidden`, first look at the plugin's state and version in the panel.

In addition, if the product module `plugins` is disabled, all `/v1/plugins/...` and realtime endpoints return `404` and `module_disabled` ([Game settings: modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md)).

## Access by identity

Every operation has an `access` value in the schema document:

| `access` | Who calls |
|---|---|
| `player` | The player session (a cookie or a Bearer session token) |
| `server` | Only a server key; not visible in the player client |
| `public` | A `GET` query that requires no identity (only `x-crx-env` is needed) |

An unspecified or unknown value falls to the safe side (`player`). A plugin cannot be called with a client API key embedded in the client: it gets `401`. Details: [calling plugins](calling-plugins.md).

## Next step

- To call commands and queries, see [calling plugins](calling-plugins.md).
- To generate a typed client and pin the schema version, see [bindings](bindings.md).
