docs.body:
# Realtime overview

This page describes the three WebSockets Open Play offers and when to use each. For in-game state (movement, room, scene) you use the plugin realtime socket, and for notifications and chat you use two separate sockets; all of them have different identity and close rules.

## Three sockets

| Socket | Path | What for | Who speaks | Credential |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Realtime (plugin) | `/v1/realtime/ws` | Game state: live input, state snapshot, durable commands and events | Two-way | Single-use ticket |
| Notification | `/v1/ws` | Pushing a notification to the player live | Server → player only | Player session (cookie or Bearer) |
| Chat | `/v1/chat/ws` | Channel chat (subscribe, send a message) | Two-way | Player session (cookie or Bearer) |

Rule: all three are **player** sockets. A socket is not opened with a server key; for server-to-server work use the [REST endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md).

## Which one should I use

| Need | Choice |
|---|---|
| Publishing the live state of a vehicle, a player, or a room and receiving player input in order | The realtime socket, [protocol](protocol.md) |
| Getting the result of a command durably and replay-safely (reward, delivery) | The realtime `Command` frame or the HTTP command endpoint ([calling plugins](../plugins/calling-plugins.md)) |
| Showing the player a "new notification" instantly | `/v1/ws`; the durable source is always the `GET /v1/notifications` inbox ([notifications](../guides/notifications.md)) |
| Channel chat | `/v1/chat/ws` or REST ([chat](../guides/chat.md)) |
| Leaderboard, store, inventory | REST; there is no socket for these |

> [!NOTE]
> The TypeScript SDK manages the realtime socket for you: getting the ticket, authentication, reconnecting, and snapshot recovery are included. You need to write the protocol by hand only for a client without an SDK (for example the Unity native socket). For SDK usage, see the [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md) page.

## Connection requirements (shared)

1. **HTTPS and an allowed origin.** Your browser game calls the API from the same origin through a reverse proxy or, if its domain is registered in an environment, directly at the Open Play address (CORS). Sockets open to the same address: `wss://<your-game-domain>/<path>` or `wss://<open-play-address>/<path>`; the handshake checks `Origin` per environment (CORS does not change this). Details: [architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md).
2. **Environment header.** A player identity is always bound to an environment and requires the `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>` header. On the realtime socket the header is given with the HTTP ticket request; the WebSocket upgrade carries no header, the ticket knows the environment. `/v1/ws` and `/v1/chat/ws`, however, require the header on the upgrade request itself. The browser's WebSocket API cannot add custom headers; therefore **these two sockets cannot be opened directly from the browser** (a known limitation). In browser games, poll the inbox with REST for notifications and use the REST endpoints for chat; non-browser clients can send the header themselves.
3. **No token in the query string.** No socket accepts a session token in the URL; `?token=` is not supported so that it does not leak into access logs. A realtime upgrade that carries a query string is rejected.
4. **The Origin header is required** (realtime): both the ticket request and the upgrade must carry `Origin`, and it must be one of the environment's allowed origins. The browser adds it itself; if it is a non-browser client, you must send an allowed `Origin` value yourself.
5. **Module gate.** The realtime socket depends on the `plugins` module, `/v1/ws` on `notifications`, and `/v1/chat/ws` on `chat`. If the module is disabled, the upgrade returns `404` and `module_disabled`; an open socket is closed with `1008` (reason `module_disabled`) if the module is disabled later, and with `1013` if the gate state cannot be verified. You manage modules from the panel: [Game settings: modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md).

## Notification socket (`/v1/ws`)

- It flows only from the server to the player. Frames coming from the client are ignored.
- The incoming frame is a JSON object: `{"type":"notification","notification_id":"…","title":"…","body":"…","data":{…},"channel":"in_game","sent_at_ms":1760000000000}`. Field names are `snake_case`.
- A live frame is delivered **at most once**. The durable source is the inbox; the same notification can arrive both as a frame and through an inbox query, so deduplicate by `notification_id`.
- The connection counts as a presence (online) signal.

## Chat socket (`/v1/chat/ws`)

Frames are distinguished by the `type` field (with `camelCase` values); the other field names are `snake_case`, and an unknown field is rejected. Example: `{"type":"send","channel_id":"…","client_message_id":"retry-1","body":"hello"}`.

| Direction | `type` | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Client → server | `subscribe` | `channel_id` | Channel subscription (one channel at a time) |
| Client → server | `unsubscribe` | — | Drops the subscription |
| Client → server | `send` | `channel_id`, `client_message_id`, `body` | Replay-safe message sending, the same as REST |
| Client → server | `ping` | `nonce` (number) | Liveness probe |
| Server → client | `subscribed` / `unsubscribed` | `channel_id` (only `subscribed`) | Accepted |
| Server → client | `message` | `message`, `duplicate` | Channel message; if `duplicate: true`, the `client_message_id` had been processed before |
| Server → client | `pong` | `nonce` | The reply to `ping` |
| Server → client | `error` | `code` | `invalid_frame`, `invalid_payload`, `forbidden_channel`, `unavailable`, `message_rejected`, `module_disabled` when the module is being disabled |

Message sending limit: 20 messages per 10 seconds per player; you see an overage as `message_rejected` or, in REST, as `429` ([rate limits](../reference/rate-limits.md)). For detailed usage, see the [chat guide](../guides/chat.md).

## Next step

- To see the plugin realtime protocol from start to finish, see the [protocol](protocol.md).
- To see what happens when the connection drops, the limits, and idle close, see [reconnect and limits](reconnect-and-limits.md).

docs.description: Describes the ticket, subprotocol, and authentication flow of the plugin realtime socket and all frames with their fields.
docs.body:
# Realtime protocol

This page describes the wire protocol of the `/v1/realtime/ws` socket: getting a ticket, connecting, authentication, and the fields of every client and server frame. If you use the TypeScript SDK you do not write this protocol by hand; but read from here to understand the behavior, write another client, or troubleshoot.

> [!NOTE]
> The protocol version is `1`. Every frame carries `protocolVersion: 1`; any other value gets an `UnsupportedProtocol` error ([versioning](../reference/versioning.md)).

## General rules

- Every frame is a JSON object sent as **a single WebSocket text message**. Binary messages are not accepted.
- The `type` field determines the frame type and is `PascalCase` (`Authenticate`, `Join`, …). The other field names are `camelCase`. A frame that contains an unknown field is rejected.
- Large integers (**sequence numbers, epoch, revision, version**) are **decimal text**, not JSON numbers: `"sessionEpoch": "7"`. Canonical form: non-empty, no leading zero, digits only, non-negative, within the `i64` range. Details: [numbers and encoding](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md). `protocolVersion` and `schemaVersion` are small integers and are sent as JSON numbers.
- `requestId` (UUID) is the correlation ID that the client generates for **every attempt**; the server returns the response and the error with the same ID.
- Before authentication only `Authenticate` is valid, and afterwards frames other than `Authenticate` are valid; a frame in the wrong phase gets `UnexpectedFrame`.

## Connection flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as "Client"
    participant H as "HTTP (REST)"
    participant S as "WebSocket /v1/realtime/ws"
    C->>H: "POST /v1/realtime/tickets"
    H-->>C: "200 ticket, expiresAt"
    C->>S: "Upgrade (Sec-WebSocket-Protocol openplay.realtime.v1)"
    C->>S: "Authenticate(protocolVersion 1, ticket)"
    S-->>C: "Ready(connectionId, playerId, sessionEpoch, authorityGeneration)"
    C->>S: "Join(pluginId, moduleId, target)"
    S-->>C: "Joined(subscriptionId)"
    S-->>C: "Snapshot or DurableRecovery"
    C->>S: "Input or Command"
    S-->>C: "Ack or CommandResult"
```

### 1. Get a ticket

```http
POST /v1/realtime/tickets HTTP/1.1
Host: game.example.com
Origin: https://game.example.com
x-crx-env: 0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-000000000001
Cookie: __Secure-crx.session=<session>; __Secure-crx.csrf=<csrf-cookie>
x-csrf-token: <csrf-token>
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: no-store
Content-Type: application/json

{"ticket":"tkt_AbC123-xyz","expiresAt":"2026-11-03T10:15:30+00:00","protocol":"openplay.realtime.v1"}
```

| Header | Required | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `x-crx-env` | yes | The player's environment. Must match the session's environment. |
| `Origin` | yes | Must be one of the environment's allowed origins; the ticket is bound to this origin. |
| `Cookie` or `Authorization: Bearer <session token>` | yes | If a cookie is present, cookie mode is always chosen; with a broken cookie it does not fall back to Bearer. |
| `x-csrf-token` + the `__Secure-crx.csrf` cookie | only in cookie mode | Double submit. A new CSRF value is returned on every successful request; store the `x-csrf-token` header and the `Set-Cookie` in the response ([sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)). |

- The ticket is **single-use**, valid for **30 seconds**, and bound to the `Origin`. Get it right before opening the socket; do not hold on to it.
- On this endpoint, identity, CSRF, and Origin errors get the same response: `403` and the plain text `permission denied`. If the module is disabled (`plugins`), `404` and `{"code":"module_disabled",…}`.

### 2. Open the socket

- Address: `wss://<your-game-domain>/v1/realtime/ws`. There **must be no query string**; if there is, the upgrade is rejected.
- `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: openplay.realtime.v1` must be requested; the server selects it. If it is not requested, the upgrade is rejected.
- `Origin` is required and must be one of the environment's allowed origins or in the global allowed list. The browser sends it itself.
- An upgrade rejection is `401` (plain text `unauthorized`); if the module is disabled, `404`.
- There are per-address and per-player connection limits ([limits](reconnect-and-limits.md)).

### 3. Send `Authenticate`

The first frame must arrive within **5 seconds** after the socket opens; if it does not, the server writes an `AuthenticationFailed` error and closes. A frame in the authentication phase can be at most **4 KiB**.

```json
{"type":"Authenticate","protocolVersion":1,"ticket":"tkt_AbC123-xyz"}
```

The server consumes the ticket (verifying the origin and the subprotocol), re-verifies the session, and replies:

```json
{"type":"Ready","protocolVersion":1,"connectionId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a1","playerId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-0000000000b2","sessionEpoch":"7","authorityGeneration":"42"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `connectionId` | The server's ID for this socket. |
| `playerId` | The authenticated player. |
| `sessionEpoch` | This socket's write epoch. It is given back unchanged in `Input` frames. If a newer socket of the same player starts writing to the same resource, the old socket's inputs get `Stale`. |
| `authorityGeneration` | The environment's authority generation; it is for server-side limiting, the client only stores it. |

A ticket that is invalid, used, expired, or belongs to another origin is rejected with `AuthenticationFailed`; the server closes the socket. Get a new ticket and reconnect.

## Client frames

They can be sent after `Ready`. The frame size is at most **16 KiB**; a frame that exceeds it gets `PayloadTooLarge`.

### `Join`: join a subscription

```json
{"type":"Join","protocolVersion":1,"requestId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-000000000010","pluginId":"package-ride","moduleId":"package-ride.street","target":{"kind":"Scene","sceneId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-000000000031"}}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `requestId` | UUID | The attempt ID. |
| `pluginId` | text | The plugin that owns the module ([plugins](../plugins/overview.md)). |
| `moduleId` | text | The realtime module the plugin defines; it is listed in the `modules` section of the plugin's schema document. |
| `target.kind` | text | `PlayerSelf`, `Room`, `Scene`, or `InterestSet`. |
| `target.roomId` / `sceneId` / `interestSetId` | UUID | The target's ID (according to `kind`; `PlayerSelf` carries no ID). |
| `cursor` | UUID, optional | An opaque resume cursor from a previous `DurableRecovery`. |

The server authorizes the target; a raw Redis key or topic name is **not given**. Success: `Joined`. After that, a `Snapshot` or `DurableRecovery` arrives depending on the module's type.

### `Leave`: leave a subscription

```json
{"type":"Leave","protocolVersion":1,"requestId":"…","subscriptionId":"…"}
```

The response is `Left`; a repeated `Leave` is harmless.

### `Input`: transient input

Player input (movement, steering) in server-authoritative modules. Loss is not acceptable, a sequence number is required.

```json
{"type":"Input","protocolVersion":1,"requestId":"…","pluginId":"arena","moduleId":"arena.movement","messageType":"arena.movement.input","schemaVersion":1,"subscriptionId":"…","sessionEpoch":"7","inputSeq":"42","payload":{"delta":1}}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `messageType`, `schemaVersion` | Must match exactly the input definition in the module's schema document. |
| `subscriptionId` | The subscription from `Joined`. |
| `sessionEpoch` | The value in `Ready`. |
| `inputSeq` | An increasing sequence number (decimal text). If the same number and the same content are sent again you get `Replayed`; the same number with different content gets `Mismatch`. |
| `payload` | An object that conforms to the plugin's input schema. Its encoded size is at most 4 KiB and the module's `maxBytes` value; exceeding it gets `InvalidPayload`. |

The input rate is defined by the `ratePerSecond` and `burst` values in the module's schema document; a general per-connection frame budget is applied separately ([limits](reconnect-and-limits.md)).

### `Command`: durable command

A command that writes durably with a database transaction (reward, delivery); the result returns only after the transaction is committed. It is subject to the same rules as the HTTP command endpoint ([calling plugins](../plugins/calling-plugins.md)).

```json
{"type":"Command","protocolVersion":1,"requestId":"…","pluginId":"package-ride","moduleId":null,"messageType":"package-ride.progression-missions.claim.input","schemaVersion":1,"idempotencyKey":"claim-7f3a","expectedVersion":"12","payload":{"missionId":"daily-1"}}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `idempotencyKey` | The required logical replay key. The same key and the same content return the same result ([idempotency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md)). |
| `expectedVersion` | Optional optimistic version (decimal text). A mismatch is an error. |
| `moduleId` | The module context for room-scoped commands; otherwise `null`. |
| `payload` | Conforms to the plugin's command schema; its encoded size is at most 16 KiB, exceeding it gets `InvalidPayload`. |

### `Ping`

```json
{"type":"Ping","protocolVersion":1,"nonce":"a1"}
```

The response is `{"type":"Pong","nonce":"a1"}`. `nonce` is optional. The application-level `Ping` measures connection liveness; it **does not count as player activity** and does not postpone idle close ([idle close](reconnect-and-limits.md)).

## Server frames

| `type` | When | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `Ready` | `Authenticate` succeeded | `protocolVersion`, `connectionId`, `playerId`, `sessionEpoch`, `authorityGeneration` |
| `Joined` | `Join` was authorized | `requestId`, `subscriptionId`, `target` |
| `Left` | `Leave` was processed | `requestId`, `subscriptionId` |
| `CommandResult` | `Command` was committed | `requestId`, `messageType`, `schemaVersion`, `payload` |
| `Ack` | `Input` was processed | `requestId`, `inputSeq`, `status`, `revision` (optional) |
| `Snapshot` | Transient state broadcast | `subscriptionId`, `resourceId`, `messageType`, `schemaVersion`, `streamEpoch`, `revision`, `payload` |
| `DurableRecovery` | Recovery barrier for a durable stream | `subscriptionId`, `cursor`, `barrierSequence`, `coveredEventIds`, `snapshot` (may be empty) |
| `DurableEvent` | A durable, ordered plugin event | `subscriptionId`, `streamId`, `sequence`, `eventId`, `messageType`, `schemaVersion`, `cursor`, `payload` |
| `Pong` | The reply to `Ping` | `nonce` |
| `Error` | Error | `requestId` (if any), `code`, `retryable` |

### `Ack` statuses

| `status` | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `Applied` | The input advanced the state. `revision` is the new revision. | — |
| `Replayed` | The same sequence number and content had already been processed. | Ignore it; a safe replay. |
| `Stale` | The sequence number is behind the current writer or a newer socket took over. | Drop this input; if there is a new socket, this socket is no longer the writer. |
| `Mismatch` | The same sequence number arrived with different content. | It is a client bug; do not regenerate the sequence number, do not repeat. |
| `ResyncRequired` | A sequence gap or an unrecoverable state. | `Join` again for a fresh snapshot (without `cursor`). |

`revision` may be absent other than for `Applied` and `Replayed`. When the field is absent, `null` is not sent; the field is simply not there.

### `Snapshot` and `DurableRecovery`

- A `Snapshot` is **transient** state: `streamEpoch` (increases when the server cache restarts) and `revision` (monotonic) are ordered together. Within the same `streamEpoch`, an older `revision` must not overwrite the new state. If `streamEpoch` has changed, a new stream has started; do not compare with the old `revision`.
- `DurableRecovery` is the **baseline** in a durable stream: `cursor` is the new cursor tied to this point, `barrierSequence` is the stream start covered by the snapshot and the replay, and `coveredEventIds` are the event IDs that the snapshot already contains (do not apply them separately). `snapshot` is filled only on a fresh `Join`; it is absent when resuming with `cursor`.
- `DurableEvent`s arrive in `sequence` order; `eventId` is the end-to-end deduplication key, and `cursor` is the new cursor advanced up to that event. Store the cursor: when reconnecting you provide it as `Join.cursor` ([reconnect](reconnect-and-limits.md)).

## Error frame

```json
{"type":"Error","requestId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-000000000010","code":"InvalidPayload","retryable":false}
```

The error frame **carries no reason text**: only the code and `retryable`. Even a plugin rejection (for example a business rule) appears as `InvalidPayload`; the reason is not given to the client over the wire.

| `code` | When | `retryable` | Socket |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UnexpectedFrame` | A frame that does not fit its phase (for example `Join` before authentication, or a second `Authenticate`) | no | closes |
| `UnsupportedProtocol` | `protocolVersion` is not 1 | no | closes |
| `InvalidPayload` | Broken JSON, unknown field, a payload that does not conform to the schema, a plugin/business rule rejection, no such resource, a version conflict, the module is disabled | no | **stays open** on a per-frame error; closes on a parse error |
| `AuthenticationFailed` | The ticket is invalid/used/expired, the 5 s timeout, the session was revoked | no | closes |
| `PermissionDenied` | No authority for the target, module, or operation; a banned account | no | stays open |
| `PayloadTooLarge` | Exceeded the frame budget (4 KiB authentication, 16 KiB afterwards) | no | closes |
| `CapacityExceeded` | The rate or capacity limit is full | yes at the frame budget and the rate limit; no at the per-player/per-address socket count limit | closes at the frame budget and the socket count limit |
| `Unavailable` | A dependency is temporarily unavailable or the placement is not ready | usually yes (no for the `IdempotencyExpired` case) | depends |
| `ResyncRequired` | The cursor is missing, expired, mismatched, has a gap, or exceeded the replay budget | — | stays open |

> [!WARNING]
> Do not infer whether the socket will close from `retryable` alone. After an `Error` frame, the client must learn whether the socket is still open **from the connection state** (the close event). On long-lived sockets, per-frame errors (`InvalidPayload`, `PermissionDenied`) do not drop the connection.

### Close codes

| Code | Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `4100` | `idle_timeout` | No player activity arrived; idle close ([details](reconnect-and-limits.md)). There is **no** typed `Error` frame. |
| `1008` | `module_disabled` | The `plugins` module was disabled. |
| `1013` | `unavailable` | The module gate could not be verified; retry later. |

## Example: connecting by hand (summary)

In the browser, use the SDK; the skeleton below shows the protocol order.

```ts
const res = await fetch("/v1/realtime/tickets", {
  method: "POST",
  credentials: "include",
  headers: { "x-crx-env": environmentId, "x-csrf-token": csrfToken },
});
const { ticket } = await res.json();
const ws = new WebSocket(`wss://${location.host}/v1/realtime/ws`, ["openplay.realtime.v1"]);
ws.onopen = () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "Authenticate", protocolVersion: 1, ticket }));
ws.onmessage = (event) => {
  const frame = JSON.parse(event.data as string);
  if (frame.type === "Ready") {
    // Send Join, store frame.sessionEpoch for Input frames.
  }
};
```

## Next step

For how to resume with the cursor and epoch when the connection drops, limits, and compression, see [reconnect and limits](reconnect-and-limits.md).

docs.body:
# Reconnect and limits

This page describes how state is recovered when the realtime socket drops, what to do when `ResyncRequired` arrives, the idle close (`4100`) behavior, and the limits the server applies. If you are writing a game that is played on a mobile or unstable network, read this page from start to finish.

## Recovery after a drop

A socket can always drop (network, deployment, load balancer). In Open Play, recovery is done by **re-joining with a new socket**; the old socket's state is not reused on the server.

1. **Get a new ticket.** Every connection asks for a new ticket (single-use, 30 s); the old ticket cannot be reused ([protocol](protocol.md)).
2. **`Authenticate`, `Ready`.** A new `sessionEpoch` arrives. When the new socket starts writing to the same resource, the player's old socket is no longer the writer: the old socket's inputs get `Ack: Stale`.
3. **`Join` again for each subscription.**
   - **In durable streams:** give the last `cursor` you received as `Join.cursor`. The server replays `DurableEvent`s from where you left off and sends a new `DurableRecovery` barrier (`snapshot` is empty).
   - **In ephemeral state:** there is no `cursor`; `Join` brings a fresh `Snapshot`. `Input`s that were sent but did not get an `Ack` are **not replayed**: their outcome is uncertain, and your game logic must continue according to the latest `Snapshot`.
   - **In durable commands (`Command`):** the outcome of a command that dropped before an `Ack` arrived is uncertain. Resend with the same `idempotencyKey` or query the result ([calling plugins](../plugins/calling-plugins.md)); do not generate a new key.
4. **If `ResyncRequired` arrives** (the cursor is missing, expired, belongs to another player, has a gap, or exceeded the replay budget), discard the cursor and `Join` again **without a `cursor`**; this brings a fresh snapshot. Do not insist on the same cursor.

### Cursor rules

- It is opaque and **bound to the player**; another player's cursor cannot be used. Do not parse its contents.
- Every `DurableRecovery` and every `DurableEvent` carries a new cursor; store **the latest one**.
- At most **256** durable events are replayed in a single recovery; anything beyond that is turned into a fresh snapshot with `ResyncRequired`.
- The cursor and delivery retention window is **24 hours**; a cursor older than that gets `ResyncRequired`.
- The events in `coveredEventIds` are already in the fresh snapshot; do not apply them separately.

## What the TypeScript SDK does

The SDK runs this flow for you (`RealtimeClient`, `client.realtime`):

| Behavior | Default | Setting |
|---|---|---|
| Automatic reconnect | on | `autoReconnect` |
| Attempt delay | `min(reconnectBaseMs · 2^(n−1), 30 000)` ms + `[0, reconnectBaseMs)` jitter | `reconnectBaseMs`: 1000 (between 100 and 10,000) |
| Maximum attempts | 8 | `maxReconnectAttempts`: between 0 and 20 |
| Authentication timeout | 5 s | `authTimeoutMs` (at most 5 s) |
| Application `Ping` interval | 15 s | `heartbeatMs`: 10 ms to 60 s |
| Durable command timeout | 15 s | `commandTimeoutMs`: 1 ms to 120 s |
| Window of inputs awaiting a reply | 4 | `maxPendingInputs`: 1 to 8 |
| Frame size | 16 KiB | `maxFrameBytes` (at most 16 KiB) |

The state machine goes through the values `idle`, `ticketing`, `connecting`, `authenticating`, `ready`, `recovering`, `live`, `backoff`, `reauthRequired`, `upgradeRequired`, `idleClosed`, and `closed`. The important ones:

- `recovering` / `backoff`: the SDK is reconnecting; the subscriptions' cursors are preserved.
- `reauthRequired`: the ticket or the identity was rejected (`AuthenticationFailed`, 401/403). Re-establish the session; the SDK does not enter an endless loop on its own.
- `upgradeRequired`: the server did not recognize the protocol version or the frame (`UnsupportedProtocol`, 426). Update the client.
- If the server sends `PayloadTooLarge` or `CapacityExceeded`, the SDK surfaces it as a backpressure error; it does not change the connection state.

> [!NOTE]
> Incomplete inputs are rejected as "uncertain outcome" when the socket drops, and are **not automatically resent** after reconnecting. `best-effort` signal messages are not repeated either.

## Idle close (`4100`)

The server closes a socket that has a subscription that **accepts input** (interactive) and sends no player activity for a certain time.

- The close code is `4100`, the reason `idle_timeout`. There is no typed `Error` frame; only the WebSocket close frame.
- The duration is **5 minutes** by default and can be changed or turned off by the operator. Because the check interval is `min(duration/4, 15 s)`, the close arrives at most that much later than the threshold.
- In the menu or before the game (when there is no subscription that accepts input), the counter does not run.
- What counts as activity is the plugin's definition: an input frame usually counts; the application `Ping`, `Authenticate`, and the protocol-level ping do not. If your game will stay connected on a paused screen too, send the keep-alive input that the plugin defines; sending a keep-alive input on screens such as pause or garage keeps the player from being counted as AFK.
- An open socket does **not keep the session alive**: the session lifetime is extended only as the player makes REST requests ([security](../operations/security.md)); the server re-verifies the session on the socket every 25 seconds.
- Do not treat this close as an error: show the player "Continue", and on confirmation get a new ticket and reconnect; thanks to the cursors the subscriptions are recovered.

If you provide the `onIdleClose` callback in the SDK, the client moves to the `idleClosed` state and **does not reconnect on its own**; call `connect()` on the user's confirmation. If you do not provide the callback, the close is handled like an ordinary drop and the SDK reconnects itself.

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/realtime-idle-close.ts -->
```ts
import { createPlayerClient, type PlayerClient } from "@ferdiunal/open-play-ts";

/**
 * Sunucu boşta kapanışında (`4100`, `idle_timeout`) SDK kendiliğinden yeniden bağlanmaz; oyuncuya "Devam et"
 * gösterin ve onayında `connect()` çağırın. Abonelikler imleçleriyle kurtarılır.
 */
export function createClientWithIdlePrompt(
  baseUrl: string,
  environmentId: string,
  showContinueButton: (onContinue: () => void) => void,
): PlayerClient {
  const client: PlayerClient = createPlayerClient({
    baseUrl,
    environmentId,
    realtime: {
      reconnectBaseMs: 250, // ilk yeniden bağlanma denemesi 250 ms (varsayılan 1000)
      onIdleClose: () => showContinueButton(() => void client.realtime.connect()),
    },
  });
  return client;
}
```

## Limits

| Limit | Value | When exceeded |
|---|---|---|
| Ticket lifetime | 30 s, single use, bound to `Origin` | `AuthenticationFailed` |
| `Authenticate` wait time | 5 s | `AuthenticationFailed`, the socket closes |
| Authentication-phase frame | 4 KiB | `PayloadTooLarge`, closes |
| Frame (after authentication) | 16 KiB | `PayloadTooLarge`, closes |
| Transport-layer message | 64 KiB | between 16 KiB and 64 KiB gets a typed error; above 64 KiB it drops with a socket error without a typed error |
| `Input` payload | at most 4 KiB and the module's `maxBytes` value | `InvalidPayload` |
| `Command` payload | at most 16 KiB | `InvalidPayload` |
| Per-connection frame rate | 40 frames/s average, a 4 s (160-frame) burst allowance | `CapacityExceeded` (`retryable: true`) and the socket closes |
| Open sockets per player | 4 | `CapacityExceeded` (`retryable: false`), the socket closes |
| Open sockets per address | 8 | `CapacityExceeded` (`retryable: false`), the socket closes (only counted if the operator puts it in observation mode) |
| New connections per address | 30/minute | the upgrade is rejected |
| Subscriptions per socket | 32 (server default) | `Join` is rejected |
| Session re-verification | every 25 s | `AuthenticationFailed` and close if the session was revoked |
| Module gate re-check | every 2 s | close with `1008` / `1013` |
| Events replayed in recovery | 256 | `ResyncRequired` |
| Cursor retention | 24 hours | `ResyncRequired` |
| Idle close | 5 min (default) | `4100` `idle_timeout` |

Notes:

- The frame rate budget is not limited to `Input`; **every text frame received** and the protocol-level `Ping` count as a frame (`Pong` does not). An honest client sends roughly 30 to 35 frames/s; stay under 40/s and do not send frames that accumulated after a pause in a batch.
- The numbers are server defaults; the operator can change some of them (idle duration, connection limits, frame budget) with the environment configuration. If you use a hosted Open Play, ask your provider for the values.
- The `Input` rate is also defined by the `ratePerSecond` and `burst` values in the module's schema document.

## Compression

- The server supports **permessage-deflate** (RFC 7692) compression, and it takes effect **only if the client offers it**. Browsers offer it on their own; you do not need to do anything separately. It gives a noticeable reduction on similar JSON frames.
- The operator can turn compression off; if it is off, the socket works without compression and the protocol does not change.
- There is no compression yet in the Unity native WebSocket client; this is a known limitation. In WebGL the browser takes it on ([Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md)).

## Server-side liveness probe

The server sends a protocol-level WebSocket `Ping` about every 5 seconds to measure connection latency. Browsers and standard client libraries answer `Pong` on their own; if you write a WebSocket by hand, do not forget the `Pong` reply. This probe does not count as player activity.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| An immediate `AuthenticationFailed` on every connect | The ticket was reused or 30 s passed; `Origin` differs from the ticket request | Get a new ticket for every connection; connect from the origin you obtained the ticket from |
| Closing with `CapacityExceeded` | Frame rate or connection limit | Lower the frame send rate; close old tabs (4 sockets per player) |
| A `ResyncRequired` loop | Insisting on an old cursor | Discard the cursor, `Join` without `cursor` |
| A drop after 5 minutes | Idle close (`4100`) | Build a "Continue" flow or send a keep-alive input |
| Upgrade `401` | There is a query string, the subprotocol was not requested, or `Origin` is not allowed | [Protocol: open the socket](protocol.md) |

For more, see [troubleshooting](../operations/troubleshooting.md).

# Endpoint reference

This page shows, for every HTTP endpoint, which credentials to call it with and which headers it expects. The table is generated from the route registry in the code; it changes when an endpoint is added. Descriptions are currently in Turkish.

## How to read it

- **Module:** the endpoints of a disabled module return `404` with `module_disabled` ([errors](errors.md)). Core endpoints cannot be disabled.
- **Credentials:** server and client keys are sent as `Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`. A player session arrives as a cookie or a Bearer session token and needs the `x-crx-env: <environment uuid>` header; with a cookie session, mutating requests also carry `x-csrf-token` and an allowed `Origin`.
- Calling an endpoint marked **Server key** with a client key returns `403`. Endpoints marked **Server or client key** have no key-type gate in the code; being callable with a key embedded in the client is a security decision, so call these endpoints only from your server ([security](../operations/security.md)).
- **Idempotency-Key:** `required` means the request gets `400` without the header; `optional` makes the request safe to repeat ([idempotency](idempotency-and-concurrency.md)). **If-Match:** the endpoint supports optimistic version checks.
- For plugin endpoints (`/v1/plugins/...`) the requirements live in the plugin's schema document; see [calling plugins](../plugins/calling-plugins.md).

Total endpoints: **225**.

## Characters

docs.title: Error reference
docs.description: Gathers the status codes, error body formats, and machine codes of the core REST and plugin endpoints in a single table.
docs.body:
# Error reference

This page lists every kind of error Open Play returns, its status code, and its body format. When writing error handling code, first look at which endpoint **family** (core REST or plugin) is being called: the error bodies of the two families differ.

> [!WARNING]
> **Most core REST endpoints return plain-text (`text/plain`) errors**, not JSON. Only the few errors marked "JSON" on this page carry a JSON envelope. Do not parse the error text; decide by the **status code** and (if present) the JSON `code` field. Plain-text messages can change between versions.

## Error families

| Family | Which endpoints | Body |
|---|---|---|
| Core REST | `/v1/characters…`, `/v1/wallets…`, `/v1/store…`, `/v1/auth/…` etc. ([endpoints](endpoints.md)) | Plain text; a few errors are JSON `{code, message[, module]}` |
| Plugin | `/v1/plugins/…` | Always JSON `{code, message, retryable, requestId[, reason, module]}` + the `x-request-id` header |
| Realtime | `/v1/realtime/ws` | `Error` frame: `{type, requestId?, code, retryable}` ([protocol](../realtime/protocol.md)) |
| Chat socket | `/v1/chat/ws` | `{"type":"error","code":"…"}` ([realtime overview](../realtime/overview.md)) |

## Core REST: status table

| Status | Body (plain text unless stated otherwise) | When | Retry? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `400` | A description of the error | Missing or broken header, invalid field, unknown command type, `If-Match` format | No; fix the request |
| `401` | `unauthorized` | API key or player session missing, invalid, expired; `x-crx-env` missing or broken; a banned account (no distinction is made) | No; renew the credentials |
| `403` | `permission denied` | The key type is insufficient (for example a server endpoint with a client key), CSRF or Origin rejection | No |
| `403` | **JSON** `{"code":"account_banned","message":"account banned"}` | On sign-in endpoints, a banned account after ownership has been proven | No; do not build a loop |
| `404` | `not found` | The resource does not exist or was deleted | No |
| `404` | **JSON** `{"code":"module_disabled","message":"module disabled","module":"store"}` | The product module is disabled in the environment | No; enable the module ([modules](../panel/game-settings-modules.md)) |
| `409` | `version conflict: expected 3, actual 5` | The `If-Match` version does not match the real one | Re-read the state and repeat with the new version |
| `409` | `already exists: <resource>` | A resource with the same ID/key already exists | No |
| `409` | `idempotent request in progress` | The first request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is still being processed | Yes, shortly, with the same key |
| `410` | `idempotent request result expired` | The key's record retention (24 hours) expired | With a new key, reading the state first |
| `413` | No body | The request body exceeded the 2 MiB limit (the image upload endpoint is subject to its own limit) | No |
| `422` | `idempotency mismatch` | Same key, different content | No; do not reuse the key |
| `422` | `unprocessable: <reason>` | A business rule rejection (insufficient balance, stock, limit…) | No; do not repeat without changing the state |
| `422` | `rejected: <code>` | A plugin business rule rejection (through core routes) | No |
| `429` | `rate limited` or `rule budget exceeded: <rule>` | Rate limit or rule budget | Yes, by waiting ([rate limits](rate-limits.md)); **there is no `Retry-After`** |
| `500` | `internal error` | An unexpected server error; no detail is leaked | Yes, bounded |
| `503` | `tenant unavailable`; header `Retry-After: 30` | The environment's placement is being moved or is temporarily unavailable | Yes, after `Retry-After` |

Notes:

- In body parsing errors, depending on the extractor, `415` (wrong `Content-Type`) or `422` (JSON that does not conform to the schema) may also be seen. Rely only on the status code for the decision.
- The `401` and `403` difference: if the **identity** is missing or cannot be resolved, `401`; if the identity is valid but insufficient for this operation, `403`. On the player ticket endpoint all identity errors return `403` ([realtime protocol](../realtime/protocol.md)).
- If you call a server endpoint with a client key, you get `403 permission denied`; if the key is unknown, it is `401`.

### Purchase (`POST /v1/player/store/listings/{listing_id}/buy`) error codes

The player purchase endpoint states the rejection reason with a **JSON `code`**: `{"code":"out_of_stock","message":"…"}` (`message` is detail text; make your decision by `code`).

| `code` | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `not_visible` | 404 | The listing does not exist or is not visible to this player |
| `listing_changed` | 409 | The listing's version (`expected_version`) changed; refresh the catalog and show it again |
| `out_of_stock` | 422 | Out of stock |
| `limit_reached` | 422 | The per-player purchase limit is full |
| `insufficient_funds` | 422 | The balance is insufficient |
| `inventory_full` | 422 | The inventory is full |

Other errors (`400` header/body, `401`, `403` Origin or CSRF, idempotency mismatch `422`) are as in the general table above. An IAP listing cannot be bought from this endpoint (`422`). Details: [store guide](../guides/store-iap.md).

## Plugin endpoints

Plugin endpoints return a **JSON envelope**; give the `requestId` value in support requests (the same value is also in the `x-request-id` header).

```json
{"code":"unprocessable","message":"plugin command rejected","retryable":false,"requestId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-0000000000d1","reason":"street_reset_too_early"}
```

| `code` | Status | `retryable` | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unauthorized` | 401 | no | Session/key missing or invalid; a client key |
| `forbidden` | 403 | no | CSRF/Origin rejection; the plugin is not enabled; the version grant does not match; a banned account (`message: account banned`) |
| `module_disabled` | 404 | no | The `module` field names the disabled module |
| `not_found` | 404 | no | Unknown plugin or message type |
| `invalid_argument` | 400 | no | Broken/missing header, unknown schema version, a payload that does not conform to the schema |
| `conflict` | 409 | no | The `If-Match` version does not match |
| `idempotency_in_flight` | 409 | **yes** | A request with the same key is being processed |
| `idempotency_mismatch` | 422 | no | Same key, different body |
| `unprocessable` | 422 | no | A business rule rejection; `reason` is a plugin-specific machine code |
| `idempotency_expired` | 410 | no | The record expired |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | **yes** | `Retry-After: 60` |
| `tenant_unavailable` | 503 | **yes** | `Retry-After: 30` |
| `internal` | 500 | **yes** | |

Details and examples: [calling plugins](../plugins/calling-plugins.md).

> [!NOTE]
> On a plugin endpoint, a banned account, unlike the core identity endpoints, does not come with the `account_banned` code: `403`, `forbidden`, and `message: "account banned"` is returned. You need this distinction only for a user-interface message; do not build a retry loop.

## Differences between core and plugin

| | Core REST | Plugin |
|---|---|---|
| Body | Plain text (a few JSON exceptions) | Always JSON |
| Machine code | Only on errors that are JSON | `code` on every error |
| `retryable` | None; decide by status code | Present |
| Retry delay | Only `503` (30 s) | `429` (60 s) and `503` (30 s) |
| Banned account | `403` `account_banned` (on sign-in endpoints) | `403` `forbidden` |
| `x-request-id` | None | Present |

## Error handling recommendation

1. First look at the status code; for `401` renew the session or have the player sign in again; `403` is an authorization or configuration problem (key type, CSRF, module, plugin state).
2. For `404`, read the body: if it is JSON and `module_disabled`, the module is disabled; otherwise the resource does not exist.
3. Treat `409` in two separate ways: a version conflict (re-read the state) versus idempotency "in progress" (wait and repeat with the same key).
4. Use exponential backoff on `429` and `503`; if there is a `Retry-After`, wait for it (the example on the [idempotency and concurrency](idempotency-and-concurrency.md) page).
5. `422` is a business rule rejection; repeating the same request as is does not change the outcome.
6. The server does not leak error detail; when reporting a problem, give the status code, the request time, and (on plugin endpoints) the `requestId` ([troubleshooting](../operations/troubleshooting.md)).

docs.title: Glossary
docs.description: Short definitions of the terms used in the Open Play documentation; studio, environment, key types, session, plugin, and realtime concepts.
docs.body:
# Glossary

This page briefly defines the terms used in the documentation and links them to the relevant page. Terms are grouped by topic, not alphabetically.

## Structure: studio, game, environment

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Studio** | The top ownership level; it represents a team or a company. It hosts multiple games. Its management is in the **Server** section of the panel. |
| **Game** | The product under a studio. It has its own environments, modules, and API keys. |
| **Environment** | An isolated working copy of a game (for example development, live). Data is not shared between environments. Every API key and player session is bound to a single environment. |
| **Environment domain** | A domain bound to an environment; it is also used as the list of allowed origins (`Origin`) in browser requests. |
| **Module** | A product part that can be turned on and off: characters, economy, items, trading, store, rewards, social, chat, competition, notifications, webhooks, scenes, and plugins. The endpoints of a disabled module return `404 module_disabled`. |
| **Panel** (admin panel) | The web interface where you manage the game. The panel API is separate from the player API and is outside the scope of this documentation. |

## Identity and keys

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Server key** | A secret API key in the format `crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`, kept only on your server. It can call all server endpoints. It is never put in the client or the game bundle. |
| **Client key** | An API key that can be embedded in the client. It cannot run sensitive commands (for example `add_xp`); however, on some endpoints there is no type gate, so use it only if it is really needed ([endpoints](endpoints.md)). |
| **Player session** | The session created after the player signs in. It is carried with a cookie (`__Secure-crx.session`) or a Bearer session token and requires the `x-crx-env` header. |
| **Access JWT** | A short-lived token returned in the body when the session is opened, which your game server can verify offline with the JWKS. It is not the same thing as the session token. |
| **JWKS** | The public key set for verifying the access JWT (`GET /v1/auth/jwks`). |
| **Guest** | A player that needs no registration; it returns to the same player each time with the same secret value and can later be upgraded to an email account. |
| **CSRF** | Double submit that prevents the browser from sending unwanted requests on the user's behalf: a cookie + the `x-csrf-token` header. Required on modifying requests in a cookie session. |
| **Origin check** | The rule that on modifying requests the `Origin` header must be one of the environment's allowed origins. The server sends CORS headers only to origins in the same domain list; CORS is not authorization, this check runs separately. |
| **Same origin** | Serving the game and the API under the same domain (with a reverse proxy); [architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md). |
| **Realtime ticket** | A single-use, 30-second identity token obtained to connect to the realtime socket ([protocol](../realtime/protocol.md)). |

## Reliability: replay and conflict

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Idempotency** (replay safety) | The same request being applied once even if it is sent multiple times. Provided with the `Idempotency-Key` header ([idempotency and concurrency](idempotency-and-concurrency.md)). |
| **Idempotency-Key** | A 1 to 200 character key, generated by the client, that identifies an operation. |
| **Optimistic lock** | Adding the resource's version to the request and rejecting the request if the version changed. Done with `If-Match` or `expectedVersion`. |
| **`expectedVersion`** | The expected resource version: the `If-Match` header in HTTP, a field in the realtime `Command` frame, an option in the SDK. |
| **Fail-open** | A request passing without being limited if a limiter dependency (Redis) cannot be reached ([rate limits](rate-limits.md)). |

## Plugins

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Plugin** | A trusted package compiled into the server that offers game-specific commands, queries, and realtime modules ([overview](../plugins/overview.md)). Loading third-party plugins does not exist yet. |
| **Command** | A state-changing, durable, replay-safe operation. |
| **Query** | A read-only read. |
| **Schema document** (artifact) | The JSON document that describes all of a plugin's operations and schemas (`GET /v1/plugins/{id}/schema`). |
| **`schemaSha256`** | The digest of the `schemas` section in the schema document; the version pinning key ([bindings](../plugins/bindings.md)). |
| **Binding** | Typed client code generated from the schema document. |
| **Pin** | The record of which plugin and schema digest the client was built with; an `upgrade_required` error on a mismatch. |
| **Access type** (`access`) | The identity boundary of a plugin operation: `player`, `server`, or `public`. |
| **Plugin state** (grant state) | The plugin's state in an environment: enabled, read-only, draining, disabled. |
| **`plugin-v1-decimal-int64`** | The encoding profile that carries plugin and realtime `int64` values as decimal text ([numbers and encoding](numbers-and-encoding.md)). |

## Realtime

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Subscription** | A data stream opened with `Join`, bound to a module and a target; recognized by `subscriptionId`. |
| **Target** | What the subscription is bound to: `PlayerSelf`, `Room`, `Scene`, or `InterestSet`. |
| **Snapshot** | A full broadcast of transient state; ordered with `streamEpoch` and `revision`. |
| **Durable event** | A plugin event that can be recovered from the database, ordered by `sequence`. |
| **Cursor** | An opaque, player-bound value that shows where you left off in a durable stream ([reconnect](../realtime/reconnect-and-limits.md)). |
| **Epoch** | `sessionEpoch`: a socket's write epoch; a new socket invalidates the old one's inputs. `streamEpoch`: the number of resets of the state stream. |
| **Idle close** | The server closing the socket with `4100` when no player activity arrives on a subscription that accepts input. |
| **Backpressure** | Work being rejected because the client queue is full or because of the server's frame rate limit. |

## Data and in-game concepts

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Definition** | A character's schema and starting values; stored with immutable versions. |
| **Trait** | A reusable schema fragment mixed into definitions. |
| **Modifier** | A temporary or permanent bonus that affects a stat (for example from an item). |
| **Rule** | An automation bound to character events ([game rules](../guides/game-rules.md)). |
| **Minor unit** | The integer equivalent of a money value (for example cents). |
| **Basis point** | A percentage unit where `10000` = 100%. |
| **Soft delete** | A record becoming invisible while its event history is preserved. |
| **Content group** | A data set published from the panel and offered to the game as a catalog ([content groups](../guides/content-groups.md)). |
| **Webhook** | Open Play notifying your own server of events with a signed HTTP request ([webhooks guide](../guides/webhooks.md)). |
| **At-least-once** | Webhook delivery being done at least once, and more than once if needed; deduplicate with `X-Crx-Event-Id`. |

docs.title: Numbers and encoding
docs.description: Describes the wire format of integers, monetary values, timestamps, identifiers, and enumeration values.
docs.body:
# Numbers and encoding

This page describes how Open Play carries numbers, money, time, and identifiers over JSON. The most common mistake is converting 64-bit integers to JavaScript `number` and losing precision; read this page to avoid that mistake.

## Short rules

| Field type | Core REST | Plugin and realtime |
|---|---|---|
| 64-bit integer (`int64`) | JSON **number** (`"amount": 250`) | Decimal **text** (`"amount": "250"`) |
| 32-bit integer | JSON number | JSON number |
| Floating point | **Nowhere** | **Nowhere** |
| Money | Minor-unit integer (`amount`, `balance`) | Minor unit, `...Minor` fields, `int64` |
| Percentage | Basis point (10000 = 100%) | Basis point |
| Time | RFC 3339 text (`created_at`) | Unix milliseconds integer (`...Ms`) |
| Identifier | UUID text | UUID text |
| Enum | `snake_case` text | `snake_case` (plugin), `PascalCase` (realtime frame types) |

## 64-bit integers

JavaScript's `JSON.parse` converts numbers to `double`; integers above `2^53 − 1` (9,007,199,254,740,991) are **silently corrupted**. Open Play therefore uses two profiles:

- **Core REST** sends `int64` fields as JSON numbers (`version`, `balance`, `amount`). In practice the values stay in the safe range, but the guarantee is a parser that reads with `bigint`. The TypeScript SDK reads with `lossless-json` and returns `bigint`.
- **Plugin and realtime** (the `plugin-v1-decimal-int64` encoding profile) send and expect `int64` fields as **decimal text**: `{"expectedVersion":"3"}`, `{"sessionEpoch":"7"}`. This way every client language carries them losslessly.

### Canonical decimal text

In plugins a signed `int64` must be written in canonical form; the server rejects any other form (`400 invalid_argument`):

| Valid | Invalid | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `"0"`, `"42"`, `"-7"` | `"+1"` | No plus sign |
| `"9223372036854775807"` | `"01"`, `"007"` | No leading zero |
| `"-9223372036854775808"` | `"-0"` | No negative zero |
| | `" 5"`, `"5 "` | No whitespace |
| | `"1.5"`, `"1e3"` | No fraction or exponent |
| | `"9223372036854775808"` | The `int64` bound was exceeded |
| | `5` (JSON number) | A plugin `int64` field wants text |

The counters in realtime frames (`sessionEpoch`, `inputSeq`, `revision`, `sequence`, `expectedVersion`, `streamEpoch`, `barrierSequence`) are in the same text form and **cannot be negative**. `protocolVersion`, `schemaVersion`, and other small counters are JSON numbers.

In the plugin schema document, the bounds of an `int64` field are also written as text (`"minimum": "0"`, `"maximum": "9223372036854775807"`); this is normal.

### In client languages

| Language | Mapping |
|---|---|
| TypeScript SDK | `int64` → `bigint`. Do not convert to a number; use `value.toString()` for display. Do not read JSON yourself with `JSON.parse` |
| Unity (C#) | `int64` → `long`; in plugin outputs, raw JSON `JsonValue` stays as decimal text |
| Raw JSON (another language) | Read plugin fields as `string` and convert to `int64` |

If you parse JSON yourself in TypeScript, use a library such as `lossless-json`; otherwise large values are corrupted.

## Money and scaled values

- Money values are **minor-unit integers** (for example cents): how many main units `250` is depends on your game's display decision (the currency's "minor digits" setting in the panel determines the display); the API carries only the integer. Balance and amount fields come as `amount`, `balance`, and in plugins as `...Minor`.
- Floating point (`float`/`double`) is **used nowhere**: not in requests, not in responses, and not in computation. On your side too, do not use `float` for money; work with integers and convert to decimals only for display.
- Scaled values in content groups are an `integer + scale` pair: `4350` and scale `2` → `43.50`. In the TypeScript SDK, `formatScaled(value: bigint, scale)` formats this losslessly (`0 to 18` digits). Do not do your own `float` division.

## Percentages: basis points

Percentage and ratio fields are **basis point** integers: `10000` = 100%, `2500` = 25%, `1` = 0.01%. Example: the group reward share `share_bp` must be between `0` and `10000`; outside that gets `400`.

## Time

| Where | Format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Core REST responses (`created_at`, `as_of`) | RFC 3339 | `2026-11-03T10:15:30+00:00` |
| Plugin and realtime (`createdAtMs`, `sent_at_ms`) | Unix epoch milliseconds, integer | `1793700930000` |
| Chat query `before_ms` | Unix epoch milliseconds | `1793700930000` |
| `t` in the webhook signature | Unix epoch seconds | `1793700930` |
| `Deprecation` header | `@<unix seconds>` (RFC 9745) | `@1793491200` |
| Plugin deprecation (`sinceUnixS`) | Unix seconds | `1793577600` |

Interpret server times as **UTC**. The client clock is not used in server decisions: time and randomness are generated on the server and written to the event.

## Identifiers and keys

- **UUID:** lowercase, hyphenated text (`0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-000000000001`). Most resource IDs are time-ordered **UUID v7**; you can use them for ordering, but do not infer meaning from the format.
- **`key` fields** (definition keys, leaderboard, quest): readable identifiers given by the game developer; use them exactly as created, do not change the case or whitespace.
- **Plugin IDs:** lowercase and hyphens (`package-ride`). **Message types:** dot-separated, plugin-prefixed (`package-ride.delivery-trip.active.input`).
- **Cursors:** opaque text; do not parse their contents ([pagination](pagination.md)).
- **API keys:** `crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`; the prefix is only for identification, the secret part is shown only once ([security](../operations/security.md)).

## Enumeration (enum) values

All enumeration values come from a single definition on the server, and an unknown value is **rejected** (not silently ignored):

- Core REST fields are `snake_case` text (`"type": "set_flag"`, `"channel": "in_game"`, `"status": "pending"`).
- Realtime frame `type` and `kind` values are `PascalCase` (`Authenticate`, `PlayerSelf`); the field names are `camelCase`.
- Chat socket frame `type` values are `camelCase`, and the field names are `snake_case` (`channel_id`).
- Webhook event types are `snake_case` ([webhook events](webhook-events.md)).
- Values listed as `enum` in a plugin schema document (for example `"image/png"`) are used exactly.

If an unknown enum value arrives in your client (it may have been added in a new version), fall back to a safe default instead of crashing; the SDKs reject an unknown value in some places and skip it in others, so follow version upgrades from the changelog.

## Text

- All text is UTF-8 JSON text.
- Fields have length limits (for example `Idempotency-Key` 200 characters, `minLength`/`maxLength` on plugin string fields); a limit violation gets `400`.
- Plain-text error messages (core REST) can be in English or Turkish and change between versions; do not use them for machine decisions ([errors](errors.md)).

docs.title: Pagination
docs.description: Describes the pagination formats Open Play uses on its list endpoints, page size limits, and cursor rules by endpoint family.
docs.body:
# Pagination

This page describes how to walk the pages of endpoints that return lists. In Open Play there is **no single pagination format**: most endpoints use an opaque cursor, while a few use a different method. The table below shows which applies on which endpoint and the page size limits.

## Cursor (keyset) pagination

Most core list endpoints are **cursor-based**:

- Request: `?limit=<n>&cursor=<cursor>`. On the first page you do not provide `cursor`.
- Response: `{"items":[…],"next_cursor":"…"}`. If `next_cursor` is **`null`**, you are on the last page.
- Next page: give **the `next_cursor` from the previous response** exactly as the `cursor`.
- The cursor is **opaque**: do not parse its contents, do not modify it, and do not assume you can store it and use it after a long time. A broken cursor gets `400`.
- The ordering is fixed and `OFFSET` is not used; if new records are added between pages, no skipping or repetition occurs (records are ordered by a stable key).
- The page size is given with `limit`; a value outside the bounds is **clamped** on most endpoints (it does not give an error). The exceptions are noted in the table.

```http
GET /v1/characters?limit=2 HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

```json
{"items":[{"id":"…","definition":"hero","version":3}],"next_cursor":"<opaque-cursor>"}
```

```http
GET /v1/characters?limit=2&cursor=<opaque-cursor> HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

## Formats by endpoint

| Endpoint | Format | Default | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/characters` | Cursor (`definition` filter) | 50 | clamped between 1 and 200 |
| `GET /v1/characters/{id}/events`, `…/timeline` | Cursor (ascending `seq`) | 50 | clamped between 1 and 200 |
| `GET /v1/rules`, `GET /v1/webhooks` | Cursor | 50 | clamped between 1 and 200 |
| `GET /v1/ledger` | Cursor (`wallet_id` required) | 50 | clamped between 1 and 200 |
| `GET /v1/items`, `GET /v1/player/items` | Cursor (with `owner`) | 50 | clamped between 1 and 200 |
| `GET /v1/assets` | Cursor | 50 (`0` or absent = default) | at most 200 |
| `GET /v1/catalog/items`, `GET /v1/catalog/characters` | Cursor | 50 | clamped between 1 and 100 |
| `GET /v1/notifications` | Cursor (`status`, `limit`, `cursor`) | 50 | clamped between 1 and 100 |
| `GET /v1/leaderboards/{key}/entries` | Cursor | 20 (`0` or absent = default) | **at most 100; more gets `400`** (not clamped) |
| `GET /v1/leaderboards/{key}/around-me` | Around the player (`player_id`, `radius`) | — | No pages; the surrounding windows are bounded |
| `GET /v1/player/leaderboards/{key}` | Single page (`limit`) | 20 | **1 to 50; outside that `400`** |
| `GET /v1/chat/channels/{channel_id}/messages` | Time-based (`before_ms` + `limit`) | 50 | 1 to 100 (the service validates) |
| `GET /v1/quests` | **`offset` + `limit`** (`search` filter) | 20 (`0` or absent = default) | **`limit` at most 100, `offset` at most 100000; more gets `400`** |
| `GET /v1/auth/admin/list-players` | Cursor (UUID) | the endpoint's default | Endpoint-specific |
| `GET /v1/clans`, `GET /v1/parties` | No pagination; the whole result (a `player_id` filter for parties) | — | — |
| `GET /v1/wallets`, `GET /v1/inventories/{owner}` | No pagination (the whole list by owner) | — | — |
| Plugin queries (`/v1/plugins/…/queries/…`) | Plugin-specific; defined in the input schema | — | The plugin's schema document |

> [!NOTE]
> In the response, the cursor field comes as `next_cursor` (snake_case) in core REST. In chat messages, to get a new page you give the oldest message's `sent_at_ms` value as `before_ms`. The pagination of the panel APIs (`offset`/grid) is for the panel interface's internal use and is outside the scope of this documentation.

## Pagination in the SDK

The TypeScript SDK offers iterators for cursor lists: `iterateListCharacterEvents`, `iterateGetCharacterTimeline`, `iterateListRules`, `iterateListWebhooks`. These iterators follow `next_cursor` for you. Important rules:

- The cursor is opaque; the iterator gives it back without converting it.
- An empty `next_cursor` ends the loop; a cursor loop (the same cursor coming back) or exceeding `maxPages` is **not a silent cut-off but an error of type `pagination`**.
- `limit` is `u32` on the wire; the server clamps it to the range 1 to 200.

## Patterns

**Walking everything** (server-to-server work): build a loop until the cursor comes back empty; put a short upper bound on pages (for example at most 1000 pages).

```text
cursor = none
repeat:
    page = GET /v1/rules?limit=200[&cursor=cursor]
    process page.items
    cursor = page.next_cursor
    stop if cursor is empty
```

**An in-game "load more" list:** use a small `limit` (20 to 50), keep `next_cursor` in memory, and request the next page as the user scrolls. Do not store the cursor persistently.

**Consistency:** cursor pages walk live data; new records added while walking may not be visible if they fall behind the cursor. For reports that need a snapshot, record the query time (for example `as of`) on your side.

Related: [endpoints](endpoints.md), [rate limits](rate-limits.md).

docs.description: Honestly lists Open Play's known rate limit buckets, the format of the 429 response, and the Retry-After rules.
headings: What you need to do on your side
docs.body:
# Rate limits

This page describes the rate limits Open Play applies today and what to do when you get a `429`. An important honesty note: **there is no general rate limit per API key.** Limits are placed on specific operations (sign-in, sign-up, chat, plugin command, socket connection); the other endpoints are unlimited and you must manage the load.

## What you need to know

- **There is no general "N requests per minute" quota.** For calls made with a server key, there is no general limit per key or per environment.
- Counters are kept in Redis and **if Redis cannot be reached, the limit is not applied** (fail-open); the only exception is the audit-row ceiling noted below. Do not use the limit alone as a security control.
- The `Retry-After` header exists only on the plugin `429` (60 s) and on `503` responses (30 s). The `429` of the core and identity endpoints carries no `Retry-After`; apply your own backoff.
- The client IP is the key of the limits on the identity endpoints. If the reverse proxy does not forward the client IP, **all players share the same bucket** ([production checklist](../operations/production-checklist.md)).

## Identity endpoints (the player sign-in line)

These limits are applied in the service layer; they are the same in REST itself. The window is fixed (it starts with the first request and the counter resets when the time expires; it is not a sliding window); an overage returns `429` and the plain text `rate limited` (no `Retry-After`).

| Bucket | Limit | Window | Key | Which endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opening a guest | 30 | 60 s | Client IP | `POST /v1/auth/sign-in/guest` (re-sign-in counts too) |
| Email sign-in | 5 | 60 s | Client IP | `POST /v1/auth/sign-in/email` (every attempt) |
| Failed sign-in lock | 10 | 900 s | Address + IP | Wrong password attempts; the allowance is refunded on a successful sign-in; a wrong current password on a password change counts too |
| Sign-up (IP) | 10 | 60 s | Client IP | `POST /v1/auth/sign-up/email`, guest upgrade |
| Sign-up (session) | 30 | 60 s | Session owner | `POST /v1/auth/guest/upgrade/email` |
| Sign-up (address) | 5 | 900 s | Email address | Sign-up and upgrade |
| Password change (IP) | 10 | 60 s | Client IP | `POST /v1/auth/change-password` |
| Password change (account) | 6 | 60 s | Player | `POST /v1/auth/change-password` |
| Recovery (IP) | 5 | 60 s | Client IP | `forgot-password`, `reset-password`, `sign-in/magic-link` (the three endpoints share one bucket) |
| Recovery (address) | 5 | 900 s | Email address | `forgot-password`, `sign-in/magic-link` |
| OAuth start | 30 | 60 s | Client IP | `sign-in/oauth/{provider}`, `link/{provider}` |
| OAuth return | 60 | 60 s | Client IP | `callback/{provider}` |

In addition:

| Limit | Limit | Key | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Display name change | 10 / 3600 s | Player | `POST /v1/auth/session/display-name`; an overage is `429` |
| Account deletion attempt | 5 / 3600 s | Player | `POST /v1/auth/account/delete`; an overage is `429` |
| Failed sign-in audit row | 20 / 3600 s | Account | Does **not** reject the sign-in; it only throttles the background audit record. During a Redis outage the record is skipped (fail-closed) |

> [!NOTE]
> The guest opening bucket is per IP. If the reverse proxy does not forward the client IP, or many players connect from behind a NAT/dormitory network, the limit of 30 guests/minute fills quickly. If you plan a launch or a load test, verify IP forwarding.

## Chat and notifications

| Limit | Limit | Window | Key | When exceeded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sending a chat message | 20 | 10 s | Environment + player | `429` in REST; `message_rejected` on the chat socket |
| Notification delivery | 60 | 60 s | Environment + player | Delivery is deferred (the provider is not hit), no error returns to the player |

## Plugin commands

Plugin commands and queries can be subject to per-minute budgets **per player, per bucket**. The plugin defines the budget; the server applies it with the same decision on the REST, realtime command, and gRPC paths. An overage arrives with the plugin envelope: `429`, `code: "rate_limited"`, `retryable: true`, `Retry-After: 60`.

The plugin that defines a budget today is `package-ride`: 6 to 60 commands per bucket in a 60 s window (for example delivery accept/start/complete 12, login bonus 10, quest reward and garage 30, collision/race bet 60). The bucket values are plugin-specific and may change; for exact numbers, see the plugin's documentation. The operator can put some buckets into "observation" mode; in this mode an overage is only counted, and the command is not rejected.

In the Unity SDK, `PluginClient.RetryAfter(error)` returns **60 seconds** for the plugin `429`.

## Realtime socket

| Limit | Value | When exceeded |
|---|---|---|
| New connections per address | 30 / minute | The upgrade is rejected |
| Open sockets per address | 8 | `CapacityExceeded`, the socket closes |
| Open sockets per player | 4 | `CapacityExceeded`, the socket closes |
| Per-connection frame rate | 40/s (a 160-frame burst allowance) | `CapacityExceeded` (`retryable: true`), the socket closes |

Details: [reconnect and limits](../realtime/reconnect-and-limits.md).

## When you get a 429

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

rate limited
```

On a plugin endpoint:

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 60
x-request-id: 0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-0000000000d1

{"code":"rate_limited","message":"rate limited","retryable":true,"requestId":"0192a3b4-0000-7000-8000-0000000000d1"}
```

1. If there is a `Retry-After`, wait that long; if not, use exponential backoff (for example 1, 2, 4, 8 s; upper bound 30 s) and add a random jitter.
2. If the request is modifying, repeat with **the same `Idempotency-Key`** ([idempotency and concurrency](idempotency-and-concurrency.md)).
3. For limits triggered by a user action (sign-in, sign-up), instead of an automatic retry show the user the wait time; on the password and sign-up endpoints an automatic retry extends the lock time.
4. `CrxClient` (server key) retries a `429` on `GET` and keyed requests itself, respecting `Retry-After` (default 2 attempts).

> [!WARNING]
> A rule budget overage (`rule budget exceeded: <rule>`) also returns `429`; this is not a rate limit but the rule engine budget (50 rules per command, 200 actions, 500 evaluation nodes, and chain depth 5). Retrying does not change the outcome; simplify the rule ([game rules](../guides/game-rules.md)).

## What you need to do on your side

Because there is no general server limit, you need to add protection under heavy load:

- In server-to-server bulk jobs, limit concurrency (for example 5 to 10 requests at a time) and manage errors with backoff.
- Measure the request rate per key on your own side; a single leaked key can make unlimited calls ([security](../operations/security.md)).
- Before a launch, cache `GET /v1/…` reads (catalog endpoints support conditional reads with `ETag` and `If-None-Match`; do not poll per player more often than every 15 s).

docs.title: Versioning
docs.description: Describes what the protocol, plugin schema, and SDK versions in Open Play mean, and the deprecation (Deprecation) practice.
docs.body:
# Versioning

This page describes the version numbers you will encounter in Open Play (API path, protocol, plugin schema, SDK) and how the server notifies you when an endpoint or operation is being deprecated. Important: **there is no written breaking-change and removal policy yet**; below, only the behavior that is in the code today is described.

## What each version tells you

| Version | Where it appears | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| API path `/v1` | All endpoint paths | The single path version; there is no `/v2` |
| Realtime `protocolVersion` | In every frame (`1`) | The socket protocol major version; a different value gets `UnsupportedProtocol` |
| Plugin `protocolVersion` | Schema document (`1`) | The major version of the plugin contract |
| `codecProfile` | Schema document (`plugin-v1-decimal-int64`) | The wire encoding; a single profile for now |
| Plugin `version` | Schema document (for example `1.44.0`) | The plugin's version text |
| `schemaVersion` | Every operation and message definition; the `x-crx-schema-version` header | The schema version of a single message (a positive integer) |
| `schemaSha256` | Schema document | The digest of the schemas; the pinning key ([bindings](../plugins/bindings.md)) |
| SDK version | Package version | TypeScript `@ferdiunal/open-play-ts` (0.x), Unity `com.openplay.sdk` (0.x) |

### `/v1` and the server version

All HTTP endpoints are under `/v1`. The server has no separate "API version" header; which endpoints exist is shown by the [endpoint reference](endpoints.md) and (for core REST) `GET /openapi.json`. `/openapi.json` is a hand-compiled document that covers core REST: it **does not cover plugins, WebSockets, or the panel API** and may not be complete for every endpoint.

### Protocol version

`protocolVersion: 1` is required in realtime frames; any other value gets an `UnsupportedProtocol` error and the socket closes. If your client gets this error, instead of retrying ask the user to update (the TypeScript SDK moves to the `upgradeRequired` state in this case).

### Plugin schema versions

A plugin schema is versioned at two levels:

1. **Operation/message level** `schemaVersion`: declared on every request with `x-crx-schema-version`. If you send a version different from what the server knows, you get `400 invalid_argument`.
2. **Document level** `schemaSha256`: any change in the schemas changes the digest. You pin your client to this digest.

The version text (`1.44.0`) is informational; make the compatibility decision by the digest. For how to verify the plugin version and the digest match, see [bindings](../plugins/bindings.md).

## Deprecation

When an endpoint or operation is being deprecated, it **keeps working**; its behavior, status codes, and body do not change. The deprecation is notified to you with these signals:

| Signal | Where |
|---|---|
| The `Deprecation: @<unix seconds>` response header ([RFC 9745](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9745)) | On every deprecated response (successful or erroneous) |
| OpenAPI `deprecated: true` | On the relevant operation in `/openapi.json` |
| A `deprecated` object in the schema document | On plugin operations: `since` (version text), `sinceUnixS`, and `replacement` (the short name of the surface that replaces it) |
| `@deprecated` in the SDK | On the relevant operation in the generated TypeScript binding |

What is deprecated today:

| Surface | Header value | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/auth/organization/*` (player organizations, 19 endpoints) | `@1793491200` (2026-11-01 UTC) | None; the organization feature is being deprecated, do not confuse it with the studio concept |
| The `package-ride` plugin's daily score queries (`getDailyBoard`, `getLeaderboard`) | `@1793577600` (2026-11-02 UTC) | The core leaderboard ("Daily earnings") |
| The `package-ride` operator player view (`operatorPlayer`, `operatorPlayers`) | `@1793577600` | The core character profile and list |

The header's value gives the moment the deprecation **started** (UTC unix seconds); it does **not** give a removal date. There is no `Sunset` header in the response.

> [!WARNING]
> There is **no** promise such as a removal date, a minimum notice period, or "a deprecated endpoint works for at least N months". Do not add a new dependency on a deprecated surface, and when you see the `Deprecation` header, make a migration plan. To track the header in your logs, record the response headers.

## SDK versions

- The TypeScript SDK is in `0.x` versions; breaking changes may occur between `0.x` versions. Follow each version's changes from the package's changelog and release notes; pin the version exactly (like `0.1.15`), and do not use a `^` range.
- The Unity SDK is at version `0.1.0` and is verified only with Unity `6000.6.7f1` ([Unity SDK](../sdk/unity.md)).
- The SDK and the server evolve together: a new SDK feature (for example leaderboard, store) requires the server version that carries that feature. Do not update the SDK before the server.
- In plugin bindings, compatibility depends not on the SDK version but on the `schemaSha256` pin ([bindings](../plugins/bindings.md)).

## What to do

1. Write your SDK version and your plugin `schemaSha256` values into your release manifest.
2. After every server update, compare the schema document and, if needed, regenerate the binding.
3. Open a migration task for every call that sees the `Deprecation` header.
4. On a realtime and plugin protocol version mismatch, ask the user to update; do not build a retry loop.

# Webhook events

This page lists the event types you can subscribe a webhook endpoint to and the headers sent with every delivery. For registration and signature verification see the [webhook guide](../guides/webhooks.md). Descriptions are currently in Turkish.

## Delivery headers

| Header | Description |
|---|---|
| `X-Crx-Signature` | `t=<unix-seconds>,v1=<hex>`; `v1` = `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{t}.{raw body}")`. |
| `X-Crx-Event-Id` | Event id (UUID); use it to drop repeated deliveries. |
| `X-Crx-Event-Type` | Event type (one of the values in the table below). |

## Webhook events

Total event types: **23**.

| Event type | Source | When it is sent |
|---|---|---|
| `flag_set` | Character | Bir bayrak (flag) ayarlandı. |
| `attribute_set` | Character | Bir öznitelik değeri ayarlandı. |
| `resource_changed` | Character | Bir kaynağın değeri değişti (yeni değer olayda yer alır). |
| `modifier_added` | Character | Karaktere bir değiştirici (modifier) eklendi. |
| `modifiers_removed` | Character | Bir kaynaktan gelen değiştiriciler kaldırıldı. |
| `xp_added` | Character | Karaktere XP eklendi. |
| `level_up` | Character | Karakter seviye atladı. |
| `ability_unlocked` | Character | Karakterin bir yeteneği açıldı. |
| `event_emitted` | Character | Bir kural özel bir olay yayınladı. |
| `character_rolled_back` | Character | Karakter önceki bir sürüme geri alındı (yeni olay olarak yazılır). |
| `store_page_created` | Store | Mağaza sayfası oluşturuldu. |
| `store_page_updated` | Store | Mağaza sayfası güncellendi. |
| `store_page_deleted` | Store | Mağaza sayfası silindi. |
| `store_pages_reordered` | Store | Mağaza sayfaları yeniden sıralandı. |
| `store_listing_created` | Store | Mağaza ilanı oluşturuldu. |
| `store_listing_updated` | Store | Mağaza ilanı güncellendi. |
| `store_listing_deleted` | Store | Mağaza ilanı silindi. |
| `store_listings_reordered` | Store | Bir sayfadaki ilanlar yeniden sıralandı. |
| `store_purchase_initiated` | Store | Satın alma rezervasyonu açıldı. |
| `store_payment_started` | Store | Satın alma için ödeme başladı. |
